title: Great in some ways, not so in others
text: Ok first off, I had the Rift before this S model, so this is somewhat of a comparison. The Rift S is definitely more comfortable than it's predecessor. The foam is soft and it seems a tad lighter. I wear glasses, and the S does not rest on them as much as the last generation, which is good. I can spend much more time using the Rift S because it's comfort is that much better. The S also slips on and off my face a lot easier than the last generation and I have a large head, being 6'5" @ 275lbs. It is great that it does not use external sensors to track movement, because it is just far less cumbersome and more of a simple plug and play device now. I have an Acer Predator 17, which has a display port, but the Rift S does come with an adapter if yours does not. The controllers are the same size and weight, which is really good. They are far less bulky than it's competitors, which makes using the VR much more enjoyable in my opinion. Headset tracking of itself is flawless, it is right on when you move your head around. However, I do get headset out of bounds type messages just looking around sometimes and that is annoying. Eye relief, I don't really know about. I've adjusted it to max (72) and least and noticed zero difference in anything. The bad news. External tracking of the controllers is glitchy and glitchy a lot. You no longer have a fine tracking experience that is so smooth, as it was in the previous Rift. Your hands in the VR like to twitch, jump and sometimes freeze. It's not 100% of the time that it does this, but it happens frequently enough to be bothersome. The rest of the time it is smooth and responsive. Optics. This is where the Rift S falls even shorter, in my experience. For starters, your field of view has reduced and it is not quite as immersive as the previous Rift. For example, it is as though you are looking through toilet paper tubes now, as there are large black areas of nothing surrounding the visual field. Tunnel vision. Although the experience is still fun, I am very disappointed in this, as it has lost some of it's VR experience as a result. The resolution is supposed to be higher, but I do not see that at all. Fonts are still grainy and it is too similar to the last Rift to say that there is much, if any improvement in resolution. The screen brightness is less in the Rift S, so it loses points for that. Although still pretty vibrant, it's just lacking something I can't exactly put my finger on. Overall, it is a step back from the Rift in the critical areas a VR should be and a step forward in comfort and convenience. It all depends on what is more important to you.

title: Excellent Value for a One-Handed Mechanical Gaming Keyboard
text: RedThunder One-Handed Mechanical Gaming Keyboard is a functional half keyboard with mechanical keys. The only issue I ran into during my use of this item was that once the re-bindable macro keys were altered, I was unable to revert them into the original "F" keys they began. The instructions were difficult to fully understand. I am uncertain if it was due to translation difficulties or a lack of space on the small pamphlet. RedThunder One-Handed Mechanical Gaming Keyboard allowed me to conserve space on my desk. The keyboard is a good starting point for any gamer interested in an mechanical keyboard that does not want to commit to the higher price for a full keyboard. With small rubber-like feet to help keep it in place and the light weight design the product can help on-the-go laptop users. The keyboard had built in anti-ghosting, so you would not drop keys when pressing multiples at the same time. This will allow more hectic game-play without dropped inputs. The half of the keyboard you get with this covers most basic PC games (most First person shooters), but may leave you lacking for games which expect a full range (such as Smite or a multitude of strategy games). A small card that came with the keyboard from the creator pressing for those with issues to reach out to the makers and those with positive opinions to share their opinion. The website advertised by the production company was mostly not useful as I was unable to find anything of great use and there was a number of translation errors on the physical box [example: "Fast eating chicken stability with many key no conflict reaction"]. Overall, I find RedThunder One-Handed Mechanical Gaming Keyboard is a good product. It's ideal for someone who is looking to reduce their wear and tear on a laptop, shared keyboard, an addition to their portable/space sensitive options, or anyone wanting to dip their toes into a mechanical keyboard. Of note: the box does not mention support for windows 10. They keys are click-y and the extra volume can be jarring for those whom live in close quarters. Thank you for reading my review. I hope you have found it helpful and informative.

My husband and I decided to try them out last night to make sure they worked well because I have sent gifts to family before to get a call that they did not work and I didn't want that happening again. The dock it's self is very slim and fit really well next to our console and didn't add any clutter. The batteries charged and were easy to put on our controllers and we played Diablo for almost 5 hours (don't judge!) and the batteries lasted the entire time and had no issues. I super happy with the batteries and I am excited to go down this month to celebrate all the holidays and give this to my brother so he can finally be in the 21st Century with gaming controllers.

title: Nicest headphones I have ever owned
text: These headphones are really beautiful. I've used a lot of different headphones and these are the most comfortable headphones I have ever worn. They don't put pressure on your ears or head. The ear cushions are exquisite. So comfortable. The sound quality is really good. While playing Valheim, I could easily detect the direction where the cackling Fulings are hiding in the brush, or when a Draugr is trying to sneak up behind me. I really appreciate that level of sensitivity in headphones. I don't have a cellphone, so I can't speak about the Bluetooth functions. I will say though , that some of the technical mechanics of the headphones were a little hard for me to figure out. The instruction manual wasn't much help. I am a technical dummy. My level of technical expertise is basically, find the button, push it, and I expect it to work. If it doesn't work, I will get immensely frustrated. I found myself getting very frustrated trying to get my headphones to work. I thought I was following instructions, but it just wasn't working. I enlisted my husband to help me. He got it working and it turned out to be something really simple...the USB cord for plugging the headset into my laptop wasn't plugged in all the way into the headset. I didn't realize that I needed to push so hard to get it to click into place. One of the things that confused me, is that the cord has a control on it, for sound. The control has no marks on it. There were 3 buttons and I couldn't figure out what all of them were for. The long was was a volume control. I got that one. I still don't understand what the other two buttons are for. It would have been nice if this was explained better in the manual, and if they were actually visibly marked with clear, understandable icons. Basically, these are really great headphones. I just think that the company is trying to hard to look cool at the expense of functionality and customer accessability. Perhaps the company feels that it's customer base are savvy techies that would appreciate the level of coolness that they are trying to achieve, but that leaves us normals frustrated and struggling to understand how to use their product. If the company reads this review...fyi. Normals like great sounding gaming too. Make these easier to use.

title: Not as good as the real thing
text: I have a horrible problem with this controller. For some people, it may be fine, but for me, I can't use it at all. Let me explain. I play RPG's, like Skyrim, Dragon's Dogma, and Valheim. I nearly always play as an archer. These off-brand controllers have a real problem getting the look sensitivity right. For a smash and slash sword weilder, this would not be a problem. For me, I can't aim my bow. As I try to aim, the crosshairs swOOOP right and left, up and down, I have no fine control over my aim. It's horrible. Adjusting the look sensitivity does nothing. I don't know why I keep trying these off-brand controllers, but I am always disappointed by them. Pass this up and get a real xBox controller. My old, broken one works better than this one.

title: Doesn't work well
text: I compare this with my real xBox controller. I just doesn't work as well. Specifically, in the look sensitivity. Off-brand controllers just never get that right. This may not be a problem with gamers who have a sword & board, mash-em up fighting style, but I usually play games as an archer (Skyrim, Valheim, Dragon Age), and look sensitivity is really important. If I'm trying to aim my bow to kill that troll barrelling down on me and my bow is swinging wildly, side to side, and I can't aim my shot, I have a problem. That is exactly what this controller does. There is no fine control in the look sensitivity. It makes it impossible for me to play with this controller. And for the record, turning the look sensitivity in the game up and down does nothing to help the problem. I don't recommend this.

title: Don't work
text: I got these for my husband so that we could play Valhiem together with our son. He could hear sound through the headset, but he could not get the mic to work, no mater what he did. He is a computer programmer, and handy diy'er, so he knows how to get things to work. He finally gave up on this. There were no instruction that would help at all. So, these are basically trash for the purpose that we got them for. If you want them just for listening, they are okay, but the sound isn't the greatest. You can find better headsets for that purpose.

title: Don't like it
text: I keep trying these off-brand xBox controllers, and I keep being disappointed by them. My biggest beef with his controller is that the controls in-game are just...swoopy! It doesn't matter how low I turn down the look sensitivity, when you look around it swOOPs left and swOOPs right. There is no feeling of control at all. It's horrible. In game, it gives you the feeling of being on a floating, with no connection to the landscape or spaces. I played Skyrim on it. If I swung around to smack a sabre cat that was attaching me, I would way overswing. Aiming with a bow was nearly impossible. I put this away after just a little while. I couldn't handle it. The wacky movement was making me sick to my stomach. Buy the real Microsoft product. Honestly, it is just not worth buying an off-brand.

title: Fail!
text: I really HATE this controller. I tried to play Enderal (a mod for Skyrim) on my laptop. It was horrible. The look sensitivity was WAY off, and no matter what I did, I couldn't adjust it or make it better. Every where I looked the view camera would SWOOP from side-to-side, and up-and down. After a short while, it actually made me feel a bit seasick. I had to disconnect it and plug in my old MIcrosoft made controller. Fantastic! My old controller worked fine and I had no more problems. This is not a real Microsoft product and it shows. It is horrible. Completely unusable. Get the real thing instead.

title: Works great
text: I am mostly a console gamer, but I wanted to play RLCraft, which is only available on PC...for now. Trying to use a keyboard for gaming was a little daunting for me. Too many keys...very confusing. I thought that getting this half-keyboard would help break me into it. I do like it. Using the mouse and the keyboard together works great. I'm still pretty clumsy at it, but that's just my learning curve, the equipment works great. Hardcore PC gamers would probably rather use a whole keyboard, and I admit that it would be better, at least for RLCraft. With the half-keyboard, too many keys overlap and I am not savvy enough with the PC to figure out how to configure everything properly. For now though, it works fine and I recommend it, especially for new PC gamers.

title: Better than my Microsoft charge station!
text: I LOVE this charging station for my xBox One controllers. It comes with batteries and a new battery cover for two controllers, as well as the charging station itself. The controller is a little fiddly to get into the slot correctly, but when you do, the base lights up red, so that you can see that it is charging. When done, it turns to green. Easy! My only issue is with the batteries. They definitely don't last as long as the genuine Microsoft controller batteries. I am only getting about 10 hours of gameplay before having to charge them. Genuine Microsoft batteries last about twice as long for me. It is easy to compare this it to actual Microsoft products, because I treated myself to a Microsoft brand charging station for Black Friday. It didn't work from day one...well...technically it works, but I have to clamp the controller to the charger with a rubber band in order for the charging components to make and keep contact.

title: Uncomfortable
text: I gave this headset a middle of the road rating. It has some good points...like good sound, nice fabric wrapped cord, easy controls, and the headpiece adjusts easily, but it has some drawbacks as well. One of the most glaring problems is the ear covers. They are just too small...and round. How many people do you know with ROUND ears? Most ears are oval in shape. I think my ears are pretty normal size, but they don't quite fit in the ear cushions. It is very uncomfortable. I tried using the headset with my xBox One in a chat group with my friends. At one point they were having trouble hearing me. There are only two sound controls, the mute switch (which works fine), and a volume control. I thought the volume control was to control the level of sound I was hearing in the earphones. Apparently, it controls my voice to the group, because my friends were having trouble hearing me until I tinkered with the volume control. When I turned it up, they could hear me better. That was a little confusing. In the end, I took this headset off and went back to using my Turtle Beach headset. I don't recommend this headset.

title: Wondered if this was a real Microsoft product
text: I had a lot of trouble syncing this controller to my xbox. Got really frustrated, until I finally just plugged it in with the charge cord. That didn't even work, at first, but it finally kicked in and synced up. The other weird thing is the center "x" button in the center. My other controllers have a button that is slightly domed. This one is flat and just feels weird. It is more awkward to press than the domed version. It just made me wonder if this was really a knock-off, instead of the real deal. It is working fine now, though, so I'll keep it.

title: Mixed Feelings. Not quite the quality I've come to expect in Turtle Beach.
text: I am disappointed with this headset. It is definitely better than the vanilla chat headset the comes with the xBox One, but not as good as my other stereo headset by Turtle Beach. The sound in the ear is pretty good. I like the "open" ear feature that allows me to hear my family when they try to talk to me. The part that I'm not as happy with is the mic and the cord. The sound quality of the mic isn't as good as the stereo headset. My chat friends notice a difference when I switch and say they can't hear me as well with this one.The other problem is the cord. I've owned this headset for less than 3 months, and the cord has frayed and is breaking at the base of the connector to the controller. Where the plug-in becomes wire gets pinched against me when I hold it. It can't be avoided, therefore it is breaking. I wish the connector was a 90 degree plug-in that I've seen on other headsets. Those seem to hold up better.

title: Middle of the Pack.
text: This headset is adequate for the job. The earpiece is fairly comfortable and produces good sound. I like the mic's flexibility. It is easy to manipulate it into a good position. The mic's pickup, however is weak, and I often find my online friends saying that they can't hear me, even though the mic is right next to my mouth, and the volume is all the way up. The headset also slips out of position, which is annoying. It's still better than the basic xbox mic/headset that microsoft sells. I will probably be in the market for a better headset soon. I need an upgrade to this one.

title: Full Immersion into Tamriel! Couldn't be happier.
text: Outstanding game! I am thoroughly enjoying my adventures in the Elder Scrolls Online. There is so much to do, I've spent hours in the game and have still barely left my original spawning area. I am a huge Elder Scrolls fan. This game definitely delivers a satisfying experience as far as being true to the history and lore of Tamriel. The quests are challenging, the stories engaging, the game world is beautiful. There are new mechanics for crafting and the skill/ability builds are different than what you may be used to in say...Oblivion or Skyrim. Crafting has been expanded and it really helps to have friends online to play with, form guilds and share abilities. That helps to let you focus on one or two crafting abilities, while your friends can specialize in others. You can all share the results of your labor to mutual benefit. I fully intend to purchase the DLC's to the game when I get a chance...and the money.

title: LOVE Dragons Dogma!
text: I'm giving this game full stars, because I love Dragons Dogma. It has the best combat play of ANY RPG, in my opinion. The creatures are unmatched in any RPG for realism, creepiness and dreadfulness as opponents. The story, quite frankly...SUCKS!...but don't let that stop you from trying out this game. DISCLOSURE: I haven't actually gotten to play the Dark Arisen portion of the game yet. I had been playing the game without the DLC for quite some time. I finally ordered the DLC version and was going to play, but a house fire destroyed my new copy of the game. :( I plan to reorder it though as soon as I am able. I have heard that it is much more challenging than the original, and can't wait to try it.

title: Fantastic! Love this game!
text: Awesome Game! I'm on my third playthrough since I bought this and have loved it! It is a great addition to the Dragon's Age story. Being able to play as a Quanari is VERY cool! The new combat abilities are awesome! The new health/healing system takes a little getting used to, but with practice I am able to play without dying...much (Of course I'm on casual mode, since I hate dying). The new characters are interesting, the story is compelling, the created world is GORGEOUS! My one complaint is that the boss battles are perhaps a little bit too easy, but that might just because I play in the easiest mode. If you want more challenge, try the harder modes of play.

title: A Little Known Gem of a Game
text: I really liked this game. I had never heard of it before, until I did an impromptu search for games by Ubisoft and found it in the list. A quick view of what the game was like on YouTube and I decided to try it. The story is interesting, and teases you all the way to the end. It has challenging puzzles and the gameplay mechanics are easy to master. I'm not a huge fan of 1st person style gameplay, but it worked well in this game and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Since you play as one type of character (mage, warrior, assassin, etc...) you can play the game more than once using a different skill set each time. You can also choose whether to be evil or good, which will change the story as well. If you like Oblivion, Dragon Age or The Witcher, I think you will really enjoy this game as well. There are multi-player online options of play as well, that will further extend your enjoyment of the game.

title: Lots of fun
text: I like when my kids play games because it so much better than staring at a screen. This was a very fun game for my kids. They really enjoyed it. It kept their interest. I really like that it gets them playing with others. It is great for them to play with each other or with us. We like to have family game nights. This game wasn’t too hard for them to learn. The quality was very good. It held together fine. I really think it’s a lot of fun for them. I also like to give games as gifts. I would recommend this one.

title: Works
text: This cable (with an appropriate charger) powers the switch faster than it uses power (so if you plug in and start playing, the battery will still charge up). NOTE: To do this, you need a good charger. I've got about a dozen battery packs, and only one of them will supply this much power! That one is an Anker, but then again, so are 4 others that don't work. The PowerCore 20,000 is the one that works, but Anker has made several versions of this and I own two and the other doesn't work. So I guess what I'm saying is "good luck!"

title: Nice keyboard
text: This is a very nice keyboard. I really like the blue illumination. After starting with an illuminated keyboard I would never go back to a plain one again. It really helps to see the keys. The blue is very pretty, and looks great. The keyboard worked very well. I thought it was very responsive. I liked how much you could customize with it. It really allows for a lot more customization that other keyboards. The anti-ghosting is a great feature. Especially when you are gaming and typing quickly, it can prevent keystrokes you don't want. This keyboard was very easy to set up. It was very intuitive. It was not as loud as a lot of the other mechanical keyboards, which I appreciated. This would be especially important if you are near someone else. I am very pleased with this keyboard and would recommend it.

title: Great keyboard
text: It worked out perfectly for me to get this keyboard right when my son spilled lemonade on my old one. Both were Logitech, and I am very happy with this new one. I really feel like it is very responsive. I like the full size keyboard with the number pad - for me that is a must. It is very comfortable to press the keys. I am a writer and type very fast so I need something that is comfortable and works well. I like the customization keys that this has. It makes it very convenient. It worked well. It was simple to set up and use. I like the lighting very much. When I first got a lit keyboard I never wanted to go back. With this one you can customize it, which is nice. I am very happy with this.

title: Outstanding keyboard
text: This is an outstanding keyboard. First,t he look: I (and my kids) love the rainbow keys. You only have... 16.8 MILLION colors to choose from so I think most people will find this sufficient. I like that it is full size because some of these are not and skip the number pad. That is important to me. It has a great look. It was also not difficult to change the colors, which I like. I loved all the shortcut and customizable keys. I can control my media easily with built in shortcut keys for for things like play, pause and volume. It than has about a dozen more keys that you can customize. I thought the performance was excellent. It was extremely responsive. It was a very comfortable keyboard to use. It was pretty smooth and quiet. Everything worked perfectly and without a problem.I didn't feel any delay at all. For people who do gaming, this can be a very big deal. This is not just a keyboard for gamers, however. It's quality and features also make it perfect for home or office use. It felt extremely durable. I have four kids, and I need a keyboard that can put up with a little bit of banging.

title: Great wheel
text: We are really happy with this wheel. It works great. We have four kids and they love playing the riding games at the arcade, but with a baby we just don't get out there that often. I don't let them ride real go carts or anything dangerous, so this is a wonderful way to get that authentic feel from our living room. It gives them the same feeling of being at an arcade right from our home. It can be used both with the Play Station or on a game on the computer. I was at first concerned about the negative reviews, but after looking through them, I realize that most of them are a reflection of the company practices and not this actual wheel. The wheel is very responsive and works great. It was easy to set up. Everything worked perfectly with no problems at all. What a difference from the normal video game controllers and other wheels we have used. I like that the brake is separate. We can set it up perfectly for our kids. The force feedback is really realistic. We love it.

title: Great game for everyone
text: This is a great game. I have three young children and it can be very difficult to get the kids moving, especially as it enters the winter months. This is a great way for the kids to get some physical activity. They can really work up a storm while doing it, and they are having fun at the same time. Most people thing of video games as a very sedentary activity, but this is a way for kids to get some great physical activity. It is also great for the adults, too. It is a lot of fun, and has many great songs. The combination of sound and video make it a lot of fun. It is also great for parties. This very has also seen some improvements over the others.

title: Mimics a PS4 controller in terms of connectivity, but quality doesn't match the original. Bad ergo.
text: The OUBANG Remote for PS4 Controller Elite is a PS4 controller from the point of view of the computer or the console. The electronics present themselves as a native PS4 controller, including being able to work with DS4Windows (when connected to a PC). The controller has all of the functionality that you'd expect. All buttons, sticks, and triggers work as expected. The touch pad, LED lights, and 6-axis gyro all work as well. On top of this, the controller has programmable back buttons and turbo mode. The main problem with this controller comes when you first hold it. The ergonomics of the controller is off. When holding it, the buttons feel too far away from the thumb and the stick locations feel wrong. During use, I had some issues with the turbo turning on randomly which was very confusing. I didn't know why I couldn't jump in the game because the jump button was on turbo. So in the end, while this controller does what it says, I still am always thinking that I should have just gotten the original while using it.

title: I switch-ified my XBox One controller
text: After a couple of years of intense gaming on my XBox One controller, the rubber on my left analog stick pretty much rubbed smooth, losing grip. Eventually, the rubber actually rubbed off. Add to that, the right stick began to stick a little for some reason. I knew it was time to attempt a repair. While doing so, I thought I'd pick interesting colors for the analog sticks to make it fun. I bought the TOMSIN Replacement Joysticks for Xbox One Series X/S Controller in the Nintendo Switch blue/red combo. The installation was straightforward. Just followed a teardown video on youtube and used the included tools. The tools came in handy to pry the plastic open and unscrew the screws holding the controller together. Replacement was simple. Just pull off the old analog sticks and pop in the new ones. They fit perfectly and now, I have a controller that feels new and responsive. Great product.

title: I've been looking for an affordable headset with surround. This fit my needs.
text: [[VIDEOID:bcce61b61b8337c3b68e072c0d20d249]] I had a USB gaming headset that worked fairly well. It had large speakers that gave the sound a "roomy" feeling, especially when paired with the driver software that it came with, but the wire was driving me crazy. I couldn't step away from my desk without removing a few things or I'd end up pulling away my computer with me. So, I was in the market for a nice pair of wireless gaming headsets. I've come across many in the 30-dollar range but none of the descriptions for those touted surround sound. Eventually, I had to look in the 60 - 90 range. This pair of OCG Gaming Headsets 2.4GHz Bluetooth Wireless Gaming Headphones were just what I needed. I wanted bluetooth capabilities because I wanted to have it as an option in case I wanted to pair it to two computers (one via dongle and one via bluetooth). I also wanted the option of using it with other gaming systems such as an XBox or Playstation. The usb dongle gives that versatility. I really don't care much for RGB as they just make my computers distracting and I'm not a game streamer or youtuber (not yet, anyway, ha ha), but if you do like them, this headset has them... So, what do I think? I'd been playing Uncharted 4 on my PC with my old pair of headphones and it sounded great. The surround didn't really seem like it worked very well. After I received the OCG, I plugged in the USB dongle and booted up the game. The game automatically detected the headset and showed that it was using virtual surround. Immediately, I found that I was hearing sounds that I hadn't heard before! As the character walked around, I heard the jangling sounds of the equipment he had at his belt, I heard the companion character talking behind me and as I turned, her voice moved around my head. I was super impressed! I then disconnected the dongle and tried the headset in bluetooth mode. The sound was a little muffled and there was almost no surround effect, even though the game still said that it was doing virtual surround. So I'm definitely using the dongle for all my gaming. I love this thing!

title: Smaller than I expected, but still useable.
text: There are many third-party switch controllers on the market and each make claims about compatibility or useability. It takes a little bit of digging to actually know which one is worth getting. The listing doesn't say it but this controller's brand is Sound Fox. It is a fairly compact controller that is noticeably smaller than the Switch Pro controller. It is actually well-built and has a great texture. The entire controller feels soft and satin with nice analog sticks that don't feel loose. The buttons feel good and the digital pad is fairly standard. Outside of these basic features, the controller has two programmable buttons in the back and turbo mode for all of the face and shoulder buttons. The programmable buttons actually can remember fairly long sequences of button presses and digital pad inputs. I used it to go through some particularly annoying menus in Xenoblade 3 that I needed to do over and over again (collectopedia). I programmed a series of presses, holds and wait times that allowed me to go through the menu 5 times with each press of the programmable button. What's more, the vibration strength is programmable, the face plate is easily removeable (although I haven't seen replacement faceplates available) and even Amiibo support is built in. It really is a good value for the price. Aside from the smaller size, this is a great replacement for the Pro controller. On the PC, this is a great bluetooth controller that can operate in Xinput mode for maximum game compatibility. This feature is something you don't find in many other third party controllers out there. The only problem I have with this controller is the fact that the ZL and ZR triggers are digital only. When using this controller on the PC, you really need to have analog triggers to get the most out of many games. In the end, this product is geared toward the Switch and has the added option to be used on the PC and mobile phones but without analog triggers, it really is only good on the Switch.

title: No need for a fancy dock.
text: The fancy docks that you see for the Quest 2 usually has a place for charging the goggles, and two spots for the controllers. The only problem is that the docks are made for the controllers without the silicone sleeves that people usually put on their controllers. In fact, there aren't many solutions out there that allow charging while using the silicone sleeves. With this All-in-One Magnetic Charging Kit for Oculus Quest 2, I'm able to resolve all of my problems. This system is well thought out. It comes with two rechargeable batteries and special battery covers that expose a magnetic charging port on the side of the controller. It also comes with a magnetic type-c connector for your goggles. By cutting a small hole in the silicone sleeve, I'm able to charge the controllers without removing the sleeve and the cables are easy to connect because of the magnetic connectors. The goggle is just as easy to charge with its corresponding magnetic connector. There are two problems with this system that you need to be aware of, though. The first is that the type-c connector is not very strong. It means that when pulling off the charging cable, the type-c plug with come with it. The second problem is that the three devices will be sharing a single cable and thus, sharing the available amps. The charging speed will suffer as a result. Overall, not having to go through the hassle of removing the silicone sleeve to change batteries makes this kit worth the purchase. I don't have long play sessions with the VR system so I'm not so worried about charging speed.

title: A good idea
text: The basic idea is that most people need a grip when using the switch controllers anyway. Add some batteries in that grip and you can extend your play time. It's quite obvious when you think about it. In practice, these grips feel good. They add more surface area to the controller than the ones that come from Nintendo, making it more comfortable to hold for people with larger hands. They click in well adn fit the controllers perfectly. When connected to the controller, the switch will show that the controllers are being charged, verifying that the batteries are indeed doing their job. The only problem I have found is that these grips will lose charge over the course of a few days if connected to the controllers. This is because the controllers will trickle charge even when they are off. This is quite a waste and it is better to remove the controllers when not in use.

title: I just can't find the right position
text: The good of this Aixoto Head Strap for Oculus Quest 2 is that it is the only one I tried that, after a few minutes of nudging, I can get a perfect view into the Oculus' optics. It means very little blurring at the corners and only a little bit of the fringing due to the fresnel lenses. My problem with this head strap is that it seems to be missing one more hinge that would make it perfect. From the picture, You can see a brace for the forehead and the brace for the back of the skull. In addition, an arm curves downward to hold the goggles themselves. The velcro headstrap at the top holds keeps the goggle from going down too much. So the degrees of freedom are the velcro strap to adjust how high the goggle sits on your head, the goggle's angle can be adjusted where it connects to the arm, the goggle can slide back and forth to fit tightly against your face, the angle of the forehead brace and the back brace can be adjusted (quite useless, I find), and of course, the tightness of the brace itself. What's missing is the ability to adjust the angle between the curved arm that holds the goggles and the forehead strap. What I find is that if I get the goggles to the correct height and tightness to my face, the forehead strap is too loose and any movement will knock the whole thing out of position. Yet, if I adjust for a good forehead strap tightness, the goggles sit too low and it's all blurry.. If I was able to adjust the tightness of the forehead strap, then move the arm up a little bit to adjust the goggles, then I'd have the perfect fit. So this product is so close to good, but just misses the mark and because of that, is hard to adjust and use for a long period of time.

title: Great nose piece but headband needs work.
text: This X-super Home product for the Oculus Quest 2 comes with a headstrap and silicone face cover. Both of these things are accessories that every Quest 2 must get and there are many options available to fit the bill. Out of the box, the Quest 2 comes with elastic straps that just aren't enough to hold the VR Goggles in place very well. When turning your head, the goggle tends to swing around and feel like they will fall off. Also, if you're one of the early adopters that purchased the Quest 2 before Facebook issued their recall where they will send you a silicone cover for the goggles, you're stuck with a cloth face cover that lets too much light through and gets pretty disgusting after just a short time using the goggle due to sweat. So the X-Super Home head strap features a battery holder at the back of the head, the theory being that the extra weight of the battery will help to counter balance the weight of the goggles, reducing neck strain while extending the play time of the goggles. In practice, the battery makes the entire setup too heavy and reintroduces the problem of the goggles swinging around when turning your head. In addition, there was a design error on the attachment bracket where the slot is shorter than the tab so the battery holder never fully slides into place. Due to the placement of the battery, the tightening knob is offset to the right of the battery. This offset design creates a problem with the tightening system where one side would tighten more than the other, giving an unbalanced feel to the strap. The silicone cover, on the other hand, is quite excellent. It has a texture on it that helps to keep a good grip around the eyes even when you sweat and the flaps over the bridge of the nose is larger than many others out there. While not perfect, it greatly reducing the amount of light that leaks in. Compare this to the silicone cover that Facebook sent as part of their recall, the Facebook cover is smooth and doesn't have a flap at all to cover the bridge of the nose. The X-super Home cover is much better. So a less-than-ideal head strap and a great silicone cover. Unfortunately, this doesn't justify the price of this product.

title: It seems like this is all you would need for your Oculus Quest 2, but...
text: I went through a bit of flip-flopping with the Eyglo 5 in 1 Accessories Case for Oculus Quest 2. When I saw the listing for this product, I thought that it was a great set that included everything I needed for the Quest 2, although from the pictures, I did note that the hand strap seemed flimsy. When I received it, I found that the head strap was made of stiffer plastic than the original straps so it was very difficult to install. I was still worried about the click-in button at the top of the hand strap and the fact that it was so narrow. I expected that any swinging of the controller could slip the strap off. The silicone eye piece fit well, but at first, it gave me a fright because when pressed against the head, the cover would flare out and obstruct the sensor that Oculus proximity sensor, making it think that the headset turn off because it didn't detect a face. I thought my Oculus was broken! Lastly, I found that the controllers were hard to fit into the case (They needed to be looped through each other just so) and even then, the case didn't close without the back piece of the headset pushing against the top, creating a slight bulge. I found that this was a case of "looks good on paper" but not great in actuality. Because of all of these problems, I was going to give this product 3 stars, but after spending some time with it, I found that I didn't mind any of those shortcomings. The head strap is much more comfortable and secure than the original oculus. The eye piece is MUCH better than the original cloth as sweat is easily wiped off (Facebook is currently addressing this issue and the Oculus will now come with silicone eye pieces). The hand straps turned out to work well enough. I don't worry about losing the controllers because I find that I don't have a tendency to flick the controller with my hand completely open. Lastly, I find that I don't need to use the case when I'm at home so I will only face the awkwardness of putting in the goggles when I intend on taking it on travel. In the end, I got a complete set of accessories all in one package and they do work. I'm much happier having this set than not. The out-of-the box experience with the Oculus leaves much to be desired and accessories are just a fact of life. Just as purchasing a case for a phone or tablet is just part of the cost of the device.

title: My complaints may be down to personal preference...
text: [[VIDEOID:a4d91a6fb11c550cd582ff40a0fe7596]] The Logitech G733 K/DA Lightspeed Wireless Gaming Headset is a League of Legends themed headset with a great design and colorful, but unintrusive LEDs. The headphones cover the ear and not on them. It also sports a suspension style headband. I'm not a streamer but this headset would not be out of place on a twitch streamer's head, in my opinion. The most important feature for me when it comes to the G733 is the wireless feature and the sound quality. The sound is clear and crisp with a good range, but not a booming bass (which I don't mind. I would have turned that down anyway). When I put on the headset and launched Biomutant, I noticed that the sound was very close, almost like in a sound booth. Compared to my wired headset, the SADES Spirit Wolf, the sound profile of the Logitech G733 is much smaller as opposed to the large hall feel of the SADES. Personally, I prefer the large, open feel of the SADES to the smaller close-up feel of the Logitech. It makes games feel bigger and more intense. Initially, I wanted to give this product 3 stars but I realized that perhaps my complaint is a personal preference and Logitech couldn't be blamed for it. This is a good product that works well, but personally, I wouldn't feel that it justifies its price when compared to the sound quality of a sub-30-dollar usb headset.

title: A must-have accessory for the switch; This is not an exaggeration.
text: Firstly, it must be stated that in the early days of Nintendo Switch's launch, Nintendo Switch's adoption of the Type-C PD standard was unknown and news began to emerge that various Type-C chargers were causing electronics to overload. This wasn't limited to just the Switch, but cell phones and laptops were suffering the same issue. At this point, news of those issues have generally subsided. Power adaptor designers have taken safety more seriously and personally, I have been able to use multiple docks and hubs with the Switch with no issues. In short, this KIWIHOME Switch Dock did not blow up my switch. This KIWIHOME USB C Charger is a very compact dock for the Switch. When travelling, it is usually necessary to pack the official Nintendo Switch charger for power. This third-party charger is no bigger than the OEM charger but has the additional advantage of a detachable charging cable, which means it is even easier to pack. Of course, the best feature of this charger is the ability to act as a dock. In a normal case, one must add the large Switch dock in addition to an HDMI cable in order to play in docked mode while on travel. This charger allows one to leave the large dock at home. It is an elegant solution. While on the topic of travel, this charger is rated for 110-220v. This means that with the addition of a plug adapter, this charger will work in Europe as well as the US and around the world. An issue that one may face due to the design of this product is that the television may not be close enough to an open power socket. This would need to be solved either with a long HDMI cable or an extension cord.

title: joy-cons fit a little too tightly and charging status indication could be better
text: I purchased this product because I wanted a grip for my second set of joycons and while I was at it, I wanted an easy way to charge those controllers. Whie this grip looks like it will do everything I need (it will charge the joycons while connected to the power adapter or on battery power and it provides a satin grip that keep the controllers secure), execution could have been better. Here are some of my complaints: -- The grip has a satin surface which is somewhat outdated, I think. Most manufacturers mold textures into the plastic to give them grip. My past experience with satin surfaces is that after a few years, they become a sticky mess. -- Perhaps it is the product that I got but I charged the grip overnight without the joycons inserted and the red charging light was still on when I checked on it in the morning so there is no indication that the charging has completed. This might mean that there is no cut-off for when the battery is fully charged. -- The joy-cons fit too snugly. It is actually a little difficult to slide the controllers in and out of the grip. This could be because of the satin finish that is sprayed on to the underlying plastic. Other features: -- Charges the joycons with the built-in battery pack. A blue light indicates that the controllers are charging. -- Not much heavier than the original switch grip. -- Wider than the original grip. For me, this is actually more comfortable. Again, this will meet my requirements but I wonder how long the internal battery pack will last if there is no charging cut-off.

title: Works with Nintendo Switch!
text: I didn't know what to expect from this product as I have never owned a pair of gaming headsets, but I wasn't willing to spend hundreds of dollars on a pair of headsets that may or may not enhance my experience. So let me break down the description given: -- 7.1 surround - I've always see this more as a gimmick than an actual feature, even in headphones that cost hundreds of dollars but don't have discreet speakers. The computer sees these headsets as stereo and not 7.1 so whatever program you run, whether it's a trailer with Dolby Atmos or a game, the output will still be stereo. While their program supposedly tries to simulate virtual surround, you would still need the source to be 7.1 discreet channels so that their driver can process the signal to simulate surround sound. These headsets do not have DTS-HD or Dolby ATMOS certification so they aren't actually able to process raw 7.1 channel data. It means that in the end, the video player is still just playing stereo sound. The end effect of turning on virtual 7.1 surround sound is that the soundtrack is more "atmospheric" or "wider" sounding, but you wouldn't be able to tell that a sound is coming from your rear left flank. Since I never expected much out of this feature, I didn't mind that it wasn't true 7.1 -- USB - True plug and play on Windows 10. I plugged these headphones in and immediately, Windows output sound through them. No muss no fuss. It just worked. You can install their driver, which turns on the "virtual 7.1" feature but that's pretty much like installing drivers for any realtek sound card. You just have access to a few extra DSP effects. Honestly, I don't like extra processing to my audio signals. Being USB, it is a completely digital signal to your headphones all the way up until the speakers themselves. On 3.5mm headphones, the audio signal is analog at 3.5mm port, at which point, you will get some signal degradation just from the connection itself. -- Gaming Headset with Microphone - I don't really play games online so I can't tell you whether the microphone is better or worse than any other headset but I can tell you that I used the Spirit Wolf with a few games and I was hearing sounds that I didn't hear in my Sennheisers. -- PC Gamers - BONUS! This headset isn't just for PC gaming, it works with the Nintendo switch, too, using the USB port on the dock. Even the volume buttons on the headset works! My overall experience with Spirit Wolf has been positive. The sound is crisp and clear and the high frequencies are very good but the bass could have been better. I'm not big on turning up the bass so it's not a big loss. I still feel that the overall sound quality is very good. The headset is circumaural which means it surrounds your ears and the speakers are not pressed right against your head. It means that noise isolation isn't as good as earbuds or even supra-aural headphones (which press up against your ear), but there's a reason professional gaming headphones are this style. You can wear them for longer periods without discomfort and you are able to achieve a wider sound. Overall, I recommend this headset for its price and overall sound quality. The ability to use it with my Switch is just bonus. EDIT: I must amend my previous conclusions regarding the virtual surround sound. I recently started playing Shadow of the Tomb Raider and as a test, I went into the audio settings for the game. The options were stereo, 5.1, 7.1, and spatial sound. Reading the description for spatial sound, it states that it is meant to be used with Windows Spatial Sound (right click on the speaker icon in your system tray and you'll see an option to turn it on). Well, I tried the spatial sound in three different ways: with only the in-game spatial sound setting on, the in-game setting + Windows Spatial Sound on, and in-game setting + XEar driver 7.1 on. All three give slightly different positional sound effects but I found that the XEar effect was the best. The sounds simulate a wide environment and I was able to distinguish the direction of each distinct sound source. Very impressive.

title: Adds grip but not a solution for big hands
text: If you have a ps5 and big hands, you have quickly realized that the ps5 controller is not comfortable because it’s made for small hands - kind of ironic since very few ps5 games are made for young kids. This does add a few mm of rubber, but will NOat make a big difference in size or thickness of the controller. Also, the rubber on the back near the USB port blocks my wireless charging dock. Still waiting for someone to make a rubber/plastic case for the ps5 controller that adds a LOT of thickness and bulk to make it comfortable for big hands.

title: Excellent gaming keyboard and a great value
text: The switches (Cherry speed silver) are great for gaming with the higher actuation point (quicker key presses) and light actuation force. The keys are relatively quiet, but can be loud if pressed hard, like most keys. Construction seems VERY solid. I love the minimalistic design (it's not compact or scaled down - just less extra area around the outer edges) - it allows more desk space and the option to use your own wrist rests rather than a crappy plastic one many manufacturers add. It has a lot of nice tweaks specifically for gaming, such as wider left shift and control keys and alternate color WASD key caps. The RGB lighting is very customizable, with lots of good presets, but this leads me to the "room for improvement" part of the review, and the only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5... The keyboard supposedly has onboard memory, but will not save custom RGB lighting schemes to the keyboard onboard memory. Arggh! This means that if you use the keyboard on multiple PCs/ other devices, the color profile you spent 30+ minutes designing won't work. Every device HAS to have the ASUS lighting software installed to use your custom RGB layouts, so that can be a problem. If ASUS fixes this, I will change this to 5 stars. One other nice tweak would be to add a silicone layer/barrier between the key caps edges and the keyboard to reduce noise from overly-enthusiastic key presses. Overall, it's an excellent keyboard for gaming and also works well for typing. I would definitely recommend it - particularly the linear switch versions (cherry red or cherry speed silver) for gaming. This keyboard is also probably one of the best value boards for gaming if you want high quality construction, quality mechanical switches, RGB lighting with various effects and the ability to customize.

title: No More Sliding Mouse!
text: I designed a computer workstation where the keyboard and mouse sit atop a desk surface that swivels over the arm of a recliner. As with any custom built item, such as this, I’ve run into unforeseen issues. One of them was, due to my preferred angle for my mouse platform the mouse would constantly move when I didn’t want it too. Now I understand this may seem like a minor inconvenience but when doing detailed graphic editing it can end up being really frustrating. I had tried solving the issue in a variety of ways but none were successful. This device ended up being exactly what I needed. The nonslip base rests at the top of my mouse platform and holds my mouses wire so there is no pull causing the cursor to move even when my hand is not resting on the mouse. My entire system is lit with RGB lighting so this cable holder fits right in and looks great. I have it plugged in to a multi port charging plug so it doesn’t occupy a port on my pc just for the power supply. Colors are easily controlled via the button on the front. The spring loaded holder that supports the wire securely holds the mouse wire without it slipping and keeps it out of the way. This is a great product that works exactly as intended.

title: More Accurately Described as a Workstation Pad - Flickers in Scrolling Mode
text: [[VIDEOID:23b66e0d4d6deb4493df890cc9f52620]] I recently built a custom computer workstation that suspends next to my recliner with the desk surface swiveling over the arm for me to work. I thought this would be a nice addition although it was simply too big. While based on the dimensions it should have worked, due to my swiveling desktop being made up of 2 surfaces, one for the keyboard and the other for the mouse, there was no way to have this lay flat across both. This is certainly not a failing of the product, only my experience. I have ended up using this beneath my PC and server on the table next to my recliner and it looks great while providing a soft surface for my computer equipment to rest. While this does not come with a micro USB cable I always have additional so this wasn’t an issue but should be known. I have mine plugged into a multi USB outlet that automatically adjusts to the power required for whatever is plugged into it, it’s provided constant power without issue. I feel that the color descriptions are accurate. I have tested this product over the last 2 months and what I have found is when set to any of the scrolling color modes it continually flickers every few seconds which is very distracting (see video). While it didn’t do this in the beginning it now happens nearly continually. This is not an issue in the breathing color changing modes but, for me, makes the scrolling modes unusable. I have tested changing cables and outlets but neither makes a difference therefore this is a defect with the product. While the lights are bright and vibrant, the patterns varied, the defect I have encountered makes this a product I would not recommend.

title: Awesome Wireless Mouse
text: I have used wireless mice for many years and have used those made by all of the major manufacturers. Without question wireless technology has come so far over the last decade. This mouse makes use of the latest Bluetooth 5.0 technology making connections dependable and consistent. While having a steady connection is critical for a reliable mouse that is only one of the factors that makes this mouse excellent. There is no adding batteries to this wireless mouse. While most similar products mean replacing batteries and locating a new one when the old dies- this one has a powerful battery built within it. All that is required is plugging the mouse into a USB port - and it can be used while the battery is charging! The mouse sleeps when not in use preserving the battery and reawakens immediately, in addition there is a power switch for when work is completed. The battery lasts far longer than I anticipated - I plug mine in to charge once a week to 10 days and I’ve never had mine die. There are 3 DPI settings which control how sensitive the mouse is or how many dots per inch it detects. This mouse is every bit as accurate as my wired mice but doesn’t have the restrictions that come from being tethered. This mouse has built in LED lights that “breathe” - slowly illuminating and dimming. It looks great whether you game or not. In terms of how it fits in the hand - I love the ergonomics of this mouse. I have found this mouse fits perfectly within my palm without over extension of my wrist. It’s comfortable to use all day without having hand or wrist fatigue late in the day. This is an excellent, highly responsive, well made mouse. It utilizes the latest technology for outstanding performance and durability. This is an excellent product that I definitely recommend.

title: AMAZING KEYBOARD to WORK ON
text: While I don’t use this keyboard for gaming I can say it is the best keyboard I’ve used for working. The design elements make it not only highly functional but very comfortable for many hours of use at a time. By designing the keyboard with a curve and having the keys at slightly different levels I’ve found that my hands become less strained when typing all day. The clicks of the keyboard give both a tactile and auditory response when the keys are depressed allowing the user to know the key has been depressed. At first I found the noise overwhelming but I soon got used to it and found I appreciated the feedback. The response rate of this keyboard is simply incredible. title: Decent HARD case for travel - charging a bit of a trick when in case.
text: Many Nintendo Switch cases have hit the market since the release of the versatile gaming system and this this one meets all of the critical criteria of a good case but falls a bit short in order to be considered great. The Switch fits perfectly in the top with adequate padding to protect the critical top glass LED screen. The 2 Joy-Con controllers fit snugly into individual slots beneath the main unit and there is another secure area to store the power adapter (and a few games) which is a huge plus for this case - which many other cases neglect. As I stated, for travel purposes, this case is excellent. While this case advertises itself as one where you can “charge and play” - that is awkward at best. First the Joy-Cons do not comfortably fit on the primary unit while in the case. If too much pressure is applied to the screen while propped on the stand it moves too much for accurate game play. I have to give this case 3 STARS - it will definitely protect your Nintendo Switch and all of its necessary accessories when traveling better than many other cases but it won’t be staying in the case as you play... UPDATE TO ORIGINAL REVIEW: Now that my son has had more time using this case he has told me that he liked it much more than he initially did. Since I do not actually use the Switch I had to write my review based on his impressions and as he has used it he has liked it more and more. Often when the Nintendo Switch is played in handheld mode the joycons are held separately from the central screen unit so the fact that they don’t fit on it in the case does not matter. In his opinion this is the best case he has used for his Nintendo Switch and we would definitely recommend it as a great way to protect your investment.

title: Like a glove

title: Better than my other devices!
text: Update, I’ve been using it on my PS4 and enjoy it very much. I love wireless VR but the benefit of this is you will never run out of battery charge as it don’t use batteries. Tidbit all VR are designed to have the sharpest part of the image towards the center as that’s how human vision works we see in a 120 degrees arc. Anyway with this I enjoy best of both worlds wired, and wireless with my other devices. I also plan to get Oculus Quest, but this psvr can handle full featured games and not just VR experiences. title: Large, quality cloth gaming mat
text: This gaming mat really enhances the look of my 'KDA setup'. I tried it under my main setup for my computer and under my work laptop. My mouse glides very smooth over the surface, I was getting incredibly accurate mouse movements playing any MOBA while using this mat. The only negative that I have is that Ahri (my fav KDA character) is in the center of the mat, that is where you would normally have your keyboard/laptop so she is covered when gaming.
