title: Overhyped IMO
text: Unfortunately, mine had issues with wireless connectivity causing juming and out right disconnecting. Overall, the design of the mouse itself is great. Lots of buttons for keybinding, lighting options, and customizable profiles. Being female, this large mouse still fits my hand, but not as comfortably as others. Works as a corded mouse, but when you pay $100+ on a WIRELESS mouse you would expect it to work as such. The only other negitive is the Razer Synapse driver, which manages everything for Razer devices, must constantly be up-to-date or it can cause issues with the mouse functions. While Razer has a warranty, I opted to find a different mouse to fit my preference. The Naga Epic just wasn't worth the frustration to me. I will say that I love Razer keyboards and have nerver had issues with mine.

title: comfortable to use and durable
text: I really love this keyboard. I was actually surprised when I got the box how heavy and sturdy this product is. I do a lot of typing, and this is perfect for my needs. The keys are deep and have a nice, resounding click that lets you know whether or not you hit the key. The sound isn't intolerable, especially if there are other things going on in your environment. Now that I have been using it for a while, I find the keystroke sound quite pleasant. The battery life seems pretty good, even with the backlight being on the majority of the time. It does have a sleep mode and it is easy to tell when the battery needs charging by looking at the space bar. This is a very well-built item. It is designed to withstand the rigors of someone who types a lot without breaking down. I like the feel of the keys under my fingers and find that after using it more and more, that I wouldn't want to go back to a different model. Overall, I'm really impressed with this product. I do, however, wish the manual that came with it was a bit more explanatory on the different functions, as I wasn't sure what all the terms meant and what difference the modes make in your typing experience. Otherwise, this is a great product for a price that does not seem unreasonable. I would recommend it to other people who type a lot and are looking for a reliable and comfortable experience.

title: I say oops a lot
text: So this game is really fun in either single player or multiplayer and I like that you can couch co-op with a friend without having to go online. There aren't enough of those games anymore, IMO. The characters in this are fun to use and their special abilities grow as you continue on with the game. Some portions of it can be challenging and it is truly one of those games where you have to work together if you are going to play in co-op mode. I like that you never really know what to expect because each new place you come into is different and you have to get a feel for how to get through it before you really make progress. There are a lot of hurdles you have to get past and they make it more fun. I enjoyed solving the puzzles and fighting the various enemies.

title: fun and challenging
text: I love all of the different farming games, but what i love about this one the most is the amount of animals you can eventually have if you keep working at it. Want 500 pigs? No problem. Want to focus on gardening instead? No worries. There is freedom to do what you want in this game, including being a goblin fighting miner. There isn't anything gross or any graphic violence in this game, so it is good for kids and parents alike. There are some difficult to solve puzzles and sometimes finding the lost items in the game can be maddening, but really, overall, there is so much to do if you get stuck doing one thing, then you can easily move on to another. This truly is a great game, although the graphics are a bit wonky, even though one expects that with these crafting games, it can make it hard on the eyes after a while.

title: still not as good as the original
text: I like this game well enough, but not as much as the first one. Most of the game is pretty good, but there's a lot that's different in the free roam mode. I like the photo abilities and the choice of vehicles, but honestly, I could have done without the planes and the boats. I like driving games and that was one of the thrills of the first game, especially with the wild run expansion pack. This game is a bit different and some of the races are too short, some of them are just silly IMO. The graphics are good for the most part and there is a lot to do, but sometimes the other players can be a real pain in the rear end and you can't always get away from them like you can in other games. Overall, it's okay, but not what I was hoping for based on how great the first one was.

title: I'm on the fence about this one
text: It works...kinda. I think? So, it is easy enough to set up and is easy enough to figure out, but at the same time, it doesn't work as easily as expected. Getting the controllers in the right spot requires an engineer with at least a four year degree and then you never really know if the controller batteries are charged or not. he light is red, then green, then red again, even when you were certain you had it in the right spot. If you put the slightest amount of pressure on it, then it changes colour. If you leave the battery packs in the controllers as they claim you can when you go to use the charger, it takes hours longer for them to charge, or in any event, for it to recognise that they are charged. Eventually it will charge them, and the battery packs fit nicely in the controllers, but it is rather a pain to use when you never really now if it is charged or not. At this point, I'm not sure what to think.

title: I finally understand what all the hype was about
text: I've been a dedicated PlayStation user for many years, but I decided I wanted to see what X box was all about so I gave in and got one. I see now why people love it. I love just about everything about this game system--except that the remote require actual batteries and does not come as a standard rechargeable. That actually seems not only silly to me, but perhaps even prehistoric. Otherwise, the games are great, and having the Game Pass and Live Gold is great too. I wanted to try those services out and now I can see that I really do want them. The X Box itself has some really great functionality, is easy to set up even for a technology numpty like me and I like the design and build of it. There are a great range of games available for the whole family, so as a parent, I like that as well. I'm no longer sure that Playstation is it for me. We will see what happens in the future of gaming, but I have to say, I'm impressed with the X Box.

title: You had better have a decent internet connection
text: I was really disappointed after waiting so long for the release of this game to find out that it is really only the first game that is on the disc and only an intro for the other two. There is a 38 gig patch that has to be downloaded before you can play the full game and if you have a slow internet connection or serious restrictions on the amount of gigs you can use, you will be in trouble with this. Needless to say, I wasn't pleased that Activision decided to release this disk as is when they could have put so much more of the game on the disk. I resented having to do such a big download even though I was capable of doing it. I feel sorry for the people who aren't able to download it. The graphics in the game look really good and there are a few changes, but nothing substantial enough to change the original feel and look of the game. I do think that they managed to break the glide feature somehow, because I don't recall it being such a pain in the butt to use before. Overall, it is still a great series of games, but the download is ridiculous.

title: There's some good and some bad
text: First, the good. I was so excited when I found out they were coming out with a second overcooked. I loved the first one and have had hours upon hours of fun playing this game with my family and friends. This second incarnation still has adorable characters and much of the original functionality that the first had. There are some new critters to use ( I personally like the octopus,) and you now have the ability to throw certain things into pots or to other characters, which is a nice improvement. Some of the worlds are challenging and there are new hurdles to overcome, like flames popping up here and there that have to be put out. So there are some good things about it, however, there are also a lot of things that I found lacking. The levels are way too easy to earn points in. With the first game, you might be lucky if you served a handful of successful dishes and earned a couple of hundred points before the timer ran out. With the second game, you can easily earn more than a thousand points with hardly any effort. I was able to play through this game with my husband in a single afternoon and beat the final level without a problem, literally in less than six hours. That was not the way it was with the first game at all. Whereas in the original overcooked, the last level, when you face the giant meatball you have to really put your heads together and strategise and probably do it over and over again until you are successful, the final level in this game is easy. There isn't much holding you back from doing the level on the very first try. Some of the levels in this game are simply annoying rather than challenging in any meaningful kind of way. The things that made the first game challenging and fun were the rocking boats, the slippery ice and stuff like that. In this game it feels like they tried too hard to go out of their way to come up with hurdles for you and most of them are just ridiculous. You can easily get around most of them after you figure it out the first time and they don't change much throughout the rest of the game. The way the menu works annoyed me, because it isn't straight forward to change characters as you wish anymore like it was in the first game, and adding or subtracting players isn't easy anymore either. The emote icons are a pointless addition that does nothing to enhance the gameplay experience and don't work as well as they should. Overall, I thought this game was a massive disappointment. perhaps for those who haven't played the first one and don't have raised expectations based on that bar being set so high this would be a lot of fun, but for me, it was just barely okay. I hope if they come out with a third one they take into account what made the first one fun.

title: Love the multiplayer modes
text: What's not to love about a need for speed where you have the opportunity to be the cop instead of just getting chased by them? This game is really fun. The graphics are kind of blocky---yes, I realise it is old...but otherwise this is really great. I think this Need for Speed has the best multiplayer mode of any of the games, allowing you to do more than just simply race one another. I like the different modes in this game in single player as well. This is fun and perfectly appropriate for younger kids, as there is nothing in it that is inappropriate for their age group. Overall, this is one of my favourite racing games and was a good addition to our library of Need for Speed games.

title: fun for the parents, too!
text: This game is a lot of fun and will keep you on your toes. I like the graphics and the story is interesting as well. The controls aren't that hard and the surprises just keep coming with every new thing you have to do. My twelve and thirteen year old boys are having fun trying to beat this game and it has proved to be fun for the parents as well. I also like it because it seems like it will take a while to get past all of it, so it should be hours of fun for the price. A good buy.

title: meh. Funny but not complicated.
text: I expected the graphics in this game to be a bit cheesy and they are, so that was no real surprise. The game itself isn't bad. What the characters say is funny, the different modes allow you to have fun in different ways and two player mode is crazy, where you can steal passengers fro the other players. Still, I don't love the main one player mode because it feels too individual and not like you are really accomplishing anything since you have to choose a new character and car again after the end of every one. It won't keep you busy for weeks at a tie, but it is okay to goof off with when you don't want to get involved with something that takes more time and effort. Cute, but not much more than that.

title: it wasn't bad
text: As far as games go, this is a decent racing game. There is a good selection of cars to choose from and some interesting tracks. I didn't love all the interruptions that the story causes in the beginning that keep you from getting to the actual racing and the way the world map works in this game is kind of annoying at times. You spend a lot of time driving from one location to another and back to the garage. The graphics aren't bad and the races are interesting and varied with drag, drift, circuit and other things to do. Not the best of the need for speed games IMO, but still fun.

title: easy controls and fun chases
text: This game is a lot of fun and is one of the better need for speed titles for ps2, in my opinion. I liked the different tracks and the cop chases in this game are a lot of fun. There are plenty of shortcuts to be taken on these tracks and the cops are determined to get you, so it is a challenge to get away from them, which makes it so much more interesting. The story isn't bad and the other characters don't interrupt you every five minutes, so you actually get to play more than just sit and wait. I liked it.

title: not quite part of the 'family'
text: I'm not convinced this game is really for people who love the Godfather. Yes, they may have used the Corleone name and there may be some characters from the books and films represented in this game, but you aren't playing as Michael or anyone else important, just a random street grunt looking to move up and become a member of 'the Family." La Cosa Nostra? I think not. While the game can be fun at times, there is also a lot of pointless running around on foot and stealing cars that look like something out of a bumper car lot at a local carnival. Some of the graphics are questionable and the controls can be oddly complicated for such a cheesy game. If you want to become a hitman, there are better games than this one. If you want to laugh your butt off at the silliness of one dimensional characters swearing at one another and spraying artificial, on screen blood across the pavement, this is your game. La stessa costa? Nope. Not in this case.

title: so much fun
text: Out of all of the need for speed games, I think I like this one the best. The graphics are really good in it, the tracks are varied and I felt like the story made more sense and was a nice. solid reason to want to put some effort into winning races and taking over territories. There is a wide selection of cars to choose from after you start unlocking them and even the two player mode on this game is a lot of fun. I liked the characters and the way you can jump from one event to another by using the world map. The canyon races are challenging but still fun and the other modes keep it interesting. Definitely recommend this to others who enjoy racing games. Love those right angle turns and shortcuts!

title: Good slashing fun!
text: This game is a lot of fun and has a good cast of characters to choose from, even in first player mode. I like the story behind the game and the final battle is difficult even when you are playing with the game set on easy. I liked the way the weapons level up and the selection screens are a breeze to get through. being able to swap out characters with the touch of a button during gameplay was fun, but may have spoiled me a bit for when I return to other games where you can't do that. The graphics aren't bad in this game and there are lots of areas to explore with your characters and not all of them look the same. This is pretty fun and worth the money for anyone who loves hack and slash games.

title: Good for younger kids
text: I bought this looking for an inexpensive game system for younger players that doesn't require DVD type disks and am happy so far with what this does. With the games already programmed in, it makes it easy for the parent. There is a decent selection of less complex games for younger kids and it comes with two controllers so two player games are no problem. The unit is lightweight but built to last and was just what I was looking for. I'm happy with it. There is a pretty versatile selection of games with this system, even including some Sonic games. Not a bad deal for paying less new for this one than some systems cost used after many years.

title: I'll get you yet feather brain!
text: So, this game is really cute. There were a lot of things to like about it. As far as shooting games go, this one isn't particularly violent, more cutesy. The characters are silly and funny and the game has a lot of funny sound effects and animations. The chickens made my kids laugh and they had a good time with it for a little while. The main reason for the three star rating, was that the first level was difficult to get past and so they kept doing it again and again until they tired of it. Since they couldn't get past that level, they soon grew frustrated. It wasn't bad, but I think for my seven and eight year old children it was a little too difficult.

title: Fun!
text: So, there is a slight learning curve when teaching a child to use the fishing reel, and you pretty much have to spend a few minutes practicing before you can make a successful cast, but after you get it down this game is a lot of fun. There are multiple levels and many different species of fish to find. They vary in weight and there are special fish in each lake. One of the things I like about this game is how much free range you have to drive the boat around. On a big screen this looks crazy cool! The kids enjoyed using the fishing pole after they got the hang of it and didn't have any further trouble with it. They liked doing the challenges and felt like kings of the fishing arena when they pulled in a big one. I'd recommend this game to anyone who likes a pretty realistic fishing experience.

title: Really? the PS1 game was better!
text: I absolutely love the Spyro games. That being said, one of my favorite things about the original Playstation Spyro games was the ability to have a little free roaming ability. I loved chasing the sheep and getting the little dragon into trouble. This game doesn't give you that option. You can't go too far out of bounds or it just resets you to where you are "supposed" to be. I was finishing this game at a ridiculous rate without even having to try. The controls are not complicated and fun like the old games. In my opinion, this one isn't worth the money or the time.

title: Endless joy for the ocean lover
text: This game is amazing. I have no experience with the first Endless Ocean game so I can't compare, but I absolutely love this one. This game is such an adventure that you tend to forget about everything else around you. I love that you get to interact and "heal" the marine creatures. Filling the aquarium tanks is also really fun. The thing that made me fall completely in love with this game though, is that after you think you are finished...you really aren't. There is still more to complete. I would recommend this game for anyone old enough to understand the basic commands of a Wii remote. This is so much fun, but I warn you, it can become quite addictive.

title: Come a long way
text: This game is really well designed and fun to play. I am simply amazed by the graphics. Boy these games have come a long way since the original Zelda games came out. I found a couple of the movements for the controller had a little bit of a learning curve, but it didn't take me too long to learn. This game is almost like watching a movie. The characters are really well developed and look much more realistic than in previous games. I love the world that was created in this game. The water and trees and other surroundings make you feel like you are really there. I would recommend this game to older kids and teens/adults. I haven't finished the game yet, but it has kept me entertained for hours already. Great game.

title: Excellent Quality for a Great Price!
text: You can't beat the price here. And the quality difference is negligible compared to the actual Switch Pro controller. If you have the Nintendo-branded Switch Pro controller and are very detail-oriented like me, the only differences you will notice are: 1) No Nintendo Switch branding-logo on the front plastic. 2) Plastic is solid black colored vs the dark opaque Nintendo Pro branded controller. And the leopard-skin-like design on the grip handles is different (but I actually really like that--looks cool) 3) The home button cannot wake your Switch. Small price to pay. Either just hit the power button first on your Switch and then home button on this and it quickly connects--or just keep a right joy con near you to wake your Switch with that. 4) The rumble feature on this controller is different. It's a stronger rumble as opposed to Nintendo Pro's more soft and subtle haptic feel. But that's okay with me; and it does feel like it's all or nothing with the rumbling--no high/medium/low levels for it; but for most games, this doesn't bother me. Only on some games where you have a lot of action/shooting/etc, it may become obnoxious (but you can always turn off rumble option in your Switch options). All in all, this is totally worth it. And just to add to this--the seller is GREAT to deal with. There was a bit of a mishap on my controller. The D-pad directions did not function correctly. I contacted their chat support, and was instructed to email YCCTEAM support; they were great--had me try a few things just to verify the issue. In the end, they quickly sent me a replacement which works perfectly. And best part was they let me keep the first controller! I am a very satisfied customer. If you are considering a 3rd-party controller but want to keep the look and feel of the Nintendo-branded Pro controller, go with this one. For half the price, you still get practically equal quality. As long as you can withstand those differences listed above, then go for it I say! To me, it's worth saving the $30 from buying Nintendo's overpriced Pro controller.

title: Very easy to set up, works perfectly, plug & play
text: This is exactly what I was looking for but didn't know existed. I was looking for a joystick to play a Mame game on my PC but I don't need a "fight stick" with a bunch of buttons. I used a microswitch arcade joystick & button from a kit & the supplied connectors plugged straight onto the spade connectors on the microswitches. It all fit perfectly in a plastic box I had & plays so much better than a thumb controller. Of course I don't use it anywhere near its potential but it works perfectly & I had no issues getting Windows or Mame to recognize it.

title: Works perfectly, plug & play for a PC, cord is over 6' long
text: Full disclosure, I am not much of a gamer & I don't have an Xbox. I ordered this to play an 80's video game on my PC. I was surprised that it was totally plug & play on the PC. I have used the thumb-sticks but I prefer the touch pad to simulate a 4-way joystick. The controller has worked perfectly & provides a lot of options to play simple games & probably more complex games that use more controls. The cord is long, like 6.5 feet long. Compared to a wireless play station, the controller feels a little light but still solid. All of the buttons seem to have a long throw but this may just be an X-Box thing.

title: Looks so cool, bright color & vibrant, lighted keys. Thick & heavy with classic feel.
text: This keyboard looks so cool. I love the bright orange color & the vibrant, lighted keys. Unlike the keyboards I get for work, this one is thick with grippy pads so it doesn't move around on the desk. I love the soft spring feel of the keys & the key separation feels like the keyboards I used long ago. The light up keys look great & are vibrant. The keys are quiet so people don't hear my typing on conference calls EXCEPT the space key is quite loud & "clacky". It is hard to make out the characters on the top function & alternate number keys from a seated position & I do miss the USB ports that are on the back of my Dell keyboard. no USB outlets keys are quiet except space bar is really loud

title: This thing is BIG
text: This is a great gamer's mousepad for a few major reasons. Yes, it has LEDs that can flash different colors and totally fits into the gamer's aesthetic along with similar keyboards and mice. But more than that, it actually responds well to the different brand mice I have tried (great response and feedback from movement), and is big enough to have your keyboard in the middle yet have some room for the mouse on EITHER SIDE! That means you can mix it up and swap hands as needed for games that you might require more dexterity with one hand vs the other! Or if you have friends that are different-brained than you, or perhaps you are ambidextrous... the possibilities go on! Just measure first and make sure there's enough room. My old computer desk had a pull out keyboard that was narrower than this mat is, so make sure you have a large enough surface like a tabletop for it.

title: Great for turn-key setup
text: As a DIY enthusiast who's bought and installed Pis for all kinds of things, I was a skeptical about this product's purpose and value. I mean, you could easily set this up yourself with dozens of tutorials online, and arguably the entire purpose of a Raspberry Pi is the DIY part of it. However, that assumes you have a spare memory card to commit to the project, as well as the time to read up on it and actually set it up properly. For only a little bit more than the cost of a memory card, you can get this one already set up with everything you'd ever need or want. That's a reasonable argument. And personally, I always said I wanted to do this to one of my Pi boards, but never did. Now that I've gotten an opportunity to try this, I see the value in not re-creating the wheel when someone has already put in the time for me. I'm still a fan of DIY if you have the time and a spare card, but I'll happily spend the time I saved playing some classic Mario on this one.

title: Pretty excellent for the price!
text: My daughter wanted to try these to replace her older busted BT headphones, and so far she really likes them! I got the pink variant, and the color makes her really happy- even the case is pink, which isn't how the last pair we got worked (only part of the ear buds were colored on that one, and not the case at all). The sound quality is pretty decent, more bass than expected and that's definitely a feature on smaller buds. The build quality was pretty good too, but I'm personally not a fan of touch-controls. I've owned a pair like them before and found that I would accidentally activate things every time I reseated them for comfort in my ear / keep them from falling out. My daughter says she doesn't mind this because she doesn't touch her ears as much when wearing them, so maybe this is something that doesn't effect all people. The microphone quality isn't great at isolating your voice, you get a lot of background noise but that's all common for this style of ear bud. It's not perfect, but for the money it's actually pretty good.

title: Great and clear audio and classic gamer style!
text: I've had good experiences with Skullcandy before, but this is my first time trying their Wage brand of headsets. I'm happy to say the experience was positive, the headphones were comfortable to wear and the sound was excellent- definitely crisper and better bass response than the classic Apple buds I've been using on this laptop before trying these (and what I'm using for baseline comparison purposes). The microphone is excellent as well, I like that it aims in front of your mouth so it doesn't pick up ambient room noise and echo voice like other headsets which have the mic on the line or even worse, on the earphone itself (I've almost never had a good experience with a mic on your ear!). And the best feature is the way the mic will mute if you lift the mic boom arm up away from your face, and then come back when repositioned. A physical action like that is far better than a button or switch. The only catch is that you need to be into the gamer's aesthetic. Someone in our home wanted to use these for Zoom meetings, and found that she didn't like looking like she had such a large headset- it didn't go with the look she wanted to have on camera. But that's no fault of this product, as gamer / audiophile 'phones are usually the bulky variety and it is expected. I think this is a really solid options for gamers.

title: The wireless version is just OK
text: I noticed a lot of positive reviews for this so I had high hopes for sound quality. I see now that there are 3 different versions of this headset however, a wired standard 3.5mm TRRS one, a USB one, and a wireless one. I got the wireless one, which is also the most expensive version, and I have to admit I'm not impressed with the sound or features. With the glowing reviews, I have to believe the wired ones sound better and the culprit is in the transmitter. The quality of the sound over the wireless transmission is just OK. It's decent enough for VOIP and voice chats, maybe even gaming, but for music or watching videos it falls flat. I was watching a movie on Netflix and the dynamic range sort of collided with itself in such a way that it was hard for me to separate the voices from the background music compared to headphones that cost half as much as these. That being said, I DO like the microphone and that it can be easily detached. For gamers that want wireless sound and mic for chats when needed, it can be a decent product when it works well. But that leads me to my next point: The transmitter and headset seem to loose sync everytime one or the other shuts off. You you don't use the headset for a while, it seems to "go to sleep", and if the computer goes into sleep or hibernate, it doesn't seem to reconnect on its own upon waking up. I was trying this on my laptop and constantly felt like I had to power cycle the headset and unplug/plug the USB to get it connected again. Honestly, I feel like I could get a better connection experience and perhaps even sound quality from a pair of BT headphones, and just use my computer's bluetooth system to manage the connection upon waking up. If your computer doesn't have bluetooth, this system can be useful because it works like a USB sound card, but honestly I feel like for the price they are asking it should have been a better experience. Giving it 3 stars because it's fine for chats, is comfortable to wear and DOES look pretty cool. I just feel like you could do better. The wired versions are likely better.

title: Cool lights!
text: So, I'll be honest, I'm not sure what makes this for "gamers" beyond the light changing LEDs within. My son is starting to get into gaming with his friends, and he's been begging me to get him something like this, so we tried it out. It claims to have gaming DPI or whatever on the mouse, but neither my son nor I could really tell any practical difference in it when using for any 3D games. It works well enough, and it definitely LOOKS cool, especially in the dark. So, if that's what makes it a gaming keyboard and mouse, I guess it serves the intended purpose!

title: Flashing colors!
text: I don't have as much time for gaming as I used to, but I do use my desktop for a lot of graphic and media applications. I love the idea of the programmable buttons on the side which can be mapped via the driver software to shortcuts. Getting used to pressing the right one takes a bit of getting used to, but it's a very cool thing to have. The flashing colors are pretty cool looking and go along with the gamer styling like my gaming keyboard and Crucial RAM sticks that shift colors inside my PC case. The ergonomics are great, I actually find this mouse really comfortable to hold and use. The resolution and response is great, too. My only complaint is that I wish the speed button in the middle was harder to press by accident. My wife was using the desktop and accidentally pressed it, and the mouse started flying all over the place and she couldn't figured out how to go back to normal until came and pressed it again for her. Otherwise, what a great product from Amazon Basics!

title: Fun for retro gaming!
text: I'm a fan of retro gaming, but installing 8 and 16-bit classics on modern tablets and phones is frustrating to say the least. You need buttons. That's where this adorable and super useful controller comes in. I love that it has several modes for different devices (act like a generic controller, a keyboard, a switch gamepad, etc), and I was able to use it both with a tablet and my Fire TV over bluetooth. It's really great on the Fire TV since the remote that comes with that stinks for gaming. The size is a little less comfortable than a full sized controller, but the portability is great. You can slip this in your pocket and take it out on a bus/train to play retro games on your phone. The button combos to switch modes are a little bit difficult to figure out at first, you need to use the instructions to understand how to set the mode and then put it into pairing to set it up with different devices. For example, hold one button and start for Switch mode, another button and start for Android mode, etc. Then press and hold the other button until it starts blinking to put it into pairing mode after that. And if you don't commit the button combinations to memory, you'll need to look it up in the instructions again. If you only intend to use this with one device, that's less of an issue as you'll probably just set it up once and never change it. But otherwise, I wish there was a cheat sheet or something printed on the back so you wouldn't need to keep the instructions around. All in all, it's still a very functional and great little remote game controller for a great price.

title: Solid and CLICKY!
text: I love this keyboard. Yes, it is slightly smaller than a full sized keyboard, but it is SO SATISFYING to use. The keys are tall and have a big mechanical click like a vintage PC XT keyboard. The sound is audible and glorious, and the backlight LEDs really make it fun to look at too. I love turning it on and seeing the circles of light dancing around the keys to tell you its powering up. Speaking of powering up, it has multiple device settings, which is something I haven't had in a BT keyboard before, or any Bluetooth device for that matter. Now that I have it I'm wondering why more Bluetooth devices don't offer this. I have it paired with my Amazon Fire stick, my phone, and our family Tablet, and a quick flip of the switch to 1, 2 or 3 can toggle which one is connected now. With other Bluetooth devices, it annoyingly usually just tries to repair with the last connected device (especially frustrating with headphones!), but with this you can really use it with multiple devices and chose which one to reconnect to at power up. Brilliant! I didn't notice any BT lag, but I understand this is something that is mostly noticeable by gamers who use wireless keyboards, and find it very irritating. If you are concerned about that, thankfully this also has a wired mode directly over USB. I was a little bit uneasy to recommend this at first because of the price tag on it, but I'm really impressed with the device overall. It's worthy of 5 stars in my opinion.

title: Lots of connection types, but annoying USB
text: These are decent low end headphones. I'm not expecting high quality sound for the price, but they get the job done and have quite decent bass, although other tones could be a little clearer. But I have some issues with the connection type, which is the exact same experience I've had with other headsets in this price range: I like that these come with an option for both stereo and mic jacks (as 2 TRS 3.5mm plugs), or a combined TRRS with both mic and stereo in one (for phones, certain laptops, etc) via an adapter. But it also comes with a big annoying USB A cable which I can't get rid of. I understand the USB cable is for power which works the lights, etc, on this thing, but unlike the 2 cables which can be combined into one for smaller portable devices, the connection ports are just messy with a dangling USB cable if you don't need it. In my personal opinion, there should be an option to detach the USB cable and/or have it plug into a null adapter on the TRS/TRRS adapter wire so it has somewhere to go. It just looks messy like this, and requires too many ports to look clean on a laptop even if you're using all of them. On a desktop this is less of an issue, however the logo still seems kind of cheesy on the side, so I guess I'm just not a fan of the aesthetics of this set. It DOES work however, so if all you want is the utility of it, it works alright. Personally, I'd go with either a fully digital USB model if you wanted that (nice clean single plug, no analog jacks), or one without the LED lights and therefore doesn't require the USB plug.

title: Works great for button based games and compatible with Motion Plus / Wii U
text: Syncs up and works great, unlike some third party Wii controllers this one even has the Motion Plus part built in (required for Wii U and specific games on the old Wii console). Keep in mind, however, this *IS* a third party controller, so not everything is 100% to spec. For example, I noticed that when pointing to the screen, the hand cursor seems to move with somewhat more sensitivity than an authentic Nintendo Wii controller. This isn't that big of a deal, but if you are used to an authentic one, you might find you need to relearn your muscle memory movements when using this one. There is no difference for games that require button pressing (brawl, Donkey Kong, etc), which is actually what I bought it for (multiplayer games that don't require screen pointing). For me, its perfect, but minus one star for not being the same motion experience as Nintendo's.

title: NOTE: Uses AA batteries like the original Wii Remotes (not AAA like description above)
text: I have installed my old Wii in my minivan as an entertainment system (long story), and wanted more remotes for more multiplayer games on the road. These are pretty great knock offs of the original Nintendo ones, looks nearly identical unless you hold them side by side (the official Nintendo ones have the letters "wii" branded onto the remote, this does not). Color is slightly more cream than the white of the official ones as well. But otherwise, it seems to work well in our setup. I thought it was strange that the item description above says "AAA batteries", however, since the original Wii uses the more common AA. Turns out that must have been a typo or something, because these sure do use the plain old double A like the OEM Wii remotes.

title: Closest thing to being an actual Jedi.
text: As a SW fan and a fan of Kinect games in general, this is just a hoot to play. My 8 year old son loved the demo on our 360, and begged me to buy it for us to play. I'll be honest, there are better Star Wars games out there. And there are even better Kinect games. But for the price this sells for used, if you've got a Kinect and even a slight affinity towards Jedi, this is a must have. Some mini games are better than others- my son and I enjoy the Jedi adventure story, and I'll admit to playing Rancor Rampage to blow off some steam now and then. The Galactic Dance Off is kind of silly, though. Sort of makes it feel cheesy and cheap, (jar jar binks style, if you know what I mean), but I suppose they wanted it to be fun for everyone of all ages and interests, so kudos to the developers for doing exactly that! If I may admit, when starting the Jedi adventure and being trained to use a light saber, I started to really get sucked into it. The Jedi Master instructed me on screen to reach for my light saber (which flew into my avatar's hand), and feel its weight as I swing it around. I did that, and for a moment I felt like "Aw yeah, I can feel it!". Tons of fun!

title: Loads of fun!
text: Both of my kids love this set. Even my 16 year old loves it, it is truly fun for all ages. The Akedo Ultimate Arcade Warriors Starter Pack contains 3 warriors, a training dummy, and a joystick controller. You can change out the figures on the joystick controller which is cool. They snap right off and on. The figures are so funny as the more you punch, the other warrior or dummy will split apart. They are held together by magnets, so it is an easy fix to put them back together again. This idea is so much fun and we can’t wait to collect more of these as they are a huge hit already in my house!

title: Perfect for game console and accessories!
text: The material of this case is strong, not super thick, but not too thin. It is durable. The zippers work well and the game console and accessories are held in place with Velcro straps. There are little slots for holding game cards. There is a front zippered pocket on the outside of the case, but it is tight, you can only fit thin items in it, game cards, or some papers. The Velcro straps are easy to open and it is easy to put the game and accessories in their place. As the pictures show, there isn't really any extra space for carrying other items. It does hold the game console, game cards, power cord, and a hand held controller. When zipped up there is a thin carrying handle. I recommend this game case if you just carry the items listed but if you want a case to hold a lot of other personal items you might look for a larger case. It's perfect for the game console and accessories!

title: Works GREAT with CloneHero, very little setup
text: I hadn't gotten back into Guitar Hero/Rock Band in quite some time, mostly because I wore out my old guitars. This came up to review and I was more than happy to give it a try. After setting up CloneHero on my PC, I got the guitar assembled (super easy, 2 parts and some batteries). I plugged the dongle in, and it connected up immediately, no pairing needed. I followed the instructions included to get it set up (as a keyboard) in CloneHero, and away I went! I had to adjust the hardware input calibration a bit, but then I was playing again! It feels exactly like my Guitar Hero controllers of old, nice stiff buttons and very responsive. The whammy bar works great, and the tilt to activate star power never missed for me. 100% recommend to get back into the rhythm games!

title: Probably more than I needed, but high quality
text: I am not sure that I needed a mouse of this quality, as I am not a hard core gamer. I wanted a quality device, that will last and work with NO issues. So far, that is what I have gotten. It is very comfortable in my hand and I am able to reach each button comfortably with no awkwardness. The buttons are responsive and feel solid. I have put quite a few 4+ hour sessions in and my hand felt fine afterwards. I have not had any issues with latency with this mouse so far, or other "glitchy" episodes. Battery life has been great, I go days without having to plug it in. Also, this mouse LOOKS great, you don't see many cool looking white mice!

title: Nice for long term gaming
text: I got these for my son, who is spending more and more time gaming with voice chat. It seems to be a requirement for gaming these days. This headset is doing a fine job of providing clear sound and ease of use, particularly. We joined these up with the included dongle, and have had zero issues since with the headset connecting. The audio clarity is very nice, almost too loud at times I have been informed. The microphone is clear and mutes/unmutes by flipping it up, which is very convenient. Battery lasts at least a whole "day" of gaming. He plugs it in at night and it is always powered up. The only complaint I have is that they feel a little cheap, plastic-y. So far we haven't had any issues with durability, but I have concerns on how long they will hold up. They don't feel as well made as some other brands. I will update if it becomes a problem. ~~~ I hope you find this REAL review helpful! ~~~

title: So far so GREAT!
text: We have had the Quest 2 for about 4 months now, and one of the biggest issues I have had was where to put it SAFELY while not in use. I got a case, but didn't want to put it away every single time. This is not only a very nice storage space for the device and controllers, but charges everything as well! It was very easy to assemble and setup, took only a few minutes. I have seen charging stations, but they don't normally have battery packs for the controllers. This is all nice and compact and tells you with LED lights when they are charging and when they are full. title: Fits with an Elite battery pack headset

title: GREAT remake of one of my favorite controller designs
text: I have always loved the Gamecube controller, especially for Super Smash Bros. This is a very nice recreation for the Nintendo Switch. Obviously, its great for Smash Ultimate, but I really like using it for most games that I play in docked mode on the Switch. If you like the GC controller, you will love this one. It has all the regular buttons, as well as the + and - in the middle. In addition, this controller also has TURBO, if you like that sort of thing. I don't use it myself, but its nice to have as an option. Battery has lasted an acceptable amount of time, no issues. ~~ I hope you find this REAL review helpful! ~~

title: HUGE improvement with the battery
text: I originally got a different aftermarket head strap, which was an improvement over the original. Then I saw this one, with an additional battery. It is comfortable and the adjustment dial on the back works well. We have not had any issues with slippage or discomfort. The battery adds a TON of time to our VR time.
