title: Nice charger, LEDs are a bit too bright
text: I got this as an additional charger for all the Joy Cons we have accumulated, as only 2 can charge at once on the Switch console. It plugs in via USB to the Switch dock so you can keep it all in one area, which is nice. It charged my controllers with no issues, good speed, consistent charge. The LED lights change from red while its charging, to green when it is done. The only drawback is that the LED lights are very bright, so it can be a distraction near your TV/entertainment area. Otherwise great! *** I hope you find this review real, helpful, and really helpful! ***

title: Should be better for the price
text: The Good: - Looks great. The white with black/red accents looks sharp. - Comfortable to use (mostly). Feels very much like an official Pro controller to me, with the exception of the extra programmable buttons on the back. More on that in a minute... - Extras. Comes with extra thumbsticks and faceplate, and a case. Nice perks The Bad: - does not support HD rumble, IR or Amiibo NFC. For a $100 controller, it should be able to do all of this and more. Disappointing - Mappable back panels. This is the gimmick for this device. I do like the idea of programmable extra buttons, but they are in an odd place and it does not feel comfortable to me. I ended up hitting them by accident a lot when trying to adjust my grip. Depending on what you hot keyed to them, that can be frustrating. Overall, its is working just fine, its a good controller, but I can't say that it offers enough extras (and some glaring omissions) that justify an extra $40 over an official Pro controller.

title: Another quality controller from PowerA
text: I have had several PowerA controllers over the years, and several for my Switch. This is the best looking "Pro" style controller I have found yet! I love the gray with the colored shoulder buttons. Very comfortable to use. It is slightly smaller in size than the official Pro controller, but for my kids, its just right. The additional 2 programmable buttons on the back are a nice feature. I have not needed it so far, but I can imagine there are games where that would come in handy. As a note, this controller does not have rumble or NFC, but most of these 3rd party controllers dont.

title: Everyone loves it!!!
text: I picked this up for our daughter, because she absolutely loves to dance! It is the end of 2020 and our local dance classes have been closed since March. So I knew she'd enjoy this game, but was really surprised at how much she had been missing dancing.... it really revived her love of both music and dancing! She hasn't stopped asking to play it since since she got it. Or singing the songs (over and over again) when she's off doing other things. Or moving in general. I can't recommend it enough!!! We all have a good time when we join her. It really has brought some life and a lot of fun into our household!!! Thank you Just Dance!!!

title: Eh...
text: Save your money. It's not really worth it. While there are a few good new things, there isn't enough. They should have made this a complete holiday pack by adding New Years, Valentine's Day, St. Paddy's Day, Easter, 4th of July & well, you get the point...ALL of the holidays. Heck, even Groundhog's Day should have made this pack! I like the costumes & decorations, but I would love more of a variety. There just doesn't seem to be enough. And how about a dreidel? I mean really? Come on...lame...but it tries to be cute so I'm giving it 2 stars. And I left out cookies for Santa...cute.

title: Take back what's yours
text: Still playing through. The Clockwork Mansion mission has a Portal feel to it with the spaces behind walls and the disembodied voice that knows where you are which I think is neat. There's a "stats" menu that allows you to track the lethality of your playthrough so you're not angry at the end because rats ate that unconscious body you hid at the beginning of the level. The mechanics and feel of the game are on par with the original Dishonored. I feel like the guards are smarter. The new powers do not disappoint so far. I was worried guards would easily see me use far reach, but that hasn't been the case. I feel like there weren't a lot of issues with the original game, so this game just improves on it. The art, music, and story so far have definitely met my expectations. I love how it really puts the original in perspective and gives you a better idea of the empire. My only issue is that after a few hours of play, my pause menu and save/load menus no longer have images, but have white boxes where the images would go. It hasn't affected game play though. Love this game. I highly recommend it, especially if you liked the original.

title: An Amazing And Engrossing Story
text: Trevor Noah is a comedian who now hosts the Daily Show. In this engrossing memoir, he writes poignantly about his childhood in South Africa. As the son of a black woman and white man, his birth was a crime since blacks and whites were separated with the strict apartheid laws and interracial marriages were strictly forbidden. His mother, an unconventional, free spirit, chose to have him with a white man whom she did not love; she wanted a mixed race child. Trevor’s Swedish father was not usually in the picture, although Trevor saw him in very rare circumstances. Trevor lived with his mother, but even going outside the house was dangerous. They would walk separately and pretend they were not together. Trevor Noah did not fit easily into any race category. He was light-skinned and considered colored, although his culture was black. He went to a private English Catholic school and spoke perfect English. Colored people distrusted his accent and thought he was trying to be better than them. His mother stressed education, and he learned to speak various African languages, something that also set him apart. I was unaware that there were so many categories of color under apartheid. The author struggled to fit into one of these groups: white, black, or colored. The categories were somewhat arbitrary. For example, the Japanese were considered white but the Chinese were considered colored. Colored people were “the almost whites”. They did not have all of the privileges of whites but had more rights than the blacks. Every year some of the people would be recategorized, uplifted to what was considered a “higher” category. These people would have to submit an application and describe their hair, skin color, and other physical features. Some blacks became colored but, in some instances, the reverse occurred. In addition to the distinct privileges of the racial groups, there were set places for the different color categories to live. This fostered hatred and distrust among the groups. Trevor Noah writes with a keen sense of humor and dedicates this book to his mother. He credits his strong, fearless mother for giving him the strength and opportunities to be the man he is today.

title: Smart Girls 2
text: My 3 yr old grand daughter likes this game; but the front screen is not color as it is on Smart Girls (1); I can see what the games are when I scroll over them because I can read. The Smart Girls (1) front screen shows her exactly what the games are. She likes these games once she gets to them. Knowing now, I would have not purchased Smart Girls 2; I will read more reviews of the other Smart Girls Series. I do like the fact that these games do keep the interest of 3 yr olds. She wants to play games when her older sister gets to play them. Overall though, this game is better then some of the games for younger ones.

title: Fantastic!
text: I absolutely love this game. That is saying a lot, as I have never been a video game player. I have never owned a system, and therefore never really learned to play them well, so I just never liked them. But then my friends bought this game, and I fell in love. The whole point of the game is to cause as much damage as possible, and have extreme road rage. It is easy and fun. The one bad thing about this game is the soundtrack, but even that issue can be solved by turning down the volume on your television.

title: NOPE! Back to the drawing board. It has too many major flaws.
text: Don't do it! I bought this for my 6 yr old and also as a back up for me (I have small hands too) since it's plug-in and not battery operated. It claims to be 40% smaller (and it is overall smaller) but has some major flaws. 1) Biggest flaw: The distance from the side if the controller to the thumb sticks is actually FARTHER/LARGER than on a standard PS4 controller. This was a deal breaker for my son who adamantly stated he preferred the original controller over this one. 2) Flaw: The thumb sticks are hard plastic and not coated with silicone. Any gamer of any age will tell you this is not acceptable. These hard plastic sticks are slippery. 3) The original PS4 controller is designed so that you can have your pointer finger on R1/L1 and your middle finger on R2/L2. This tiny controller made it hard to hold it that way for both my son and I. 4) The D pad (cross shape on the left) is also sub par. Slippery and one piece as opposed to the segmented type found on the original PS4 controller. Returned it the day I got it.

title: I can't believe this controller gets such high rating. I've never owned a single Xbox. An unbiased review.
text: I can't believe this controller has 4.5 stars. The only thing I can think of is Sony fanboys inflating the reviews. Here's my honest review from a casual gamer who's had a Sega Master System, Sega Genesis, N64, Dreamcast, Wii, PS3, and PS4. I'm not loyal to any brand or company, so my view should be unbiased. GOOD: 1. The small speaker on the controller isn't much, but I like it and think it adds something to gaming. 2. The headphone jack is also helpful. 3. The light bar is cool, not only for looks, but to identify the player. 4. Sticks are better than the PS3 sticks. 5. L2/R2 curve in (not as much as it should) which is a big improvement from PS3. 6. The grips are a nice texture which give you a good feeling of control. 7. Sticks are symmetrical (I prefer this). BAD: 1. Quality/design issues. I've had two controllers break with a faulty R2 button. I was able to repair them myself via YouTube videos, but as a casual gamer, this shouldn't happen since I don't play all that much (2 - 5 hours per week). 2. A big one....battery life sucks. The battery life is about half of my older PS3 controllers (even with the light bar dimmed all the way). I'm always having to charge or worry about if my buddy's controller will fire up since it might have been sitting awhile. 3. Quality/design issues 2: I just noticed the rubber splitting on one of my controller (the one I use the least!). This is unacceptable. 4. Not a big one, but annoying....the option and share buttons are too small and should be more triangular and follow the curve of the circle the face buttons are on (hope that made sense). And I have very small hands for a man. 5. The grips (though well textured) are just round cylinders and don't feel like they mold to your hand. It's not terrible, but could be much much better. 6. Touchpad. Love the idea, however it seems like it's barely used, which means that real estate could have been better used for a one color LCD screen or something else. That's it! The controller gets the job done, but for how much crap people give the DS3, this DS4 improves upon the DS3 in some areas, and fails miserably at others.

title: I know I'm in the minority, but this game is bad.
text: I had MVC3 and traded it in and waited for UMVC3 and I completely wasted my time and money. Hard core fighting gamers will probably love this game, but I consider myself a casual to moderate fighting gamer. Here's the pros and cons: Pros: -Graphics are pretty cool and stylistic -Characters are varied -Marvel superheroes are always cool! Cons: -Online mode is supposed to match you up with people your own skill, however I'm noticing many "beginners" and "rookies" are kicking my butt. Then I realized that they aren't really rookies, but people either resesting their stats or creating separate accounts and starting over to easily beat people. That's why everyone I sometimes face user names like "taj134dod" -The endings are super lame and a huge disappointment. -Galactus seems a lot harder on this version than in MVC3 on normal. -Air combos. Worse thing every to happen to fighting games. EVER. Back in the day, Street Fighter II styles, it was about timing and guessing your opponents moves. Now, it's about landing that initial strike (which is good), but then being rewarded for it by doing almost unlimited air combos and taking all of your opponents energy for one initial hit. One opponent used Magento and took almost all my life with one consistant air combo. Go back to a thinking man's fighting game and not fast fingers and NO EXPLOITS. Knocking an opponent into the air and then slamming them back to the ground is fine, but this is just ridiculous. -You can't quit an online match before it begins. This is especially annoying when you are put up against a way higher ranked player than you and you can't exit. -Loading and saving. If this game isn't loading it's saving. If it isn't saving, it's loading. I could go on and on about the game's cons, but unless you're a hard core fighting gamer, than stay clear away from this game. I am trading in my copy for Batman Arkham City or anything else really.

title: Meh!
text: I love tactical-style games and I wanted to love this, too. It gave me a few hours of mild enjoyment, but I had no real desire to pick it up and keep playing. I didn't feel hooked at any point in time. The story is exactly what you'd expect - background fluff without much of interest, generally easily ignorable with a couple of laughs here and there. The puzzle elements are a chore and a roadblock if what you're really salivating after is the tactical combat. The combat itself is fairly enjoyable for what it is and the fights have a decent level of difficulty to them that ought to satisfy casual players or those who are new to the genre. There was nothing I couldn't beat within 1-2 tries. There are genuinely some nice features, such as the ability to team jump across the map and dash-attack. Being able to push or slow/stop enemies with the different status effects was fun, but the game did very little to explain any of it. Unfortunately, I just wasn't thrilled enough to even finish the game before handing it off to someone else.

title: It works!
text: The shipping was much faster than stated. The kit comes with cleaning wipes and a small cloth to make sure the screen underneath is perfectly clean and dry before application, which worked just fine. It has a card for getting bubbles out, but it's a little flimsy and I wound up using an old credit card instead to much better effect. I botched the first application, but was able to lift the cover up, smooth out the bubbles, and lay it back down without the adhesive losing much integrity, but if you totally ruin the first one, there is another one included if you need it. So far, the glass has held up well both docked and undocked for hours and hours of gameplay and I haven't seen any warping or other signs of wear.

title: Worst Lego game, in my opinion. It's fine if you just want to pass the time.
text: I love Lego games. I own them all. This is my least favorite for several reasons. There are only about 14 levels. Most of those levels are ridiculously long. If you save halfway through, you are likely to lose some of your mini kits. There are so many things crammed onto the levels that it can get annoying. I hate having to keep going back to change Batman or Robin suits. I hate that I can't just pick a suit in freeplay mode. I can only use a suit when it's there and needed. My game only had a couple glitches, but it just added to the frustration I already felt. Google helped me fix the biggest problem....you finally defeat the Joker robot, Lex and Joker are together, and Robin comes to Batman's rescue. It would freeze right there so that I couldn't finish the level. I just pressed the big green xbox button on the controller over and over and over so that the game could "catch up". It worked, but there are other solutions online. The other glitch was in Lego World. If I used the batmobile to go up the ramp to collect studs, the car would crash over and over and over forever. I had to start over, losing my progress. You can walk or fly around a really cool Gotham City. It's pretty cool, but it takes forever to get everything and it gets monotonous. The worst were the flying controls. I would be about to land perfectly, and the controls would stop me, turn me around, and leave me quite a distance away from where I was about to land. It was so frustrating, but I like to finish things so I just kept at it. It took me forever to figure out the map, but once I did, it was easy to navigate and find the things I needed. I'm at close to 100% on this game, but it has taken me forever. I only get a few hours to play every few days and I've been at it for weeks. With the other games, when I was almost finished, I'd just go through finding the mini-kits, then save/finish level. It shaved so much time off, but this one won't save the mini-kits unless you play all the way through. At least I hope they'll save that way. I haven't found out for sure.

title: Fun and challenging game. I simply re-beat a castle every time I need to save.
text: I want to give this five stars since I really do enjoy it, but the problem with not being able to save upon exiting is pretty annoying. Some levels are challenging enough for me to need to take a break before trying again, but most levels are very easy if you just want to run through. If you want to unlock everything and find all the star coins, then the game can be challenging enough. I haven't played multi-player yet, but I'm looking forward to it. If you want to save, just go back to World 1 or wherever and beat a castle boss.

title: I love Lego games!
text: We got Lego Batman for free with our XBox. I practically rolled my eyes when my husband suggested we try it. Well, that game kept us both occupied for weeks, then we bought Indiana Jones, then we bought the original Star Wars. I feel silly for enjoying it so much, but it is incredibly fun. And you do not just go around smashing things, although you do alot of that. You really have to use your head to figure out the puzzles and where important objects are hidden, especially when there are two of you playing the game at the same time. I would think you'd have to be at least 8 yrs old or older to beat alot of the scenes. It is very cute and very enjoyable and I can't WAIT to buy Lego Harry Potter for my birthday coming up.

title: Worked fine the first day, next day had problems
text: The cable worked great the first night. I read reviews by other people about the poor quality, and thought that I must have gotten lucky. Well, today I am having problems with my audio buzzing. It's almost as if the chord is grounded, and I have to bend the cable at just the right angle to get clarity. Everyone was right, the chord is very cheap. I initially bought a different branded chord before this one, but Rocksmith wouldnt recognize it. They must have some software that forces you to use their crappy brand. I have also tried using a coupling and one of my regular guitar cables, but I am still getting that persistent buzzing. I am probably going to try and exchange this one for another one, and try a different set up. After only a day, I am disappointed because I love the actual game so far. 4 stars because I knew initially that is was working fine.

title: Decent carrying case
text: I got one of the nerf controllers for my x-box and I really liked the cushy material on the underside of the controller, so I figured I would try out this case and see if I liked it as much as I liked the controller. The material that the case is made out of is not the same as the material on the controller, it’s similar but its a little bit harder. The case fits the switch very securely and snuggly, there is room for you to put games if you want. Overall it’s a pretty good carrying case, and I like it.

title: Comfortable controller
text: I seem to go through controllers more often than I would like, so I’m always in the market for a new one. I have to say I like this control a lot. The controller itself is a little sensitive, but other than that it’s just like a regular controller. I have to say the feature I like the best about the controller is the nerd material on the back. It makes it super comfortable to hold especially if I am playing for a long period of time. If you are someone who has sweaty hands I think the backing would really help with grip.

title: Fun game would have been better without the toys
text: I thought the concept was cool, and that the actual game itself was really well made but that the toys kind of took away from the game play. When I opened the box I was actually really kind of excited about the toys aspect of it, it was definitely an interesting concept. I liked the starter ship and how you could alter it based on what you had plugged into it. The thing that bummed me out the most about the toys was that you have to pay to get new parts of whatever, so this is one of those games that are a bit of an investment and I didn’t enjoy the toy aspect enough to want to make that kind of investment. About the gameplay, it was good, I enjoyed it. The controls are really fluid and intuitive. The air combat was really good, a lot of times those things made me motion sick, but this didn’t. The graphics were nice. The story was good and it kept me entertained. The game would have been rated better for me if you could customize without the toys.

title: Very comfortable and adaptable
text: First off the headphones were very well packaged. The actual headphones swivel so it makes it easy to find a comfortable position even when moving your head around. There is some noise reduction properties to the headphones, which is nice, but they aren't noise cancelling. Overall the material is well made and sturdy, particularly the cables. The only downside to the headphone for me is the microphone, the bracket that holds the mic itself doesn't feel like it's made of the same sturdy material as the rest, so I am a little bit concerned with it holding up over time. I have used it with my computer, XBox, and Switch, and I have enjoyed it a lot. If you are a person with bigger ears, these headphones work great, especially without squishing your ears.

title: good for the price, not overall
text: Long story short: the keys that are there work great - good brown tactile feel and sound. It's nice for typing. HOWEVER there is no programmability. There is a dedicated key for lighting and I can think of a dozen things off the top of my head I'd rather have for a dedicated key. I wish I had done more research and found a keyboard that is more malleable. If you study the keyboard layout and you think this will work perfectly for the lifespan of the product, go for it. Otherwise, I would aim for something with a little bit of programmability.

title: Get the K3 instead - with white backlight.
text: Bought this to take with me and use with phone, tablet, Surface. It is relatively compact, though the thickness is prodigious. I'm not mad about that. I have been using it for a few weeks and I am not coming any closer to familiarity with the DELETE and END keys (on FN1). It would have been much better to put end where the dedicated RGB button is, and then use FN1 + BACKSPACE for DELETE. My second choice - still much better than the way it is - would be to use FN1 with the arrow keys to get PAGE UP, PAGE DOWN, HOME, END, since the analogy is easy to sublimate. I had a laptop with that arrangement years ago and I got used to it. There is no app to program keys (like G-Hub for my Logitech products). Maybe I will look into third party remapping apps, but it's not the same. I already use AutoHotkey, so maybe I should just add something to my home script. As it is this keyboard is no fun to write on. The keyboard is continually taking me out of my flow to look down and poke at essential keys. The mode switch would be better IMHO with OFF and WIRED reversed. Again, it's a matter of attention. If you are using this wirelessly, you have to focus your attention and check that you have turned the power button to the center OFF position. When used in wired mode, you generally leave the keyboard plugged in and switched to WIRED, so it would make more sense to put WIRED in the fiddly, difficult switch position. Better yet, it could have another, dedicated switch for simple on/off. This keyboard has good action, feel, and sound. It is nice to type on - until it isn't. I would say that if you don't use the DELETE or END keys, you can be happy with this. It's probably the best use of my time to cut my losses now and switch to the K3, which has a slightly bigger footprint, in exchange for dedicated DELETE and END keys plus F1-F12. Or maybe I should look for something that it properly programmable. I am frustrated and disappointed with this keyboard. BTW I have ordered a K8 for my desktop computer (plus a Cherry numpad). I have been using this K6 on my desktop since my regular keyboard started having trouble. Keychron seems to make a decent keyboard for a good price, and a big draw for me is that the look is pretty much exactly what I would choose if I built it from scratch, anyway. I love the grey.

title: Good feel. Works with all my devices.
text: First of all, the key switches feel good. I have a nicer desktop keyboard with brown switches and this feels familiar, if not better. I really like the feel of typing on this keyboard. I use this with iOS, Android, and Windows. It works with all three OS's. I do wish that it had OS specific keys mapped, like Home, back, etc. I have a little folding keyboard that does this marvelously, so I know it can be done. It could be the case that all these keys are mapped and simply undocumented. I do occasionally, accidentally find keys and combinations that give unexpected results in iOS. E.g. holding function and hitting the right arrow twice bring up voice dictation. My only other gripe is the documentation. It's like the Woody Allen joke: poor and too little of it. I do wish all the mystery mappings were documented, and I wish the documentation were provided as a PDF or ePub or both so it would be easy to bring up on every device, with or without wifi. IMHO this is the ideal for this type of keyboard. It is cheap and works well enough. I think if it cost as much as a good desktop mechanical keyboard I would be less happy with it. As it is I cut some slack in consideration of the low cost.

title: Incredible bang for the buck!
text: If you're anything like me involving the oculus, your biggest gripe with it is the battery life SUCKS. Without a battery pack extension to add on to the headset--which they also sell on Amazon and if you haven't bought that yet, stop reading this and immediately buy one of those too--you get maybe 3 hours of playtime. Then it takes four hours to charge the headset. This docking bay cuts the charge time in half and it also gives you a cool stand to hold the oculus while not in use. Highly recommend, if you have an oculus this is basically a required addition.

title: Hmmm... you get what you pay for.
text: Well, I bought this to save some money, and the reviews are pretty much good. The power supply arrived yesterday. It looks nice, like a good copy of the original Xbox One power supply. It feels a bit cheaper than the original, but that is to be expected for something that costs less than half of the original. What I DIDN'T expect was that this would make sound (fan blowing) even when the XBOX is off. It sounds like a cheap build. I also didn't expect the strong smell of hot plastic which permeates the living room. Again, even when the XBOX is off. The power supply seems warmer than it should be, so I am skeptical about keeping this. Lesson learned. I don't want to take a chance on burning down the house. I wouldn't buy this again.

title: Awesome bright blue braided cable
text: This is a very nice cable. I got a USB to USB-C straight cable in a stunning bright blue. The cord itself is a nice braided cable that keeps it nice and sturdy. This one is 6.6 feet long. It is a fast charging cable that works very well. This cable seems to work for fast charging as long as your phone and charging output both are cable of supporting a fast charge. This cable is on the shorter side which is exactly what I was looking for, a 6.6ft length. This is great for charging around the car or whenever you are fairly close to the outlet.

title: Quality cable but they can't get the type of cable in your order right!
text: This would be overall a nice cable. It is a stunning blue and 6.6 ft long. I did NOT get a USB-C to USB-C cable and I also did not get a 90 degree angle on one of the ends. The cord itself is nice braided cable that keeps it nice and sturdy. The reason why I am slowly switching all my cables over to this type, the 90 degree angle at the phone end is just so much better. It doesn't get in the way and is not as prone to damage as the regular straight on ending. This cable seems to work for fast charging as long as your phone and charging output both are cable of supporting a fast charge. This is a fail for me though since one, I didn't get the right plugs on both ends and I didn't get the 90 degree on one end as I was looking for. I am not sure how this company can stay in business. This is now the third time I realize that I ordered an item from this company and 2 of them they got wrong! I would recommend to purchase cables from a different vendor. They do sell nice cables but odds are you will not get what you wanted.

title: Exactly what I needed - works really well
text: I love this cable, but it isn't cheap at $24! It is very long at 10 feet which is perfect and exactly what I needed, charging my phone from the wall plug in and have enough length to get to the night stand. It still gives me plenty of length that I can actually have my phone plugged in and still use my phone while laying on the bed! The cable material is very nice and feels very solid and sturdy. I am a huge fan of the 90 degree angle at the plug in. I just feels it makes it easier to hold your phone when you still work with it and is not in the way like the others usually are. It also seems more durable and reduces break off. That was one of the main reasons I got this one. I just hated the old regular design and wanted to give this one a try and really like it a lot. I use it with a fast charger and it works very well and I have no issues fast charging my phone with this, a Moto Z force 2.

title: Must buy.
text: It's difficult to describe the attraction of Xcom: EU. I never played the original and had no desire to play EU until I read some of the glowing reviews. As a big fan of bother Western & Eastern RPGs, I value the time that is placed into a game. I was not disappointed. If I could summarize EU's story in any way, it would be described as the deveolpers giving you the tools to write your own story. The charaters are randomly generated and have no backstory other than the one that you imagine for them. Sound corny? Trust me, it isn't. For the console version, there are a few minor bugs, but otherwise it plays out wonderfully. It's definitely worth the money and time.

title: Cool
text: I bought this on ebay a couple years ago and it worked very well for most of that time. Recently, the actual docking hardware failed and now it won't connect to anything or power on. I'm hopeful that I can find a new dock which will work with my Xbox one day one edition so I can use my digital games again! It did work with the original side panel left on the console, though it was a little loose. That looseness was user error, I bent one of the metal retention tabs while I was trying to install it. Use a little care and finesse to attach it to the console, and format it to the Xbox operating system and you shouldn't have any issues at all!

title: Need a replacement? Can’t go wrong with this!
text: It feels much different than the original Switch Pro Controller, however it is a matter of getting used to it. Once you ge the hang of it, though, it feels “ok” in the hands. It isn’t the most ergonomic controller out there by any means, and the diagonal input from the left feels very weird, but the button response is much MUCH better than the original Pro Controller. Rumble is also a bit too aggressive right out of the box, but this is something that can be adjusted. Battery life is fanstastic, so one full charge can last you around 2-3 days of gaming without having the need to charge it back up (played for 6-10 hours per day during the span of 2 days and didn’t have to charge for up around the third day)

title: The ONE to rule them all? *NO SPOILERS*
text: FIRST IMPRESSION I didnt like the intro music. It sounds pompous and deviated from the atmosphere created by prior Souls series starting from Demon's souls (Didnt like the remake intro either. But Im OK with it now). However, actually getting into the character creation and into the game, that initial impression completely vanished. There isnt much music in Souls games in general, other than in Boss fights. But what little it had, was perfectly suited to the world. Elden rings, other than the intro, is no exception. There is music almost all the time. The compositions are perfectly suited for the world and really paints a wonderful picture. Beautiful with bleak and dark undertones. The musicians did a heck of a job 35 HOURS IN: Character creation- Alot of interesting possibilities including cosmetics, which wasnt much of a focal point. Graphics- Top notch. Beautiful artwork. The only issue is inconsistent 60FPS even in performance mode. Performance mode highly recommended still. Gameplay- Dedicated Jumping on foot and horseback adds a vertical dimension to Souls games which makes it more interesting to play by giving more strategic options to tackle bosses and areas. Overworld- interesting and actually fun and not just mindless wandering unlike other games. Game gives you subtle directional clues to major areas of the game but still get to decide where you want to go. I didnt realize this until 30 hours in as I wanted this to be a completely blind run and not reading any youtube videos- which ruin the experience. Dungeon/Castle combat- side areas are easy and straightfoward understandably but the major areas have the same souls like intricacy and detail. Enemy/Boss AI is top notch and fun. Not overly difficult. Easy to get around. Convenient stations to respawn and transfer to. Story- same as prior series. A bit sparse by todays "standard", but less so than prior Souls games. Still need to piece things together and use your imagination. Games/Movies today are just so verbose that it leaves little to the imagination. Difficulty- Easier than prior souls games. It seems that they have many more respawn/transfer stations, which makes backtracking and progressing easier. Also, they give you a much bigger stamina pool to start off. You dont have to raise this stat unless you want a tankish build. This makes the game alot easier. In other Souls games you dont have to raise it either if you played the glass cannon builds, but the stamina pools were smaller and so you had to be more selective and strategic. There are also more clues as to where to go. The map is well done and interactive allowing you to pin areas of interest. Also they give you summoning options in certain areas, which makes it easy for you to do damage while the npcs tank for you. Works on most bosses. Not all. You still have the option of summoning other players. Suggestion- Take it slow, soak it all in. Enjoy this wonderful creation. Avoid grinding/power leveling and collecting every little thing while playing. Avoid watching Youtube videos and reviews unless you are stuck at a boss for days on end. Its fun figuring out how to beat bosses. Its part of the fun. On difficult bosses, I usually spend one night dying over and over again, thinking through strats and then the next day I beat it rather quickly. Which makes me wonder why I couldnt do it before. I find this a rewarding experience. Usually im underpowered so my strats have to be perfect. But obviously there are ways around this. But is it the best of the Souls Series? Its the most well rounded of all of them. Major Quality of life improvements makes the game more accessible and easier to get into and get back into and replay. But each Souls game absolutely stands on its own- Demons Souls, Bloodborne, Dark Souls.

title: Thumbs UP?
text: PROS: * Clicky responsive buttons. Nice feedback. Very impressive. * Nice aesthetics. Looks quality. * Assembly not too involved if you dont have two left hands (or right if you're lefty) CONS: * Plastic not as good as OEM. Noticed a crack on tabs and some falling off after assembly and reassembly. Main problem with back buttons is that the plastic seems to wear down or get bent out of shape just enough that it doesnt make enough solid contact with the pcb trigger. This is a huge issue bc it results in missed inputs and the trigger no longer “clicks”. I had to return mine and get a new one after about 3 weeks. * Somewhat cramped. I have average to above average size hands and I keep accidentally pressing the middle buttons. Itll take getting used to since Ive used the razer xbox, razer ps4, ps4 backbutton attachments and xbox elite. The others have a more comfortable layout for me. Still great. Just happy they have something for PS5 Ultimately though the biggest problem is the cheap plastic that they use. Otherwise design is fine. I just hope that they can address this issue in future revisions. I see that they will be making a real metal button option which would address the main issue I have. Still highly recommend it Since there really isn’t any other alternative. Itd get 4 to 5 stars if it wasnt for the cheap plastic.

title: Spoiler-FREE Review
text: Rating: Graphics/Art 5/5 Gameplay a 4/5 Modernized Music 5/5 Translation 5/5 Added Scenes 4/5 Voice Acting (English) 3/5 Voice Acting (Japan) 5/5 4 stars doesnt seem that great, but its a nice remake. Not on the level of a Demon's soul remake, but still nice. Whats important is that they kept to the spirit of the original. My favorite part of the game is how wonderfully they redid the music. For me, retrogaming is a good part about the music. I didnt think Id like it because I enjoyed the original so much. It was quite tastefully done. I think everyone will enjoy it. The only bad part is the option to play original compositions. It didnt come out so well. They must have paid very little attention to the transfer. The original compositions come off somewhat harsh. They shouldve borrowed my original SNES, which is modded for digital audio output with upgraded caps, audio quality internal wiring and power supply. Main quibble with the game is the voice acting. Budget must have run thin considering they may have had trouble gauging what kind of reception the game would garner. Id opt for the japanese voiceover, although the English voiceover for Popoi is fantastic. I really like that they added character development scenes, but the drawback is I ended up liking certain characters less- probably due to poor voice acting. The other nitpicks are some of the animations which are needlessly long and drawn out- i.e., when talking to an NPC. Otherwise the art work is very nice. The other notable thing is the difficulty. It has been modernized so that you can beat it without any effort or grinding. Kind of sad really. I dont like the grinding, which is fine. But the difficulty is skewed too much to the easy side for the bosses. Overall, I think the gameplay experience is much better on the SNES even though this version is very much worth experiencing for the music, upgraded artwork and additional scenes.

title: NEW but may need work
text: First, about the Dpad. It is awful. Even playing low-demand turn based rpg games becomes fatiguing and painful to use. The dpad doesnt feel right. Its too shallow and have to press firmly for a decent response. The 2.4 GHz aspect of the controller works fine. No issues. However, it does not make up for the D pad issue. Personally I would rather use something with a better D pad with Bluetooth if I have to. As of now I just swapped in Im my PS 1 to snes adapter. And then plugged in an old wireless ps1 logitech receiver /controller with a superior D pad. (For those who dont mind wires- performance ps1 dpad is one of the best and happens to be very cheap used) It does end up costing more, but not having to aggravate about the D pad is worth it plus with the converter you can actually use a real joystick on the SNES for shmups and whatever else you can think of. Their other controllers arent any better. The NES is the worst of the controllers. The Genesis is a bit better but not as comfortable as the original. UPDATE: Tried to figure out the cause of the poor performance. I was able to improve the responsiveness by cleaning up the dpad pcb with a cotton swab and IPA. Its new but why so dirty? Possibly these pcbs have been laying around the warehouse for a while before entering production. Who really knows but now the responsiveness is instant and feels a bit better but still the dpad design needs work because it still is not comfortable. I still prefer the other solution even if it isnt as cheap/elegant.

title: It works
text: It works. There was a review of this saying that it had issues. Looks like it got redesigned. It holds the HD steady. However, I had to cut the tabs with a wire cutter bc it wouldnt allow the HD to go all the way in. No big deal since the tabs were just 3d printed plastic. But the HD went too far in so I stacked two pieces of double tape together on the other end of the HD and it fit perfectly. Plastic is flimsy, but you dont need anything fancy in there. Hopefully it wont break with repeated removal but its not jammed in there like it was in the review, so should be okay (unless it deteriorates due to heat!)

title: Fantastic on PC
text: Highly recommended. Used the Virtua Stick on PC. No perceivable input lag judging by how I was able to pull off split second moves. I imagine the controllers work on PC as well judging by others comments. What would be great is if they could allow it to transmit bluetooth signals to the PC so you could use the controllers "wirelessly" so that itd work with say an 8bit do receiver. Id pay more for that. Another suggestion for Mayflash would be to create a saturn to multi retro console converter. Saturn on one end and snes/megadrive/pc engine on the other. And another model going from saturn to gamecube/ps1/xbox. Anyways good job!

title: Best of the Hori stick?
text: I like Sanwa parts, and although it doesnt have them, the hayabusa parts turns out to be just fine for me. Very easy to pull off split second moves. the stick and buttons are light, quick and responsive. Low effort and accurate. Its lighter than a sanwa, which in turn is lighter than the seimitsu. The only thing necessary to swap out imo is to replace the square gate with an octagate. For reference I have other Hori arcade pro sticks- 2 and 3. Also a few other retro sticks. I prefer the shape of this stick vs the other Hori ones, which are too wide. Why would you need anything that wide? The shape and size of this model is similar to the RAP 1, 2, 3. Overall, almost perfect imo. But can we get a wireless 2.4ghz version? Its 2021!

title: Beautiful BUT some GLARING imperfections
text: 4.5 out of 5. This remake, overall, is excellent. However, what plagues this game is what seems to plague a lot of the modern games which is that while it is technically superior to its predecessor, it doesn’t quite live up to the same level of emotional experience that you would get by playing the original. I am not saying this just to be an originalist or a video game snob. Here are the reasons: 1) The musical arrangements are elevator musicesque in some ways. Compare opening sequence. It doesnt have the sense of doom and dread that you have with the original. The opening cutscene art direction suffers from this as well, albeit still stunning. 2) visuals are fantastic and so detailed and is a wonder to see BUT it also detracts in a way bc it takes away from this dream state like nightmarish experience. Don’t get me wrong I love the new visuals but I became more of an observer than one who was actually experiencing. The PC emulation version was great for that reason, retaining the dream state like experience but with updated technicals with 60 FPS performance. That was really what PS3 version lacked. It would have been great if they could have included a technically updated ps3 version as well on the ps5 or even be able to play original ps3 discs with improved performance like xbox series x is doing with all their legacy titles. As an aside this is why I am a huge fan of the new xbox again. 3) for all its beautiful graphics and performance, what happened to the wonderful cut scene artwork that was in the PS3? They added depth and substance to the game. It wasn’t just an afterthought. While I grant you that the load times are so fast that it would have been hard to have the time to appreciate it. Why not at least include a section for it as a homage. Anyways still an absolute must play.

title: Phenomenal
text: Works flawlessly. Button clicks feel premo. Easy to customize the button. Designed to fit and work naturally. Very impressive. These are the other backbutton controllers I have/had- razer ps4 TE; Razer xbox wolverine; xbox elite 1; SCUF controllers. Out of these the best by far is the razer wolverine. The only problem is its not wireless. Compared to the wolverine, they are both great. Feel is the only difference and obviously the build material. Wolverine is metal. This one is plastic. Both are responsive and clicky. SCUF is an avoid. So is the Razer ps4 TE. If it had extra two back buttons like xbox elite/wolverine, that would make it perfect, but really not necessary. Made a decent ps4 controller great. Add a pair of analog stick height extenders and you are set.

title: Dissapointing
text: Bought two of these. First one had issues loading. Returned, tried another one, had some issues but wasnt as frequent so thought it may be my cart slot. Spent many many hours cleaning cart slot. Thought I was just out of luck. A few months later, this new cart completely died out. Doesnt load at all. Its just trash now. Cant return it. Turns out, it was just really poor quality control, absolute bargain basement parts. Ultimately, it wasnt my saturn cart slot. I bought an ALL IN ONE 4mb expansion cart with psuedo saturn kai preloaded. Worked the first time and every time. Never had a single issue. Still working after many months without any issue. Another plus is the all in one cart is black and not this ugly, beige, rainbow colored case. Good grief.

title: Very Nice offering
text: This is a good retro controller. 1) Size on the small side, still manageable because the buttons aren’t too far apart which makes for quicker reactions; 2) Form factor smooth and rounded without any odd shapes making gaming more comfortable; 3) D pad is okay not bad, not great. Its nothing like the original genesis's improved controller. That one by far is the best I have ever used. 4) Connectivity is superb. You never lose connection and responsiveness is good. Latency ill have to do more testing. This is obviously one of the most important qualities. It is a good thing that they did not stop there and went the whole 9 yards with the controller itself. The edges on this Dpad are hard and unforgiving. Thumbs get tired quick. 5) Build quality is good . nice weight and solid without feeling heavy. Their hyper dub limited edition controller is better. DPad feels better and better tactile feedback. VS other wireless. Havent tried retrobit and joyzz. Retrobit version im not sure I want to spend the money to try since I wasnt thrilled with their saturn offering although it is the only wireless solution for saturn available. Joyzz is quite a bit expensive but if its the same as the original genesis improved controller, it would be worth the money.

title: PROS & CONS for retro enthusiasts LF wireless
text: Surprised to see all the five star reviews Positives: 1) I will say that it looks nice, the design is nice; 2) Somewhat comfortable, good size, weight which is not heavy, and form factor; 3) Comes with nice packaging, which I do appreciate but I have mixed feelings about it which I will go into below; 4) very reasonably priced Cons: 1) Build quality is poor- feels rather light and flimsy. I like that it doesn’t feel heavy but it feels too light. If you have ever held an 8bitdo controller you know how solid it feels yet it is light. This does not. They really should have used the extra plastic on the controller instead of the “fancy” packaging. 8bitdo used the cheapest packaging possible and saved the plastic for the controller, yet it was all tastefully well done and executed. 2) Tactile feedback is lacking. Compared to 8bitdo, very poor. Retrobit's you can kind of tell you pressed the button because you pressed the button but there is absolutely no feedback. If feels loose and flimsy. As if the buttons can just come off. This goes for the D pad as well which does not feel solid and responsive. There is a feeling of hollowness. 3) USB connection to Nintendo switch is not 100% supported apparently because it seems to lose its connectivity midway through use at times. This can be sporadic- I don’t know why it happens. This is also not strictly limited to USB. I also bought a Genesis receiver and while it seems to work on the majority of the games I have tried one game in particular- terminator sega cd, does not work properly for whatever reason. 4) most importantly connectivity. It works on its saturn and genesis. BUT there is noticeable latency. Easy to see/experience if you play streetfighter or any fighters. Pulling out next to last second uppercuts are very difficult. Use a wired joystick/controller and its back to normal. With that being said, This is the only wireless solution for Saturn. Its a nice controller overall especially but mainly bc it is relatively cheap BUT only if you arent playing games that require instant responses. Best controller is the original WIRED saturn controller obviously.

title: SHMUP as Art
text: This game is art as its finest. You can tell the personnel involved from top to bottom are professionals and makes other SHMUP makers look like amateurs. Its what Demon Souls/ Dark Souls is to the modern action RPG genre. Even though the first game was a groundbreaker, this "final" reiteration is at the top of my SHMUP list. Sound 10 Graphics 10 Gameplay 10 Story 10 (extremely minimal but effective) From the opening scene to the end, the creators did a great job taking you into their world. Its dark, its foreboding and its beautiful Its not about having super fast reflexes, dodging a million bullets at a million MPH, which has its place and is fine for other SHMUPs, but this franchise is different- you weave your way through traffic as if you are in the matrix- thoughtfully and deliberately, moving your force back and forth and angling them at just the right place. As the game moves along, it builds upon each stage, getting darker and presenting you with more unique and interesting challenges and bosses. This game should be played with sound via the digital out port of the PS2 and into your stereo, properly attuned for best sound. Video wise either you use a component cable or RGB and have it line doubled via an OSSC or the like. It will be worth it because they did not skip on any facet of the game. It will suck you right in. Unlike other games which sound like you are in a techno club, (which can be fun) this game takes a different route and throws you into the midst of a cinematic experience with the quality sound and visuals. This is one of those buy and keep games, no matter what console comes next.

title: PROS and CONS- Updated
text: Im usually very critical when it comes to products. But when they work and they are good, I give them their due. I rather NOT spend 100 bucks on this thing. But it works and it works well. It upgrades your consoles whether your console directly outputs via HDMI or has to go through upscaler like an OSSC. It improves the visuals output from every single console from retro to ps4. The colors generally are richer and images are cleaner with more depth. For example, I have a RGB modded Genesis Model 1 Non TMSS with every improvement you can think of to soup it up to get the best visuals possible. The problem is the tech is old and so you are prone to some blurriness when random motion occurs. If you are used to slow paced games, then you wont get the max benefit from it, but you still will because of how much it cleans up the signal making it look nearly HD. Most reviewers show static pictures or pre-recorded intros rather than actually playing on the thing to show how effective it is. Fast paced, quick random motions- this is where its improvement is noticeable. It produces a smooth experience. It wont add more pixels or any of that. But it will clean up the image and get rid of that haze that your console is producing. This will make the image look richer, NOT brighter. It will also actually seem to reduce the lag in your gameplay because of the clarity and smoothness of the relayed video. You will respond much quicker because of this. If you like shooters like I do, it is helpful here. Also, the 4:3 mode is very nice. When using OSSC on some modes it stretches the image mode too much and this helps bring the image back into a more proper ratio. YMMV On a PS3/PS4 you should get a similar improvement, but in a subtle way, believe it or not. If you have a discerning eye, it will be readily apparent. Games like Nier, which has an obscene amount of blurriness, will greatly improve. Colors look richer and visuals will have more depth. PS3 and PS4 are especially prone to blurriness because of the heavy demand on the processors. When you pop in the McCLassic, its like playing on your PC without the additional resolution. Just more clarity, richer colors, rock steady visuals. I play alot of Bloodborne, and your reaction time will be better because of the reduced motion blur and increased clarity. If you get one, turn the MCClassic on and play it for a while. If you dont see the difference turn it off after a while by putting it on bypass mode. You will never go back to it off. You can see this clarity clearly in scenes where there is fog rendered. I hadnt noticed the fog as much before, but with the McCLassic, it adds so much more to the experience. Did I mention reduced lag experience? Those times you got hit and you swore you didnt see what hit you? Thatll happen much less often, if at all. When you get hit, you'll know why. As for whether its worth it? If the above doesnt convince you and dont find as much worth in it and assuming you get marginal improvement, think of it this way. If you own more than 1 console, and you own an HDMI switcher and you plug it in the output, you can effectively upgrade every single console you own. Divide the price by how many consoles you own and thats the real cost for the upgrade. Cons You need to reset the Mclassic from time to time. For whatever reason, when you switch consoles and it puts out different resolutions, the image doesnt register. This happens rarely so far. I believe this is when it usually doesnt work temporarily. The only solution is not to go to bypass mode, but to completely unplug the mini/ micro HDMI power cord from the Mclassic and power it down. Plug it back in and you're good to go. Assuming this issue doesnt keep cropping up as well as other potential issues, its a straight up buy recommendation. I will update as I spend more time on it. Edit: I use OSSC line doubler. X in photos 2x,3x, etc. can only get 2x line doubling with ossc + m because of the unstable output from OSSC. (May be related to the retro console itself rather OSSC.) UPDATE: Still works fine as it is supposed to. Any issues encountered in switching as noted in this review and comments below can be solved by simply unplugging the power and hard resetting it. Even if its on "off mode." Another item I would like to add since Ive had this since its inception is that some people may prefer the pixelated blocky look. Personally, I like this blocky look, but it only looks good when you have razer sharp output from your console, which usually takes modding, decent monitor and, what people dont mention, power quality. If you have poor power quality, it will affect your visuals. However, solving power/electricity quality issues costs more than this upscaler. Having a good power/electricity source, I prefer to NOT use the Mclassic just because I love the blocky, crisp, detailed look. Improving the quality of your power/electricity source will make everything look and sound exponentially better WITHOUT altering the original content. Doing this is better than the result you get from MClassic. However, it costs more and takes experimentation and certainly not easy to do. All in all, Mclassic is an easy way to upgrade your experience.

title: SKIP this game- NOT necessary to play Nier Automata.
text: This game couldve been so good, but it turned out to be somewhat of a poor game. First the good. Combat mechanics are fun, not great like dark souls, but its fun. The magic spells are fun to use and execute throughtout the game. The ability to change out spells in mid combat makes it not a complete real-time combat, but thats fine. Its a nice compromise considering you are limited to using a joystick. The graphics are good for its time, if not a little gray. But it becomes really good and the colors and motion become much richer and fluid with an upscaler. The bad: Dialogue, I appreciate that they are trying to wax poetical but its too verbose. I understand that they had alot to say, and alot of ideas, but they werent organized very well. Its also not elegantly written either. Its just all over the place. That being said, it does have to be translated so its probably better in Japanese. If you take a look at games like Demon's souls, Dark souls, Bloodborne, you dont have to write volumes to get the point across that life is harsh, brutal and cold, but with some beauty sprinkled into what we call life that sometimes makes it all seem worthwhile. Souls series does it through focusing intensely on creating a visual atmosphere and sparse dialogue that hints at what is. But what this series does is try to expound verbally, what can hardly be expressed through words. Even the epilogue is completely verbal. Could they not just throw in some animations to carry the message and make it worth watching? That brings me to the next huge negative- Kaine. She could arguably be the most annoying supporting character Ive run across. Even her walking around half naked couldn't make up for it. She could even beat the handler in Monster Hunter World. The only saving grace is that you don't hear Kaine all the time unlike the handler. And at least in the PC version of monster hunter world you can mute her and even change her face. Thank goodness for that. In any case, I understand what they were trying to do, make a volatile, seemingly complex character, likeable by helping the player empathize with her background through small but meaningful moments throughout the game. But no, it just fails to work. Perhaps the Japanese version works, but this utterly fails imo. The last negative- Music. Sound quality is fine. but the music is so repetitive. If they were going to recycle the same music over and over again, could they not use low impact, no vocal instrumentals? Or just use it once in a while to create a nice, lasting impact? Its fine to hear the full track a few times, but over and over again, it just becomes hard to bear. This is really a huge negative as music is a huge part of any game. They need to master things like this, which I will say, in the newest Nier Automata game, they seem to have done. So bravo for that. All in all, this game is not necessary to play Nier Automata, a complete standaline, which so far plays like a masterpiece of a game in all areas. You can avoid this game and really not miss a thing.

title: State of the games today.
text: This game is a prime example of what is wrong with today's game industry - it's absolutely confused. Its a perfect representation of what is going on today in more ways than one. It tries to appeal to everyone and in the end, the result is horrendous. Its a game with little imagination, it trivializes everything, the tone is completely off, the dialogue will set you back a few dozen IQ points. The game just doesn't take itself seriously, and frankly you shouldn't either. I received this game for free after upgrading my video card. Im usually a completionist but I could not bear to finish it after the first chapter. Go play games like halo, dead space and bio shock (not the sequels) and you will understand. If you haven't played it in a while, Id suggest you try again. Great serious, story telling with fun game mechanics. Ive replayed them recently and it reminded me how terrible much of the games are today. The pros- Wolfenstein's graphics are nice. I ran it in ultra-wide multi-monitor setup without a hitch. But on a 2080ti, I expect it to do so. Game mechanics ran fine. About the only positives I can think of. So it gets 2 stars for the visuals and that it ran smoothly. I cant believe this is my first amazon review and its about this game. Its honestly not worth my time, but I didnt want anyone else to waste theirs. Maybe itll snowball, into a revolt against game makers of this ilk-just wishful thinking. But if it helps one person thats good enough for me. In any case, Id suggest moving on and looking for something else.

title: omlord... Kids love this
text: Tons of layers, free play available after you complete the mission. Great videos on YouTube give you ideas about how to get through the levels. Played by 3, 4, and 5 year old grandchildren. Lots of cool things for girls as well as boys to enjoy but cuckoo cloud land gets a little much for the 4 year old boy. He prefers the street missions. The 2 girls love Unikitty and Wildstyl. There is a LOT of need to totally trash items to rebuild items which all of the kids enjoy. It was the only thing that would tear them away from Toy Story 3 which is also a great PS3 game for the very young. Grandma and parents very happy with the game although now starting to hum "everything is awesome" way too often.

text: I bought this for my son on his 15th birthday. We think it's malfunctioning, that or it's really disappointing. Flower is a tad more pleasing but fit for kindergarten audience. Flow has worse graphics than free downloaded phone games- nowhere close to the beautiful oceans on our planet.
