title: A Cure for "Short Cord" Syndrome
text: Finally! When you buy a phone or a tablet today they seem to be under the impression you have power outlets everywhere, and you can just plunk your electronic gadget down next to the outlet and connect with that shrimpy-short cord they include with it. This one is over six feet long and can be used even at work where you have to thread a cord down the back of the ugly modular cubicle structure and reach the power strip you've had to buy yourself because you're never given enough power outlets for the things you have to run at work. I also love the braided cord. It's easy to grasp, doesn't have that creepy plastic cord feeling under your hand, and makes the whole cord feel much more sturdy. Siwket makes several versions of these cords; however Amazon appears to list them on the same page. I received two different kinds, both which I found outstanding: one a 6.6 blue (yes!) cord with a standard USB plug at one end and a USB C plug at the other. The second was a grey 6.6 cord with a USB C plug at either end. One end is bent 90 degrees which is very useful when you have your power outlet next to a table, bookcase, etc. and need the cord to be directional.

title: Bluetooth Connection is Not Reliable and Headphones Keep Shutting Down
text: I got these headphones for my husband, who games occasionally and who was also looking for a set that would double as a high-fidelity, comfortable wireless set of headphones that also did Bluetooth for use when he is teleworking. He freely admits that he finds the headphones very comfortable, and the sound excellent. A lot of his calls are long distance; some even come from out of the country, and the sound is not always sterling. He was also pleased with the fact that the boom mike works flawlessly and his callers could hear him clearly and there was little request for him to repeat himself. However, the Bluetooth has been a total disappointment. On the first day it took some time for the headphones to initially connect to his cell phone (a Google Pixel). He is usually taking calls one after the other, but after each call he must write a report where he is not actually using the Bluetooth, and also, at this time of year, people do not call as much because they are away for the holidays. So, as he waited for his calls to come in or as he wrote his reports up, the headphones would regularly shut themselves off after a pre-determined period of time. This seems like an energy-saving feature that I'm sure is helpful when you are gaming so you don't waste your battery charge, but if you have to be immediately available for a telephone call, it is definitely detrimental. He would slip the headphones off and turn them back on each time it happened, but this gets annoying having to do it over and over every 20 minutes or every half hour or whatever the time period was (he didn't time it). [I timed it after connecting the headphones to my Acer laptop. If you don't use the headphones after 20 minutes, they power down.] However, the moment he did turn the headphones back on, the Bluetooth immediately reconnected. So he did use them for the remainder of the day. However, the next day he had the same difficulty connecting with the Bluetooth initially, and when the headphones shut themselves off automatically and he reconnected, the Bluetooth did not automatically reconnect. This happened several times, which was the final straw and he went back to using his old headphones. I wondered if this problem stemmed from not having loaded the Turtle Beach app. Perhaps there was some way to turn off the energy-saving feature. That would solve all his problems. However, I did not find that option on the app after loading it on his phone. In short, the sound is excellent as is the delivery from the boom mike. But the Bluetooth is not reliable, so we cannot give these headphones a good rating. (If someone knows how to keep the headphones from shutting off while being used for Bluetooth only, please let us know! He was pleased otherwise with the headphones and would love to give them a higher rating.)

title: Entry level headset good for gaming or office work.
text: The BINNUNE Dual Wireless Gaming Headset with Microphone is a descent headset and priced accordingly. It arrived nicely packaged with no issues. To sum it up, design, quality, sound, comfort are all average to slightly above. If you expected top of the line headset at this price point that is putting unrealistic expectation on the product. The design could be improved to increase flexibility and range of motion of the ear cups. That would improve comfort. Not every head is shaped the same. Sound could be better but the sound works just fine. It is clear and loud all though you do not have the atmosphere of a higher priced headset such as Astro. It’s not a deep rich sound you would find with a Higher end gaming headset. The microphone could be improved to better the noise cancellation. That would help it not pick up as much background noise. Also, it could have a swivel mic mute in addition to a button. It is hard to find the button. The headset connects easily via the USB transmitter or blue tooth. I had no issues connecting to my PC or using the USB transmitter with my sons PlayStation 5. Note, it’s is only for PS not Xbox. Overall, it is a good affordable headset for entry level gaming or evening office work like I use it for. I have used with teams and webex with no issues.

title: Nice mouse but design hinders hand placement and comfort some.
text: Overall the mouse is good. The left and right buttons are quiet clicks. The mouse scroll wheel works well does squeak, is smooth to spin only indentations. The digital display is handy and easy ti read. The led lighting can be turned on or off via the switch on the bottom. The mouse tracks well on screen and the adjustable dpi is useful. Forward and back buttons work as intended. It does have an auto off feature that increases battery life if not used for a period of time. Wiggling the mouse brings it out of hibernation. My only complaint is with the design. Due to the curve of the base my forth and fifth fingers do not have a comfortable resting spot. I can live with it but that should have been taken into consideration. I have small hands and a person with larger hands is likely to have more of an issue.

title: Good beginner wheel but expected more for the price point.
text: [[VIDEOID:499ac84584cf56f9db85b46180571b61]] This is my first experience with Thrustmaster and a wheel in general. My expectations based on price and the Thrustmaster name were not completely met with the T128P for PS4/5 and PC. It’s a great $100 wheel but slightly above average $200 wheel. Primary user of the wheel is my 12 year old son but for testing purposes I have been driving race cars like I stole them, lol. Arrival: The wheel arrived nicely package all component were in working order with no issues. However, I immediately notice some of the creature comforts I expected were missing based on price of the wheel such as cushion wheel or higher quality buttons with smooth action. Instructions: Th instruction for setup were clear except for the computer driver download portion. A little more emphasis and larger font would be nice. Took me a second to locate them due to size of font. Wheel: The wheel itself is made of hard plastics, buttons appear of low quality and make a loud audible click when pushed, especially the paddles shifters. They lack the quality you see with PS5 and the Xbox elite 2 controllers. The clamp worked fine but make sure you have room underneath your desk to attach, see pictures. Pedals: I have similar thoughts when it comes to the pedals. The pedals assembly is very light and lack common sense in the design. It doesn’t take and engineer to understand center of gravity and how a lever works. To explain the pedals will slide forward when in use and have a tendency to want to pitch forward off the floor due the center of gravity begin shifted so far forward and the lack of weight to counter this affect. The design seemed to completely overlook that someone had to actually use this in game under various conditions. I guess that is why a pedal stand is sold by Thrustmaster as an accessory for ~$90. Just my thoughts but human in the loop and ergonomics should be considered in the design process hint…hint. You have to hold the pedals in place with your off foot, use a weight or hey buy their pedal stand. Hooking up: Once everything was hooked up it was first tested on the PS5 with no issues. Worked well with GT7. For the computer…driver download was easy. Thrustmaster done have control panel for making adjustments to the settings. We first tried with Forza 4 and had issues. The game would not recognize the wheel. However, after some internet research we found this is a common issue across many brands of wheels and Forza 4. I found no immediate work around so we tried using the wheel with Forza 5. The wheel was recognized as a T248 and Forza auto-configured the wheel. The wheel worked as intended with all features being functional. My son did adjust the button layout to his liking. When also tried the wheel with the Crew 2 demo and it worked but not as well. Not all function worked on the wheel, mainly the center shift lights were not operable. This could be due to the game being only a demo though. So to wrap this up the wheel is a good beginner wheel but without the creature comforts I expected for the price point. The design lacks in key areas of functionality and quality, especially regarding the pedals and use of quality components such as buttons. The dynamic functionality of the wheel lacks the feel I expected and in my opinion is cheap considering the price. Note: the cord routing and layout could have been incorporated better considering it is a clamp on type mount. The cords are easily pinch during mounting and do not stay in the routing channels. My review is solely based on my experience with this wheel and isn’t biased as I have never owned another.

title: Good fit and excellent grip. The company stands behind their product.
text: My son has been wanted some grips/protectors like these. He has a habit of losing the controllers when he plays which cause me to get excited. First, good quality material, appears durable. The grips are easy to install, fit tight, and all cuts out match well. My son had on before I could blink. The grips themselves have a good feel and provides much needed additional grip especially when hands get sweaty. The material thickness is just the right size in my opinion. The lanyards has a wide range for adjustments to accommodate various hand sizes. Completely satisfied and my son is happy as well. Update…they stand by their product. I had an issue with the hand strap related to the bottom grommet breaking. The company responded quickly and provide a replace set. Great to see quality customer service.

title: Awesome fit, great protection!
text: The product came nicely package and once my son unboxed it, installation was easy. The cover snapped into place with no issues. Very good fit, all cutouts aligned. There were no issues with the BoboVR m2 head strap, fitting in the case and CNBEYOUNG VR Face Cover he has installed on his oculus. The shell itself is hard plastic with a soft texture coating that appears very durable. It does allows for a better grip which is good when a 12 year old uses it. Definitely provides much needed protection from bumps and handling. My son and I are both satisfied with the product and have no complaints or issues. Update, his mom made vinyl stickers eyes which adhere great!

title: My son love the scroll wheel
text: According to my son this is a great all around mouse. Only thing that could make it better would be a rechargeable battery. However, you can overcome this with a rechargeable energizer battery. Fits in his hand nicely, he is 12 years old. It is comfortable for me as well. He loves the fact the scroll wheel can be either notched or free spinning. This comes in handy for mining in his Star Citizen game. Responsive is great and can be easily adjusted. Programming the thumb buttons are quick and painless. It’s Bluetooth capable if you do not wish to use the usb transmitter. I have not heard him complain about the mouse.

title: Battery lasts 4-EV-R
text: These are super cute! I love them! They have great range and the battery lasts FOR_EV_ER!!! I haven't used the detachable mike. The built in mike seems to work just fine. I also have not used them with the cord. I haven't had the need since the battery in these lasts so long. I was feeling a little guilty about spending so much on new headphones, but I'm so glad that I did! I use them mostly with my iPad. I use them for FaceTime and just to listen to podcasts while I clean my house. They are so comfortable that I have also been using them to listen to meditations while I go to sleep. I definitely recommend these! Plus they are adorable!!

title: Terrible battery life!!!!
text: First impression is that the mouse is pretty comfortable in my hand. It has a lot of adjustable settings and you can switch to 3 different profile settings with a tap of the button. It is very lightweight and the lights on it are pretty cool. Sometimes I get mouse lag when I try to move the pointer. Con: I bought this mouse so I could stay wireless and game away without staying wired to my desktop. The battery life is horrible. I have had wireless mouse that I could play for weeks or over a month before charging or replacing a battery. This mouse has a battery life of 2 days max. If u are in the middle of the game and your mouse dies out it kind of sucks there is no clear indication that it is low and will die at any minute.

title: Now I have peace and quiet
text: Why I'm asked to give stars to a "game" when I'm reviewing a headset I'll never know. Get it together Amazon. My son doesn't have the same taste in music as I do. Mind you he's 36 and I'm 62. He has been on this opera kick and I'm a pan-world fusion kind of gal. I ordered the Universal PC/Stereo Gaming Headset because he could also use it with his X-Box. My son says it is comfortable, "I've been using it since it came it. I like the slider clip thing on the cord. I don't notice outside noises. The mic's flexibility is fun although I've not used it yet." As for me... I do not miss opera, thank you very much. In exchange I wear my headphones when I listen to ZapMaMa. Hah!

title: It's more than you'd think for the price
text: Considering the favored astrology software cost as much as my new laptop, WinStar was a relief to find. I thought I'd just be able to cast a natal chart, maybe do transits and synastry charts. Even though one can cast charts at astro.com for free there's times when there is no WiFi where I'm giving an astrology reading. I needed software installed on my new HP Laptop. Budgets being what they are for me I "settled" on WinStar. I didn't expect what I found, a little treasure of an astrology program, and believe me I've been using astrology software since back in the day when I had to Boss my DOS, ok? What I found that surprised me: A second disc with tutorials for the beginner, and it's good to have as a reference even if you're not a beginner. Atlas: An atlas that I've not been able to stump yet. Reports: Natal, Transit, Synastry and Progressed reports that you can generate and save as pdf or text files, that you can email as an attachment to yourself or your client. BIG PLUS! Wheels galore: An assortment of wheel types, single, double, different house systems. You can also email those. To email wheel charts or reports hit "print" and it goes to a pdf format, from there you can save, print, or email. When I'm out and about doing astrology readings in a cafe with WiFi I can email the wheel and report to my client as something to refer to when they get home. I also email myself the same material for the client's folder on my home desk top. If I am not where there's WiFi I can burn the report to a DVD disc with my laptop and hand the disc to the client right there, on the beach, in the forest, under ground in a bunker. When doing a double wheel the transit option comes up automatically. Nifty! If you want to select another chart for synasty you can do that but I like that the transit option comes up first. Transit "Time Line": It's transits done for 3 days, 1 week, 1 month, 1 year, as a multi-colored ribbon, the dates run along this "time line". It shows when planets go into a new sign, or transit a new house for the client. It shows the transiting planets aspecting the natal planets in one color, progressed planets are shown in another color, solar arch are shown in another color. If you ever had a client ask just how long transiting Saturn is going to be opposed their natal Moon you can easily see it on this time line. One draw back is you can't do a time line for the current day, like if you just wanted to do general forecasts. The work around is to cast the birth data for yesterday, do the time line for a week or a month and you can have the information you need. I know I have not exhausted the possibilities of this software. Don't let the price fool you. It's not light weight. It has helped me a great deal when doing readings away from home in my laptop and away from WiFi if that's the environment I find myself. I'm very pleased.

title: Returned after 1 day
text: I bought this on Wednesday, paid $18 for 1 day shipping, received it Thursday, used it Thursday night for a couple of hours. The light really does not reach the far corner. I thought, I could live with that for the convenience of having a Kindle case with a built in light. I used the Kindle in the case on Friday for less than an hour while out on errands. On the way home on the bus I get a "Low Battery" notice. My new Kindle 3 was fully charge and had only been used a few hours before I got the case. I had the WiFi off which was supposed to save battery life. I did a search online about Kindle low battery and found many people who have their Kindles in the "Official" Amazon Kindle case, with or without a light, had battery drain. That the battery drained even if you weren't using it, WiFi off, sitting in a drawer. I was wondering why it was taking so long to recharge while in the case and I read that one person had LESS battery charge after recharging the Kindle in the case over night. That's unacceptable. So after having the case w/light for one day I'm returning it. It will cost me another $7.00 out of my refund for shipping it back. I spent $25 to experience the Official Amazon Kindle Case with Light. This is the first item I've returned to Amazon. The return process was easy I must admit. Update: I am being refunded the $18.00 for one day shipping. Nice! Again I will say that Amazon.com's return and refund process is very good. Now if they can tweak the Kindle case w/light so it wasn't a battery drain we'd purchase it again.

title: The Smaller Size Is Nice But It Does Present Some Issues
text: As an old, retired guy I spend a lot of time online gaming every day. My favorite MMO is complex enough that I use three computers while gaming. The main one is for the game itself. A second one is for Discord so I can easily track who is talking and/or any text messages sent on that app. The third window is for the game's wiki and various other information sites that I often need to reference on the fly. As you can imagine, three computers on a desktop makes for some clutter. So the smaller size of this keyboard is very nice. That smaller size does come with some issues though that gamers particularly need to be aware of. For one thing, there is no number pad and the function keys have been combined with the number keys. For me as a gamer, those kinds of changes have several ramifications. Most keyboards are standardized enough that switching to a new one is no big deal. In this case though, with significant changes to the keyboard arrangement, this one requires a learning curve to train the muscle memory to the new arrangement. My favorite game also uses a lot of keybinds. So, removing the number pad while combining the number and function keys, removes a noticeable amount of possible keybinds. The final issue I've had with this keyboard is that it's smaller size and novel arrangement means that I am hitting the wrong keys a significant number of times. That is not a good thing when the combat in your game is hot and heavy. There is one other thing of note about this product. The white keyboard and it's light show looks like it was designed for a pre-teen who is into rainbows and pink unicorns. I don't have any strong reaction either way to that design aesthetic myself. Other folks may love it or hate it though so just be aware of that in case such things matter to you. The de-cluttering usefulness of the smaller size is useful enough for me to give this keyboard a 4 star rating. I'll just put it on the machine I use the least and certainly won't use it on my gaming machine. That way I get the big advantage without worrying about it's disadvantages.

title: An Excellent Set of Gaming Headphones
text: As an avid MMO player, I used gaming headphones a lot. When engaged in coordinated raids and such with other players, I'm in Discord chat for extended periods of time. While roaming solo across my game world, I like to listen to music and audiobooks, again for long periods of time. So a good headset is very important to me. Over the years I've tried any number of headphones, across a wide variety of price ranges. This headset is one of the best I've ever used. The sound is deep and rich, with wonderful bass tones. The surround sound works very well, with clear audio separation of distinct sounds, which is very important in a game that used audio as well as visual cues in combat. The headphones are comfortable to wear for an extended period. And they are genuinely plug and play, which is also nice. Just plug them into a USB port and they are good to go. One minor but significant point when using Discord - When I plugged in my last headphone set, also into a USB port, the only thing that showed in the Discord audio settings were Default input and output devices. While the headphones themselves worked fine that way, there were problems with the mic. Other players could barely hear me, even with my volume cranked all the way up on both their end and mine. That's why I got this headset. As soon as I plugged it in, Discord picked up both the headphones and the mic as USB audio devices, with both the headphones and the mic working just fine. I am more than satisfied with this product and at its price it's a real deal.

title: The In-Game Sound Is Truly Beautiful, But...
text: These headphones really do have the deepest, richest, most immersive in-game sound field I've heard yet from any headphones or speakers in the under $100 price range. For me though, that is not enough for a 5-star rating. Your mileage may vary of course, depending on how you use headphones but let me lay out the issues I had with this headset. While the in-game sound was awesomely good, the audio quality for movies and tv shows as well as music and audiobooks were the same as most other headsets and speakers in this price range. The MMO I play the most has separate volume controls for music, environmental sounds, dialogue, and special effects while movies, music, etc, generally have a single volume control. I don't begin to understand the technical issues involved but that may have something to do with why these headphones can take the different sound files in a game and weave them into a very real sounding, three-dimensional sound field while being unable to do so for other types of audio files. Where this becomes an issue for me, and where your mileage may vary, is in what I use headphones for. There's two times I plug in headphones - when I'm gaming with fellow players via Discord or when I'm listening to something loud at night and I don't want to disturb my upstairs neighbor. Other than that, I don't use headphones to listen to the sounds of my video game. Instead, I'll be listening to music or audiobooks on some decent computer speakers while gaming solo. Their sound for such things is as good as these headphones. The advantage of speakers is they don't start getting uncomfortable after extended use, like headsets do for me. Which brings us to another issue I had with this headset. The product page touts their comfortableness. When I first put them on, they did feel more comfortable than other headsets I've used. After two hours of running ingame raids with some guildies though, the headphones were becoming uncomfortable. I was glad when we finished our group raid so I could sign off of Discord and take off the headphones. So it really comes down to how you use headphones. If you game with them on all the time and are comfortable wearing a headset for an extended period, you will love this product and it will likely be 5-star headset for you. If not though, this item will likely drop to 4-stars for you, excellent in one area but average in most others.

title: Pretty To Look At, Not Much Practical Use, But Ants Seem To Like It
text: As a casual gamer I can't tell if this keyboard is serious overkill for me, is just filled with unnecessary frills, or is some combination of both. In any event, it has no noticeable impact on my gaming. Let me give a bit of context. As an old, retired guy in the midst of a pandemic, I actually have a lot of time for gaming and easily spend 6+ hours a day in my favorite MMO. I call myself a casual gamer because I am too old and slow to be a hardcore, competitive player. So I don't play to beat others but to simply have a good time. My favorite MMO is Guild Wars 2, which has a variety of game modes, from relaxed casual to hardcore competitive. One of those game modes, World vs World is a series of open maps where players can roam as individuals, in small groups, or in massive zergs fighting other players to capture keeps, towers, supply camps, shrines, and the like. It's a nice mix of casual and competitive and even an old, slow guy like me can run wild there and the ingame rewards available make it worthwhile to do so. The action is fast-paced, fluid, and always changing and I usually spend a couple of hours a day or so in WvW. That's the context in which I tried this keyboard and it worked no better than the basic $15 keyboard I had unplugged to try this one. Guild Wars 2 does not allow the use of macros so that feature did me no good at all. Roccat's macro set up seem clumsy anyway. You need to hit two keys, while looking at the keyboard to get the right ones. Other keyboards I've seen have a much better implementation of macros. My favorite option was one that had a dedicated set of extra buttons just for the macros. One button to hit and once you got the muscle memory down, you wouldn't have to look at the keyboard to hit the right key. The "swift, precise key stroke" touted in the product copy had no practical effect for me. At times when my group was being swamped by a larger enemy horde, making swift action imperative, this keyboard seemed no faster than the basic keyboard it had replaced. Several times I had to hit a key twice before it responded. Even something as simple as the audio controls seem clumsily implemented on this keyboard. There's three buttons and a knob. One button is for muting. One says FX and I still haven't figured out what it's for. The third button seems to turn the volume knob on, and the knob then adjusts the volume. The basic keyboard this one replaced had three audio control buttons - mute, volume up, volume down. Much simpler. This is also not a plug and play product like basic keyboards are. After plugging it in, I had to go to the company website to download the necessary software. Once that was installed, I had to download/install an update. Once that first update was installed, I immediately had to download/install a second update. Not only was it a lengthy process, but the keyboard locked itself down during the download/install process, meaning I couldn't do other things on the computer while all that was being done. Once all the software and updates were finally installed, I learned how unnecessarily irritating it was to use the software. The only instructions included with the keyboard were to go to the company website to download the needed software. On the website itself, there were no directions for actually using the software. So for me, it was a clumsy, hunt and peck process, trying different buttons to figure out how to do such basic things as set the color scheme, select the sound played when hitting a key, and set the profiles to change those settings depending on what I was doing. The company website was very pretty to look at but some simple step by step instructions for using their products would have been much more useful. That description of the company website, "pretty to look at but of no practical use" is pretty much the way I would describe this keyboard. Yes, the lights are pretty. Yes, it's fun to choose the sound that plays when you hit a key but none of that does a thing to improve my gaming. The local ants really do seem to like this keyboard though. This morning when I sat down at my desk, they were swarming all over it, running around through its maze of colored lights. I have no idea what that was about but they seemed to be having fun.

title: Excellent Headphones
text: The sound is very good. The headset is perhaps the most lightweight and comfortable I've used so far. It's also completely plug and play. You plug the headphones in and you are good to go, no drivers or other software needed. Some headphones show up as unique items under the audio settings. So when you want to use them, you need to go to your settings to manually select them after you plug them in. Not these. Just unplug your speakers, plug in the headset and go from there. A lot of manufacturers seem to think all gamers are middle school kids who need and want flashing lights on everything. The last set of "gaming" headphones I tried put ridiculous colored lights on the headphones. I say ridiculous because you can't see those lights when you are actually wearing the headset. So I appreciate the fact that this headset eschewed such nonsense, focusing instead on audio quality and the comfortableness of the headset. There are two cautions I need to add. Though neither was a big deal to me, you should be aware of them. The first is that the cord on this headset is shorter than other headsets I've used. My set up is a main computer that I actually game on with a second computer to the side that I run Discord on. That way I don't have to flip in and out of the game to deal with Discord issues. The cord on this headset is fine for use with my main computer but is too short to reach the secondary machine. Depending on your set up, the length of the cord may or may not be an issue to you. For me that also means I haven't tried the microphone on this headset, just the headphones. Given the quality of this product I wouldn't expect there to be an issue with the mic, but you might check the other reviews here to see what they say about that. Thanks for reading this and I hope you enjoy this product.

title: Adequate Bur Not Particularly Awesome
text: As a cranky old guy who spends a lot of his retirement time gaming in MMOs, I had some mixed reactions to to these headphones. On the plus side, they really are plug and play. No special software is needed, no tricky set up issues, just plug them in and they are good to go. MMO means massive multi-player online and it generally indicates the kind of game where you cooperate with some players while combating others. In a situation like that, headphones with a mic are essential to fast coordination. Gamers I know generally use Discord or Teamspeak to verbally communicate with each other. Once again, the set up was basically plug and play. With the headphones connected to my computer, I had no problem using them with either of those programs. There were a few things that kept me from giving these headphones 5 stars. For one thing, the sound is okay but is nothing special to write home about. That's fine for gaming but if want to listen to music or watch movies, you'll probably want to switch back to your regular speakers. Which touches on another thing, this one positive. Some headphones and mics show up as unique items in my audio settings. So when I want to use them I have to plug them in and go into my settings to select them. This headphone and mic just show up as generic default input/output devices in my settings. So I can just plug them in without having to also adjust my settings. Another negative is how flimsy the headphones feel. It took some effort to pull the earphones out enough to fit them properly on my head. It felt like I might break the thing if I pulled too hard so it took a bit to get the earphones extended as far as I need them. Moreover, the padding under the headpiece is similar to other headsets I've tried, only to have that padding rip and fall apart after only a few months of use. One other positive should be mentioned. There's an on/off switch for the mic on the headphone's cord. That's very handy as a mic that's always open can lead to echoes and squealing feedback that the other folks playing with you will not appreciate. Oh, and there is one neutral thing to close with. Like most "gamer equipment" these headphones come equipped with pretty lights. That always seems like a silly marketing ploy to me, one aimed at 11 year old gamers. Those pretty lights are even more ridiculous than usual on a pair of headphones. The headphones are on your head, you can't even see those pretty lights like you can with a keyboard, mouse, or other "gamer gear". So all in all, this headset/mic seems like it will do the basic audio job I need it for, talking with other gamers in the midst of fiercely fought battles. There's just nothing outstanding enough about it to boost its rating up from 4 stars to 5.

title: The Lights Are Pretty But Otherwise It's Just A Mouse
text: As a plug and play mouse this one does the basic job expected of a mouse. As a gaming mouse it may be a bit more problematic. The teeny tiny instructions direct you to a website to download a driver. It took a bit to find the correct download on their site and when installed it doesn't seem to do anything. The download did put a shortcut on my desktop but when I double click the shortcut or the application file directly, nothing happens. The mouse itself works the same as it did before installing the driver. If I click the DPI button it does indeed change the cursor movement on the screen but there is no way for me to know what the actual setting is. So if I accidentally click that button again, it's a matter of blindly clicking until I get back to that setting or something close to it. Also, for my gaming style, a 6 button mouse doesn't offer much more flexibility than a regular mouse. The two extra buttons aren't enough to make a significant difference in my game play. So as a regular mouse it works just fine with some pretty lights flashing continuously. As a gaming mouse it doesn't do much for me.

title: An Abrupt Crash From 5 Stars To 3 Stars And Possibly Lower
text: EDIT: I'm leaving my original review below to show you why I initially loved this keyboard and gave it a glowing 5 star review. Sadly, just a few days after posting that review things took a sudden turn for the worse. For unknown reasons the G Hub software controlling this keyboard crashed and burned completely. Not only is it no longer working beyond the basics but the crash also pushed the keyboard into default mode. That means the extra macro keys that were so helpful in my game reverted to being standard F1-F5 function keys. My game already uses those function keys for essential combat moves so now, after deliberately training my muscle memory to use the macro keys, those keys do entirely different things.. Even a casual gamer like me knows how that destroys one's game play. A google search showed that this G Hub crash is a common enough occurrence that there are YouTube videos and reddit articles on how to try and deal with it. I followed some of the basic suggestions - rebooting the computer, reinstalling the software, unplugging the keyboard and plugging it back in again, all to no avail. The G Hub loading screen just spins endlessly and I have no way of altering the default settings of this keyboard. The next step is to trying dealing with Logitech support, which does not have a good reputation online. At 70 years old, I'm too tired to deal with much hassle so I don't know when I'll have the energy to take that on. If they can't, or won't, help me, the rating on this review will go even lower. If they can show me how to fix the problem, the rating will stay at 3 stars or possibly go back up to 4 stars depending on how much difficulty is involved. In any event, the first bloom of 5 star love is definitely over. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- First, let's give this review some context. As a retired guy I'm too old and slow to be a hard core gamer. I have five grandsons in high school and junior high who are hard core and their game play is in a whole different universe than mine. This review is not for them. I'm a relaxed, casual player and that's who this is written for. With that in mind, let's move on to this keyboard, starting with the fun stuff. Fun - The Bright and Shiny Lights A lot of gear branded for gamers seems to feature brightly colored lights and this keyboard revels in them. Before it arrived I wondered why it bothered to even have lights. When I first took the keyboard out of the box and plugged it in, the lights were so bright and were flashing so quickly that I was like "Whoa, how the heck can I even use this thing?? Those lights are just way too distracting and confusing!!!" Silly me. When I downloaded the control software I quickly discovered that I could tune the keyboard to my own liking, using other people's lighting designs or easily create my own. With a vast array of colors to choose from as well as a variety of shifting patterns and lighting sequences, I happily set about creating a lighted keyboard I really, really liked. Heck, you can set each key to have it's own color sequence if you want and you control how much the whole thing flashes and how often it all changes color. As far as I can tell, the colored lights have no impact on my game play but it's like having your own Christmas light show all year round and I love it! Why would anyone want one of those old, unlighted keyboards? Fun - Clicky, Clicky, Clicky and Other Sound Stuff When you order one of these keyboards you have have a choice of three different keyboard sounds. I got the Clicky version which sounds and feels a bit like an old school typewriter. The sound is unobtrusive but nice. I couldn't tell you why but that clicking in the background as you type feels comfortable to me. It's letting you know that you are actually doing something when you hit the keys. Again, why would anyone want one of those old, noiseless keyboards? They are so boring. 🙂 Another sound thing is the volume control on the keyboard. I don't particularly need it with my current set up as I have a small speaker, with volume control sitting right next to my keyboard. Still, my previous computer was an all-in-one who's volume control was awkward to use. So the keyboard mounted volume control would have been handy then. The Serious Game Stuff - Macros and More Macros Here's where we get down to the serious stuff. For those who don't know, macros are small scripts for doing a series of actions by pressing one key instead of having to press one for each action. For example, say you are playing a cowboy shooter and you ride into an ambush. You need to dismount, draw a rifle or pistol, aim, shoot, and reload when necessary. Normally each of those actions would require a separate key stroke. With a macro though, you could set it up to do all that with one key instead. As you can imagine, macros can be powerful, powerful tools in the game world. They are so powerful that the main game I play forbids using macros for more than one action at a time. Even with that limitation, the macro capability of this keyboard is still very useful. There are five new keys on the left side of this keyboard that can be assigned to any use you'd like. Currently I have them set up to quickly mount and dismount from the various critters I can ride. That in and of itself is nice. However, you can also set up different macros on those keys which can be swapped in and out at the push of a button. There are a variety of professions and skills I can use ingame so if I wanted to, I could set up different macros to use with different characters in addition to the mounting/dismounting. I haven't done that yet but I fully intend to. Just as nice is that the control software makes macro creation easy peasy. The control interface is minimalist in design and you have to poke around a bit to figure out how to use it but the learning curve is not onerous and once you have figured it out. using the software makes macro creation incredibly easy. In case you can't tell, even as a casual gamer I love this keyboard. Hard core gamers will probably appreciate it even more than I do.

title: A Good Headset With An Irritating Learning Curve
text: THE BOTTOM LINE - Getting the headphones and mic to work properly took some irritating effort for a newbie but was worth it for how it immediately enhanced my online gaming. The headphones themselves are nice. The sound is excellent and the headset is the most comfortable for extended wear I've found yet. Wireless Bluetooth speakers often stutter while streaming audio but these non-Bluetooth headphones worked flawlessly. The controls are positioned a bit awkwardly, on the lower back end of the right side ear cup. I've hit the wrong controls several times while trying to do something as simple as adjusting the volume. The set up was extremely irritating for me. The minimal directions are on one very large sheet with 95% of the content being the same few sentences in a myriad of different languages. I don't mind multi-lingual instructions, it was just the layout on this particular broadsheet that was frustrating. I had to keep flipping from one side of the sheet to the other trying to figure out what to do. Then it took me 20 minutes to get the headset to actually work simply because I had pushed the USB cords in as far as they seemed to go but they needed to be pushed in even further.A google search showed that folks have had similar problems with other Astro gear. Someone used to these kinds of headsets will probably have a much easier time but for a first timer like me, this was a very irritating exercise indeed. It turns out that the Astro website has a set up video that is dramatically easier to understand than the included instructions so keep that in mind. Then, after I finally got the headphones plugged in and working, it turns out I can't get the mic to work. A google search did not help here as people have had problems with a variety of Astro gear but I couldn't find anything pertaining to mic issues with this particular headset. About 45 minutes ago I put in a support request on the Astro website. So I also get to test how good their support it. Once I've dealt with them and hopefully gotten the mic working, I'll update this review and adjust the rating accordingly. EDIT: Upgraded the rating from 3 stars to 5 stars. Customer service got back to me within a day as promised. They gave me a check list of things to try (included below). Testing the headphones on a different computer was the one that worked for me. They worked flawlessly on a different machine so the mic problem had something to do with my first computer, not with the headphones themselves. The reason for moving the ratings upwards to 5 stars is that setting up and using the mic was pretty straightforward and using the mic opened up new game realms for me. Just now I used headphones and mic for the first time ever in an online game, running some missions with my guildmates. Being able to talk to my guildies was a whole new level of companionable gaming, one I thoroughly enjoyed. Even with the 5 star rating though, I do have to reiterate a caution I gave earlier in this review. Using this gear will likely be a cakewalk for a techie who knows what they are doing. For a newbie though, getting to the sweet spot with this gear took some frustrating effort. If you are a newbie, I suggest that you start with the appropriate astro a20 set up video on youtube and if you have any problems, try this checklist from Astrogaming support. Good luck. The suggested trouble-shooting checklist: - Watch the set up video to check your settings. - Check to make sure your A20’s Base Station is in PC Mode. The PC/Console Mode switch is located on the back of the Base Station. - Resync the A20 Headset by plugging the headset into the A20 Base Station as if it were charging. - Test the alternate USB ports on on your computer. Test your equipment on an alternate computer or console. Use a different voice program (Discord, Skype, Teamspeak, etc.) - Hard reset your A20 Headset by simultaneously holding down the GAME Button (Located below the volume wheel) and the EQ Mode button located below the power button. Please note: When doing the hard reset, have the headset plugged in directly to a confirmed power source, without the Base Station. Let charge for 15 minutes, then retry.

title: A Solid 4 Star Product With A Couple Of Minor Issues
text: As I am neither an audiophile nor a techie, this is an ordinary person's simple take on these headphones. First, the positives. The audio is really good, as is the noise canceling. Plus, they look cool. :) The minor issues are that the microphone is okay but not exceptional and that you can't adjust the size easily. That means they might be a bit problematic for folks who wear a larger hat size. So these are worth checking out but if you need to use the mike a lot and/or you have a bigger head, keep the shipping container handy just in case.

title: Finish the game but still had like 75% to unlock for more money
text: I'm not sure if I'm reading the game or the person I bought it from but everything worked well. I have been out of video games for a while. title: Actual baby hands (5'0 female) and I LOVE my new keypad
text: I'm a 5'0 female and have extreme baby hands. I've been using the Nostromo for years, but unfortunately it's been fading fast. I hestitated to upgrade considering the reviews for users with smaller hands were so poor, but I am in love with this new Tartarus keypad. I see a lot of users comparing it to the Nostromo, and while I understand the argument of size, it's also important to take into account there is an additional entire row of keys on the Tartarus. Mind you, that missing row of keys drove me INSANE and I am so happy they added it. Sure they are a bit more challenging to reach with smaller hands, but in gaming I have them as programed as my numbered inventory and in editing for less used keys. The padding is really soft and the product is very durable and feels superior in it's quality compared to the Nostromo. The d-pad is night and day compared to the old model and much easier to use. The only physical draw back I've found after several hours of use so far is the scroll wheel feels somewhat fragile. The software is very simple to use and still offers a seemingly endless amount of options to personalize the device's use. Having my mouse work seamlessly with the device, and even together with programing options, is a huge plus. If you have smaller hands and are transitioning from the Nostromo it's important to remember the addition of the 4th row (which is fabulous). If you are using a razer keypad for the first time, I would suggest some patience and assure you that you will grow to love it. Well worth it.

title: Smooth
text: This mouse is light as AIR. It's a bit bigger than I anticipated, but the weight compensates for the size. The battery life is something to be desired. I followed the instructions on charging out of the box, however I have yet to hit100% battery charge despite long hours of charging. 97% is the closest to full. I game and work on social media and spend roughly 2-4 hours at least on the device daily. I have had to charge the mouse every day I have owned it. The connection fails randomly which has not helped my KDR. If this doesn't fix itself I'll be returning it. It's a shame because my AK spray has improved significantly since using this mouse. I am not a fan of the buttons on both sides. I ultimately disabled the buttons on the right, but I can appreciate the fact Razer is keeping it's left-handed customers in mind. All-in-all, I am a big fan of Razer products, but disappointed in the price of this mouse and the quality. I'm dedicated to the company and hope to find resolutions to these issues.

title: Buy it now.
text: If you have the computer to handle the Rift, you need it. With the price down all the way to $399 for the Oculus Rift + Virtual Reality Touch System, you truly can’t pass up this deal. The Oculus Rift is by far the most fun I’ve had with video games in some time. When it comes to the actual physical system, I’ve noticed a significant amount of complaints with the excess wires. The Touch System includes the headset, 2 sensors, and 2 wireless remotes. The headset requires an HDMI port and USB, each sensor requires a USB port. I can admit the wires can be a bit frustrating, but honestly I really haven’t noticed them at all. In fact I’ve actually used the wire from the headset as a reference to stay centered in the room. The tracking is amazing and the boundaries you set up for yourself around the room make punching the wall a rarity. The controllers, as designed, feel like natural hand motions and are easy to use even with my toddler hands. The headset is a bit big for my tiny-ass head, but no one else seems to complain about it, so I’ll live with it. All the features lead to a truly immersed feeling for the player. I am really blown away by this system, along with everyone I’ve also had try it out. If you’re even questing the Rift, the answer is yes. For the love of god yes.

title: She loves this keyboard and uses it for work not gaming.
text: When I ordered this I thought maybe her son could use it since he is a game developer. When it came, I showed it to my wife and she liked it. She hooked it up to her work computer and REALLY raved about how much she loves this keyboard. So it is not just for gamers. Grandma's that work from home, spending countless hours on the computer can use this model too! She says it is much easier to type on and appreciates the tactile sound the keys make. She claims she can type faster on this keyboard. As long as she is happy, so am I. She recommends this one highly. Try one out for yourself. You may like it too.

title: Completed My Work-From-Home Setup
text: The was the missing element to my ultimate Work-from-home setup. I work in a call center and I needed the absolute best microphone on a headset that would also be comfortable for use long term. These filled that exact gap! I love these so far and I'm not sure why they aren't so mainstream! I connected them via usb with a cheap $10 adaptor. Everything works and they sound great! I'm no audiophile it anything but I can say these are some of the best in the market. I was also recommend to get the replacement Dekoni earpads and I can say they do make a difference. I disliked the material of the stock pads. 100% will recommend.

title: Initially Biased review: How to Set-up and Impressions
text: I had given a bad review for my first review. I clearly had failed to read the instructions which you so need to do in order to utilize this keyboard. To switch from wired to wireless mode hold fn + r and the pair hold fn + either z,x, or c for 3 seconds to activate pairing. Note that this pairing lasts for like 6 seconds so you gotta be fast. Great board. 1.5 pounds is great for portability. I know it's going to look great once I replace the keycaps. As for the bluetooth, yes there's a little bit of lag here an there when it hasn't been used after quite a while but this is expected. I love this keyboard and the price. 5/5stars for me

title: Keeps the headset/chargers neat and organized!
text: I gifted my husband an Oculus (Quest 2) for Christmas. He loves it and spends a lot of time in the “verse.” Ironically, when I purchased the Oculus I didn’t realize that it was simply the headset and the two controllers. These things just sit on top of a piece of furniture. I was considering keeping the parts in a basket. However, when offered this device for an honest review, I jumped on it. This VR Charging Dock is just what he needed. It allows him to charge the device and keep all the pieces together. Looks neater and more organized with a random basket. Did I mention it looks cool too! Definitely a must have for those with this device. I’d recommend it.

title: The perfect Christmas gift!
text: My husband and I were at a friend’s house (a few months ago) who owns a Meta Quest 2. He invited us to play and I noticed how much my husband enjoyed it. So, I decided this device would be the perfect gift for him, for Christmas. He seems to be really enjoying it and so do other members of the family! The set-up is simple. Once connected you are ready to begin downloading games. Some are free and some aren’t. You can even travel to different countries (which is cool), go on a safari, mountain climb, play golf and so many other activities. There are informative and interactive videos. The graphics are great and offers you a realistic view (360 degrees) of whatever you are looking at. There are also chat rooms (if you are interested in that type of thing), interactive and multi-player games (like Saber), and much more. Some of these games (like Saber) improve hand/eye coordination. It can be a family friendly game/environment. The set comes with the headset, 2 controllers, and a storage bag/cover. It is lightweight and portable. It even comes with an adaptor for eyeglass wearers. Overall, while a little pricey, I think it is worth it (especially for a man who has everything).

title: Let the gaming begin!!
text: My sons love gaming! Both of them and they are in their early 20s. They have the Xbox 360, the PS5 (one son has a digital version, the other has a disc version) and I recently purchased the Oculus VR for my husband as his Christmas gift. [I really hope he doesn’t read this review.] With my “gamers” in mind, I thought this would be a nice accessory them. I have noticed, when I do venture into either of my son’s room, their PS5s seem to give off a little heat! This device (by Heatfun Store) is perfect and has multiple uses. You can organize, charge and cool. The stand allows you to keep your device vertically while cooling with a fan! It is easy to assemble. The fan is pretty quiet and has 3 settings (low, medium and high). You can store up to 12 games/DVDs beside it and charge your controllers. Overall, he is extremely satisfied and gives it 5 stars. **Note: I am going to have to order enough for my other son.

title: Protection for an expensive device. 4.5
text: My son loves his PS5 and definitely would be upset if it were damaged while traveling back and forth to college. As a result, I selected this product for an honest review. title: Let the gaming begin. 4.5 stars
text: My son purchased a PS5 for Christmas and is over the moon. I have never seen a young man (he’s 19) so happy about an electronic. title: Let the gaming begin.
text: My son loves the T. Flight US Air Force Edition Gaming Headset. This headset is lightweight and wired. It works great with his PS4 gaming system. The sound quality (i.e., audio) is good. While I can’t get into Fortnite, I was able to connect it to my laptop and listen to some music. I agree. The design is nice and pretty rugged looking.
