title: Game on.
text: The Lupsan Gaming Headset in a nutshell. Positives: -The sound quality is great. -This headset is noise cancelling. -It can be used on multiple devices (i.e., lap top, PS4, Xbox and cell phones). -The ear muffs are well padded. (see other concern below) -The boom is flexible and easy to adjust. -This item is reasonably priced. -Comes with a stereo cord. Negatives: -The ear muffs are semi-comfortable. They fit fine on my head, but my teenage son (whose head and ears are slightly larger) says that over time, they start to feel a little uncomfortable. Even adjusting them didn’t make a difference for him. -The mute button is located on the mic, under the foam cover. My son, who likes to mute the mic while playing FORTNITE, found the location of the mute button to be inconvenient. He would rather have it on the cord somewhere. In conclusion, with a few simple design changes, the Lupsan could have had a perfect score, instead I’m giving these 4 stars.

title: Click Click!
text: AUL Mechanical Keyboard is pretty sweet. It has a great ergonomic design. It is sleek and cool looking. Space-agey. Easy to connect and store. It is a wired keyboard. You simply have to connect via USB to your device. The keyboard is illuminated and colorful as you type. You can use it with your PC, laptop or gaming system [PS4]. Most of the keys are in the same location as those on the traditional keyboard. There is a magnetic (removable) hand rest. This is super convenient for those who don’t like hand rests. You can change the color by pressing the large round dial in the upper righthand corner of the keyboard. Not to mention there are over 20 options of color combinations. You can make is strobe or stay constant. It’s up to you. I like the keystroke and the ease of pushing the buttons. Whether you have large hands or small, you can navigate this keyboard. It is pretty light, so not too heavy. The quality of the keyboard appears to be decent, but of course only time will tell for sure. It will take a few months of constant use for me to tell how durable it is. In conclusion, this is the perfect keyboard for a gamer or someone who wants to use with a PC or laptop. I’d recommend it.

title: Perfect for gaming on TV or on the PC.
text: This “Cool 2000” gaming headset is great. They are aesthetically attractive. Kind of space-age looking. The ear portions are bold and vivid. They glow red when plugged into a USB port. These work on the Xbox, PS4, Smartphone, Tablet or computer. We use ours on the PS4 and computer. The microphone rotates 360 degrees. They are extremely comfortable when wearing them. The ear muffs are padded. The sound is decent. You can control the volume by turning it up and down on the ear. You can also turn on the LED and microphone on and off in the same place. Overall, this is a pretty great headset that can’t be beat especially if you consider the attributes and the price. I’d recommend it.

title: Game on.
text: The Razer Electra V2 is fantastic and perfect for gaming teenagers or young adult gamers. I can count on two hands the number of headsets that I have bought or received because my kids are careless and broke them. To parents in similar situations, these (the Razer Electra) may be the answer. These over the ear headset are extremely attractive (black and neon green) and compatible with several gaming systems. We have both Xbox One and PS4. They are affordable, the setup is simple and they are easy to use. The (surround) sound quality is good. They are noise canceling, meaning you really can’t hear outside while gaming (but it probably helps that my sons listen to their games and music extra loud). You can control the volume by a slide control and you know you’ve muted when the orange light is on. The (aluminum) headband is comfortable and can be adjusted easily. The headset is light and can be stored anywhere. The only drawback is that these are not wireless, but the cord is long enough (3-4ft) to play without being too distracting. The cord is long enough to use while sitting at a desk, on a sofa or in a chair. You should not have any issues. And finally, the microphone does detach. Overall, I am very pleased and would recommend them. I give them 4 out of 5 stars.

title: If you can handle the TRUTH this remote will DELIVER.
text: This review is based on my teenage son’s observations. **Note he spends countless hours playing 2K and Call of Duty. Therefore, he is comparing this controller to his white, wireless one. Appearance: This remote looks like the classic XBOX controller. It is black with the traditional analog joysticks, buttons and signature XBOX logo. And while there are a few new features (i.e., buttons), the overall look is the same. *NOTE: He feels that this controller is lighter (in terms of weight) than his other one, but attributes that to the fact that it’s wired versus wireless, which means rechargeable batteries. *The cord has a nice length (several feet) so you don’t have to worry about sitting super close when gaming. You can sit back, play XBOX and chill! New features: (1) You can control the volume of the mic from the controller. (2) You have the ability to reassign controls (rb/lb) using the rolling buttons located on the bottom. AND (3) You can change the color or design of the face of this controller. Versatile (computer or game system): You can use this controller on the PC or the XBOX 1. Simply plug it in. Now the cons: In the end, my son gave this remote only 4 stars. While he likes the cool new features (controlling the volume and assigning controls), he loves the versatility that the wireless one offers. He said that when you compare the cost of the two devices (wired vs wireless), the difference is worth it to have the versatility and freedom of movement.

title: Just what I needed! Better than I hoped! Worth the money!
text: I have one of the older Kindles and the only complaint that I have had over the years is that while traveling or at night, I can't read without some kind of light. Of course I have purchased various independent lights that either snap-on or attach to my old case, but this also means keeping up with two things (the Kindle and the light). So I finally asked myself "wouldn't it be easier to invest in one product that would offer both protection and light"? So I purchased this case and have not been disappointed! I'm glad I made the investment. For the cost of the case, you get: 1. A sleek, attractive case that not only looks smart but is extremely functional. This case is made from a leather (a durable material) on the outside, and is well padded (in a charcoal grey material) on the inside. It definitely appears to be well made (sturdy) and seriously protects the device. The device attaches to the case with two prongs that secure it in place. It is pretty easy to attach. The bottom of the case is open, so you can access the area for the charger easily. Thus, charging your Kindle while it is in the case. 2. The case (with the Kindle enclosed) is not heavy. You can comfortably fit in your purse, book bag; backpack or briefcase, and it won't weigh your bag down. 3. There is a built in expanding (rubberband) type cord that is attached to the case that will allow you to either keep the case open or closed (as desired). 4. The light conveniently rises out of the top right corner of the case. I will warn you that there were times when it seemed difficult to pull out. (Just be mindful that you don't force it, but instead pull the tab up by the indention provided.) However, once it is up, the built-in light does illuminate the screen (more than I ever thought it would) well. The light cuts on and off with the device, so there are no batteries. The light works off the charge of the Kindle, and you control when you use the light. (I also haven't found that the light drains the battery any quicker normal). The light gives just the right amount of illumination, and isn't so bright as that it will bother others sleeping in the same room. My husband always complained that when I would read at night, in bed, that the lamp (on my nightstand) was too bright and kept him from falling asleep. And when I used the traditional clip on book light when traveling in a car, he use to complain that my book light was too distracting. He actually doesn't seem to be distracted or bothered by this gem. Perhaps because it seems to be more defused or softer. In the end, I don't regret my purchase. I definitely got more than I had hoped and would definitely recommend this case. It is affordable and the benefits outweigh the cost. 5 stars!

title: Skiing to the top!
text: (This review was done by my 10-year-old son, Chad Beck who can't wait to become a reviewer. These are his words.) We Ski is a game with lots of challenges. When you ski you can do awesome tricks like the corkscrew,rodeo and back flips. When I first got the game, I thought "Man it's not boring" and when I started playing it, it was actually fun. I asked my brother, who is 7,what he'd rate We Ski? He said he would probably give it five stars! So I guess he agrees with me. To me We Ski is a game that you should really get!

title: Small, But well built!!!
text: This is a very good keyboard in a small package. Comes with a 4 ft USB-A to USB-C 90° Cable. Comes with 4 Mechanical switches to replace any damaged ones with. The tools to replace them also is in the box. Pros: Small form factor. 90° Cable helps tons. RGB is pretty good. Light weight. Good recoil on pressing the keys. Cons: Took awhile for my Windows 11 Computer to recognize it. Rubber grips on the bottom come of easily. (Fixable with hot glue or Superglue.) Not great for people with big hands or fat fingers. Overall a great keyboard for the cost. Love the sticker that came with it. Will play hours of games with this. Great job on the packaging and presentation. Worth it for a small keyboard!!

title: Awesome! Best Expansion Yet!
text: While it is true, many have had issues with the download versions of Generations, the problem has been solved, and when I downloaded my game, I had absolutely NO issues! To solve the issues, FIRST do the folowing: (as in BEFORE you download Generation, this makes the download smoother, but you can still get your game to work if you download first. You will just have to search for the download in your computer files to find the correct install file) * Delete all MODS and Custom Content you have downloaded. * Open your EA Download Manager and preform the update (it will prompt you, or it did for me) * Open up your Sims 3 game, and open the * Restart your computer. * Download/Install Generations. You may or may not need to restart your computer again. After these steps you're game should work perfectly! Mine did, and it really is worth the trouble! You get all kind of new items and interactions. I laughed when I saw the "be frisky" interaction pop up under the "Romantic" tab. You won't be disapointed, it's definitely the best Expansion they've relesed!

title: Great for Knee Rehab
text: I've been working out with my Wii Fit for a number of years, primarily the Wii Fit Plus and Nu You (sp) Yoga and Pilates. After knee surgery and going through physical therapy, I purchased My Fitness Coach to try out. When going through rehab, it's good because it doesn't rely on the Wii Balance Board and I knew I wouldn't be told how bad or weak I was. It also allowed me to modify activities that I couldn't do quite yet. I like Maya, the trainer. I like the variety of exercises that you can unlock. It provides a good cardio. Cons: there are too many physical challenges (required) to go through to "evaluate" your progress. It's too difficult to unlock additional venues and music (you have to meet their recommendations -- which doesn't work if you travel). She stops and asks you how you're feeling too often. And the rests are too frequent (but you can solve that by working out through the rest periods). I think it's a good addition to my in-home work out routine (and a nice break from the Wii Fit Plus's "snarkiness").

title: Good workout
text: I have the regular Wii fit and get annoyed with the stop and go on the Yoga and Strength Training workout. I decided to try this and it's a much better workout. You can even break out a sweat. I still don't like the stop and go, but they make you hold a pose longer. I think sometimes the calibration may be off, but as long as you don't mind your trainer telling you that you're not so good, and then the next time saying you're perfect, you'll be good. I need to try the customized class so I can get a longer workout, but the preprogrammed classes are a great way to start the morning.

title: Perfect Case even with a Console Guard
text: I knew I needed a bigger case for my Steam Deck as I bought a whole body protector for it. I was initially worried that this case would not fit the protected console but the dimensions and depth in the pictures convinced me. Glad I bought it!! Worked out perfectly. It has a deep storage area under the console for the cord, netted pockets for SD card, or whatever. This worked out better than the original case the Steam Deck came with. It would not even zip all the way up. Highly recommend. You won’t regret this case, especially if you placed a slip on console protector.

title: Underwhelming
text: For the price, I didn't expect these ear phones to feel as lightweight and plastic-y as they do. The wires are cheap feeling flat plastic wire, and the ear buds are metal. The ear buds are long and heavy and have to be placed securely in your ear or else they fall out easily bc of their length/weight. I swapped out the ear pieces for the smallest set. (Comes with one larger and one smaller inner ear piece set) The sound is great when used with a switch, but surprisingly subpar when used for watching videos or talking on the phone. I know these are marketed as gaming earphones, but for the price i expected them to be more well rounded. I'd say unless you really like the look/style of this pair or are into collecting items, you would probably do well finding better quality ear phones in the same price range.

title: So clicky!
text: So I'm not a gamer, I just use this as a regular keyboard. It's flat design took a bit to getting used to, but it's fine now. The lights are very cool and you can adjust them to the color you'd like or for them to constantly change. In the beginning it was a bit distracting but I forget about it now. I LOVE how clicky this keyboard is though. Feels and sounds great. The only issue I've had is that when I'd press the "t" key it would print t two or three times. I didn't know why it was doing that so I just disconnected it and then reconnected it and it's been fine since!

title: Very nice headset but some problems with PC
text: This headset is the best headset I've used to date. I used this exclusively for PC, and I moved to these from the Corsair Void Pro. These are much nicer quality, but it did have downsides. Sound - best sounding gaming headset that I've ever tried. It sounds super crisp and has plenty of bass. Mic - the recordings sounds pretty good for a headset, but nothing great. Fit & Feel - Fit is great, very comfortable. Feel is meh for a $300 headset, feels plasticy and adjusting the arms (which you have to shorten most of the way for it to fit into the charging dock) feels a little janky in the way that it moves slowly, but if i apply more pressure, then I might break the headset. Other notes: This is for XBox 1 and PC, but it feels like it was made more for the former, and merely is compatible with the latter. It has a volume toggle control on the side (as well as 4 other buttons, switches, and rollers) that is labelled "Game" on one side and "Voice" the other. I somehow triggered one of them that rendered me barely able to hear the audio even with my system maxxed, app volume at max, and even the headset volume roller (that for some reason does not control the system volume) at max. It made me wonder why I have 3 seperate volume controls, and then a 4th toggle that somehow also dramatically affects volume. It is because these were made with a console in mind (and it makes perfect sense for a console), but having that many additional buttons controlling just volume seems ridiculous when you have a mouse that can easily interact with volume sliders and a physical volume roller on my keyboard.

title: Above average gaming headset
text: The corsair virtuoso is a pretty good headset. I previously used my Void Pro SE, and draw most of my comparisons off that. I broke down my thoughts into few categories. Fit: The headset feels stiff and a little tight on the sides of my head. I prefer the fit of the void pro. I think I have a pretty medium sized head, and I felt a fair amount of clamping pressure on my ears. This also makes the headset feel lighter because there was less weight resting on the top of my head. I wish this were more adjustable because it's a little too tight. Sound: (tested in wired & wireless mode, and experienced similar results): Just to clarify, I am no audiophile and have not owned a high quality set of headphone, but the sound seems ordinary. I tried to give this a big sample of uses: thx intro video, streamed music, I still have some .wav files, and gamed a bit. The headset handled all of it, but in much the same way as my void pro. Mic: This was my favorite part of the headset. My experience with detachable my microphones has been less than stellar. Most of the time they look incredibly flimsy and generic. This mic matches the rest of the asthetics of the headset, and has sounded better and crisper than any mic I've tried. The mic is flexible, but I wish you could change the color of the mic LED. It is solid green when unmuted, and red when muted. Design, look, feel: very nice corsair style. Perforated side RGB is cool, ear pads are a nice cushy leathery feel. It feels like all the surfaced are metal, padding, or coated plastic to make it nice to touch. With the mic removed they look like a nice set of headphones. Other thoughts: I had some pains with the setup of these. They did not auto sync with corsair's icue software, and had a lot of crackling when used just with plug n play. I had to manually update the software and plug the headphones into the usb via cable. This fixed the sound issues, but the headset will sometimes not show up next to my other corsair devices in icue. This is frustrating, and I did not have these problems with my Void Pro. I feel like these are very nice for a normal gaming headset, but it doesn't seem to be worth more than $200. Hope this has been helpful:)

title: Can’t use a screen protector. No instructions whatsoever.
text: This is my first skin for my switch light, and it would’ve been nice to have some instructions or tips. Even a website to go to watch a video. But there was nothing like that. More importantly, it doesn’t work with a screen protector. There’s a picture in the reviews that shows a switch with a screen protector and the skin, and I thought that that would work on mine. But it doesn’t. I thought maybe I could take the screen protector off and put it on after I applied the skin. That didn’t work. The screen protector doesn’t stick to the vinyl, so all that’s holding it on is a spot of adhesive in the center of the screen which is the only part which touches due to the thickness of the skin. Which is really annoying to look at when you’re trying to use it. Not to mention, I damaged the screen protector when I pulled it off to put the skin on so now I’m going to have to pull the skin off and buy a new screen protector. :-( Finally, the cuts aren’t that great. The one strip up at the top (where there is a really thin edge of vinyl) stretched while I was trying to pull out the piece in the cut out which wasn’t fully cut. It’s a cute skin, but obviously I would never buy it again.

title: Lack of instructions is annoying. Should include positioning tape.
text: I got this to give to my mom for Christmas to go with her Nintendo switch light that I bought her as well. Thankfully I decided to put one on my own switch and then put a screen protector on hers rather than just give her the package. Because she’s never put a screen protector on anything and I know she would’ve had no idea how to do it. There are no instructions whatsoever in the box. Many times manufactures just stick a piece of paper in there with a link to a YouTube video to explain how to do it, but there wasn’t anything like that either. I’ve done screensavers on phones and iPads and digital cameras and stuff before so I know how to do it. but not everybody does. Missing from the package were the positioning tapes that most glass screen savers use to make it easier to apply the screen in the correct place. I used washi tape I had laying around. Also, they had a little sticker that said some thing about this being the back. I pulled that little tiny sticker off and the protective film on the back did not come off. I stuck the little sticker to the box to get it out of my way and then realized that you were intended to stick it on another portion of the protective film on the back of the screen protector and then it would stick and you could remove it. I do not understand why they did that that way and with no instructions, you were left to figure it out for yourself. The screen protector itself is nice. Once I got it on I had no bubbles, I don’t even know it’s there, it doesn’t seem to interfere with the touchscreen, and it seems to be good quality. But the lack of instructions and other issues make me unable to recommend it.

title: It was great fun until my town turned into a wasteland....
text: I got this game as a new to videogames player. I loved it. I thought it was cool that the snow seemed to be 'melting'. Then it snowed for two days straight, but I didn't get any more snow cover. I wondered why. So I found an online animal crossing community and learned the awful truth: playing the game destroys the look of your town! What??? Yep...all that wandering aimlessly lost I did in the beginning, racing around in hide-n-seek games, running to catch a present, and all the saves required by multiplayer gaming combined to turn my town into a virtual desert. I have probably made my last snowman. No snow also = no grass when summer comes as well. I am very sad. The grass/snow will regrow eventually, but it will take months if not years, and you can't walk on it AT ALL during the process. My other choice is to tear down my town and start over, reminding myself to walk around as little as possible and NEVER run. Not as much fun anymore. Or I can just resign myself to life in the desert. Animal Crosssing: Desert Dwellers. Yippee. Whatever, a lot of the lightheearted fun of it is gone for me now that I hesitate to walk in spots where there still IS some snow. I don't wander around looking for fossils or shaking trees, and hide-n-seek is out of the question. What is the purpose of planting and watering flowers and trees and pulling weeds if my town is still going to look like a dustbowl town when I'm done? Boo to Nintendo for not testing this "feature" fully before release and not fixing it when when it became a problem. I would not recommend buying this game until a patch becomes available.

title: I LOVE THIS GAME
text: This is the greatest RPG ever!!! Fantastic storyline, perfectly suited soundtrack, great character development, tons of class & item customizations and a robust fighting system. This game holds a high replay value due to the vast amount of class/weapon options available. I would say that this is my favorite game of all time!!! I've been a fan of Bioware since playing Jade Empire on the original Xbox (which was a great game also)!!! The only things that I think should have been added to improve the experience would be to add a fast travel option to get back to already visited areas and quicker load times. It was a steal at retail price...and anything less than $60, is unquestionably a value for this awesome game. I'm looking forward to Dragon Age 2 in March 2011. :D

title: A major hit!
text: Bought for my nephew's 10th birthday and the squeals of delight were so worth the rush delivery costs! (Though, next time I'll shop a little earlier!) Product arrived on time, wrapped and with my personalized message! I was very pleased! While I prefer that he divides his free time equally among other activities, it is nice to know that these Mario games are designed to teach as well as entertain. That in itself is a tough task because kids these days get bored FAST! Since he has so much to keep him occupied, he will be enjoying this game for a long time! The game even entertains his brother who is 1-1/2 years older. This game gift made me an instant favorite aunt! LOL!

title: PS4 game
text: This comes with a download of the game. You get a code to enter at the playstation store to download the game. It took about 3 hours to download on my ps4. Once it was done you have to go through the steps to set it up/calibrate it. The instructions say the camera has to be the same length from the tv as the size of the tv. I did this on a 40" so I measured 40" away, but ended up having to move it around when it needed to be calibrated. So you dont have to do what I did since it will have you calibrate it and ok it when it's at a good distance. It did take me about 2-3 minutes to calibrate. It seemed to lag as I moved the camera around to try to get the circle to match up with the one on the screen. Once you have it there, make sure you dont move it or your shots will be off. Also, the camera ended up being right in the middle of the tv so you would have to stand off to the side when youre playing the game. The game has different levels like sharks, etc., not just zombies. I think it's a fun game and something interactive, which is good for kids.

title: Bluetooth controller
text: There were no directions on how to start use/connect the item. However, I was able to figure it out because the booklet included just a labeling of the buttons and what those buttons are for. Most of the buttons are labeled on the controller so you know what they are, but some on the back and top of the controller are not so you have to look at the booklet to know. It resembles the design of an xbox controller. The controller does work well. I paired and used it with a galaxy s10+ with a GTA game and all the functions worked. You'd have to play it along with whicever game oyu choose to understand what buttons control what functions. Also, the clip is adjustable to the phone size and fit my phone well.

title: Headphones
text: I like these wireless headphones... the color is really pretty. I especially like the lights as well. However, I thought it would be some ombre or glowing effect with the lights, but instead, it is a ring around the earphone and it changes colors. But it still looks nice. The sound quality is good, they can get pretty loud...nothing deafening though. They are not the most comfortable headphones I've ever used, the cushioning isn't too soft. They do adjust easily as well. I've been using them for about an hours or so every other day and they still haven't died on me yet. Also, they were very easy to pair to my phone (I have a galaxy s9).

title: Android gaming controller
text: Pros: Easy to connect and use. I connected this through bluetooth with my samsung galaxy S9 and my Samsung chromebook plus (I did not have any of the devices listed for this item so I couldn't test the fit of the cases, but I was able to mount a case inside one of them for my phone and can play with the controller that way. But I mostly use it for gaming on my chromebook that is flippable, so it's like playing on a gaming system). The device was recognizable and instantly connected with no setup required. The app shows you all the games that are compatible with the item and lets you customize the buttons. The battery life is insanely long. My son has been playing with this thing for two days straight and it still has not died. It does not have a cheap feel to it. Cons: Does not come with it's own charger. Have to charge each side individually. The letters on the buttons are not easily readable, they are very skinny.

title: Charging system
text: This is a easy to use and convenient charging system for PS4 controllers. There's a piece that goes on the back of the controller, which plugs into the usb port. Once that's on, you can just set the conttroller (with that part attached) onto the charging system and it's good to go. And when you're ready to use it, and it's done charging, you just pick the controller up and play. I wasn't able to time how long it took to charge, but it's average. There is a light indicator on the bottom of the charging system to let you know that the power is on. Overall, I would recommend. It's easy to use, doesn't take up a lot of space, and charges the controllers with no problems.

title: This is my favorite mouse. V2 seems slightly nicer. Slightly
text: EDIT: After a couple of weeks, it has started not registering Left Mouse Clicks at least 20% of the time. Seeing how this is only 3 months old (used only for 6 weeks of that), I asked for a replacement. Razer support however is fighting me over installing the newest Firmware! So.... at some point, the initial Firmware, wouldn't support capturing LEFT MOUSE BUTTON CLICKS!!?? Initial/old 5 star review:----------------------------- To me, this is the best mouse in the market. Amazon accidentally sent me a Viper Ultimate last time, but for me and my large hands, this is far superior, even with two less buttons. Just perfect.

title: This mouse is SUPER light, but is too small for my hand, coming from DeathAdder
text: Though I saw reviews about it being too big, it's noticeably lower and smaller than the Razer Death Adder and feels like half its weight. It is nearly effortless to move it around, but it also feels not substantial, like it's made out of thin plastic (which I guess is exactly what it is). The left-hand side buttons are as you'd expect but are dramatically smaller than the DeathAdder and higher. The right-hand buttons seems just fine with me(I'm right-handed), I never accidentally click them. Though I can really only make use of one, can't feel which is which. You can define one button to be a "clutch/shift" allowing you to hold it down and have/program all the buttons do something different while it's held down. The wireless only works if you install the software. But it works beautifully as a wired mouse. The cable is nothing short of exquisite. All in all, most of my negative feelings is because I'm used to the bigger, heavier, with bigger side buttons, Death Adder. Already ordered the new V2 Death Adder.

title: -NOTHING- compares to Corsair macro programming options!!
text: I've tried Logitech, Razor, MS, and every other low and no brands out there. I've tried keyboards, mice, and keypads. Inboard hardware macros or program-ran ones. The Corsair Macro options are everything I dreamed of, and more. EAISLY created, EASILY edited, exact delays or random range of delay on EVERY SINGLE ITEM. AND on how random options on how far apart a macro should repeat. Speaking of repeat, you can have things run once, X number of times, or toggle continues. ALL with beautiful graphics interface that's not at all hard to figure out! I've not had to look up a single thing. Just freaking beautiful. Everyone else in the industry should follow Corsair and hire actual educated, disciplined, capable programmers. Oh my god what a breath of fresh air after years of utter garbage. That all said, while my partner likes this keyboard, I'm not a fan of where the G keys are. I keep pressing them instead of CTROL, Shift, Caps Lock, and Tab.

title: BEST programming software! But there is false advertising here.
text: EDIT: Changing my review to 2 out 5 instead of 5/5 because I feel there is false advertising here: You CANNOT program all the buttons. You EITHER get the 2 buttons on the left, OR the 2 on the right. NOT ALL FOUR. -------- INFINITELY better than Logitech and Razor's programming/macro software. EVERYTHING can be programmed, on either their mice or keyboards. So, yes, mouse movements and clicks recordings on either. Keyboard recordings on either. And EVERY step's delay/time can be randomized. You can play a macro once, X number of times, or infinitely till pressed again. The time between each iteration can also be randomized. When I say random, I mean between x and y seconds that you specify. I've bought and tested at least 20 different items from different companies over the last couple of decades and NOTHING compares to this. SO easy to record, edit, and program! Oh, and I have two this mouse AND my Razor connected to the same computer, on either side of my keyboard. This mouse's programmed buttons do not interfere with my other mouse. So I basically use this mouse as a gaming keyboard, clicking its buttons to run macros. Thank you Corsair for hiring actual designers and programmers instead of people with Underwater Basket Weaving degrees! And thank you to whoever those are! Such a pleasure when hardware and software does everything you actually would expect them to do, and then som.
