title: This is is really thin & FLAT, it goes from about 1/3" to 1" so not ergonomic.
text: The software is just garbage. No help, or even about, or link to the website, auto updater, nothing. You have no clue what version you are on or what's the latest. Macro recording does record mouse clicks but not movements. Though macro programming window doesn't stretch correctly as you can see words are cutoff, super Windows programming armature hour. Biggest programming issue: *There is no option to run something infinitely or toggle a loop on and off!* If the toggling option was present, I'd keep it and just have it on the side of my keyboard. It's way to flat on my desk and keys are way too loud to actually use, but I could at least automate some tasks. But not being able to just toggle a set of things to START running for a while then STOP it, that's a deal breaker. It's going back.

title: OMG I was sooo worried about not finding another SUPER thin pad. This is AWESOME!
text: I bought 3 of this other brand's mouse pads (stickers?) before they stopped selling them: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B01FU0AK54/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1 And had been looking for another super thin, sticker like pad. I'd use my desk (and did for years) but the surface slowly becomes too slick over time. As others have said, this is not as bright as pictured, not even as birght as customer pictures. Sitting on my black desk, black everything down to the carpet, the colors don't stand out or clash. Just lovely!!! Already bought a second one of these. Even though one of these is the size of two of the other pads. THANK YOU Razer!!!

title: Super comfortable, but microphone is horrible. Changing from 5 to 1
text: Bought both the wired and wireless. Happy with both purchases minus the following issues: On the wireless, the sounds is...acceptable, but not great. People say it's the transmitter, but since I don't have another transmitter, it's all I get. On the wired, the braided wire makes a surprisingly large amount of noise that you can hear as it brushes against anything, like your clothes. On phone calls, Zoom and Team calls, the wired is basically useless as people often can't hear me, or can't hear me for the first 10 seconds as the microphone adjust (I assume to noise cancellation). And when they can hear me, it's often broken up.

title: Six hours later, the DVDs are in the trash, and I'm downloading 27 gigs, into a directory I didn't elect
text: Trying to battle the retarded installer from the 80s, picking drive D, it created D:\Program Files (x86), create D:\Origin, created the folder that I ACTUALLY specified (though it put nothing in it), created shortcuts to nowhere on my desktop, etc. After easily 1.5 hours of basic installation off of 4 DVDs (hadn't done that in over a decade) and 3 more hours fighting the installer, then fighting the supremely low IQ Origin app, I have a dozen deleted directories in my Recycle Bin, and downloading 27 gigs from the internet. Oh did I mention it is still not where I would want it? The Installer and Origin application is not smart enough to be able to have things installed off of a main drive. You can't install it on, say, D:\Dragon Age. It HAS to be in a sub-sub directory. Oh and you can't change it's directory name. So mine is installing under D:\Dragon Age\Dragon Age Inquisition. You spend all this money making games, and ruin it by having art or history majors program your installer or your feeble attempt to create a Steam center lookalike.

title: Great sound, but major hardware and driver problems
text: I am generally a fan of logitech and have two of their other headphones but I'm having a lot of issues with this one. First the cable is too stiff and you can CONSTANTLY hear it in the headset scrapping against your shirt. You immediately become aware of just how much and how often your head moves. This noise is horribly loud and annoying. You can hear it even if the headset is not plugged into anything so this is a physical design issue. The headset seems to work all of 20-30 seconds when using Google Voice, which was the primary reason I got them. Then it just simply cuts out speaker and microphone, EVERY SINGLE TIME! Basically useless. It will however play music just fine. I even tried playing music, then starting a call. First it cut out the music, then the call, then a few seconds later the music cut back in. That's reliability. So I decided to download their drivers rather than relying on Windows 8.1 drivers. Their drivers made all sound on my laptop useless. Gone is the smart switch from the headset to the laptop speakers when I unplug the headset or the other way around. So is the builtin ability to have a default sound system for playing music and a default system for communications. Worst of all? The drivers stop the ability to open Sound from Control Panel. I rebooted, tried again, then went to uninstall their drivers/software. Surprise, the Sound settings popped up on its own as soon as the it was uninstalled. It was being held back by the software. HORRIBLE programming.

title: I bought 3 mice, including my two old ones, and this one won.
text: I got the E-3lue Cobra , this and Razer to replace my MS wireless mice at home and work. All amazing mice. 3lue's thumb buttons are too close to you/palm of your hand and hard to find. But for $11, that was great for work. Anker and this were very comparable. Both have great feel, quite, both have braided cloth cables, though this has a slightly softer thinner cable. As far as design & LEDs, and Anker was better. I like it's curve better and of course you can change the LED color to anything, and you can't change Razer's. The buttons on Anker blew me away. They are ALL comfortably reached and distinguishable with ease (and I'm not good at that). AND they are programmable with a simple downloaded app. That's not to say Razer's buttons aren't great, they really are, but you get the standard 5 buttons. There you can 3 programmable thumb buttons that are fantastic for figuring out which is which by feel, and 4 buttons for your middle finger. The software on the Anker also won. The Razer mouse software wants to log into their server every time you boot (or always stay connected as another option). As everyone else has said, WHY FORCE US TO CREATE AN ACCOUNT AND STAY CONNECTED?? Anker was going to be the winner in all fronts, including price for me, but alas I don't use a mouse-pad, I just put my mice on my desk with a wrist pad, and unlike the 3lue and Razer, the feet on the Anker would EVER so slightly stick to my desk. Never while in motion, but when trying to point at something precise, I'd end up a millimeter to the side, and trying to move back would mean the ever so slight jerk to get it from the ever so slight sticking to move, ending the cursor yet at the other side of where I wanted to point. So I'm going to keep the Razer as my gaming mouse... because its feet don't stick to my desk, it slides around quietly and effortlessly on my desk. So, if you have a mousepad, I'd recommend Anker instead. More buttons, better design, cheaper, no loggin in, great software, great LED colors, all around better mouse (though the Razer's cable is slightly nicer). Otherwise, get the Razer. If you don't have much money or don't care about the side buttons, then get the E-3lue Cobra Type-M EMS131BK High Precision Gaming Mouse Ps. The "programming" software you see everyone talking about is fairly useless. You can't program the buttons. What it allows is assigning a program to execute when a button is pressed, to assign different button numbers than the defaults or have a mouse button map to a keyboard (so pressing a button will press that key). But you can't create programs or scripts.

title: Fantastic Mouse, LOVE the buttons, very comfortable
text: I got the 3lue, this and Razer to replace my MS wireless mice at home and work. All amazing mice. 3lue's thumb buttons are too close to you/palm of your hand and hard to find. But for $11, that was great for work. Razer and this were very comparable. One thing I did not see in the add that should be mentioned is that this has a very nice cloth braided cord! Much like the Razer. As far as design, LEDs (can set it to any color, can't change it on Razer), feel of the mouse, this is the best mouse I've ever tried. The buttons blew me away. They are ALL comfortably reached and distinguishable with ease (and I'm not good at that). AND they are programmable with a simple downloaded app. This was going to be the winner in all fronts, including price for me, but alas I don't use a mouse-pad, I just put my mice on my desk with a wrist pad, and unlike the 3lue and Razer, the feet on this one would EVER so slightly stick to my desk. Never while in motion, but when trying to point at something precise, I'd end up a millimeter to the side, and trying to move back would mean the ever so slight jerk to get it from the ever so slight sticking to move, ending the cursor yet at the other side of where I wanted to point. So, if you have a mousepad, I'd recommend this instead. More buttons, better design, all around better mouse. Otherwise, get the Razer. If you dont' have much money or don't care about the side buttons, then get the E-3lue Cobra Type-M EMS131BK High Precision Gaming Mouse

title: Great alternative to Joy Cons - just without rumble.
text: These are a great substitute for the Nintendo Joy Cons. Especially considering how seemingly delicate they are. The drift on those is notorious and it ended up happening to me too so I was looking for a good replacement that wouldn't break the bank like a new pair of Joy Cons would, and be less of a risk. I could have also gotten them sent out and fixed for free, but I also wanted something more comfortable and akin to controllers I regularly use. The Hori Split Pad pretty much does these things. They're comfortable, sturdy, and work very well and as they're intended, without setting me short $80. For me personally, the only downsides to it is the fact that they don't support rumble features. Makes me wish they had a separate model that did and if it turned out to cost a bit more, I probably would've payed it. But hey. If you don't mind that or don't care, you should definitely go for these. I'm enjoying them and now I can actually take my Switch out with me again without having to bring my separate Pro controller.

title: So very glad to have this
text: I never leave home without a computer(s) of some form or another. When I got this I tossed it into a bag and left for a trip. HA! Covid 19 came along and I needed it. I LOVE that it's rechargeable. I just drop it on my qi charger and it charges very quickly. Since I'm "working from home" it's come in very handy and it's very responsive. I haven't had any trouble with it. It's smooth, fast and accurate. The battery seems to last a long time (usually about a week or more of constant use) and it's easy to fix if/when you run out of juice. Just plop it on a charging pad. No cords, no cables, nothing to get in the way. I could do without the lights but they don't bother me either so it's a winner.

title: Excellence Matters !
text: Un-put-down-able ! More on this later ;) Webb distills his experience and learning into two words "Excellence Matters". The book is inspiring as it show cases the mental toughness and training needed to succeed in the dangerous world of war. There are several books in this genre, but this one stands out for being an easy first person account read that even a non-military person can breeze through and go back to re-read the technical parts. Throughout the book, there is an emphasis on the training and instilling of qualities needed for success in any line of work- thoroughness , preparedness, alertness and constant practice. I started it this morning and was completely riveted with the re-telling of Webb's interesting life. Finished the book 8 hours later. Will go and check out "With Winning In Mind", recommended by Webb.

title: Gorgeous Palette- Works Best With Eye Shadow Base
text: I am a makeup artist. That means that I use all sorts of makeup from drugstore to high level professional. There are many things about eye shadow that I look for which determine if it is something I can recommend. HOW THIS COMES This came with no padding, no protection in a plastic mailer with no bubble cushioning. There is a plastic sheet over the surface of the eye shadow and no mirror in the case. There is no brush. COLORS The colors are beautiful. They have nuances that are very difficult to capture on camera. There are matte and shimmer colors- some of which are duochrome- something I look for in shadows. HOW TO USE THESE These eye shadows (like almost all other brands of shadow from professional down to drugstore) are best used with a very good eye primer. That will keep them in place and keep them intense too. The only eyeshadow I have ever come across which can be used without a primer and great success is Viseart. QUALITY These eye shadows are on a par with the high end cosmetics you find in the more expensive sections of makeup departments. They have a good amount of pigmentation and are velvety smooth too including the mattes. MATTES The mattes are not chalky, but are smooth and velvety. They show up well but again, these are best used with a primer. SHIMMERS These are some of the most gorgeous shimmer colors I have seen in a while. The collection compliments each other beautifully and look stunning on the eyes and even just in swatches. ANY ISSUES I have very sensitive eyes and these shadows did not cause any burning, watery eyes, or irritation of any kind the two days I wore them. THE BOTTOM LINE This set of eye shadows is gorgeous. For the price, it is excellent quality and is on a par with shadows much more expensive than these are. MY RATING I LOVE these shadows. The colors are gorgeous, quality excellent, and performance above most other shadows in this price range- just be sure to get a good eye shadow primer.

title: VERY Happy To Find These- Pinball Wears Out My Controllers Fast
text: It is difficult to find parts for Playstation 3 these days, so imagine my thrill when I found a dual set of these controllers. HOW THESE SYNC These sync perfectly when plugged into the base unit via USB cord. They work great. PERFORMANCE These perform just as well as the older controllers I have. The only issue I have is the center PS button which sticks sometimes if it is pressed too hard. The buttons and triggers all work about the same. I am not worried about really long term because this machine is old. I do love pinball, however, which wears the triggers out quickly. These help me enjoy pinball a little longer so far. CHARGE The charge lasts just as long (sometimes longer) than my SONY controllers. I have a charging stand which does two controllers at a time, so I use that. THE BOTTOM LINE This set of controllers syncs well, performs well, and holds the charge well too. MY RATING FIVE STARS. I am really glad I was able to get these. Now I can play pinball tournaments a little longer at my house. We all refuse to get any of the newer units because of the spyware and location in them. So, PS3 it is until it doesn't work anymore.

title: Works Like The SONY Version So Far
text: I am one of those people who still has a PS3 that is working. I really love to play certain games that were phased out of the newer sets so my whole family all stuck with their PS3 units. So far we have two left that are working. HOW IS THIS PACKAGED? This comes in a box with a cord, and pads for the joysticks. HOW TO USE Remember to hook up the controller using the enclosed cord which hooks into the PS3. Once it does, you turn it on and then it is synced with the PS3 and you are good to go. WHY I WANTED THIS I play a lot of pinball. Sometimes the 2 trigger breaks down quickly and it is hard to repair. I have quite a few controllers I have gone through but only a couple still work well. I wanted to be able to have them charging up on my charger while this one can be used with the PS3. DOES IT WORK? This seems to work just as well as the original controllers so far. I am happy with it. No lag, no issues yet. BATTERY LIFE Seems a little less life than the others, but not much. THE BOTTOM LINE This seems to work as well as the original controller for PS3 that I have used for the games I want it for. Just remember to set it up with the cord before you try to use it. MY RATING FIVE STARS so far. Since PS3 is being phased out more and more, it helps to be able to get this controller and have it work so well.

title: My Headphone Fanatic VERY PICKY Kids Love These
text: I originally got these headphones with the thought that I could play my playstation with them. Unfortunately, I forgot that you can not use headphones with a PS3. So, my kids got to try these. Let's take a look. WHAT ARE THESE LIKE? These headphones are really nicely designed. My daughter said they are brilliantly designed. The top that goes on top of your head is very stretchy and the wire part about it is one position. MICROPHONE The microphone is not retractable, but folds out of place if you want it to. It lights up when it is in use, and when it is disabled, it is not lit. The mic is clear and very loud. It is easy to control. EARPHONE PADS The pads are very comfortable and cushioned well. We can wear these a while before they have to be taken off. It is quite comfortable to all of us who tried these on. They are not leather, so if you have sweaty ears, you might have to remove them for a bit now and then. CONTROLS The controls on the left ear are all in the back. They are difficult to control unless I take off the headset. However, one of the kids has no problem doing it with them on. I guess it depends but either way, it is not difficult. CORD The cord is only about 6ft long which means you can not sit very far away from your PC or gaming machine, unless you have an extension you can add to it, which I suggest you get prior to purchase. LIGHTS The lights on these are really cool. They are colorful and can be turned off if you want. If you have a keyboard or gaming pad that has lights on it, these will go well with them. SOUND QUALITY When used with PC games, the sound quality of these is really nice. The kids love the sound, nice base, vibration is decent, and the separation of the sounds is great. Even without the drivers installed, it worked really well. My kids are VERY critical and picky, so for them to rave about these is significant. DOES THIS WORK WITH PS3? If you have a lot of USB ports on your TV you might be able to use these with your PS3 through the TV but not use the mic as that has to be put in a different way. If not, then it won't work with the PS3 although you can use the mic, just not hear the sound effects through the headphones. THE BOTTOM LINE These headphones are excellent for PC gaming and if you can get them to work with PS3 or PS4. The sound separation is great, the 3D is nice and even without the drivers on the CDROM included, the headphones work well. MY RATING FIVE STARS. For the price, these have been a surprise for our family. The PC gaming is really nice with them, and if I can get my PS3 hooked up to a TV with USB ports, perhaps I can make it work for that in the future. For now, I am content to play PC games with these, if I can get them away from the kids, that is.

title: Fun Lighting, Works Well With Alienware Laptop
text: ALIEN MOUSE When you get a top of the line Alienware laptop, of COURSE you are going to want an Alienware mouse to go with it.. Let’s take a look at how this performs with the Alienware M17 R2 laptop. WHAT IS THE MOUSE LIKE? This is a very ultra light USB mouse with RGB enabled lights all over it. It can be programmed to coordinate with the Alienware laptop and in individual games via the Alien Command Center. CUSTOMIZABLE DPI You can customize the DPI on this through the alien command center. SCROLL WHEEL The scroll wheel has worked well for the internet and pages we need to use it for. It has been pretty accurate without any frustrations so far. BUTTONS Most of the buttons have a basic set up which you can find online, but you can program the buttons too. It takes some work to be able to program them as there is a bit of a learning curve on this mouse. We have had some issues with the Alien Command Center being complete for some things. This mouse is one of them. It could be from our original problems with the laptop and trying to re-download everything. PERFORMANCE The mouse is nice and robust. The textured raised pattern makes it really easy to move it back and forth without slipping. This performs like expected for gaming. There is no lagging in tracking and it will work on almost any surface. The basic programming we have done has worked so far. We have not done anything intense or complex with it yet. We just use it as a mouse that lights up. PAD FOR THUMB REST The pad for the thumb to rest gives you dependable grip and helps you keep track of your thumb while gaming so you are not pressing buttons. There are three buttons above the thumb rest. CORD This has a mesh covering on the cord which allows the cord to move and keeps it from catching on surfaces or tangling when you are winding or using it. THE BOTTOM LINE If you happen to have an Alienware laptop (in our experience the M17 R2) this mouse is a great companion. I has extra abilities to be programmed in sync with lights on the laptop as well as setting features through the Command center. The cord is tangle free and really nice to use. The mouse works very well so far on a number of surfaces. MY RATING FIVE STARS. This has more potential than we have learned yet. We have had to spend so much time trying to get the laptop straightened out after an initial period of frustration that we have not had as much time to explore all of the dimensions of the mouse. So far, it is really nice and it has worked well for what we have programmed it to do in games and other applications. UPDATE I will update this in the future if we discover any more to add to this review.

title: My Family Is SO Jealous.. BTW, Might Need Longer Cord
text: I know, it is silly. Having this HUGE mousepad which rests under my keyboard and that I can also use as a mousepad is really cool . I mean after all, it does light up. Let's take a look. WHAT IS THIS LIKE? I have to say, I was a bit confused when I first saw the photos of this. It looked like it has all of these fancy designs on the pad. In reality, it is just the edging that changes, that is all. It is still cool though. This fits across the entire slide out ledge for my keyboard and mouse. It is plenty large enough for both and then some room too. LIGHTS? The edge is what lights up. This either is a static color, a slow fading from one color to another, or a combination of two colors fading on each corner of the edging. It is fun to have and really does look cool when gaming or using the computer in a darkened room. It also has a low and high setting. The high setting supplies just enough light for a darkened room to help see a bit better. CORD The cord that comes with this was a bit too short for my set up. I have it on the slide out shelf which the keyboard rests on. The plug in for the mat is at the front edge, but it has to double back to the computer USB connection and not get in the way of the shelf sliding in an out. I had to get a longer cord for this as the cord that came with the unit was not quite long enough. PERFORMANCE? This performs very well as a mousepad both as gaming or every day use. THE BOTTOM LINE For a great addition to a keyboard/mouse area that covers the entire pull out shelf of a computer desk, this pad is fun to have. It is not hard to use, but I did need a longer cord to make it work for me. MY RATING Despite needing a longer cord, I am giving this five stars. I like it. It is fun to have and has worked well for quite a while. The color changing edges are really fun to have and add a great touch to my computer area.

title: Solid Headset For Computer Gaming, Adequate for Tablet and Phone, Make Sure To Download The Software
text: When it comes to headphones, my family is a bit obsessed. There are always plenty of opinions and preferences flying around our house, so when I had the chance to test these out, there was a grabbing contest and then we had a winner! Let's see how these rated with our headphone fan. WHAT ARE THESE HEADPHONES LIKE? A full set of headphones, these are meant to be full coverage. There is plenty of padding on the top of the headphones and in the ears as well. There is a wheel volume control on the left side. There is a flip down mic that flips up when you don't need it. There is also a button on the left side that turns the mic on and off. There is not any light indicator to show if they are on or off. The mic comes with a foam head that you can apply if you need to. There is a regular plug for a tablet but if you want to use it on the computer, the adaptor allows me to plug into the computer via USB. There is a dolby option for surround sound that seems to be only for the computer. If you want to use this with Xbox One, you need to purchase an adapter HOW DOES THIS PERFORM? I am going to break down what areas that this has performance in. GENERAL SOUND Just by itself on a tablet or phone, this is okay. It is not overly impressive, but still works well enough to be worth using. Later on in this review, we will explore the sound after the software engine was used on the computer. CORD The cord is a little over 6 ft long which is plenty long enough for comfortable moving around while listening. COMFORT These headphones are really comfortable. The cushioning is great and allows for many hours of use without any problems. The swivel of the ear pieces is fabulous. The set up is wonderful. These headphones excel in comfort and the way that the parts work as far as wear on the head goes and operation of the mic and such. The foam on the ears and top of head is cooler to wear than leather or synthetic leather as it breathes nicely. CONTROLS You can use volume on the headphones but also the base unit you are using it from. The controls are handy, so you don't have to be bound to use only the base controls from what unit you are using. The mic button is handy and much nicer than a wheel control. MIC Calls were heard fine and so far the mic seems to be good to use - people can hear well and it is clear. Used with voice activated systems it worked very well. When used with the foam cover it seems to block outside noise well. DOLBY It makes it sound like you are in a tin can. It just is not that great. DRIVERS The best performance from these headphones is using the Conair Utility Engine (CUE). That is only available through the computer use. It is really a nice separation of sounds, base is excellent, and the allowance for custom settings is great. This satisfied everyone and they really liked these better once this program was used. Gaming was greatly improved using this engine. It is great surround sound using computer games which is what this was designed to be used for. CONTRAST EXPERIMENT We tested out the same song recording on a phone, tablet, and then on the computer. The sound difference was worth mentioning. When listening on the tablet and phone, the sound was muffled and there was not a great separation of sound. It was adequate but nothing to write home about. When listening to the same song on the laptop using the Corsair Utility Engine it was like a very different set of headphones. COMMENTS Is this a jaw dropping set of headphones? No. Is it a great set of headphones to game with and enjoy when you want a decent set that is comfortable, but if you are very picky about your headphones and are fanatical about sound separation and definition (aka realism) this is probably not the headset for you. THE BOTTOM LINE This set of headphones is a good starting set of gaming headphones. VERY comfortable to wear for long periods, the mic on these is good and works clear enough to be heard and operate voice activated software well. Separation is best using computers with the Corsair Utility Engine, but is adequate for tablets and phones if you just want to hear music or something without anyone hearing you. These are not top of the line, but they are a hit with our daughter who uses them constantly for everything from phone and tablet, to gaming and voice activated lessons. MY RATING Despite them not being top of the line, our daughter really likes these. We all feel that they are one of the most comfortable headsets we have ever used and they serve us well for her basic needs. As for five stars, I would say four is more accurate. The rating is more like FOUR AND A HALF STARS

title: A Few Frustrations But Overall Great Gaming Experience So Far (And Some Things I Wish The Instructions Said)
text: My entire family is into gaming and other applications that use headphones and speakers, so I was very interested in try out the Siberia P800 series wireless gaming headphones. There are a lot of excellent highly technical reviews out there for these, but I intend to approach these headphones for someone who is not as into gritty tech details as they might be into practical every day applications. I am writing this review for those who really want to know about products prior to purchase. I am as detailed as I can be without being overly so, because I want to provide information that I would like to know before purchases. This is an expensive purchase, so it deserves some explanation and time given to research. WHAT COMES IN THE BOX? The box that these come in is excellent. It is sturdy and you can keep it for storage of the extra cords and parts if you like. Inside the headphones come carefully pressed into a molded insert. It comes with a wireless transmitter box, every cord you might possibly want to connect it to the Playstation, PC,or Xbox. It also comes with a mobile cable and analog cable for use with TV or mobile device. The startup guide is, well, let me say really not as good as it should be with an expensive set of headphones like this. For visual learners, you might have some issues unless you are a real techie. There are no pictures of the back of the transmitter box or of the back of the playstation (or other items) you want to connect to so if you are not really good at understanding what goes where, you might have to look up online somewhere how to hook this up to your console or other devices. WHAT ARE THE HEADPHONES LIKE? The headphones themselves have a cushioned top and small ear covers on them. The retract and get slightly bigger, but not a huge amount. The top is cushioned and they hold onto the had pretty well, at times feel a bit tight. That will loosen up over time, I am sure. The left ear pad has a retractable mic in it. When the mic is turned on, a red ring lights up. The disc on the outside of the left ear pad also twists off and that is there the lithium battery is put. When you want to replace, you quickly twist off the cover, replace the battery and you are good to go. There are two arrows that line up for you to replace the cover quickly so you don't have to fumble with it in a hurry to continue your game. The right ear side has the on off switch on it located just slightly toward the back of bottom of the circle. If the ear pad was a clock with 12 at the top and 6 at the bottom and 9 toward your front with these on, it is about at 5 o'clock. To turn it on, you press for about a minute or so. The switch will light up. If you want to turn on the mic, you tap the same switch once and the mic goes on. Tap again and it goes off. On the right ear side, there is also a control. It is a wheel which controls volume, but when pressing it, will change the menu on the transmitter box. Then if you move the wheel it will scroll the menu. The ear pads do fold flat which makes them a bit easier to store when not in use. I also find that the longer I use these, the more comfortable they seem to become- I imagine they will continue to loosen up over time. HOW DOES THE TRANSMITTER BOX WORK? I tested these headphones out on a PS3. I found very little on the internet about using these headphones with a PS3, so knowing that many still use the PS3, I wanted to test using that gaming console first. SET UP WITH PS3 Optical cable- plug in to optical out on PS3 in back then plug into optical in on the back of the transmitter box. USB- plug in mini USB side of the cable to the transmitter box and plug the regular USB side into the front of the PS3 POWER - this is optional. The power plug can be plugged in where it says DC but keep in mind that means the transmitter box will be on at all times. If you prefer that it turns off when your PS3 is off, then don't use it. The advantage of the power plug is if you want your battery to charge up when the unit is not on, you can have it plugged in for that. Once done, you can still remove the power plug until needed again. SIDE SLOT This package comes with an additional battery. One battery had a single bar of charge on it and the other had two bars of charge on it. So, while using on, the other is charging in the box. I found that with the power plugged in, it took about 45 minutes to reach a full charge or so. One battery took almost an hour. The battery pushes in and locks into place while charging, and then if you push on it again, it will dislodge and come out so you can use it and replace with the other one if you like. FRONT PANEL The front panel has a white light up design. It shows the battery charge, that the headphones are on and if you are using gaming and voice and the balance of the two. There is a dial on the right and a back button to the left of that. When turning on the headphones, I get a light that shows they are on then a quick large display of battery power left in them, and then it goes to the screen that shows me PS3 and how much volume is being used at that point. It will also show me the current battery charge of the battery that is charging on the side of the unit too so I can keep track of when it is ready to use should I need it. The menu is pretty simple to adjust. You press the button to change menu and turn the dial to run through it. There are presets for equalizer and you can also set custom. WHAT THE DON'T SAY IN THE INSTRUCTIONS Call me dumb if you want, but although I have programmed computers and done a lot of technical work, I guess I was having a dull moment when I set up these headphones. I could not get them to work. I went through every setting over and over again and just could not make them work right. Since I have never had headphones on my PS3, (I am the only one who hasn't) I did not realize that I had to change the settings in the sound menu. I should have, but I didn't remember. So, after much looking around, I finally found the setting that has to be changed. There is no mention of it at all in the instruction book. Since this review is geared more toward the casual gamer, I thought you might like to know that small important fact. You have to go into the PS3 settings menu for sound and pick either the optical sound or you can have both going if you like- through the TV AND headphones. I like to do that when the family wants to be in the room and see what is being played but I want to hear details of sound you normally don't catch on just the TV speakers. You just have to remember to change the settings when you change how you prefer to transmit the sound. HOW WELL DO THESE HEADPHONES PERFORM? I am going to have to really work with these for a while to find the ins and outs of them. My first impression of them was awful. I really was disappointed. There was hissing, crackling and all sorts of noise with sound effects on various games. The music seemed fine, but every time there was an explosion or some sort of noise that was supposed to be electronic in nature, the headphones had so much other noise in them it was distracting and annoying. I messed with volume and settings and everything and it just didn't get as good as I thought it should have. I kept on, however, changing to various games. As I moved through all sorts of different games, I realized that some games must be designed with engines that do not seem to transmit clearly over the wireless headphones. They just are awful. Then other games seemed to be clear and a lot easier to play. DOLBY So far, I have had the best results when removing Dolby on all of the games I have tried. I am not sure if that is because the headphones are designed for 7.1 and the PS3 is designed for 5.1, but it seems to be more muffled with the Dolby on and there are more annoying features that come up with sound effects. I will continue to play with this and see how to make it work if I can. I will update this review at that point. We have several different gaming consoles we can try these with, so over time I will elaborate if I find solutions or differences. The listing on these headphones does specify that it will work on both PS3 and PS4 so I plan to see what I can find out about this over time. MUSIC I have watched videos on these headphones and found them to be excellent. I can hear all sorts of nuances that I did not catch on just the TV speaker. I watched them via Netflix and also Bluray on the PS3. Sound was much better than some games. Like I said, however, it could just be the software used when developing some games that does not translate as well into the headphones as others. I do want to point out, that these are GAMING headphones. They are not going to be the top of the line for music listening, so if that is primarily what you want them for, they probably will not be what you want. For the variety of needs I have on the PS3 of videos to music in games and movies, they are surprisingly good. MICROPHONE I have not had the opportunity to test out the mic yet with other players. I will update as that opportunity presents itself and will comment on performance during gameplay. THE BOTTOM LINE So far I really like these headphones but have a few issues with them. Some games do not sound right in these at all, and others sound beautiful. That is not always the fault of the headphones, but it does make for annoying experiences in some games. The design of the headphones is nice and I do love how they work when they work well with games. The transmitter is easy to use and battery life seems a bit shorter than 20 hours, but I like the fact that you can keep a battery charging while playing so when you need to replace you can. I also like that you can opt to have the power on to them while the PS3 is off so you can recharge battery, but then unplug it so that it only turns on when the PS3 is on too. For the price, I have rated these four stars at this time. As I continue to use them and learn more about them and the ins and outs over time, I will update and amend my rating if need be. FUTURE UPDATES I plan to test these out with other games as well on my PC games as well as tablet in the future and will comment on those experiences as well. GAMES TESTED SO FAR (more coming soon) Monkey Island (newest one) Hydrophobia Zen Pinball Peggle Planet Minigolf Spellunker HD Beyond Two Souls

title: Not Super High End But Great For Most Applications
text: I have a family of headphone fanatics. My daughter listens to music or does her school work using headphones most of the time. What is very helpful is having a microphone built into the headphones for some of her work which requires responses such as Spanish. My son is a headphone enthusiast who goes into such depth about each set of headphones that my eyes tend to glaze over and I am not quite sure what he is talking about. It is THAT in depth. His favorite are Turtle Beach. All three of us have tested these headphones. I think they are great for music and gaming. I think they are pretty nice and I like using them. They cancel noise outside well too. My daughter loves them when doing her school assignments because they cancel outside noise and it is hard to get her attention when she is using them for work online on our PC. They are comfortable and she does not remember she has them on a lot of time. She loves the extendable microphone but she wishes it was just a half inch longer or so. She likes all of the different extensions that come with it. The cord seems to be a good length. The only other thing she was not keen on was the plastic quality. My son's major comment about them is that often companies will sacrifice the midrange sounds in an effort to get the higher highs and lower bass sounds and he said that seems to be the case with these. For what they are, however, the three of us agree it is a decent buy and pretty good for use in games, school programs, and listening to music as well. We don't have an iphone to test it on so I can not comment on that application of it.

title: Excellent Quality Cable for a Great Price
text: Because we like to try out electronic cables and devices for a while before drawing a conclusion, I have made sure to test out this cable for several months now. The verdict is in- this cable is a very high quality cable which works beautifully with no problems at all. Despite it being thick and a little tricky since you can not bend it at a sharp angle, it is easy to work with by looping a bit as the 6+ft of cable gives us plenty of room to do so, but I would advise you to check out any holes in furniture or other small areas that the cords might have to pass through to be sure you have enough room to pass this cable through if there is any question- BEFORE you install it. We have checked this cable with various devices- PS3, HDTV, Blu-Ray player and most recently it is being used from a high quality amplifier to a very high level audio-visual computer system. In all cases, the picture/sound has been top notch, with no disintegration of information flow or integrity of signal. The quality of this cable is definitely high and equals or surpasses the performance of cables that are much more expensive on the market but have brand names that people are more familiar with. We have a LOT of cables and cords in our house as we have an electronic addict in our home, so we have a lot of HDMI cables and devices to test and compare with. This cable is also a good choice for future equipment upgrading as it will be compatible. The frustration free packaging is brilliant, by the way. Makes life a LOT easier! I highly recommend this cable, as long as you are not required to make a sharp angle for installation with no extra cord to loop around, or as long as your cable does not have to pass through a very tiny space (as is often the case when you have multiple cables running through holes in furniture, or other small spaces.

title: The Most Fun Our Family Has Had in Years
text: I waited a long time to write this review. Why? Because I wanted to test this game out thoroughly. Also, I wanted to play it just one more time before writing my review. Buzz Jr allows you to play in multiplayer mode- up to four players. There are four buzz units which are connected at one point. Anyone can enter information that will be recognized by the game. We played this across the room- about 8 ft from the PS3 and had plenty of room to move around without feeling restricted by the controller cords. You can also play singler player. There are practice options so you can learn the games. You can also save and load games, align the screen, and there is a widescreen option. We played in widescreen mode. When you are ready to play you have the following options: marathon single player short game medium game long game We played the short and medium so far as we did not want to be locked into anything long- everyone wanted a chance to win. To play a game you have the choice of quick start, standard, and custom games. The nice part about custom games is that you can set up a list of games that you especially like and play them without having to suffer through games that you don't enjoy or that frustrate you. The list of games to choose from is this: Totem Poles Whack a Squirrel Wheel Running Balloon Battle Bridge Out Bubble Bath Card Counting Elephant Baseball Free Fall High Voltage Voting Island War Jungle Hurdles Keep It Up Leaping Lily Pads Lion Taming Monkey Bomb Monkey Bingo Monkey Catapault Monkey Slide Odd One Out Primate Penalties Rocket Riders Run Around Simian Shootout (not sure of that one- can not read my own writing!) Splat WHAT I LOVE ABOUT THIS GAME There is so much that I can write about this game in the positive mode- it would take pages. For the first point, it is there is color- LOTS AND LOTS OF BRIGHT CHEERFUL COLOR! That in itself makes the game enjoyable to play. We loved that you could personalize your monkey with crazy glasses, clothing, and feet, and the ability to name them is great too. The music is delightful and fun - very happy music but it does not get to you to hear it over and over like some games. The game controllers work beautifully. They are very responsive and everyone had chances to win games. The game is easy to use, and yet challenging enough for everyone that no one was bored. What I especially like about it is that the games were challenging without being insulting or off color in attitude. There were a couple of crude things that some people might object to such as gorilla flatulence underwater and a few things like that, but on the whole it was really fun. ONE THING I DID NOT LIKE I did not like voltage voting, however, I thought that was in bad taste- that was the only game I recall being so irritated with that I refuse to play it- voting will electrocute a gorilla I think it is and it just seemed sadistic even cruel- and although it is just a cartoon, the attitude behind it upset me and I don't think it is family oriented. FINAL COMMENTS However, the rest of the games- and I think we have played all of them- are really fun and entertaining. All of the games take different skills so each member of the family had a chance of winning. That made it fun to keep going back to try playing over and over. No one felt that they were not able to have a chance at winning. All in all this game is a huge winner- it gave the entire family a chance to play on Playstation without any concern for content and suitability for different family members. Playing this game has been one of the highlights of the last few months. Our son said it reminds him of Mario Party 3.

title: Very good lighting
text: The lights are cool. The stick-um works or doesn't work depending on what you're sticking it to. My case's interior is enameled, and it doesn't particularly stick very well to that. Of course, there's always the possibility of using your own adhesive. The lights are bright. I found I had to reposition them because the light hit my eyes directly. So now they are out of direct sight, yet still light up the interior of my case pretty well. I used a Sabertooth TUF motherboard, and a Corsair power supply that uses black cables. The motherboard has a plastic covering, so there's not actually much to see inside. When you're getting lights, keep in mind what it is that you're lighting up. These lights themselves are good, but I'm disappointed that my rig ends up being so monochromatic that the lighting is kind of pointless.

title: Collectable game, a "window in history"
text: This game is very dated, with chunky graphics, and in monochrome (no color). It's not an Xbox, or even a Wii, but it's fun to see the roots of the current hand-held games. Many old-timers like myself will enjoy the nostalgia of experiencing again what was state-of-the art not so many years ago now. And many others who regularly play the latest consoles or online games, with great graphics and high frame rates, can take pleasure in the much simpler (but still very challenging) Game Boy. If you're expecting to have some retro fun, you'll have a good time with this. I'm one of those guys -- heck, I still like Tetris.

title: Stopped working after 3 days of use.
text: I ordered the 'G-STORY Cooling Fan for Xbox Series X' for review and would like to share my experience. I thought this would be a great idea to help cool my new Series X and my first impressions were that this should be a great product. However, after only 3 days it stopped working. It would not let me switch to manual so that I could adjust the fan to run at high speed for my gaming session. When it did work, the fan was loud no matter which speed it ran at. This wasn't necessarily a bad thing as I usually wear headphones while gaming but it is worth mentioning. The fan does fit perfectly and the USB connected cord is the perfect length to reach top back USB port of the Series X. It actually looked good too and I would have kept using it but unfortunately it no longer allows me to switch it to manual. Another thing I did not like was that it doesn't seem to allow you to switch between Celsius or Fahrenheit. It only shows Celsius. This was not a deal breaker but it was a little annoying. Overall, had it not stopped working, I would have rated it at least a 3 star and possibly a 4 but as it stands currently (not working) it's a solid 1star.

title: Great build quality!
text: I ordered the ‘Logitech G915 TKL Tenkeyless Lightspeed Wireless RGB Mechanical Gaming Keyboard, Low Profile Switch Options, LIGHTSYNC RGB, Advanced Wireless and Bluetooth Support - Clicky, Black’ for review and would like to share some of my “unprofessional” thoughts. I have been using the Logitech G815 wired keyboard for several years now and I absolutely love it. It has actually been my all time favorite keyboard and I have used many different brands throughout the years. The G815 is basically the same style/construction as the G915 TKL except that the G815 is wired and has the ten key pad. The G915 TKL (Clicky) is very well constructed and flex is minimal due to the solidly built metal frame. Because it is the TKL version it is considerably smaller and fits well on the pull-out drawer of my computer desk and it gives me the freedom of being able to easily pull it out from the pull-out drawer and place it either in my lap or on top of the desk. I also like the idea that I can use it with my smart TV. I love the media controls on the G815 and was very happy to see that even though the TKL version is smaller, they still included the media controls on the G915 TKL. If they would have removed those, I may not have been as fond of the TKL version. I also love the fact that the G915 TKL has two different angle settings which are nice and sturdy. The battery life is actually pretty amazing especially if you turn off the lighting but I tend to keep the lighting on and even then battery life is impressive. Personally I am not all that savvy with keyboard switches and the different benefits so I can not give any specific details as to how well the switches work other than I love the feel of the shorter throw compared to other keyboards I have used in the past. The “Clicky” keys are not as loud as other switches on other branded keyboards that I have used and I feel like I prefer the “clicky” keys vs the “Tactile” or “Linear”. This may be due to my love of the G815 that I have been using for a while which also uses the “Clicky” switches. To me the other two feel mushy. Overall I love this version and feel like Logitech has continued to make great products throughout the years and it is a brand that I trust! Personally I feel that the G915 TKL is a bit on the pricey side but you really are getting a solid and well made keyboard that should last a good long time if taken care of. *On a side note - I am having some issues with the Logitech G Hub software which I had to uninstall, as it was not working properly and now I can’t get it to install. I would dock stars for this but I think it has to do with my current PC which is not aging very well. When the software was originally installed it worked fine so I am hoping with some effort, I will be able to get it installed again at some point.

title: Absolutely love this controller but....
text: This is my all time favorite Xbox controller. I can't go back to the regular controllers because of the extra bottom buttons. The weight is perfect but I am not a huge fan of the materials used for the grip. It's a rubber type feel which you would think it would have more of a grip but it is not, its a bit slippery. Although I absolutely love this controller for the most part, I am starting to have the thumb controller drift. For the price this controller should NOT be already failing which is why I am giving the 3 star rating. I don't think it's still under warranty which is unfortunate.

title: Great product!
text: I ordered the "Razer DeathAdder V2 Gaming Mouse: 20K DPI Optical Sensor - Fastest Gaming Mouse Switch - Chroma RGB Lighting - 8 Programmable Buttons - Rubberized Side Grips - Classic Black" for review and would like to share my thoughts. I have been a long time fan of Razer products and have used many of their different gaming mice and this V2 of the DeathAdder has not disappointed. It is very responsive, it fits well in my right hand, and the build quality is as expected for a Razer product. I have not had any issues thus far and though I am not very "technical" when it comes to DPI performance, I must say that I am quite satisfied overall with the DeathAdder V2.

title: Sound great but issue with random static/lag
text: I ordered the 'Corsair Gaming VOID RGB Elite Wireless Premium Gaming Headset with 7.1 Surround Sound, White' for review. First I would like to mention that I had originally ordered these in White. The box I received was tagged as white however it was mis-tagged and the headphones are black. This was not a huge deal to me but you may want to make sure you get the color you order before you open the box. I have had these for a while now and I must say that I am a Corsair fan but these are just a bit of a disappointment actually. The build quality is great, the sound is pretty good but the issue for me is the random static or lag that these have with my fresh install of Windows 10 Pro. I don't own a PS4 to test them on unfortunately so this review is entirely based on how they have performed on my PC. They do connect super fast and effortlessly to my system, they feel comfortable but they are a bit on the large side for my head. The feel just a tad bit loose. I think the static or lag issue may be due to that these run off of the 2.4ghz bandwidth and I am using them in the same room as my wireless router which may be the issue but even so they should (in my opinion) be flawless in this situation. I can't say that I don't like these, but I can say that they are not my favorite. The RGB lights on the side are pretty cool but my guess is that they can and will drain the battery faster. As for the sound quality, they really hit the Bass, Mids and Highs spot on. The battery life is actually great for Wireless gaming headphones and they seem to charge fairly fast although I have not completely drained the battery yet. As for the charging, I do have to point out that they charge via Micro USB which is another disappointment. It's 2020 Corsair and USB C should be the standard in my opinion. Overall I do like this headset, but it will be more of a backup to others that I have that I think are much better for the price. I hope that this was helpful.

title: So far so good!
text: I ordered the 'Sliq Gaming Xbox One Controller Charger Station and Quad Battery Pack Edition - Includes 4 Rechargeable Batteries - for Xbox One/One X/One S/Elite - Black' for review and would like to share my thoughts. I ordered this charging station and batteries for my son who was having issues with another kit similar to this one where the batteries were not holding a charge for very long any more. So far this kit has performed quite well and the batteries seem to hold up much longer than the original batteries and even more so than the batteries from the the other kit he was using. The batteries are a perfect fit and the charger itself works well although sometimes you need to give the controller a bit of a jiggle once in the charger slot to get the charge going. This seems to be typical for charging stations of this type as I have the same issue with another brand that I personally use. Overall I think that the value in this kit is well worth it and the fact that you get 4 batteries makes it even more of a value.

title: My new favorite mouse!
text: I ordered the 'Razer Basilisk v2 Wired Gaming Mouse: 20K DPI Optical Sensor - Fastest Gaming Mouse Switch - Chroma RGB Lighting - 11 Programmable Buttons - Classic Black' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts. I have tried several gaming mice over the years and though I am not so much into gaming as I once was, I still love a good gaming mouse. This Razer Basilisk v2 has become my new favorite "wired" mouse to date. I use it mainly for PC use as well as video and photo editing, and it has performed flawlessly. It is also has a nice grip to it which really ads to the comfort and control. I also love the included optional thumb button that magnetically snaps into place and can be macro'd to commonly used Photo and video editing keys. The mouse glides smoothly across any surface and all the buttons are nice and clicky. Razer makes a great mouse and they are always innovating and creating better and better peripherals. Overall this really has become my favorite mouse to use, and I have to say that for a wired mouse, it is the most comfortable and reliable. I hope that this was helpful.

title: Sound, comfort and quality are absolutely amazing.
text: I ordered the 'Plantronics RIG 800LX wireless gaming headset - Xbox One' for review and would like to share my thoughts. So far I am loving this headset and it has performed quite well for me. The comfort is one of the best that I have tried so far and the sound quality has exceeded my expectations. The only issue I have had is that when using them with my X-Box One, is that every once in a while they will cut out, but I am not sure if that is the fault of the headset, rather my set up or possibly the radio interference in my home at the moment. title: There is value to this kit however .....
text: I ordered 'RGEEK Elite Kit for Xbox One Elite Controller Accessory (6 Different Metal Analog Sticks, 4 Paddles and 2 D-Pads, 2 Magnetic Base, T8 T6 Torx ScrewdriverRepair Kits Parts' for review and would like to share my thoughts. I was really excited for this kit however after inspecting it once it arrived, I found that to use the thumbstick adapters, it appears that you will need to disassemble the controller to install them as they wont fit over the original base. You will also need to disassemble the controller to use the D-Pad replacement base. The replacement D-Pad cover itself does fit without dissembling the controller however. The replacement paddles fit fine however they are a little mushy compared to the original paddles (not as clicky). Now with all that said, I do find value to this kit in the sense that if you need these parts to repair your controller, you will have what you need to repair and replace parts. It is not a kit that you will be able to use easily to replace a lost or damaged thumbstick as they will require you to disassemble the controller to install the included replacement base first. The two D-Pad covers (the round and the +) can easily be swapped out but the D-Pad base replacement part will also require the controller to be disassembled. With all that said, I honestly did not expect any of this when ordering this kit. I figured it would be just as easy as snapping all the the included parts into place. Again, I do see a value to this kit if you absolutely need to repair or replace original controller parts as the kit is pretty complete with tools and replacement parts to get the job done in a pinch. I do like the padded case that keeps the kit together and protected. It looks nice and compliments the original Elite case but for me will most likely be set aside in a drawer for emergency purposes only. I hope that this was helpful.

title: Currently my favorite!
text: [[VIDEOID:15c368008dd4839790dca1b2e254fb9a]] I ordered the 'HyperX Pulsefire Raid - Gaming Mouse - 11 Programmable Buttons, RGB, Ergonomic Design, Comfortable Side Grips, Software-Controlled Customization' for review. title: Saves my AA stash.
text: I ordered the 'Xbox One X Slim Controller Charger, GYORGKSHI Dual Console Charging Dock Station Stand with 2 x 800mAh Rechargeable Battery Packs for Xbox One X Slim Elite Controllers' for review and because my daughter was eating up my AA stash. title: Looks awesome!
text: I ordered the 'Tilted Nation RGB Headset Stand and Gaming Headphone Display with Mouse Bungee Cord Holder with USB 3.0 HUB for Wired or Wireless Headsets for Xbox, PS4, PC' for review and would like to share my thoughts. I have been wanting a headphone stand for my wireless gaming headphones for some time but I have not found one that I really like. This Tilted Nation stand has everything that I was looking for. It's sturdy and looks really nice on my desk. The RGB lighting is pretty sweet and the color options are nice and work well, although I have had one time where the lights shut off and I had to unplug the device then plug it bag in to get the lighting back on. I am not sure what happened but since then it has worked fine. I love the fact that I can also use the base to plug in a couple other USB 3.0 devices such as my RGB mouse-pad and even an SD card reader.
