title: Looks nice but has a few quirks......
text: [[VIDEOID:5fb4b847c95831afd3178dd8722131d]] I ordered the ‘MOJO Wireless Charger Mousepad - Qi Quick Charging Gaming Mouse Pad with RGB Lighting’ for review and would like to share my thoughts. First off out of the box this looks and feels great however I wasn't sure about the the top surface material. I am more used to the feel of a fabric top that is padded. I am not sure how they could have used this type of material with the wireless charger so I understand the material choice, but I really am not sold on the overall design. There are small very thin rubber pads on the bottom of the pad that are supposed to keep the pad in place, however even on a flat glass table top, it does not grip enough and tends to move around while using the mousepad. I have attached a bit of video that demonstrates this a bit as well as the wireless charging. Speaking of wireless charging, it does work but it does take some getting used to where your mobile device needs to be placed. When you find that sweet-spot, it does work but it does not Fast Charge unfortunately. This may be due to my 5 year old computer and my USB 3.0 ports may not provide the power to do so. There is also a fingerprint touch button at the top middle of the pad where you can touch to change the color options and this is fun to play with however I have noticed that while playing, the button is easily “accidentally” touched, which messes up your color choice. It’s not a big deal but it does get annoying if you have a certain option that you like and need to press through the options to find the one you prefer. Overall my thoughts are that this is a pretty nice mousepad and does have value however it’s not my favorite design. I do appreciate the wireless charging capability and it makes for a convenient way to keep your phone close while gaming and have it charge.

title: A little laggy but overall fun and easy to set up.
text: I ordered the 'PDP Xbox One MARS Starter Pack - Voyage of the Dead, 048-132-NA' for review. I was curious about this latest take on the arcade style lightgun and I feel that MARS has done a great job at their design however there is one thing I'd like to see improved. Before I explain that, I'd like to share my overall thoughts. First I would like to state that I had absolutely zero issues with setting this up on my Xbox One S. I was leary because so many others had issues with calibrating the camera. I set mine up in a mid sized living room about 8 feet from our old 55 inch plasma TV and for me, the set up and calibration was a breeze. There are many different games you can play besides the main Voyage of the Dead game. It totally reminds me of the old Duck Hunt from back in my day. All of the games are fun to play but I do wish it would have come with two guns. It would have been a more "complete" kit in my opinion. With all that said, the real issue I noticed is that although the gun is quite accurate, there is a bit of lag. This tends to get a bit annoying but it just takes some getting used to. I would hope that eventually this could be improved. Other than that, I think MARS has done a great job on this product and I look forward to more from them in future games.

title: Nice build quality but pretty plain and simple design.
text: I ordered the 'Kain 200 Aimo RGB Gaming Mouse - Black' because I am a sucker to try any new gaming mouse. This Roccat Kain 200 is definitely a great build quality and I do love the wireless connection and have had zero issues with that. I love the little included cable adapter which allows you to plug into the back of your PC with the included cable, then bring it closer near the mouse, then plug the wireless USB adapter into the cable adapter (see attached images). The mouse is nice and performs well and I actually like the button that allows you to (on the fly) adjust the DPI. Most of the others out there you can adjust the DPI, but you are required to open the associated app and find the setting from within there to make the adjustments. The scroll wheel on the Kain 200 is a little on the tight side but with that said, it does make it less likely that you will scroll to quickly as others on the market tend to do. The scroll wheel also has a nice rubber feel with that satisfying sort of smooth clickyness. It just feels good. Again, build quality on this guy is great but the overall look and feel is just sort of plain to me. Some might like this but for me personally, I like a more ergonomically designed mouse. Plus I like more grip. The design of the Kain 200 has a smooth finish and not much grip. Overall I do believe there is a market for this mouse and many people will love the simple design but for me, I will be moving back to my favorite gaming mouse.

title: Nice build quality but not my favorite.
text: I ordered the 'Alienware Mechanical Gaming Keyboard AW310K: Cherry MX Red Switches - Nkro - Per-Key White LED - USB Passthrough & Media Control - 5 Onboard Profiles' for review and would like to share my thoughts. I love the Alienware brand and had high hopes for this keyboard and though I am a big RGB fan, I felt that I would still give this (white only lighting) one a go. My first impressions were that this was a really nice built keyboard but after playing with it a bit I found that I do not particularly like the feel of the keys. They are not really clicky (but loud), and the keys seem to have a fairly long thrown to them. They are quite sensitive, but to me they feel like you really need to press them all the way to ensure that they are being registered. It's not the case, as it doesn't take much pressure but it just feels like you need to press hard because of the long throw they seem to have. Another thing that I don't really like is the media control buttons. Personally I prefer a dial or knob rather than buttons for this feature. Overall I am happy with the build quality but I feel that for what you get, it is retailed a bit steep. Don't get me wrong, it's a nice keyboard and again very well built bu there are others in this price range that I personally would prefer.

title: Buttery smooth "clicky" keys!!
text: I ordered the ‘Logitech G815 RGB Mechanical Gaming Keyboard (Clicky)’ to review, and because I have been a long time Logitech fan, but never have owned a keyboard made by them. My first impression when I opened this G815 was that it screamed Quality and it's absolutely gorgeous! It's solid and heavy for a keyboard of this size and I couldn't wait to get it hooked up and install the Logitech G Hub software. I am not so much into PC gaming as I once was, so I won't be able to really put this "Gaming Keyboard" through its paces in that sense, but I will tell you this, I absolutely LOVE the ever so smooth "clicky" mechanical keys. They aren't as loud and annoying as other keyboards I have owned. The keys are (IMO) perfect. Clicky yet not loud and they are very responsive. Not only that, but there is very little throw to them. I would almost go as far to say that they are a "buttery smooth clicky", if there is a such thing. Seriously though, the G815 has now bumped my other favorite keyboard off my desk, and it has now become my favorite keyboard of all time. I also love the lower profile and the RGB lighting effects are super cool and it's been fun customizing them via the G Hub software but honestly I just stick with the default presets and animations. I mean you can really go to town on customization if you want, and it can be a bit overwhelming. Oh, and I almost forgot to mention that the volume control and buttons for your media is very nice too. The wide volume roller bar is pretty sensitive, but the placement is easily accessible, yet not so much that you will accidentally bump it during normal use. Overall, I think if you are looking for a solid quality keyboard at a great value, you should most definitely check this one out!

title: Not compatible with the Xbox One Astro Command Center App.
text: I ordered the 'ASTRO Gaming A20 Wireless Headset, Black/Green - Xbox One' to use as my main X-Box One gaming headset and because Astro is such a great brand. Now that I have had plenty of time to use and play with the headset I am ready to share my thoughts. Pros: 1 - This headset sounds great for gaming and for music both on Xbox One and PC. They are nice and clear and quite satisfying. 2 - I find that even after a few hours of wearing they are still comfortable and do not irritate my ears, nor my bald head which is impressive, as I have tried others that tend to either cause my ears to feel as if they are being squished and or irritate the top of my head. This set is nicely padded both with the ear cups and headband. 3 - The Mic performs better than most and I find that compared to others that I have tried and tested, the Mic performance is probably the top of my list out of all that I own. 4 - I have had zero issues with this headset connecting and pairing up (quickly) with the control module, both when connected to the Xbox One or PC. Cons: 1 - Seeing as this was going to be my main Xbox One gaming headset, I was extremely disappointed that it would not connect to the Xbox One Astro Command Center App. I tried several things and eventually contacted Astro Customer Support. They were quick to respond stating that the A20’s were not compatible with the Xbox One Astro Command Center (ACC) and could not tell me why. They stated that even if they knew why, that they probably wouldn’t be able to tell me. This is my main gripe and why I docked one star. I mean, it makes Zero sense to me that if the A20’s are made and designed for the Xbox One and PC then why should I also need a PC to connect to the ACC to make adjustments to the EQ settings and update firmware. Fortunately, I do have a PC and was able to do this, but for those that don’t, good luck. 2 - The placement of the volume control makes it so that if you are wearing a hoodie, and because the volume control is easily adjustable, it can easily be adjusted just by moving your head. Now with that said, it’s not a huge deal because fortunately it adjusts in very small increments but it is still a bit annoying. Also the A20’s don’t remember the last volume setting and every time you turn them on you need to adjust the volume, which for me means rotating the control up several times to get max volume. 3- I wish that the Mic was removable. Now this isn’t huge as it is nice to just be able to rotate the Mic down and it’s on, and rotate is back up and it’s muted but it would be nice to be able to remove it if you wanted. 4 - lastly I don’t like the overall look of this headset. I was concerned that because of the “square” boxiness look, that it wouldn’t fit right but as I stated in the Pro’s, this set is perfectly comfortable and because of that, I will give them kudos - but they do look a bit funky compared to other brands and styles out there. Overall and even with the listed Cons, I love this headset and think that Astro has produced a fantastic headset at a great value for the money but again, it makes no sense that it doesn’t work with the Xbox One ACC App.

title: Volume control design is probably my favorite feature!
text: I ordered the ‘HyperX Cloud Stinger Wireless Gaming Headset with Long Lasting Battery Up to 17 Hours of Use, Immersive in-Game Audio, Noise Cancelling Microphone, Comfortable Memory Foam, and Designed for PC’ to use mostly for video editing and listening to music on PC. I would like to share my thoughts after quite some time using these headphones thus far, but first I would like to say that I am a big fan of HyperX and the quality products they produce. Cons: Comfort - My initial impression was how light these headphones are and expected them to be extremely comfortable, however after about an hour into wearing them I noticed that the head padding just doesn't work for me. I have a bald head and find that many headphones just don’t have either the right amount of padding, or use a “not so comfortable” material. I much prefer my wired HyperX headphones for comfort. Sound - Although the sound quality is good, I expected it to be much better. For me there just isn’t enough Bass nor Volume to these Cloud Stingers. Don’t get me wrong here. The sound is nice, clear and not muddy but I really think that my wired HyperX cloud headphones sound much better. Frame - The Steel Slider frame is nice and light however the slider is a bit loose and tends to adjust too easily which gets annoying when you find just the right fit (btw they fit big in my opinion). Pros: Swivel Earcups - I absolutely love the Swivel Earcups which make it easy to turn the earcup away from your ear so that you can listen to someone talking to you in the same room without having the headphones slide off you head. I wish my other headphones had this feature. Sound - I may have expected better sound quality however as I stated in the cons, but they do actually sound good and are very clear. Earcup Padding - I have no issues at all with the comfort of the Earcups nor padding. In fact they are very comfortable, just as my other HyperX headphones. Wireless Connection - The 2.4Ghz Wireless Connection has exceeded my expectations and works much better than Bluetooth in my opinion. I can walk into the next room without any loss in sound quality or losing connection. Battery Life - I have not fully tested how long the battery “actually” lasts but it does last a long time. I don’t charge them after every use but I will say that I have used them for hours at a time, then turned them off and came back days later to find them still capable of several more hours of use with zero issues. Volume Control - Though the Cloud Stingers don’t have the volume level that I expected, I do like that the volume control is nice in the sense that you can “fine tune” the volume level. By that I mean, as you slide the volume control it doesn’t jump up or down super fast as most do. As you rotate the volume control, it’s very gradual. The control doesn’t stop either way you rotate it. To adjust the volume you need to rotate it several times to go all the way up or down and the tension is absolutely perfect. This makes it nice so that if it slightly gets bumped by just putting the headphones on or taking them off (or rubbing against your hoodie) you’re not going to suddenly change the volume by much at all. I appreciate this feature probably most of all! Other Thoughts - The Swivel Mic does seem to work well the few times I have actually used it however I kind of wish that it was removable. The USB Dongle is nice and small however I have to admit that I have lost it a few times. I have recently however found a solution to this problem by placing the Dongle flat inside the earcup and twisting it slightly to fit snug and secure (see attached images) Overall I am a fan of HyperX products and do feel there is definitely value to the Cloud Stingers and I do plan to continue to use them for video editing. However, I think there are better “wireless” headphone options for gaming and listening to music, but you will spend considerably more for those options.

title: Solid gaming mouse!
text: [[VIDEOID:5f4afe2ac85800e8e30c919d83ea9432]] I ordered the Lenovo Legion M500 RGB Gaming Mouse, Up to 16000 DPI 50G 400Ips, 7 Programmable Buttons, 3 Zone 16.8Milion Colors RGB, 10G Optional Magnet Weight, 3 Onboard Profile, 50 Million L/R Button Durability to use with my gaming laptop. I have never used anything by Lenovo before and I was surprised to see that they made Gaming Mice. I knew that they made laptops but not other peripherals. With that said I am quite pleased with the M500 RGB Gaming Mouse and I would say that it compares to other high end gaming mice on the current market. The weight, shape and feel of this mouse fits my hand perfectly and is very comfortable to use and control. The RGB lighting is amazing and the Lenovo Legion App makes it so easy to configure not only the lighting, but for fine tuning and setting up profiles for the mouse. I have been using the M500 now for a few weeks and I absolutely love it. There are a lot of Gaming mice on the market right now and I have used a few different brands, some well known and others not so, but this one has definitely made an impression and will be my go-to Laptop Gaming mouse for quite a while.

title: Great sound for the price.
text: The sound quality from these Razer Kraken Gaming Headset 2019 - [Green] Headphones is pretty good actually. I'm not only impressed by that, but the material quality of these is quite impressive as well and the foam ear pads (and head cushion) are very comfortable. I love the soft braided cable and that it's not stiff like many others out there. The mic does very well (but needs to be fully extended) and I never had any complaints from any friends while chatting via X-Box games. The only issue I felt there was with the headphones was that they didn't fit as snug as I prefer, which made them lack on sound isolation.

title: Precision is spot on!
text: [[VIDEOID:18ba20ed40be8cc07d6211425f7b00de]] Right out of the I didn't have to make any adjustments for what I am mainly going to use this mouse for. I used to game pretty hard core back in the day and my favorite mouse back then was one of the higher end Razer mice which was a bit bigger and more involved to use. This new Razer Basilisk Essential Gaming Mouse was a breeze to set up and is the perfect size and has everything I need and more. For the little PC gaming I do now the Basilisk has plenty Macro options and I love the Chroma effects which sync perfectly with my Razer keyboard. The slightly textured rubber grips actually give me better control than I initially thought they would. The buttons are nice and clicky and feel like they will hold up to some heavy smashing. It glides super smooth which is due to the butter smooth pads, weight and the perfect soft flexible cord.

title: Razer quality as always!
text: I have always been a big fan of Razer products and the Razer BlackWidow Mechanical Gaming Keyboard 2019 did not disappoint. The new Synapse app has been updated and much less buggy than when I last used it which was nice. The keys on this keyboard are nice and clicky (Razer Mechanical Switches) yet feel solid and not mushy. I love how customizable this keyboard is with the Synapse app. Color options are endless and you could spend hours personalizing every key with a different color if you wanted to. Personally I just like the presets that are available to tweak to your liking. Through the Synapse app you can also create Macros to your hearts content, however my Macro days have long since passed. It's even got on-board and cloud memory for your favorite programmed presets. If only this new version BlackWidow would have been available back in my WoW days! Seriously though, 5 stars all around!!

title: Sound and function great but my ears get sore after about 30 minutes.
text: I put these T.Assault Six Collection Edition headphone to the test with some extended gaming sessions the last few days and overall I'd say they are pretty nice however there a couple issues I've noticed. As I noted in the headline here, after about 30 minutes of wearing them during some gaming sessions they started to feel like they were squeezing my ears a bit. Sound quality was great and the microphone worked almost better than a more expensive set that I own. The inline mic control works as it should and I like the volume control that's located on the left ear piece. They are easy to adjust to fit my medium sized head comfortably. The mic is removable and once inserted it's a little tricky to get it back out and when doing so, I broke a little plastic tab off the mic where it locks into place. the mic still works however, and seems to still stay in place anyway. There is also an included plug that fits into the headphone jack when not using the mic.

title: Great gaming headset for the $$
text: My son's talked me into trying these out as they love theirs and I needed a new set. I bought them a while back when they were on sale and haven't regretted my purchase on bit. I know there are better headsets out there but for the money, these are a win for me. They do what I need and being bald, they are quite comfortable for many hours of use. Other headsets tend to get uncomfortable and hurt the top of my head after only a short while. Also, I wear glasses and was worried that these would get uncomfortable because of that however I've got no complaints. Totally would recommend these to anyone looking for a solid headset.

title: Rerelease the games for PS3 or PS4, Squaresoft
text: I wish Squaresoft games will do what they did for Final Fantasy X & X-2, and rerelease Final Fantasy 7-9, completely reformatted to play for BOTH the PS3 AND the PS4, so die hard fans can finally play their BELOVED Final Fantasy games again. *pouts* Who wants to download it and play it on the COMPUTER, when just about ANYTHING can go wrong in the game play from computer viruses wiping out EVERYTHING in the system, to the computer itself breaking down, etc. Or in some cases that I've read from other download buyers, the downloads don't even WORK at ALL on their computers, so it was a complete waste of money to begin with. I want my Final Fantasy games where they BELONG which is right on my Playstation system, hopefully with an reprogrammed and updated version of the games so they will play on the PS3 and PS4 without problems, where I simply relax either in a comfy chair or lie down on the floor or my bed, as I watch my favorite game characters fight to the death against their enemies. *lol* Plus has anybody heard the 'news'? What's the point of rereleasing the guides when barely anybody can play the games unless the guides coming back out is a sign that the games themselves are going to be rereleased soon in PS3 or PS4 format.

title: Where's Skyrim: Dawnguard?
text: I've finally decided to get this game for myself, but just as I was about to get the nerve to buy it, I saw a commercial on tv advertising for a NEW version of Skyrim called 'Skyrim: Dawnguard' that has added bonus features like a feature to allow the player to create a PC character that can either be a vampire or a werewolf in the game and a lot of other features that upgraded it from the original Skyrim version. I want to try playing as either a vampire or werewolf. I'm all set to preorder Dawnguard, but I don't see it anywhere on the sight, even though if i do a search for it through Amazon's search engine a drop box shows up with dawnguards name if i just type in skyrim, but all I'm getting is the old Skyrim games when I hit the search button with no sign of Dawnguard anywhere.

title: Not the best case...
text: I got this case for my kid's Switch because the photos made it look like it could hold all of the extra controllers and games we have added to the collection. Unfortunately, the case has very limited padding and by the time we got all of the extra controllers and games in it, I was too worried about closing it because it felt like it was putting too much pressure from the stuff on the other side of the case right where the Switch screen was located. So, I was worried it was going to crack the screen. So, we decided to go back to our old case, as it felt a bit sturdier and safer for the game system. We'll just have to live without the space for the extra controllers until we can find a suitable alternative. I wouldn't recommend this case.

title: Game is challenging to us... we are only occassional gamers
text: I have to start by saying that we are not hard core gamers in our family, but we do enjoy playing our Wii and XBOX 360. We found this game to be really fun. It is not high stress like a game such as Titan Fall, but it is more of a thought game with timed events. My 13 year old daughter got a little frustrated getting through the first couple levels because it kept starting her over in spots because she would not complete the task fast enough. But, eventually she figured it out and was having a lot of fun with it. Now, with that said, one of her hard core gaming friends came over and played it and he had finished all levels within a few days only coming over for a couple hours at a time. So, I could see how some hard core gamers might get a bit frustrated with it because of how short it is. We found it to be a lot of fun and just right for our family and I would definitely recommend. As a parent, just be aware that there is some profanity and violence. The profanity is probably less than a child would experience in a school hallway so I wasn't to bothered by it.

title: AWESOME headphones!!!
text: These headphones are incredible. First... I have to say that noise canceling was amazing. The minute you put them over your ears, it blocks everything out even without sound turned on. They sound great too. Overall... here are the pros and cons: PROS Noise cancelling is amazing Very easy to pair to any Bluetooth capable device The sound is very clear when listening to music, gaming, or even just talking on the phone Not just great for gaming... they are great all around headphones Lightweight, so it's not an issue to wear them for a long period Earpieces fold in so the become flat for storage Zipper case is compact and makes them easy to store Battery life is really great CONS I wish it had a little more bass to the sound The price is a bit steep, but still... they are great headphones Wish I could pair to more than one device at a time (for example... iPhone for incoming calls and a gaming system at the same time) Overall... I would highly recommend them. They are a great set of headphones.

title: For and old Mom like me, this is a lot of fun!
text: So, I am 43 years old and I have so much fun playing this game with my 11 year old daughter. It is a fun little workout and definitely gets you off the couch and moving. My daughter has the Just Dance Wii, Just Dance XBOX 360, Dance Central XBOX 360, and all the Zumba dance games for the Wii and XBOX 360. She said this is her favorite out of all of the ones she owns. Most of the music is really catchy. She said said she likes about 80% of the music and dances. For an "old" mom like me, I like about 50% of the music and dances. Of course, my daughter plays it in a much harder mode and loves it. She said even the advanced mode is a bit too difficult for her and she has been part of a dance company for 8 years. I like the easy mode, as that seems to be hard enough for me. It seems to pick up your moves accurately, so I think the Kinect works well, unlike some of the Kinect games we have. So, I would highly recommend it... a lot of fun... very challenging... and a good, get off the couch, workout.

title: I normally love Amazon Basics... but not this one
text: I normally love Amazon Basics, but this one was a disappointment. First, we had to take the silicone covers off and the little square Wii motion sensitivity sensors on the bottom to get these to recharge. This was a really big pain and I was afraid I we were going to lose the accessories. The remotes are a little wobbly in the charging station and you have to make sure the wrist strap fits in the little notch in the back to make them a bit more secure. The other thing that drove us a bit crazy was the fact that it was a USB attachment into the Wii station instead of using its own power cord. So, it was always glowing right in front of the TV. If your Wii is turned off, then it will not charge the remotes. It has to be at least turned on (green light showing on Wii) or in the standby (yellow light showing on the Wii) position. We have always just used batteries, so we were hopeful this charging station would work well. However, I think we will go back to using our regular batteries. Maybe if we were true gamers and played all the time, I would think twice, but right now we only replace the batteries in the four chargers ever couple of months and maybe only play the Wii a couple times during the week.

title: I would wait for a bit to buy this...
text: Our family hasn't played rock band on any other platform than the Wii, so we really don't have anything other platform to compare it to. Now, having said that, we are having a blast with it. However, we wish we would have waited for a few months for the Guitar Hero World Tour - Band Kit to come out and compared the two. We like the music scores better for Guitar Hero than the ones that came with Rock Band. It would also be nice to see if multiple guitars can be used with the new Guitar Hero Band Kit that is coming out, as it doesn't seem like multiple guitars can be used with Rock Band... or at least we haven't figured out a way to do this yet. Don't get me wrong... Rock Band is a lot of fun. But, after seeing the previews for the other, I wish we would have waited a few months.

title: Great FPS Mouse
text: I bought this mouse as my Corsair RGB Saber was having clicking issues. I decided to go with this mouse as it was a great price for similar buttons from my previous mouse. As with most corsair mice, you can customer the colors, buttons, and DPI using the corsair dashboard. This mouse has a "sniper" button where your thumb rests which at times can be annoying when playing a game. You can customer the "sniper" button DPI so when you press and hold it, your mouse speed is increased or decreased. When playing Battlefield 5, i ran into accidentally pressing the button which was annoying to me as i tend to clench the mouse when i fire a gun with the left mouse click. The workaround was to change the DPI of the "sniper" button to my default mouse speed. I feel i will never use the "sniper" button feature but may come back to it and try it out again. Overall, this is a great mouse and have not had any issues.

title: This combination completes my setup.
text: This is a great keyboard and mouse combination. Been using it for a week and so far it has been working flawless. Pros: Keyboard design fits best and optimal travel for your fingertips. Rainbow brightness just rocks and it is just soothing to the eyes. Mouse had adjustable dpi and has buttons on it to increase or decrease dpi. Mouse sensitivity and responsiveness is also good. Cons: It is difficult to use the keyboard without the rainbow light and I recommend to keep it turned ON most of the time. Update: After some weeks of usage found I that the keys combination doesn’t work with Mac properly. I might need to buy a separate keyboard for Mac.

title: Was great
text: I've had this controller since 4/2020 I love the design. It's comfortable and reminds me of a combination of the Sony PS controller mixed with a Super Nintendo controller. I loved it. Until It started acting up within the last week. I have not even had the controller a year yet. I do not abuse my controllers I take very good care of them. I am not happy that the controller has joystick drift and the d-pad buttons start to automattically push them selfs. I can put the controller down and my character in whatever game I am playing will move without me touching the controller. Tried to contact seller but Did not find anyway of getting ahold of them.

title: No auto-off features, huge and clunky
text: The controller is extremely large and bubbly in odd places. If you bump a button, the controller will turn on. If you set the controller down too hard, the controller turns on. That's all great, however it will not turn itself off. And it runs only on AA batteries.. which will give you about a week of play. I can't really stress how fat the controller is.. I have small hands and am a woman, so a man may have a different experience. Also there are weird buttons underneath the controller that will back you out of things accidentally. Overall, very meh and absolutely not worth the price to me personally. 5/10 On the plus side, if you have kids and don't want your joy cons torn up by little monsters, this is a good alternative as chances are you'll want to throw it away eventually anyway.

title: Don't be put off by simple user error. Awesome game
text: Awesome game... a lot of these reviews are just pure user error. You need to install origin first, make an account.. easy and free. Then you will redeem the code and download the base game. After downloading the base game, click on available content packs.. and voila, Pets. There are instructions on how to install origin as well as this game online... That being said, I bought this game when it first came out. I literally got around 2000 hours or more of play out of it until Sims 4 came out. This game is very build heavy, content heavy, so if you enjoy building etc this is an awesome game. You also have a variety of places to go and tons of stuff packs that are now like half off. It's an open world and very in depth game.. parents can ground their kids, teach their toddlers to walk, buy cars.. endless fun

title: Too Many Glitches, And Rude To French People
text: The Burger Shop and the Sushi Shop are loads of fun, and not too difficult. The Cake shop has lots of glitches: you clearly won a level by exceeded the money goal for the day, but for some reason the game says that you didn't, this happens for a lot of the Cake shop levels. Also the `play' button for the Cake shop once in a while is unclickable, so you cannot even begin the next level, it just freezes up. The Flower shop is just way too difficult and takes all the fun out of the game. Also, there is a town money glitch: I had upgraded all my shops, but for some reason the Flower shop wont stay upgraded. It reverts on it's own right back to the first level before upgrading, but yet all my money that I spent on upgrading it is gone. All the other shops stay upgraded, so I don't understand why the Flower Shop doesn't. One thing I am very disappointed about is the blatant reference to the French people. In the game, when upgrading Jill's cake shop, she says: "Ooh la la, Customers Will Think They Are In Less-rude Version Of France". If the game writers had said "Wow, Customers Will Think They Are In A Less-self Centered Version Of America" I bet the gaming public here in the USA would be upset and making complaints. But because this uneducated, derogatory, racist comment is directed at another country it is overlooked and dismissed I guess. I know from first hand experience from actually being in France, that this disgraceful stereotype is completely incorrect and unjustified, and shows the writers to be ignorant. No entire group of people or country should be labeled in such way, it doesn't matter if it's Americans, Canadians, Russians, Germans, Italians, or the French etc.. There are rude people everywhere in the world, that does not mean that the entire population of one country are rude just because some of it's people are. The writers for this game are labeling all the people of an entire country as being bad-mannered and discourteous, when ironically their offensive comment shows them to be the ones who are bad-mannered, discourteous, rude. I wish I could get my money back for this game.

title: Be careful of the PSU.
text: Cable works awesome for my use. I run it from a server rack, through a wall, up into the attic, down another wall and into the next room. I have an anker 3.0 powered usb hub connected on the end. I initially tested without using the cables own power adapter and it worked just fine. When I plugged the PSU into the wall, my pc would no longer boot. The fans just spun sporadically in short bursts. Once I unplugged the PSU, the pc booted fine. I've had no drop outs at all and I power my headphones, mouse, keyboard and joypad through this cable. I don't use wireless anything. Minus 1 star only because the included PSU kills my system, there may be a short in it internally.

title: I really like this charging dock because it is super convenient to ...
text: I really like this charging dock because it is super convenient to charge three controllers at the same time. It does take a little practice inserting the controller onto the docking bay, but once you figure it out it's pretty simple. When the controllers are charging, the light on the controller blinks, but the charging station itself has no indicator-it is constantly blue. You have to look at the back end of the controllers to ensure that the light is no longer blinking (indicating that it is fully charged). The dock itself is very light-weight and purposefully designed. Each controller bay has a cover to prevent dust from getting into the USB port when that charging station is not in use. The rubberized feet on the bottom of the charging station are strong enough to ensure that the unit does not slide around when you are inserting the controller. Disclaimer: I purchased this item at a discount in exchange for an honest and unbiased review.

title: Repaired faulty joystick on Occulus Quest 2
text: The replacement joystick works fine. I don't expect good tools with these kits, but just what's needed to do the intended job. I have good tools and I know what they cost. The problem here is the provided screwdriver bit holder is just a very poor fit because the shaft is so short and the handle too bulky to get at the screws at a perpendicular angle. Instead of throwing in a multi-bit holder with a few bits that aren't needed, the kit should feature the one screwdriver that's needed in a format that actually fits not just the screws, but the part that it's intended to work on. The hand controller for the Occulus Quest 2 needs a Torx T5 bit or driver with a long skinny shaft, not a short fat one. A screwdriver of the same quality that fits correctly would not cost any more than the ill-fitting one provided. Because I had my own T5 screwdriver, this kit worked fine for me. I'm giving it 4-stars mostly because I'm happy that the hand controller could be repaired affordably. I'm grateful for that.

title: Absolutely horrible :(
text: This is coming from someone who has owned a G910 orion, Now the keyboard itself is really nice, compact and as advertised all the keys on the keyboard are programable. Cool right? but when it comes down to programming the keyboard the software included is so complex to understand, Now i spent hours comprehending the instruction and was like okay i got it, so i program the keyboard save and reboot as instruction says, once its rebooted not even the single key that i programmed work made me almost want to throw the keyboard outside of the window. if you have somewhat programming knowledge you might be well off figuring it out, but for a regular individual i would advise you to stay away. Horrible enough to make you want to say why in this world i ordered this junk.

title: Great Expansion
text: This is a great expansion to The Sims 2. As mentioned in other reviews there are several new cheat codes. The most useful ones being familyfunds and maxmotives. The maxmotives one I use several times it sets all the motives such as hunger, tiredness, comfort, environment etc to maximum. This is really useful when you want your sim to do something but they wont because they are tired,bored or hungry or even worse all of the above. The sims can now own their own car and have a garage to put it in. Make sure they fit it with an alarm because it can be stolen as I found out the hard way. There is also a downtown area with a variety of stores, clubs and gyms.

title: Check before you buy
text: Check that your system meets the requirements before you buy the game. I replaced my video card to get this game to work, I planned to upgrade anyway. A tip for those who say they have the requirements but it doesn't work, make sure your graphics cards has the latest drivers installed, they can usually be downloaded free from the manufacturer of your graphics card. Also make sure your AGP has the latest GART drivers if it's not an Intel motherboard. As well as making the game work they'll improve the performance of your system too! I have a P4, 1.8GHz, Windows XP, Radeon 9200 128 Mb, 768 Mb RAM system and it works fine for me. The only problem is getting to my computer because my wife is always playing The Sims 2 on it :)

title: Quite good but some problems
text: I wish I could give this 3 1/2 stars but I'll settle for 3. It is huge fun at first to see yourself in The Sims. I have had no trouble importing the created Sims into the expansion packs, at least up to Hot Date anyway. The problems are that there really isn't enough data points when defining the Sims head so the end up with almost block like heads. Another thing is the heads are about 3 times the size they should be so you end up with something looking a little like you but with a huge squared off head:) I wish they'd had enabled more points to define the shape of the head and had more bodies to choose from. All in all fun for awhile but could of been a lot better. Point to note, this is for the original SIMS NOT SIMS 2

title: What an improvement
text: I must say this expansion has added so much to Sim City 4! Now you can drive around your city on missions, you can put in toll booths to raise some money. You can now name your streets, add avenues (which is a usefull intermediate between streets and highways) to ease traffic congestion, and view how and when your streets are used by commuters. The only down side is that, as others have stated, this requires a lot of processing memory, both RAM and video. You'd be advised not to run it with all the graphics set to maximum unless you have a very powerful computer and video card. Have fun and try to drive carefully around your streets.

title: Warning!
text: Warning, I bought this and although my system seemingly meets the minimum requirements on the box it wouldn't run on my computer. What they don't tell you is that it requires a nvidia card in order to work properly, or at least not a ATI card like I have. Their website offers no help except the discussion boards suggest they may issue a patch to fix this at the end of the year or the begining of next year! That's just TOO long to wait. Why didn't it say this on the box? If it had I wouldn't of bothered obviously. Add to this that it locked up my computer and even their latest patch didn't fix the compatability problem... So unless you have an nvidia card don't waste your money!

title: 1200mAh of nostagia!
text: Recently found my old 2001-slim model PSP but was missing the battery for it. I did research on many replacement batteries and heard a lot of them do not hold a charge for long and would constantly "cut-out" or have a sudden loss of power. Though not many have bought or reviewed this battery, I went for it as it did not have many negative reviews or low stars and it was well worth it. I can now play "Coded Arms" without having to be stuck to a wall socket. This battery lasts for quiet a while (longest I have measured while in constant gameplay) was about 5-6 hours. At times I might not touch my PSP for about 3 days to a business week and even still, it turns on and so far has not "cut-out" on me. For those who want a piece of their nostalgic childhood or the good-old-days, buy this battery and bring that discontinued relic of the early 2000's back to life.

title: It's cheap because you don't get much for it
text: This (G413 SE TKL) is a very basic mechanical keyboard with no bells and whistles. If you're looking for something inexpensive in a mechanical kb, this is possibly worth considering, but you can get a lot more for just a little more money. (Check ratings and reviews on a site like PCMag or Wirecutter.) The good: it's compact, and the mechanical keys are ok. It has key backlighting (with brighness adjustment, see below). That's it. Not for the not so good: The keys are a bit stiff, and typing on this is going to take an adjustment. My much more expensive Razer keyboard is a whole lot smoother and has a significantly better feel. (I no longer recommend Razer because their Synapse software is horrible, and is blocked by some corporate IT departments because of perceived vulnerabilities.) This is not an RGB keyboard (no colors): all you can do is adjust key brightness (using FN + F1/F2) through a few preset levels. You can't customize anything. (Note that some reviewers complain about the side-by-side key symbols: that's what you get in a backlit mech keyboard, because the middle can't be lit, being blocked by the post. IMO you get used to this pretty quickly.) Overall I can't recommend this, and I'm still considering returning it to Amazon. I bought this because I needed something "good enough" in a hurry, and it was available and on sale. In retrospect I should have spent a little more to get a better keyboard.

title: Works as it's supposed to, and better than that composite cable thing.
text: I needed something to hook up my son's old Wii to a newer TCL tv that doesn't have any compositive audio/video input. This looks like a generic product sold under many obscure brand names, I just picked one at random that had many reviews and a high rating. The adapter/converter plugs in snugly to the Wii port where that old cable went, and with a decent HDMI cable I had video and audio on the tv. This combo is way more compact than the cable it replaced. I went into the Wii settings and told it to produce 480p and adjust to a 16:9 tv, which made the image a bit better and wider (I didn't try to fill the screen). So, a simple, inexpensive, hassle-free solution to a problem that had the potential to greatly increase the noise level at home. No complaints. Not even if it breaks in a year and I have to buy a new one. (No, it definitely won't upscale to HD or 4K. Nor will it magically improve the games.)

title: Good sound, hassle-free use, but hard to fit comfortably because of non-adjustable support
text: As you would expect, using a corded USB headset is really hassle-free: you plug in, turn on, and go. This one did as expected. Pluses are: good sound, long cord, easy to use control unit (with a clip) that can be positioned on the waist or anywhere else above. That said, I'll compare this to the wireless model (HyperX Cloud II Wireless) I recently reviewed. Some of the comments for that one apply here as well: "I've also used them extensively to listen to high-quality streaming and MP3 recorded music on my computer, and am very pleased with the sound. I think my Shure earbuds might be just a tad better in tone, but I'm not completely sure about that (yet)." Same thing here. The major problem I have with this model is that I couldn't get the headset to sit comfortably on my head: the over-the-head support bands are not adjustable, the inner one slides easily to stop at the rigid outer band, which is one size only. So, with my head not being as big as their design model's, the whole thing wanted to slide down further than I wanted, so it felt like a heavy headset resting on my ears. Ugh! So, although I really like everything else about this headset, I have to take points off, and can't recommend it for most buyers. You're better off getting the Cloud II model (either wired or wireless), if you want to stick with HyperX.

title: Very good headset for general use
text: I wanted a good over-the-ear headset for video conferences, with good sound and hassle-free user experience. I'm very satisfied with this one. It was simple to set up: all I really needed to do was to (1) charge the headset using a USB-C charge cable; (2) plug the USB dongle in; (3) turn the headset on. For video conferences I do need to make sure that I'm selecting the correct speaker and mike, but that's not difficult, and it all works without a hitch. I've also used them extensively to listen to high-quality streaming and MP3 recorded music on my computer, and am very pleased with the sound. I think my Shure earbuds might be just a tad better in tone, but I'm not completely sure about that (yet). One downside, perhaps because I'm not used to them yet, is that I tend to talk a little louder than normal, and my voice sounds a little funny to me. But the first is easy to correct, and the second happens no matter what kind of headset I use, so I guess it's just how it has to be. I'm not a gamer and have not used these for gaming, so can't help you there. I don't see why that would change anything, but I leave that to interpretation by those who know more about gamer needs. Overall, a very nice headset, at least for general use. A bit pricey for the purpose, perhaps, but that's for the buyer to decide.

title: Feels a little too light, but otherwise good
text: This is a pretty decent mouse, but short of perfect. I think they made a mistake to make it quite so light: compared with a Razer DeathAdder for instance, it feels just a bit too light, so for me at least, not quite as comfortable to use. It's also a bit small for my large hands (slightly smaller than the DeathAdder), so not what I would pick as my main mouse for use all day. It works pretty nicely for my second computer that I use much less frequently, perhaps a total of an hour or two a day. (I'm now considering giving it to a family member with smaller hands.) Note that I use these for "normal" computer use, not for gaming. I prefer gaming keyboards and mice for their greater precision, that's all. So it's possible for example that an avid gamer would say "lighter is better!" and I'm not going to dispute that (although I think it would be a very personal preference). Overall, if you want a better mouse, and don't mind it being lighter (and don't have large hands), then this one is definitely worth a look.

title: Very nice mechanical keyboard with clicky keys
text: If you're familiar with Razer keyboards, you won't be disappointed with this one, it has that same lovely tactile feel when you're typing, and fast response. The "green" keys are a tad louder than than the others (orange and yellow), but not unpleasant, although those in a shared space may want to check if the typing might bother others nearby. I find that I have much lower fatigue using a good mechanical keyboard, and like the overall consistent response I get from them. Also note that these are the newer keys in which the shift characters are on the top row as well, so that both characters on a key are lit. Setup was easy: I decided I didn't want to bother with a wireless connection and the need to remember to recharge regularly, so I left the cord plugged in and used it as a wired keyboard. (Yes, it's just fine to do that.) The only minor criticism I have is that the keys should really be brighter. The main alphanumeric keys are a little dimmer than I'd ideally like. Overall, an excellent keyboard from Razer.

title: This is a really nice TKL keyboard.
text: I decided recently to upgrade both of my keyboards to mechanical ones, and after doing quite a lot of research, I decided that these BlackWidow TKL linear switch keyboards were the best fit for me with price and performance in mind. Overall I'm pretty happy: the touch and feel of the keyboard is wonderful (I really prefer the linear switches), the wrist rest is essential and quite comfortable, and the TKL size allows me to position the keyboard near the mouse, which for me is ergonomically much better. (I had been using a Logitech Wave for years, and I'm still a bit surprised by how much better this keyboard is for me overall.) Downsides? Firstly, these are the keys with the secondary characters not lit: if you want those lit, you have to spend about $30 more to get the PBT keycap upgrade package. (Or you can buy another Razer TKL product, most likely without a wrist rest.) Secondly, I don't like the light under the keys, I think that's quite unnecessary and distracting, actually making it harder to read those unlit characters. Oh, and my pet peeve is the Delete key being the same size as the others: I happen to use it almost as often as I use backspace, and much prefer keyboards where that key is made larger. Finally, you want to hope you never need Razer customer service. My experience with them has been pretty bad: they're really slow, they don't do what they say they'll do, and it can take several days and multiple attempts to do something that with Amazon takes about 5 minutes. They don't seem to take it seriously enough.

title: Lovely keyboard, worth considering.
text: [Note: I updated this review and changed rating to 4*, since I was mistaken about the lighting.] This was the first mech keyboard I tried, and I really liked the feel and responsiveness. I was switching from a Logitech Wave keyboard, and found that the slightly smaller keyboard and different layout gave me a little trouble at first, but I began to adjust fairly quickly. The Logitech G-Hub software is ok: in my opinion not quite as good as the Razer Synapse software in ease of use and configurability, but good enough. Unfortunately, the new GX keys do not allow the secondary characters on the keys (the symbols accessed by using Shift) to be illuminated. So there I am, looking at brightly lit characters, and finding myself peering occasionally to be sure I'm hitting the right key for the shift character. Maybe a perfect touch typist wouldn't care, but I need to occasionally look, especially when I'm typing the less frequent characters. (My understanding is that this is a limitation of most mechanical keys: only the upper part of the key can be properly lit, so the only solution is to have the two characters side by side at the top.) A minor flaw is the need to use two USB slots to plug in the keyboard, because one powers the pass-through USB slot. What? How is that useful? I'd rather just use a separate USB cable or hub and have the option of using USB 3, multiple ports, etc. I think this is just dumb, although I know that many buyers want a pass-through no matter what. I ended up returning this one and switching to a Razer TKL with linear switches, which has even better responsiveness and feel, and is just a bit more convenient to position. And as I said above, I like the Synapse software better.

title: cloud feature is disappointing
text: I upgraded (from 2012) in order to have mobile access to the data. And that is a useful & long-desired improvement. Unfortunately, Intuit did its usual half-hearted, half-designed job with this feature, and it's quite disappointing: 1. You can't sync investment accounts. The old investing.quicken.com site is very limited, not worth using. (For example, you can't see simple consolidated views of your investments, can't run basic reports. etc.) 2. The sync from the desktop isn't automatic, and takes a long time. If you're used to other online products that sync to the desktop (think Dropbox & Google Drive as two very popular examples, there are many others), you will find this clunky & old-tech. Everytime you open Quicken, it will tell you you made changes, whether you did or not, and suggest that you sync. This should be an automated, behind the scenes process, it's not hard. 3. The alerts are rather dumb, and they're essentially hard-coded. You can't create your own rules, and you can't even do a lot with the built-in rules (you can just pick some parameters from a limited list). You can't delete them all either, if you consider them dumb and pointless. Again, not hard to do a lot better. There are no significant improvements in reporting, or in investment analysis. If you look at the "What's new in 2013" page, you see mobile, alerts, and "more flexible budgeting", whatever that means. There is a tweak to how accounts show up in the nav bar, where you can put some accounts in the "Separate" list, which means "show but don't include with main set of accounts". This is mildly useful. There's also a feature to mark an account "closed", also slightly useful -- in theory. These account still show up in the list of accounts when you're doing a transfer between investment accounts! Clearly someone forgot what the word "closed" might mean. So all in all, same old Intuit, same old Quicken. Buy it if the mobile feature is useful to you. (BTW, I tried Mint as an alternative, and I couldn't stand the heavy-duty selling on every darned screen. Maybe some people can tune this stuff out, I couldn't.)

title: some ui improvements over Office 2007
text: There's not a lot that's obviously changed in this version from Office 2007. (See [...] for detailed descriptions of changes.) But I do like the improvements in the ribbon: firstly, you can hide it, to get more usable screen; secondly, you can customize it! Both of these were missing features in Office 2007, desired by many (if not most) users. There are also some security improvements that are useful: e.g., Word opens downloaded files in a protected mode; PowerPoint allows presentations to be restricted from editing/copying. If you're trying to decide between this version and a previous one, definitely I'd recommend this one. If you're trying to decide whether to pay for an upgrade, it depends on how irritated you get with the limitations of the ribbon in the 2007 version. For users in a business setting, some of the collaboration features (using Sharepoint Server) might also be of interest. See link above for more info.

title: CM10 is a fairly good program with flaws (does run on Vista)
text: This is a pretty good chess program for beginners & intermediate players, has a lot that helps you learn, including of course not-too-bad player simulation. It's not perfect, but I would recommend it if you're looking for something for anyone who wants to learn or get better. There is a long list under "how this program could have been better". See some of the other reviews, but my top 3 gripes are: (1) dumb programming that chews up the CPU even when the program is supposed to be idle; (2) bugs, especially a "hang" problem on single-cpu/single-core machines, where the game program just gets stuck somewhere (looks like a race condition; solution is to temporarily lower the priority of the TheKing processes by using TaskManager); (3) explanations of bad moves, or recommendations of good moves, provide detail but not the big picture. Finally, it does appear to run fine in Vista: I installed it normally and have been playing it without problems. (I haven't seen the hang problem, but since I have a dual-core machine now I don't expect the race condition to occur.)

title: Economical replacement option.
text: I have two sets of joy cons and both experienced drifting problems eventually. The first 2 times I was lucky that they were still under warrenty with Nintendo, but that was no longer the case so buying these replacements really helped out. Taking apart my Joy con wasn't the easiest thing to do, but it was doable as long as I was really careful. This part is slightly smaller than the original joystick, but not noticeable enough to change the feel of how I play. Being slightly smaller actually made it easier to replace because the original joystick put up a fight when coming out. The smaller size might affect the use of some custom nubs though I suppose. I never really use any so I can't say for sure. All in all I am satisfied with the part for the price. Other replacements also send you the screwdriver that you need to take apart the controllers but that ends up costing a little more. I didn't need it since I have amassed several tiny screwdrivers from other electronics that I have fixed and I hate to get more when I don't need them. It always feels like a waste when I have 9 of the same tiny screwdrivers but only ever use one. Bottom line is that this is an economical replacement and I will update this review when I have to get the next eventual replacement so I can provide a sense of durability for these. Unfortunately the way these sticks are built they just don't seem to last very long without experiencing issues.

title: Loved it, great for any Zelda fan!
text: Loved it! Zelda is one of my all time favorite video game franchise's and so it was fun to be able to decorate our Nintendo Switch in a Zelda theme. Breath of the wild is an amazing addition to the franchise and I couldn't be happier with this purchase since I got it for a good deal on Prime Day. The grips fit fine, but I do not use them at all. The control feels better without them in my opinion. I will keep them handy though because I am sure they will become useful one day when I eventually wear out the stock grips. The application was easy. The cut outs are big enough to give you room for error if you aren't a pro at placing stickers on precisely, but still exact enough to cover most of the surface so you can truly enjoy the design. I also really liked that it included a screen protector as well. I do most of my playing on the TV, but having a screen protector makes me feel more comfortable to take the Switch out of the dock on occasion. Five stars all the way, any Zelda fan will definitely enjoy this!

title: Good, but if you want to step up your game then spend more $
text: My madcatz freq 5 finally bit the dust and wanted to see what else was out there. These guys aren't the top of the line but you get what you pay for. The mic quality is pretty good, and picks up your voice well, though it does not detach, so these are solely a gaming headset rather than an optional set of headphones. The audio quality is where I see the lower price point. Definitely as good if not better than anything else at that price point, but was a step back from my last couple of headsets. The build seems durable though rather lightweight and the earpieces are smaller than I expected. I don't have large ears, yet these pads rest on my ears rather than around them. If you want a discount headset that gives you exactly what you pay for, then this is right for you. This will make a great backup pair for me, or a primary pair for my 5yr old son. If you want to step up your game night with better sound quality and a comfortable fit around your ears, maybe plan on spending closer to $50-$75.

title: it's pink and lights up
text: I admit that I got this keyboard because it's pink and lights up. I wanted something fun (hence the pink, though there are white keys I can switch in if I want), and the LED lights which are programmable. Those are actually important since due to migraines, I sometimes have to darken my office and having a keyboard that lights up helps me to keep working. I like the 'feel' to this keyboard and its size. There is an audible clack when you use the keys, which may annoy some, but it's fine for me. There's the whole gaming thing, but I just use it for work and writing.

title: pretty good VR gaming headset
text: I have tried a few VR setups in the past, but the Oculus Rift S is the first VR headset that I have owned personally. I like the fact that it doesn't need any external sensors, as it gives you a lot more flexibility with how you can set it up in a room. The setup is really easy, and it's quick to get up and running. It doesn't really come with much in terms of apps or games, other than some tutorials, so you have to purchase games or apps through the Oculus store or Steam. I picked up Robo Recall so far, and it's a fun game. A couple things I noticed that detract from the experience slightly are the field of view and the audio setup. The field of view seems less than on some other setups. You can see quite a bit of black-space to the sides in your peripheral view, which takes away from the immersive feel. Also, the speakers are in the headband near the ear, and are not an over-ear setup, which from an audio perspective also takes away from the feeling of being really immersed in the environment. Overall for the price, I feel it is a good value, especially if you want to set it up in a room where it might be difficult or cluttered to try and position sensors and sensor-towers. If you are looking for a more immersive experience, than the pricier alternatives might be a better option for you.

title: Great result, challenging project
text: I love the result, but proceed with caution. the design of the joycon housing is very efficient, but this makes it tricky to replace. instead of a case around a block of components, the components are mounted directly to the housing, both sides of it. this makes it a little tricky to do the replacement. If you take your time and are careful I think anyone could do it, but this is a project that is likely to frustrate new tinkerers and DIYers. The included tools can get the job done, but are very cheap and will wear out if you are not careful, I ended up using an iFixit toolkit If you take it slow and study where things go it can be a fun and rewarding project, just don't expect to "quick-swap" the cases.

title: Underrated
text: Possibly one of the most Underrated and Undersold accessories ever. Steam marketed it to Desktop warriors, but honestly i think they are a great tool for pretty much everyone. Yes, you can obviously use it to play computer games on your TV without having to re-arrange your PC setup, but it is so much more than that. I've come to see it as a super-powered Chrome-cast. Literally anything & everything you can do on your computer can be streamed to this. This & a wireless keyboard and mouse and you can easily use your computer on a display across the house. Not without some minor drawbacks. Wifi can be a bit laggy when gaming or streaming video, so you're best off plugging it into your router. Doesn't support the xbone USB dongle, so you either need to plug your controller in or get one of newer Bluetooth ones (which can connect without a usb) or really any other Bluetooth capable controller.

title: Not just for gaming
text: [[VIDEOID:af12c4ac6adcc20db60f109775eccfa0]] I realize that this is supposed to be for gaming--- and it's great for that--- but it's also great for every day use. I have a rare genetic disorder that causes severe joint damage and as a result, I have limited strength and mobility in my hands. This one feels more natural in my hand compared to my regular mouse. It leaves my hand in a more neutral position and the buttons are easier to click. I really like that I can program the buttons on the side. The cord is very long so it reaches all of the way across my desk. It can be folded up when it's not in use.

title: Excellent Board
text: I read several reviews before making the purchase. The price is excellent. Here is my thoughts on a few things mentioned in other reviews....First it clearly says Wii Fit U....that means it is for the Wii U not the original Wii. The bottom of the board has Nintendo on it, made into the plastic. The area on the bottom with the pencil marks is more than likely from the assembly line, many items are marked after inspected.... I had no issue with this board connecting, you put the disk in and batteries in the board...then when the game starts and you select what you want to play ( or the exercise) it will say to tap the power button with your foot, then it will tell you when to step on. There were no issues with my disc. The box was sealed upon arrival and all items are genuine. The price is low, yes, because the Wii U has been out for a long time, in a sense it is "old".....I am happy with my purchase, all of it works as it should, the item is new.

title: Not perfect, but it works, nothing was broken :-)
text: From purchase to setup, I am pretty pleased. However the hiccups were there. While others chose All Access, which is actually separate from this bundle offer, considered a "new model." I chose the Black Friday limited time offer, then paying in equal installments over 12 months, using Amazon Prime Visa. I did this, because I converted from Live Gold to Ultimate Access, recently, and have two years prepaid. Over two years, though, the Xbox One X bundle is actually cheaper, when considering Ultimate is two thirds of the cost. On top of that, All Access requires a Capitol One credit check, and I didn't want that in my wallet. The order was shipped across the country, why? I don't know, I would have thought the local Amazon warehouse would have had it ready for same day delivery. When it arrived, it was raining, though no attempt was made to deliver it to the door. It was dropped 6ft over the fence. Strange, you tell them once, deliver over the fence for a soft package you weren't going to be home for, then for the rest of your life everything gets tossed over the fence, no matter what it is. Fortunately only the outer box got soaked. The rest remained dry. Somethings I noticed. The Xbox One X was made mid 2019, yet Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is a new game bundle. There was a secondary set of circular stickers sealing the sleeve to the packaging. Also the primary box was dusty. I have a theory. Somewhere along the chain, the box was opened, and the contents replaced/changed/updated, then the bundle sleeve was added. I don't know who does this, Microsoft or Amazon. I was disappointed that the game was a digital download, and not a disc. The item presentation suggests a disc. Still, I cannot play the game. After downloading over night, it has 11 hours left. Not everyone has gigabit. Setting up the unit wasn't as easy as documentation suggested. The iPhone Xbox App does not use the camera, therefore you cannot use the QR code to set things up. Also because the unit was so old, there was a 700MB+ update required and this disrupted and complicated the setup. Where I could type in a code to setup the unit from my phone, it forgot after the update, and I had to do it again on reboot - the iPhone app was no longer able to participate. Also, I had to manually enter codes to add the game license and extend Xbox Live Gold, by 20 days. What ever happened to using the camera and OCR to read the codes? Oh that feature is with the QR code reader - non-existent. I replaced my Blu-Ray player with the bundle, on a new 4K TV. I decided to reuse the HDMI High Speed 1.4 cable, already run to the previous component. This may have been the source of screen blackouts during setup. I have reseated the cable and it hasn't blackout since. But the situation has been noted. I liked that the Xbox detected the TV was 4K and a switched over to the higher setting.

title: There is quite nothing like it, even to this day.
text: We bought this for our eldest son, about 3 years old, in 2001. To this day our children are fond of this game. Our youngest, now 8 years old, became upset when we talked about passing it on to some friends. We discussed how we no longer had a computer that is compatible. What now? How about building a PC that can play this game. I researched a little. There are some other Tonka playset games, from the same era. However no one else has made a game that is similar or current that is designed for Windows 7 or Mac OS X. Here on Amazon the value of the game has gone up really high. Originally thirty dollars, now the price has doubled and tripled. This is the same elsewhere on the net. I better get started on that PC. Or maybe VM.

title: 1st time Guitar player, and i'm EXCITED!!!
text: I'm picking up a guitar for the very first time at the age of 30 (almost 31). I have been "playing" for about a month, reading from a book, and going at my own pace. I knew "Mary had a little lamb". I ordered this game, honestly because if Slash puts his name on it, it CANNOT be crap! I just received it today, put it in the PlayStation, and hooked up my guitar, and started playing.. 4 HOURS LATER, I have to force myself to put the guitar down because i'm finally developing the coveted "guitar fingers" (calluses) ... This is such an amazing TOOL!! It is exactly what i expected, in that it is MOSTLY a teacher, sprinkled with plenty of fun. But i'm already playing hammer-ons, and palm mutes!! lol yes i just started today! The best part of this game is, it won't let you just get comfortable with one string and one chord, if it believes you can advance, it throws more strings and more chords at you during the song practices! But don't worry, if you don't pick it up right away, it will either take the chord away, or slow it down just a bit for you. Bottom line; if you are skeptical on this product, DON'T BE, it teaches you REAL guitar, and it is ALOT of fun doing it!! I'm in Afghanistan right now, but i cant wait to get home and start downloading all the downloadable content for the game!!

title: Click click click, this is responsive and clean
text: During my very first typing class in 7th grade, I had an instantaneous awe of the way I could press a button and the letter or number on that key would appear on paper. Older computer keyboards felt a little similar but not the same, really, you know like when you're thinking and rub your fingers on the keys. If you type a lot or enjoy gaming on a computer, responsiveness is critical for speed and comfort. With the tactile but pretty quiet keys on the [[ASIN:B00N2ROO2S Corsair Gaming K70 RGB LED Mechanical Gaming Keyboard - Cherry MX Red (CH-9000068-NA)]], I'm brought back to the days when I typed on that old typewriter and even though the area of the keyboard is smaller, I'm in heaven. For gamers, this keyboard will likely take you to heaven. Since the K70 is now in RGB, you can set it up with colors beyond the imagination and save your profile/s for play on any machine. For non-gamers, the RGB is not really necessary, but it sure adds another dimension if you type, as I do, in the dark. If you don't want the keys lit, you can dim them or turn them off. The black aluminum case of the Cherry MX Red version which I have is classy to look at and impressive to hold. I especialy love the right angled corners and I use the removable wrist rest which has a texture that is smooth, almost leathery. On a table or desk, I can keep it flat and rely on the rubber strips to hold it in place or I can raise it with four simple feet. Right now, I'm typing with it on my lap and I have the computer on a chair a few feet away. Although the quick start guide says I must use both of the two USB plugs, I have simply plugged in the one with the keyboard on it and it's working fine. For gaming or utilizing more than just typing or with a computer of USB 1 or USB2, both plugs are needed, but with a USB3 port on the computer, the single works fine. A complete manual really should be downloaded and if you've ordered this keyboard, you can do that while waiting for it to be delivered, so you'll be ready when you take it out of the nice looking box. I know that some people have criticized the software, but I have not had problems when I used this on a Windows computer. On the Mac, I was unable to access the Cue software at all. I've switched between a Mac and a Windows based computer and since I saved the profile, it's working fine on both. I am really hoping that Corsair is able to develop for us Mac users. So, in summary, if you want a mechanical keyboard and use a Windows computer, this is wonderful. If you use a Mac, I'd suggest skipping this RGB version if you love the keyboard and save some money by getting the previous version. The out of the box red LED lights are nice, but you don't need to pay for the color spectrum if you can't access them and some of the functions are not accessible on a Mac. Since I don't really do gaming on the Mac, I'm good.

title: Protection and handy light outweigh its cost
text: With the reduction in price and the advent of the Special Offer Kindle, countless more will find their ways into the homes of readers all over the world. The Kindle itself would not give a true bibliophile the sensory stimulation of a bound ink on paper book, but this leather lighted cover adds a little bulk to the electronic device making it more resemble a small book in size, while providing protection and illumination. The Kindle Lighted Leather Cover is lighter in weight than I'd expected, more rigid, better constructed of a high quality beautiful leather, and ergonomically designed for every day use. With care during installation of the Kindle, I expect it to have a long life, particularly since I do not attempt to move the rear cover away from the Kindle device while it's housed. Letting it be and simply lifting the front cover to open, folding it back for reading, and returning it to the closed position for storage should keep it intact. When the front cover is folded back for reading, the round elastic band can be reversed around both front and back covers to keep them joined and make the covered Kindle easier to hold. When the case is closed, the elastic band fits into a small groove on the front of the case where the two different leather textures are seamed. I love that detail. A small leather tab can be slid along the elastic and it also can be flipped to face either right or left. I sometimes move it up or down as a hint to remember something. It has the impression, "amazon kindle," so I'm likely to remember what's in the case. The light is powerful, considering its small size, and it's very easy to pull out and push into it's corner home. It is unobtrusive and quite functional. My brain on more than one occasion guided my hand to the rear of the Kindle for the reading light and it took a few seconds for me to realize I needed to put my fingers on the case and not the Kindle. Because of its angle, the light makes the screen a bit brighter in the upper right quadrant, but my eyes quickly adjust as I read further and become immersed in the words. If I find myself thinking about the irregularity of the lighting on the screen, I go to my Home Page and select another book. I highly recommend this cover for Kindle owners who want to protect and illuminate their investment and their eyes. Once you make the decision to purchase, good luck when deciding on a color!

title: Lights cant be used with game consoles. Poor design.
text: I bought this for my son to use with his PS4. He likes how it looks and he says it's comfortable to wear but he was very upset that he's not able to make it light up. While this may not be a life or death situation, to a 10 year old who specifically picked these headphones for the "cool lights", it's a huge disappointment. Whoever designed these headphones is not the sharpest pencil in the box because the lights only come on when you plug the USB cable in. Well, considering the fact that the headphone jack for the ps4 is on the controller but the USB port is on the back of the console, that makes it pretty much impossible to plug the lights in. If i had known this, i wouldve definitely bought a different product. I'm pretty disappointed.

title: Sadly over hyped
text: The game itself is extremely linear, making it difficult to go off and exploring in between quests, everything is excruciatingly easy, and the only way to really win the game is by acquiring a ton of money via real estate. In the end, if you don't save your people, they all die and never respawn, making selling items/gear/houses impossible, and no one will rent your real estate because they are all dead. The transformation aspect of the weapon is really cheap and nothing awe inspiring, and you don't get to see your 'true form' until the very end of the game, and even then, its no where near as interesting as they were in fable 2. The new profession interface is a joke and incredibly boring. The plot itself isn't really anything all that exciting, either. Honestly, you're better off just playing Fable 2.

title: Best Star Trek Game Made Yet!
text: I have to say that this game is by far the best Star Trek game on the market. It is also one of the best first person shooter games out there.
