Like other reviewers have said though you need a good system and a great graphics card to play it. I have a 550 Amd k62 with 128 mb of ram and an ATI all in wonder 16mb video card. It is a little jerky when there are a lot of opponents in the room. It was a little smoother on my friends 1ghz Athalon with the same video card and 256 mb of ram. The single player game may be too easy for hard core game people, but for us average folks it's great game play. I'm most impressed with the multiplayer games. They run smoother graphics wise and is great fun playing on the internet or disconected. The first patch is out for this game but I have not yet downloaded it, maybe it will help with some of the jerkyness in the single player mode. This game with it's single and multiplayer options is almost like getting two games in one as the two modes are so different. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is the system requirements and some ocassional jerky graphics in single player mode.

title: Definate Click
text: As my hands age, I have been having more and more issues with keyboard fatigue. Tried many different (non-mechanical) keyboards, including ergonomic keyboards like the Logitech wave, and nothing seemed to help much. The LEOBOG had a cool name, good price, and great reviews, so I decided to give it whirl. The keys make a nice clicking sound, and provide good feedback, so it is easier to train oneself to not jam down on the keys any harder than necessary, thus minimizing unnecessary impact on the knuckle joints. Honestly, if you are having issues with your non-mechanical keyboard, I recommend picking up one of these and seeing if it helps you. At $25 it's a perfect gateway mechanical. I have worked in IT for now on 15 years, and hold a very keyboard intensive position within IT. During that time I have tried keyboards from pretty much every manufacturer, and none come close to the feel of this very reasonably priced LEOBOG It has multicolored lights like pretty much every product of Chinese manufacturers. The good news is that the review of Alyssa Wilson teaches us how to turn that stuff off. She has a big 'ol list of all the different color functions in her awesome review, but below is the one that matters the most. The solid blue is a personal favorite of mine;green is pictured because its the first one that comes up. FN+PGUP - Solid Color Backlight (FN+F8 Cycles Solid Colors)

title: Difficult key replacement
text: After purchasing two Razer Huntsman Elite key boards both had key fade after a year + of use. The company's warranty policy would not repair or replace. After much communication with the excellent service response I was told of the solution of buying the Key cap upgrade kit. The installation of the replacement keys was very difficult and the instructions not clear. The replacement is a two hour project with added confusion of keys different keys meant for US and British key boards. Once the up grade keys were installed, the problems were solved and the key board is back to use.

title: Great When They Worked
text: Issues with audio flipping and mic cutting out. Great when they worked. Had to run the mic at 100 at all times with boost for my voice to pick up. Got used to them over the course of about two years before pieces just start falling off even though they had never been dropped or mistreated. Within a week, both the mic-side cup and the right-side cup eventually just fell as the material started to wear. Tape kept it going for a while. Eventually the sound stopped coming through the mic side cup even with no real cause, as I couldn't see why material wear would also result in wear to the wire.

title: Buyer Beware
text: Lowest I can go is one star. Simply: The drivers were not recognized on Windows 10. Although the product page says these released in 2016, there was no download available for the software through digital means (only a disc -- and I was lucky enough to have a drive to quickly connect). The headset itself refused to be recognized beyond "Generic 7.1 Headset" or something approximate, even after installing the software. The latest drivers from the site (which was a .cc and not the .com stated in the documentation) did not recognize the headset even with the software installed. Likely due to the fact that Windows 10 itself did not recognize the headset. Strangely, changes the software made to the audio quality did take, even if it was only just recognized as "Generic 7.1 etc". No matter, as both recording and playback were saturated with a constant and grating static sound. I would not recommend these to a Windows 10 user. Especially not when the company FAQ suggests no interest in fixing compatibility with Windows 10. Again, this is supposedly a 2016 product.

title: Does not work on new Wii
text: Please note the following information from the Nintendo web-site if purchasing. This does not work with a new Wii. Difference Between the Models of Wii Consoles Information: Two models of the Wii console have been released: Model Number RVL-001 Released in November 2006. Model Number RVL-101 Released in October 2011. Has the same look, feel and function as model RVL-001, with the following exceptions: Designed to sit horizontally rather than vertically. The Nintendo GameCube controller sockets and memory card slots have been removed. The system is not compatible with Nintendo GameCube game discs or accessories. The system does not support Wii titles or accessories that require the use of the Nintendo GameCube controller ports. Because they require Nintendo GameCube controller ports to work, the following Wii titles are not compatible with model RVL-101: Active Life: Explorer Active Life: Extreme Challenge Active Life: Magical Carnival Active Life: Outdoor Challenge Ultimate Party Challenge The following titles will have limited functionality when used with model RVL-101: Dance Dance Revolution DanceDanceRevolution II Dance Dance Revolution: Disney Grooves DanceDanceRevolution Hottest Party DanceDanceRevolution Hottest Party 2 DanceDanceRevolution Hottest Party 3 Walk It Out

title: You've gotta get this!
text: This is the controller I use most often when playing on the SNES and NES classics (I've got both and use this with both). The top of the controller has an LED that changes to red when it needs to be charged. I've played this for many many hours without needing a charge and it hasn't cut out on me prematurely (though I do try to charge it when I'm not playing). The battery seems to last longer than the Xbox One controllers. The feel of the controller and the buttons are really really close to the official controller. No complaints at all for what it is. One thing that would make this better is a USB adapter so I could use this with a computer + emulator.

title: I'm glad they include two in the package, because I needed both of them to put it on correctly
text: The glass protector seems to be good quality. The only trouble I had with it was that it's difficult to place it correctly while also getting all the air bubbles out. The instructions included say that pressure applied should start from the center and then be worked outwards. This is extremely difficult to do while also aligning it so there is no overlap over the edges. My first attempt left a sizable air bubble that I couldn't work out to the edge, and I also managed to get a stray piece of fluff or dust under it so I removed it (which is fairly easy to do if you try, and left no residue). My second attempt was much better and I'm happy with the result. You can barely tell there's a protector on there now. With the protector I removed, I decided to break it just to see how strong it was and it took about a 30-40 degree bend before shattering and putting glass dust everywhere. Seems like it would really protect the screen and I'm glad I have it. I think this product could be improved by some other guiding strips or something to help with centering, so that the hands are free to start applying pressure from the center to avoid air bubbles.

title: Great product for strategy, RPG, and "long hours" gamers
text: Serious gamers who spend long hours at the controller will definitely benefit from the xtendplay. I tend to get lost in long hours of strategy and rpg games -- guess I'm a binge gamer. The xtendplay simply makes my gaming more comfortable. I'd even go so far as to suggest it makes me burn a few calories because I now often find myself standing to play with the xtendplay propped against my stomach. You kind of forget about the fact that you have it once you've got one, it's just there as a new part of your controller, but I really notice that I can game longer, and more comfortably. Whether longer hours of gaming is a good thing in your life is something you have to decide for yourself, but if you want to game longer one of these will help.

title: Mmm great graphics BUT typical MS programming
text: OK so after my first session playing... the graphics are astounding, the game play is a little realxing but fun, its sort of Nox meets Unreal and pretends to be Diablo. But its crashes about once an hour (on a 1ghz Athlon, raid, 32MB ATI, 128MB CAS 2) irregardless of settings. And when I say crash, I mean crash, its brings not only the game but also my usually impervious win2k system to its knees. No task manger, no reset, hard power cycle only!! I dont remeber any of the Diablos crashing ever, or the Baldur's Gates... typical Microsoft, releasing something late and expensive and unfinished! There are tons of cool ideas in this game but its a bit like the original arcade Dragon's Lair once the wow factor is over you have to live with the limitations... Everyone should see this game but I wouldn't reccomend anyone actually buy it. If you're short of cash (or sensible about such things) then wait for Neverwinter Nights - most likely a much better investment...

title: Sadly don't fit in the New Nintendo 3DS
text: My son lost his Nintendo 3DS stylus on an airplane on a recent trip. We searched all around his seat and it was nowhere to be found. So he found these replacement styluses and we ordered them instead of others by non Nintendo makers. We thought since these would fit because they were made for the Nintendo 3DS. Sadly these do not fit his device and must be for older versions. I guess it's a good thing they come in a 3-pk because I could see losing them since they don't fit inside of the 3DS and you have to carry them separately.

title: Great package deal!
text: I bought this for my husband for Christmas and he absolutely loves it! He's been playing with the PS3 and the Force Unleashed game regularly. We set up a router so now my husband can access game features on the internet and even play with other players. I love that the PS3 has a blue-ray player and a very easy to use remote. We've watched a few movies on it already and they look and sound amazing! I would recommend getting a second controller for the PS3. He got a few other games and some of those require a 2nd player for certain levels. He's now sucked me into a few of his games and that 2nd controller will come in very handy. We love that the controller is cordless. It makes it so much easier to play and move around the room. It charges through the PS3 and hold the charge for quite some time.

title: Fun simple game
text: I picked up this game because of the low price and I wanted a filler inbetween some of the Nancy Drew games I like to play. The ND games are very addictive so I thought this might be a simple game that didn't involve too much thinking and would be something to have on hand to play every now and then. Well this game is very addictive and I've only had it a week and I'm almost done with it. It really is a lot of fun. My husband saw me playing and then got into it himself. He's been avoiding it lately because when you start to play, you get hooked and lose track of time. The good thing about this game is even if you finish the actual game, there is a mode where you can just do endless play that allows to keep going until you lose 4 customers. This records your high score and you can keep playing till you get a higher one. You could acutally do the same with the main game play as well because it keeps adding up the total amount taken in at the restaurant through each level. There is a certain amount you are supposed to earn each level and once you hit that mark, you can try and reach the expert part and that gives you a start for that level. I only got a few stars and there were 2 levels that were so difficult and frusterating that I was just so happy to be past them and didn't care if I reached the expert level or not. Overall this is a really cute fun little game for all ages. I'm 34 and really enjoy playing it.

title: Fun and challenging
text: This was the first Nancy Drew game I played and it got me hooked. My husband was walking by during one of the puzzles I was trying to solve and he sat down to see what it was about and ended up playing the entire game with me. We both found this game to be very challenging and addictive. This is a great game for all ages although it might be a little scary for some youngsters. One thing that we found amusing about this game was a little hidden text. There is a challenge where you will go downstairs to a room (kind of like a lab) and read some letters and notes. This is towards the end of the game. The main part you are supposed to read is darker than the rest of the text. If you strain and read the lighter text, you will see some interesting things there. It's been a while since we played it so I don't remember the exact text but it had to do with views towards the current president. We thought it was amusing that the writer/programmer put that in there. Overall a great game with some difficult puzzles.

title: Avoid this finicky turd. I have to unplug and replug it all the time.
text: If you're just charging one controller, it's probably fine. But I play 2-player games with my nephew every day, so every day, I have some kind of issue with this turd. If you're charging two controllers, you have to absolutely baby this thing. The method below avoids the flickering charging error about 75% of the time: - Turn off the light! It will eventually turn itself back on, so you will be turning the light off all the time. But having the light off reduces the chances of the charging error. - Put one charger in. - WAIT. - Put the second charger in. IDK how long, but wait first. If you try to put two recently used controllers on this thing at the same time with the light on, be prepared to unplug it and do this whole process several times until it accepts the controller without flickering out. I'm just going to buy the original PS charging dock at this point because I'm tired of returning crap charging stations.

title: A great mouse but not for me, not full-time anyway
text: I had high hopes for this mouse and wanted to love it. I will probably keep it, but it won't be my main mouse. Pros: * It is heckin' adjustable! I wasn't expecting thumb depth to even be a thing. — The clickable side is adjustable to a higher angle than any of my other vertical mouses. — Thumb tilts in several directions, moves forwards and backwards (closer and further away from your palm), and it's possible to pull the thumb rest out further from the clicky side. Cons: * It still feels really large for my hand. — I can adjust to a good shape, but I feel like I barely have hold of it and it's going to slip out of my hand at any moment. — Something about trying to grab it with my widdle hands means I often click accidentally when I don't want to and end up accidentally closing out windows. Oops! — Also sometimes when I lose my grip on it, the thumb rest moves out of place. Maybe my hands are just too messed up to use mice any more. It's a real possibility. * It's not silent. I know it wasn't advertised as silent, but I have gotten used to silent mice, and kind of expect that now. So no false advertising or anything, but I prefer silent clicks. * I feel like it needs a skirt or some part protruding out the back for my hand to rest on. I don't like vertical mice with giant skirts, but a not toward a skirt might help me feel like I'm gripping it better. * What the heck even with the middle button. This is maybe a "just me" thing. But I'm not used to middle buttons, and I keep hitting the middle button when I want to right-click, and DISASTER. I tried to reprogram the buttons with X-Mouse button control, and it fixed it sure enough, but then it messed up all of my other mice. [Edit: I set both middle and right buttons to right-click, so no more problem there, I guess.] Oh yeah, time out: I have to alternate through a bunch of mice due to various RSIs, so having to reprogram buttons is no bueno for me. Also maybe a sign the mouse is too big for my hands. So I doubt I'll send it back and will keep it for arm pain flare-ups, but it's not worth $80 *to me*. The concept is gold, and with some tweaking and maybe actual different size options, the product itself could be outstanding. Maybe with more use I'll get used to it. Le sigh.

title: Boring and repetitive
text: I love Sims games, but this one is by far the worst I've ever played. Compared to other sim games, this one is very shallow in terms of the plot and goals. It's highly repetitive (as other reviewers have described as well) as you have to feed and pet animal after animal, area after area, without much else to do. I gave up halfway through because it was becoming so tedious. The graphics and navigation movements are quite crude considering the year this was put out. Also, the rough way the controls are set up to accomodate using the Wii controller (and the wrist movements you have to make to collect and plant seeds, and pet the animals), your hand and wrist can become painful and sore, almost like carpal tunnel. If you are looking for a cute Sims game, My Sims Kingdom is 10 times better. If you are looking for a fun animal sim game, Viva Pinata is unbeatable.

title: Lovable Cards
text: After playing my own game included with the New 3ds, I don't feel there is any pressing need for the amiibo cards, since the game itself isn't that deep, and the character's will eventually show up. I made a mistake on the placement of Katt's house. I didn't realize at the time that I could move it later, so turned it off. When I restarted, I was sad to discover Katt was not there, but other character's were. Maybe this could be used to get your favorite villagers without using the cards. It's my understanding that only the special character's, like Nook, Isabelle, etc., need the amiibo cards if you desire to decorate their homes. I have purchased a lot of the amiibo cards, but have not felt the need to use one with the game yet. I guess I just don't care enough to use the cards, maybe later. We haven't even played the game in a few days. The Animal Crossing amiibo cards really are cute. My daughter decided she'd like to collect the set. This has proven to be more of a challenge than I realized. I refuse to pay more than retail for an expensive game add on. I would have liked the option to purchase the complete set as a whole. The last 6-card set I bought only had one card that wasn't a duplicate. I already regret getting caught up it the collecting. I've spent enough money already. After purchasing 21 sets so far from various stores, I'm about to call it quits. At least I haven't paid more than retail for them. Just be patient, it's not like they won't be restocked.

title: Yay!! Smaller New 3ds!!
text: Finally, we in the U.S. get to buy the New Nintendo 3ds. We had been looking forward, planning on getting this smaller size since it was announce. It came as a huge disappointment when we learned we would not be able to purchase this size after all. After using them I can happily say we are pleased with the smaller size. It's convenient for carrying if you have a smaller purse. I like the lighter feel of it in my hands. The cover plates are definitely fun! The only down side is for those that weren't interested in purchasing the game, or the cover plates. Having to spend $220.00 is a high price for anyone only interested in the New 3ds. It's really not a big deal for us because we love Animal Crossing so much. Of course, the new included game can not compare to the original Animal Crossing game, but it's enjoyable for what it is. We would love to see some of the things from ACHHD included in the next true Animal Crossing game.

title: Fun Little Side Game to Pass the Time
text: This is a cute, enjoyable game, if a little boring after a while. Designing character's houses, inside and out is fun, but it's not nearly as great as the original Animal Crossing game. It'd would make a nice add on for the next true Animal Crossing installment. This bundle deal is the best way to purchase if you're interested in the amiibo reader because of the savings. As for the game itself, I'd give it a three star because it's overpriced for the type of game it is. I'd have felt better a lot better about my purchase if Nintendo would have charged $29.99. If not for this bundle deal, I would have waited for a sell price later.

title: Disappointed Overall
text: My daughter and I ordered the digital downloads directly from Nintendo's eShop, plus two pre-orders from Amazon to give as gifts. After playing my game for 15 minutes I was wishing I hadn't downloaded it because now I'm stuck with it. I can't give it away, and I can't trade it in or resell it. Only option we have is to play, and make the best of it. But I will be spending the $5.95 to return the two unopened games to Amazon. We have played the two previous ds games and loved them both, the 2nd was better than the first one. Because of our experience we were very excited to play the new 3ds release. There have been many changes made, some good, but more bad. The graphics are a nice improvement, and being able to play with in-game friends is a welcome addition. We think it's cute having Nibbles, the vivosaur follow you around. We feel they have made what used to be a fun game very annoying, and more juvinile. The instructions are a little vague at times. The Bone Buggies, while nice, are harder to control. I realize that further in the game there are upgrades that improve this, but it will take some practice, patience, and feelings of frustration at the time wasted trying to maneuver into the position you want to go. We don't like how you only have one chance at digging up a fossil. Meaning you can't save before you clean a fossil in case you want to retry again. But it can be convenient because you don't have to keep going back to clean them when your pockets are full. It's nice that the jewels you find are automatically sold too. Also, we do not like that they took away the ability to see where you are on the main Park. The bottom screen shows the map, but now there is no dot on the map making it easy to know where you are, and where you want to go. I found that convenient, and used it all the time on the other games. It takes getting used to this change, and wish it was still available. One last thing I want to point out is there is no way we think this game should be compared to Pokemon. It is my opinion it's being compared as a selling tactic because of Pokemon's popularity. The Pokemon games are a favorite with our friends and family.

title: Good, but flawed product
text: Pros: 1. It's kind of like playing real guitar with rock band 3 2. It seems sturdy, I've been wailing on it for a month now and It's still working. 3. It's wireless with batteries included 4. No restringing or tuning frustrations like with real guitar. Cons: 1. Strings don't extend up the fretboard, so there's no physical correlation between what you're picking and what fret you are pressing. 2. All buttons are the same height, no physical difference between the top "string" and the bottom "string". 3. Only 17 frets, the neck is 2 inches shorter than my gibson. 4. Strings are plastic, and make an awful scratching noise when you pick them. 5. I don't want to think about what will happen if one of the 100s of buttons stops working or if one of the strings breaks. 6. No string bending, pinch harmonics, or pick scratching are detected by the game. I've had a lot of fun with this game over the past few weeks. I've been playing it several hours a day using only this controller. Using the controller and the game I've learned a lot of songs that I otherwise would not have bothered with, such as Rock Lobster, Whip It, and Stayin' Alive. Skills learned playing Rock band 3 translate over to playing real guitar, but I think you do need a real guitar to get the most out of this. Many times I can't figure out what I'm trying to play in Rock Band without banging it out with the real guitar first. It's just too frustrating trying to figure out what you're pressing and what you're picking, especially when playing arpeggios or guitar solos. In a way, the mustang is kind of like playing two different instruments with each hand. I plan to buy the Fender Squier that is coming out in March, but I had to get my hands on this game. I do not regret buying it and I will continue to play it, but when the Squier comes out I'm not going to use it anymore.

title: Love this game wish there were more.
text: I read all of the reviews before I decided to get this game. I too, like Deepak Chopra and I was excited to find this game. Some reviews said they got more and more frustrated with each level and found they had to make wild movements to get the game to work. I didn't find that to be the issue for me at all. I have found this to be a very relaxing game and I feel calm and centered after playing it. There is a playing mode and and reflection mode for meditation. On the play mode each level is centered on the chakras starting at the root chakra and moving up. You have a planet that rotates and from the center comes a colored spore that gives birth to a tree or mushroom. Before you start the level you see your mandala begin to pulse in and out and set you breathing to this rhythm, this is also the same rhythm for the remote for the side to side motion to rotate the planet. And each level progresses in this manner. The point is to cultivate relaxation, the more relaxed you are the easier it is to play the game. I have noticed that when I play other games I don't get so riled up and I can stay calm and relaxed which does make it easier to play and retry a level without frustration. Good tool for the rest of life as well. Knowing this helps to keep the focus in the game. Once you have gone through the play levels on all the chakras the free style meditation is unlocked, otherwise if you choose the reflection side you have only the guided meditation that is unlocked. I have found these to be very helpful to start my practice again. I sit in a regular chair not on the floor. If I sit on the floor I use a pillow folder over to get the height and stability needed. I find it works just as well. I am pleased with this game and I continue to use it since I am gaining great benefit from it in all areas of my life. To help me relax I have incorporated an adrenal support that aids in relaxation and have found this has helped immensely.

title: Average MMO, but still fun.
text: I played this game for a few months. It was ok, but it's a pretty average MMO. It didn't do anything different and I wasn't satisfied with its art. It was sort of cool, but I don't get why everyone is acting like stuff like WoW has never been done before. WoW is nice in the way that people can pick it up, play it, and learn the basics within the first few hours. However, it just seemed pretty average to me. While it is a nice MMO and is, in my opinion, much better than Everquest 2, it just is..repetative. I found it boring and quite frankly pointless. I found Guild Wars to be much better.

title: The Ultimate MMORPG!!!
text: Hello! This game really impressed me! First off, NCsoft was very generous in whiich they give you every expansion away for free! Lineage 2, unlike Everquest, has assigned quests. Most of them are just going around killing things, but it never gets old! It has great graphics, cool worlds, and a great character selection. Ok, it takes forever to get "leveled up" but it's worth it! A lot of people never wait to get into the cool stuff. There are castle sieges, and there are huge bosses! However, the down side is that there are a lot of "player killers" that hunt down newbies. Usually PKers get killed before they cause any harm, but it's always good to be careful! In overall, this game is pretty satisfying. I'd give it 5 stars. No true gamer can go without playing this! P.S. Most of these people writing the reviews are just noobs. They aren't far enough in the game to know what the good stuff is!

title: A great protector, or how I learned to banish dust particles from my Switch
text: Intro As we all know, the Switch comes with a plastic screen. Whether it was to save money, or to make a more durable product, a plastic screen is obviously very easy to scratch up. This was especially true as putting the Switch inside the dock could easily cause the screen to rub against the side of the dock. Thus, I went ahead and bought this screen protector. It was one of the best reviewed ones at the time, and also one of the best deals, and I am very happy with the purchase. Durability I haven't had any issues with durability. I haven't dropped my Switch, but I've taken it on many trips and have yet to see any scratches. Fit The fit is very good on the protector. It fits over the entire glossy black area on the switch, including the bezels around the screen itself. Clarity I haven't had an issue with this. Most of the time I don't even notice the screen being there. Application Process I read through some reviews and many people were having trouble with installation. Since it's such a large screen it's a lot easier to get dust under the protector - one of my pet peeves. My process was to remove any towels and carpets from my bathroom and to steam it up and to do some minor cleaning. Then I sat down with the switch on a table in the bathroom and cleaned the switch and protector carefully with rubbing alcohol to remove dirt and discharge static. I practiced some dry runs, and then used some canned air to blow dust off the switch and then quickly checked for dust, removed the backing on the protector, and applied it immediately. This resulted in no dust on the first try, which was great. I have seen that the Switch itself could also be bent a little (it seems like a common problem), so if yours is bent you might have some trouble applying it. In that case it might be better to get a plastic protector. Conclusion Overall, a great product and highly recommended. The fact that they include two is an even better bonus in case you break one or fail on an application attempt.

title: But i think it's better than using Illegal drugs OR having a hobby of ...
text: WARNING: PLEASE DO NOT get this video game console unless that you're sure you know what you're in for! title: "My Nephew Loves This game!"
text: I bought this game because my dear nephew is insisting to have it and I told him I want to see good grades from him and he promised me he would. About 2 weeks later he showed me his graded assignments and he's bragging that he got good grades so i bought this from Amazon. A day later we got it and he never stopped playing it the minute I handed to him until later that night, I needed to pry him out and threatened to take it back if he didn't stop playing it and prepared himself for the next school day. A great game for the xbox!

title: A great video game !
text: I bought this as a gift for my nephew in law's son who i babysit. He's 11 years old & has been playing Black Ops every single passing day for the last 9 Months and now was begging me to buy him this game as an early Christmas gift to w/c i bought one of these from Amazon and since I'm a Prime member, i got the game overnight. Right now, the kid is playing it, I cannot even say anything because he says that I'm distracting him so iI can't watch T.V. downstairs and this kid is gulping Red bull energy drink right & left and he's planning an overnight stay and camp out in front of our couch fro the next 2 days playing this damn game! it's a good thing that this kid lives only 15 feet from our house.Needless to say that I'm happy for him playing this game but I'm really concerned as well for he's trying to stay awake for a game marathon about this. He says he love this game so i wholeheartedly recommend it (Hell what does a 51 year old man know anything about video games these days? When i was his age, I was playing with a paddle w/ a rubble ball with a long string attached to it).

title: Good for Left-Handed Gamers!
text: This mouse originally came with my RoG G74S a couple of years ago. It's seen a LOT of heavy use, has traveled around the country with me, been dropped, been spilled on and the original now has one button that's a tad "sticky". As a left handed gamer/mouser with long hands/fingers, this has been the best mouse I've ever used. It fits nicely in my hand and because of the placement of the side buttons, I can use them easily with my ring finger. I appreciate that it doesn't have teeny tiny buttons too small for even toddler fingers to press singly, but rather nice sized buttons that won't having accidentally casting (and wasting) a spell/ability. The new RoG mouse doesn't feel the same in my hand and has different button placement - it may have been a matter of being used to this one and not giving the new mouse enough play time to get used to it, but I switched back to this mouse and ordered a 2nd for when this one bites the dust.

title: Unplayable and boring
text: I bought this game because I loved New Super Mario and wanted to find another game I found addictive. First of all, this game is for little kids. But I can't imagine anyone enjoying it. It seems like it has no point. Sonic speeds through this "roller coaster" type course that goes so quickly it's not possible to follow. And there is nothing really to do. There is no challenge value, all you do it push the forward button and sonic moves really quickly until he gets to the end of the course or runs out of time. Maybe I missed the point of this game, but I wasted my money on this purchase.

title: Quite possibly the world's first perfect video game system
text: Why on earth would anyone buy anything else in terms of a system? The point is, Wii gets you off the couch and requires you to socialize! This system is for multiple people! And it's fun! You are not wasting away exercising your fingers here. You are actually up and jumping around, it's incredibly fun to play wii tennis with a friend. This is a very social system, and is really what video games have been missing. Between playing a long, solitary game that requires me to expend no energy, and playing the wii which is unbelievable work of accomplishent on nintendo's part. I think the graphics are fantastic from what I've seen, and most importantly, everyone -- even people who don't like video games -- loves to play it.

title: Some fun games but doesn't match Club House
text: This is a great game and the Texas Hold'em Poker is a lot of fun to play. It's not a big deal that some of the games are locked, if you are losing, you can just turn off the system and restart, and then you can only elect to save once you've earned enough money to unlock the more advanced levels. There are even some things I like about Sega Casino more than Club House, like the Texas Holdem game seems to go faster and I like that you can bet all your money at once, as opposed to Club House. However, overall Sega Casino is 4 starts compared to Club House's 5 stars in my ratings book. If you are choosing between, I'd go for Club House.

title: Great controller for the price!
text: This is the best generic PS3 controller I've had so far. I love the fact that it's a WIRED controller, because I don't have to worry about charging. It's definitely lighter in weight compared to the Sony Dualshock PS3 controller. The only thing is, sometimes when I press the left arrow on the D-pad, the upper arrow also reacts. Also, the joysticks are not as sensitive, so you might wanna tweak with the settings if you play shooting games and such. I'm planning on getting another one because when I bought it about the year ago it was $14.99, now it's only $10. It's also pretty darn durable.

title: I really like this keyboard, despite...
text: The fact that I should have chosen one that required more actuation force. I discovered (again, I have had this problem with other keyboards that I've liked, too) that when typing and occasionally pausing for thought, I rest my fingers very lightly on the home keys. This can cause me to look at what I've resumed typing on the screen and finding a string of one of the home keys spread across the line like ;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;; which of course is easy to correct. Just go into Settings for the keyboard and increase the period before it auto-repeats when a key is held down. I can't find the home keys by touch easily yet, but that'll come with use: the bumps on the F and J keys could be a little larger to help me there. I used the keyboard's configuration software to program the "Pause" key to be a single touch "sleep" key, which works for me very nicely. The lighting level can be adjusted so that it works for you; this is extremely helpful to the comfort level at having lit keys.

title: It works well and is decorative, too
text: A very good mouse, does everything it needs to do quite smoothly and without trouble. However, I use a bead-type wrist rest with it that causes me a completely unexpected problem: when I am playing a game or doing "photoshopping", I become so intent that I grip the mouse tightly. This means that as I move the mouse towards the heel of my hand, I sometimes lift it unknowingly and the mouse stops, of course. I have learned that for such situations, have to work without the wrist rest and then there are no problems. The default RGB is very nice, gradually changing without calling attention to its slow changes.

title: Much nicer keyboard than I thought it would be
text: This is a great keyboard, it is a bit smaller than what I was used to and it felt strange at first because it is shorter, but so far, it's been working out great for me. The light up feature wasn't a huge draw for me, having the lights under the keys doesn't make it any easier to see the keys when it's dark out, but it is really pretty and I like that. My hands seemed almost too big for this keyboard, but I quickly adjusted to the shorter size and in fact, my fingers and wrist felt less strained after writing a few pages of text. The pictures show how a users size is in comparison to the keyboard. My cat Lana really loves this keyboard, she tried to sit on it multiple times no matter how often my husband and I objected. This isn't a great portable option mostly because it weighs more than a regular keyboard. Also it is a bit louder than the apple keyboard that I use most of the time. But there is something satisfying about all the loud clickyness of this keyboard.

title: Excellent keyboard
text: I have lots of positive things to say about this mechanical gaming keyboard 1. The keys arent too sensitive which is a good thing since it makes it harder to fat finger them and do something wrong ingame 2. The keys have a reasonable amount of space between them which means I don't have to be really accurate when typing or doing stuff ingame. 3. The lighting under the keys and the colors of the keyboard in general make it really easy to see the keys as opposed to some LED lit keyboards i've had in the past where the lighting feels too dim or too difficult to see because of the reflected color of the LED lights. 4. But my personal favorite thing about this keyboard is that this is very compact,it has the number pad, the F1-F12 keys, but it is still compact enough that I can fit it really well on my desk along with my wrist pad and a large mousepad. I've had trouble in the past (since I keep my mouse very close to my keyboard 90% of the time) with having the edge of the keyboard, which normally juts out at an odd angle, end up pressing against the mouse which forces me to click it again. This was an ongoing problem with my last keyboard and it's really good that I don't have that happen now with how well this keyboard fits on my desk. Now for some negatives; Just one, I'm not a huge fan of yellow, I wish this came in a nicer color.

title: This is my first gaming mouse even though I've bought a few before
text: I am not the big gamer in my household, that would be my son. I got pretty into minecraft, Dont Starve Together, Mass Effect and Mortal Combat, but other than those games, I wasn't really a gamer. But, like I said, I've bought a few gamer mice for my son and even one for my husband. So, for me this is a totally new experience and I'm happy to say it has improved my enjoyment of games. I feel like it is a bit quicker and that it doesn't overshoot the mark the way my old cordless mouse would. Also, this lights up! I've never had a mouse that has a light iin it and ists strange but sometimes it feels like it knows I need or it to stay lit. The roller ball action is super duper sensative, I feel like I've been handed a pair of sharp pair of scissors after spending my life tearing things with my hands! Anyways, since I only play a few games, the mouse been used for just normal, non gaming stuff; emails, clicking, double clicking, you know the like.

title: Great for moist hands
text: Just a few things about this silicon cover; 1. It says two in the package but I received only one. I like it so much I gave it 5 stars anyways, no reason to rate it downward but its important to know if you want to cover more than one controller. 2. Easy installation - I had a painful burnt finger so I got my kid to put the cover on this controller and it was quick and simple. 3. My hands are weirdly moist now. Maybe it's all the pandemic lockdown handwashing and then moisturizing but ten minutes of gaming and the controller feels as slippery as a pumpkin seed. Its gross and I want it to stop. This cover is keeping me from dropping it. 4. I like the cover, it adds a dollop of color to an otherwise dull white controller, like a sportscar with a bra (is that what those leathery front covers were called, bras?). 5. Inexpensive - I got it for free, to review, but I'm going to buy a second fo my other controller.

title: Great new mouse
text: Things I like about this mouse; 1. It has cool glowy lights that glow at a slow, pulsing rate that makes it look like the mouse is an insect that is breathing (think the iratus bug from Stargate Atlantis). They cycle through yellow to purple and blue. 2. It didn't require any software installation 3. It has a super long cord, in case that is something you like or need. 4. The mouse wheel is like a lego tire with a very grippy tread. 5. The mouse has a good shape and all the butons have good click action, the side buttons have forward and back motion and this is the first time ive seen it before, a dpi sensitivity switch that cycles through several dpi settings. 6. You can't change the pulse rate of the lights or turn off the light (someone said in a review that you can turn it off by holding down the button, not sure if that is true, because it isn't working for me with this mouse). But the lights are so amazingly pretty that I don't even care. Things I don't like about this mouse; 1. I would like the option to change or turn off the lights sometimes, but this a minor issue and hardly affects my overall joy with this great little mouse.

title: Nice upgrade
text: This is a gift for my son, he's a gamer, he really likes it. It seems a bit more responsive than his previous mouse. The added responsiveness really eliminates lag and makes gameplay more accurate. So far he hasn't done much programming of the mouse because the standard settings are working pretty great for him with this newer version of Doom (he's been playing it nonstop for a week now). As for the ergonomics, the curved shape is nice and the mouse is pretty lightweight, he does still get thumb fatigue, but I don't think there is any way around that.

title: Great product
text: This bluetooth controller works great. It was, very responsive and there is zero set up, you just pop it on and go. My only concerns are that the holder will work but it doesn't feel as secure as I'd like, as if it could slip off or that the phone could fall out. Very disconcerting. I used it to play minecraft, which was very fun and a bit easier with the controller. Then I combined it with a handsfree cellphone carrier (Don't Judge), called 'Flexible Long Arms Stand Clip Holder,Hanging on Neck Universal Mobile Phone Stand Lounger's Bracket for Mobile Phone' and I sat in my recliner and read a book on my phone and used the bluetooth to flip pages in the book. It was surprisingly comfy and other than looking like a lazy slacker, relaxing.

title: Wonderful Quality, no pinching or sweatiness
text: These are very comfortable for gamers or anyone else who wears a headset for more than two hours straight. The sound quality was good enough for me to hear whispers and to really feel the action. Sweating - I've had a problem with getting a hot, sweaty ear and it was distracting and in one instance, gave me an ear infection. Since then I've been hyper alert to this potential problem. Somehow I think these headphones will not cause that problem. The noise cancellation is really amazing, I was wearing these outside while waiting for the bus and I didn't even hear the bus arrive and then it was leaving without me!

title: Swamp ear
text: These are the nicest headphones I've ever experienced. Here's what I liked about them. 1. Sound quality. I didn't realize how tinny and flat my old ones were until I tried these. I guess part of the difference is the tight suction over the ears that blocks out everything or it could be the speakers. 2. Durability. Well, I've been using them for a month, once I sat on them, black headphones on a black seat! But they are still working and I haven't managed to break the speaker, perfection! Here's what I don't like. 1. Hot Ear. I haven't run out to buy canned air or tried my hand at inventing cooling gel ear muffs, but so far I can't wear these for more than an hour at a time without getting super sweaty hot ears. It's sorta swampy and gross like spandex butt, 'cept its on your head. The headphones really clamp down on your head and sometimes the tension can make my head hurt. But other than the head pain and itchy swamp ear, these are pretty great. Good luck!

title: Nice
text: Pretty nice mouse. I'm not a super gamer, in fact, I only play a few games; Spore and Mortal Kombat. Anyways, since I only play for an hour or two a week, I only notice a few differences, that it requires just a whisper of movement to use and that you have to be careful not to brush against all the extra buttons. My son is the super gamer, he likes Team Fortress, Portal, Spore, Five Nights at Freddies, Goat Simulator, etc. He says this mouse is a super upgrade from the cheapie mouse he used before. He says his game play has been chiller and he 'own's' the world. Honestly, I don't really get it, for me the mouse seems almost the same but for all the different buttons.

title: 4 year old grandson loves it.
text: My grandson is 4 YEARS 7 MONTHS. He had been quickly bored with my Wii games. He loves the Wii Excite. He loves it because I have a wheel, and he can steer it like the games at an arcade (Pizza place, bowling alley). He loves it because there are no rules. He can constantly crash into trees, go off cliffs, and sink in water. No problem. The game allows you to keep going and even awards points for good crashes. In other words, he loves it because he can have fun playing, without having a clue what he is doing. It's a great game for youngsters. It's also fun for anyone else that likes truck racing games.

title: Great game for all ages. Takes seconds to learn.
text: Retiree here. This is my first video pinball. I was a pinball addict 50 years ago, but am not familiar with these games. Received it today, and played it for 2 hours. It's outstanding, and really is a must purchase for anyone having a Wii. Takes seconds to learn and entertaining for anyone. There is one negative. I have HDTV, and the Nintendo component cables, but found the graphics more blurry (less in focus), than other games. I suspect this is caused by the need to have a tremendous amount of detailed graphics, of many different colors, in a very compact area. I do have my Wii and TV set to the proper resolution. Other games, such as MLB Pro, and Super Swing 2 have great graphics, considering the Wii does not come in high definition. That said, the entertainment value of this game more than makes up for this deficiency, and it is still a must have game.

title: Long manual. Takes time to learn.
text: Update: Followed discussion advice and purchased a classic controller. It made the game much more enjoyable for me. As a newbie, I didn't realize the classic controller plugs into the nunchuck slot, so I still have a totally wireless connection. Original review: Retiree here. This is my first baseball video game. I am using the Wimote/Nunchuck only. In the easiest modes, this is very entertaining. The wimote mode is fun. It's great seeing every major league park, in excellent detail. Rather than repeat earlier reviews, I'll add a few things. I find hitting very difficult. I went to the practice mode to practice hitting, and I still have a tough time, lining up the sweetspot with a fast moving baseball. The fielding is starting to come together. I'm going to stick with it because the graphics are good, and the game has great potential. I gave it 5 stars because I didn't want to penalize it for my shortcomings. I would appreciate any tips.

title: Nice game for 4-8 age group.
text: Retiree here. I just purchased and played the easiest version of each minigame. I purchased this so that my 4 1/2 year grandson could have an easy game. Rayman was too difficult. He found Endless Ocean boring. Though this game does require some use of the buttons in all minigames, (at least if you want a good score), it will still be his favorite game. Tetherball and slot cars are probably the easiest game. Dodgeball is probably the most fun, but more difficult. Wallball is a nice game, but like dodgeball, on the more difficult side (for a 4 year old). I would rate each minigame in the package, entertaining. I think it's a nice 4 star game. Simple games with minimal instructions can be very nice. Another plus. I think he can play this game without damaging the TV or himself. Update: My grandson now plays and loves slot car racing.

title: A golf game that makes you laugh. Not for serious golfers.
text: Retiree here. After reaching pro level on Wii golf, I wanted to play a different golf game. The same course (Wii golf) is too repetitive. I agree with the other 2 reviews posted to date. Just purchased it, have played for 2 hours, and will update this ASAP. It's a fun game with very good graphics. I have not read the directions yet, (like to jump in and play first), and found swinging confusing until I realized how it works. You lift your club until the blue line on the power bar, equals the distance you need to drive. Totally different than Wii golf, and should not be confused with a real golf match game. However, there is enough golf, and interesting scenery, to satisfy my desire for a second game. This game is a sleeper, and will get much more playing time than some other titles I have reviewed. While Miis are not used, the characters are a definite plus. They are lifelike humans, rather than cartoonish. When you have some winnings, you take your character to the clubhouse, and dress them as you like. The costumes range from conservative to highly suggestive. I wasn't able to purchase the new clothing, but I was able to change my character into the different outfits. Initially, you only have a choice of 2 characters. I am using Hanah, a cute and personable girl of about 20. She has a cute voice. Based on my initial 3 hole practice round (done 4 times until my first birdie), I expect to put quite a few hours on this game. This is my update. I have now read the directions. Marginal help. Then I went through the tutorial again. I was making a lot of mistakes. You need to go through the tutorial a second time. It means more after you have played. You can change the direction of your putts and drives, just like Wii golf. The special shots are fun. I just finished 3 more hours of play. The game is addictive, once you understand it. You have to like humor. I like Rayman Rabbits. I think 8 years and up is an appropriate age level. Girls 8+ will especially like the different costumes and accessories available. Boys will just like the game play. It's also great for adults. I'm a retiree. The key is to go through the tutorial several times. Once before you play. then at least once after you have played for 1-2 hours. I was initially frustrated before I went back to the tutorial. I think this is a great game and will be playing it quite a bit.

title: Why can't they make a decent sized bag for the price?
text: I purchased this bag to keep my Wii games and nunchucks in. I wanted an attractive bag in my family room, next to my Wii. I realize that is not the intended purpose of this bag. It is so small that with my 6 games (in plastic cases), and two nunchucks, it barely closes. The cardboard cased Links Crossbow and Wii Sports fit in the front pocket. Instruction manuals don't fit. Hoped my extra two guest wimotes would fit. No chance. The quality of the bag is fine. It looks nice. For the prices charged on Wii goods, give us some value. I wish I went I went to the local bowling alley and purchased a child's bowling bag to keep my Wii accessories in. They are $15, larger, and more attractive. The bag is not large enough for its intended purpose. I usually give high ratings. See my reviews. Not on this mini.

title: A nice pleasant game. Priced right.
text: Retiree here. This is a relaxing game, and priced right at $29.99. Probably would have been dissapointed if the price was higher. For a relatively low price, this is a relaxing game for anyone, and highly educational for youngsters. Very nice for occasional play. After spending some time with this game, I plan to take my 4 year old grandson to the local acquarium, and then let him play the game. He will enjoy it after visiting the aquarium, not before. As a skin diver (not scuba diver), I consider this game realistic, and it brought back memories of skindiving in Hanuma Bay, Hawaii.

title: You will burst out laughing.
text: Retiree here. My rating is based entirely on the laugh factor. Being new to gaming, I am slowing progressing through the levels. Made it to the hedgehog race, but failed it four times. Many of the games frustrate me, but the laugh factor keeps me going. Good graphics, nice games. As a senior, I recognize the value of this game. It forces you to use, increase and maintain hand/eye coordination, and timing. The dancing games are especially helpful. Some of the other Rayman Rabbid minigames have increased my heartrate to 125. That adds worthwhile aerobic exercise to the game's other pluses. Too difficult for my four year old grandson. One negative. My wife doesn't play this game, but she leaves the room whenever I play it. The dancing game makes her dizzy (just being in the room when I play it bothers her). If you have a problem where fast dancing/flashing lights/quick though pleasant music bothers you, do not buy this game. See my review of Rayman 2.

title: Enjoyable. Generates laughter like Rayman 1.
text: Retiree here (retired CPA, Professor). New to gaming. Started with my Wii purchase, Dec 31, 2007). I play these games solo. Wife won't play them (other than Wii Sports-she's addicted to that one). I'm really enjoying Rayman 1, so I purchased this one. I find this game more relaxing than Rayman 1, because it's easier to progress. If I was a hard core gamer, I'd be dissapointed. I enjoy playing in the different countries. I am 60+, have difficulty progressing in Rayman 1, and am often frustrated. Currently bogged down in the hedgehog race. I would recommend both games for seniors. They help maintain hand/eye coordination, sense of timing, and both make you burst out laughing-if you enjoy the slapstick silly stuff. I do. My wife doesn't. I think younger children will find Rayman 2, easier to play. I'm not a hunter, but there's something about shooting rabbits with plungers, that makes your troubles go away. Own: Rayman 1 and 2. 4x4 World Circuit-another Ubisoft game. Excite Truck. Endless Ocean. Links Crossbow. Wii Play. Only Wii Play has dissapointed.

title: Addictive fun.
text: Retiree here. This is an addictive game for me. The gun is easy to load and play. Taking the silicon cover off the remote (30 seconds), is the most complicated part. In other words. Not very complicated. The shooting game is worth the purchase price. Some of the targets, (skeletons and other vile creatures), may frighten younger children and cause nightmares. This is a relaxing game to play after burning energy playing Wii Sports. For $20 (purchased one today at Best Buy, since Amazon is out til February), it is a value purchased, compared to other Wii items. Unless you hate arcade style shooting games, buy it.

title: Unique Christmas-Themed Stories of Unexpected Connections and Love!
text: In this collection of unique Christmas-themed stories there are many unexpected connections and the women find the love of their dreams despite circumstances they can't control. "A Joyous Christmas" is about an author and motivational speaker who writes books like "Me First" and "You Deserve It All." Except after her life is saved by a stranger she feels fate pulling her in a different direction. This movie deals with a lot of issues that are common during the holiday season. I felt this movie was one of the most loving and encouraging expressions of Christmas I've ever seen. All the main characters find happiness in the end. In "Romance at Reindeer Lodge" the most unlikely of things happen when the characters least expect them to. A woman wins a radio contest but ends up in freezing Vermont instead of warm Jamaica. Imagine packing all the wrong clothes. She thought she was going on a beach vacation but ends up with a lot of snow. This is a slower story with romance and holiday themes but a satisfying ending. "Rocky Mountain Christmas" was my favorite of the three movies. When a woman leaves New York to get away from her problems with her ex she doesn't realize that she is still attracting fame into her life. Even a famous actor preparing for a film role recognizes her so in some way they have one thing in common, staying out of the news while at a real ranch. Lots of things happen including a great deal of Christmas decorating, parades and ranch work with horses. But what is going to happen when Christmas is over and everyone heads home to their real jobs? As is common in many Hallmark movies the woman has a choice between the man or her job? Which will she pick this time? So if you are looking for some cozy Christmas movies these are fun. My husband even enjoyed them. Usually he can figure things out way better than I can and gives me insight into the characters and plot. He always seems to know something before I comprehend it. So it makes watching these fun. ~The Rebecca Review

title: Cute story about a writer struggling for independance
text: My main interest in this movie was the story of Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings. She is a writer who is leaving her life to pursue her writing dreams and find fulfillment in publishing a novel. Her husband is not interested in her dreams. She decides to seek solitude in an isolated orange grove in Florida. Little does she know, this will not be an ideal life. After 30 years of urban life, she is not prepared for a small Florida town. After many rejections, Marjorie finally realizes "Gothic Novels" are not her specialty. Her agent helps her see how interesting her life actually is and she begins to write about what she knows best. In the process she falls in love, makes a best-friend, helps the community by hiring everyone who lives around her to help remodel her house and fix up her orchard. Cross Creek is based on the best-selling memoirs of Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings and has some very human moments when you realize the beauty or ugliness of life. The local business man (Peter Coyote) who falls in love with her, does something so amazing. It reminded me of when my father bought my mother her first car. I only know the story, but the situation is similar. Marjorie of course is very head strong and not about to take help from another man. Until she realizes what Norton Bascomb has secretly done. Slow-paced movie that is more "cute" than "dramatic." Although, there are a few heart-wrenching moments. I thought they dwelled too long on the party, however the chocolate cake sure did look good! Only view this movie if you have chocolate cake in the house! Preferably decorated with candied orange slices. ~The Rebecca Review

title: Not as good as previous games
text: I've been playing Mario Party games for a long time and this one is disappointing. The game play is fun, but I miss the old game play style. I miss getting vending machine objects to sabotage other players. I miss choosing options for your board when you only want to play a short game with only 10 rolls. And I miss the mini games after everyone rolls. This game is just lacking. I wish they would have integrated the Amiibo play into the actual game instead of making it a side game with the same board design with different graphics for every Amiibo. Any Amiibo's that are not in the "super mario" category you can scan once a day and play a scratch card game to get points which you then use in the store. The problem is after you play 3 games on the real board you have enough points to buy almost everything. You get the unlockable characters right away instead of having to work for them. I understand that they were trying to change the game so it wasn't the same as their other games but they took out the best parts of the Mario Party series.

title: I like this one better then the original
text: I have the original for Wii which I like but always thought the screens loaded too slow and some of the games are really hard to play. The New Carnival Games took care of both those issues. It also added a ton of new games while keeping the atmosphere of the old game. It does still have ski ball and a basketball game but they are different from the old game. I like how fast the menus switch between screens and they added a much needed skip button so you can get through the graphics quicker for impatient players like myself. In every area there is also a side quest with some member of the carnival looking for an item. I haven't figured out how to get those yet though. For those who would like a list of games..they are as follows - Area - Mystic Court Arrow Shoot (archery) Gold Rush Alley Ball (ski-ball) Super Gold Rush Alley Ball (unlockable) Pool Shark Bank a Ball Fortune Teller - costs tickets Area - Mousy Lane Haunted House Lucky Clover Swish It (basketball) Super Swish It (unlockable) Gone Fishin Wheel of Cheese - costs tickets Area - Suprise Blvd. Prize Suprise - 20 tickets to pull out a prize Tractor Pull Pitch a Plate Super Pitch a Plate (unlockable) Horseshoe toss Fishbowl bounce Twist n Win (tickets) Area - Pitstop Parkway Speed Bingo Balloon Blast Target Shoot Start Your Engines Bumper Cars (unlockable) Ticket Racer (costs tickets) Area - Snapshot drive Clown Face Tic Tac Toe Under 7 over 31 Photo Booth (costs tickets) Bottle Stand Up Super Clown Face Area - Players Alley Shows your prizes and achievements.

title: Finally wireless freedom while maintaining traditional gaming expectations
text: So to answer the question at the start, Yes this is a good mouse and no wireless doesn't hold it back from maintaining gaming performance. I'm coming from an older logitech gaming mouse the G500 which I've used and enjoyed for years due to it's ergonomics and gaming performance. I've always enjoyed the G500 so this Logitech G403 does carry many of the similar ergonomics as well as overall feel. The surface of the mouse has a nice soft touch plastic which gives it a good grip as well as comfort for longer use sessions. Not having a wire is really fantastic, as that was one of the drawbacks to the G500 in that the wire would often make you feel restricted when moving the mouse in specific directions. By default the G403 does feel really light, but comes with a weight to install which I would recommend using. I've not played around with the RGB lighting as of yet, but it does cycle through a gamut of colors so you could easily tailor the colors to match your pc lighting or match an rgb keyboard. The build quality is top notch, and the cable has a nice sleeve for a clean appearance. To charge the mouse you need to connect the mouse to the cable itself and it will allow you to use the mouse as a corded option while charging if you would prefer which is a great option for Logitech to have included. The mouse is super responsive and the buttons have a satisfying click to them and I've not noticed any increased latency in games while using the mouse wirelessly. Overall I'm very satisfied with this mouse and glad that I can finally have the freedom of wireless gaming without having to sacrifice either performance or comfort!

title: Can be a two player game - awesome!
text: I have two stepboys, ages 11 and 12. They CONSTANTLY fight. I only have them every other weekend. It is a struggle to find a game they will both like. Typically, I end up getting two different games. With this game, you can have two players. My boys played this game for about 45 minutes together.... AS IN WORKING TOGETHER... One doing the mission, one protecting the other. WOW!! Never in my wildest dreams would I have thought that would happen! This game allows you to play multiple characters and you HAVE to in order to accomplish certain missions. I enjoyed watching the boys play and played some myself. I think this is a good game for the $30 I payed for it.

title: novice gamer loved this game!
text: This is my first shooter game. You have to use both the right and left control sticks together. (that gave me a bit of grief! ha!) I am not sure why this game didn't get better reviews because I have really enjoyed it. I am a 42 and just started gaming about a year ago. I never got stuck anywhere and couldn't figure out how to continue the game... so that also made me happy. I am playing it on the normal setting. The hard setting might be different... but why make things harder if you don't have to? HA! I would recommend this game fo $20.

title: Folklore from a novice player
text: This game has two characters to choose from. The plot is the same, it revolves around murders that occurred 17 years ago and seem to be happening again. The great thing about this game is the character plot is not the same. If you choose Ellen (the easier version) you travel down one path. If you choose the reporter (the harder version)it takes you down a completely different path. You can play both players. You battle the same bosses, but your interactions with people are different and your clues are different and your 'IDs' (ie, the animals you fight with are different) thus your strategy on how to beat the bosses are different. As there is alway two sides to a story, one character follows one side and the other character follows the other side. I am only on the 3rd chapter out of five. At this point the characters have choosen sides and are at cross roads with each other. In the beginning they started out helping each other. Anyway, this has been a unique and fun game so far.

title: Beware of Uplay
text: I love buying software from Amazon. The whole process is easy and if you need to download it again, it's right there in your digital cloud. That said, Anno2070 uses a software pirate protection called Uplay. It's a separate program that tracks your name, email and serial number. If you have any problems, their technical assistance is unhelpful and unbending. Their servers went down and all users got was the wrong name, password and a message saying to start a new account. If you do start a new account, you're done playing the game forever. They will not cancel that account. All you get is a message saying you can only have one account. This the last time I buy a game from Ubisoft.

title: Excellent RPG
text: Sacred 2 is a well-rounded RPG game where you can play solo or join the great online community. [...] The game is fun, fast-paced and can be especially challenging if you play hard core (die permanently). Each region of the huge map has a 'boss' monster. These range from dragons to machines. [...] Online playing with others is free and extremely well run. There's a Sacred 2 Wiki section that shows all the characters, equipment and mounts available. [...] Two versions of the game are available: the Collector's Edition includes the ability to have better graphics and a Multi-player in-game Imp who carries your stash chest where ever needed. It's a really fun feature. I highly recommend this game to RPG players

title: Love grips and matte finish.
text: I purchased this controller from Amazon because my husband has one (different color) and when I used his, I was so jealous! I love the grips and the matte finish is awesome! I didn't realize how bad my hands would stick to the original glossy finish controller until I used this one. Great upgrade, for sure. I actually experienced "sticking" of the A button so I contacted Microsoft and described my issue. Since the controller was covered by the 90 day warranty, I was able to get a replacement at no additional charge mailed to me and it works perfectly! Highly recommend if you're a gamer.

title: Check those distances.
text: Does exactly what it said it would, and holds the xbox securely. I elected to mount it behind the TV directly to the plaster using the provided anchors. Two users issues, if your mounting it near your TV wall mount. 1 Make sure and orientate the retaining edge in the direction you wish. I overlooked this but luckily got it right on the initial mounting. 2. Make sure and leave enough space between the bracket and any other mounts so you can actually place the unit in the mount. I came super close to not being able to get mine into the mount. Very sturdy construction.

title: Its not a bad controller. The wife and I purchased 2 for ...
text: Its not a bad controller. The wife and I purchased 2 for our boys a few Xmas ago. It works really well. I wish it were supported easier on the Mac for more games. But no big deal at the moment. I am hoping for more use if the rumors are true and you can start using iOS apps on the Mac. The only issue I have is the battery, it fails to charge properly, after only a year or two of very casual usage. This in only exhibited on one controller so. I wish the batteries were changeable for the price I paid. Even Xbox controllers have user replaceable batteries. I am not sure I got my money out of it. If it had that user replaceable battery I would feel better.

title: The exact same as a T300RS GT Wheel, but Ferrari branded
text: [[VIDEOID:5cd5e0ec0290ea1ff2fc6dd397327205]] I came from a Logitech Driving Force GT & the T300 is a huge step up from that. I got the servo base alone with the Ferrari 458 Challenge Wheel and T3PA Pedals. I got this used from Amazon, but it was basically in Mint condition. I can literally feel the wind in my hands as it spins from the wheel because the wheel base spins fast. You do notice the rubber though and because it's new, it really grips to your hands. If you want more of a slippery wheel or drifting/rally, I'd get the alcantara version or get an adapter from Ricomotech for around $45 and put your own custom wheel. That adapter works with this wheel & the GT wheel. Also, the paddle shifters have a very satisfying click. Not magnetic of course, but probably better than the Logitech G29/920/923 although I can't say for certain. Other than that, it is a great wheel for the money!

title: The Only & Best Upgrade I've Got In a Long Time
text: [[VIDEOID:7ca123ccd3dd1bbdc9a34cfad37a5388]] I came from a Logitech Driving Force GT & the T300 is a huge step up from that. I got the servo base alone with the Ferrari 458 Challenge Wheel and T3PA Pedals. Considering it is brand new, the dual belt driven, brushless motor wheel is the smoothest thing I've felt and it spins more than enough for anyone looking to drift. I can literally feel the wind in my hands as it spins. I can't speak for the longevity of this wheel base, but I'm definitely going to take care of it while also putting it through the ringer. (I bought a used one from Amazon before buying this brand new one. The used one was absolutely thrashed on the inside for some reason.) Also, the table clamp works on desks with short lips and a bar. I was actually concerned if this was even going to work, but to my surprised it cleared flawlessly! I know someone out there probably has some sort of cheap desk like mine and I think that’s helpful to know.

title: Be careful with the angle of the jack
text: As with other reviews, my cat chewed up the original cord for my Arctis 3 headset so I've been using a regular 3.5mm cable for audio only. I got a second, brand new PS5 controller and the cable works perfectly with it. No volume loss, microphone is working and is clear, no rubbing noises because the cable is rubber, no voice chat echo, no game bleed into the mic. I decided to get this cable for that reason given the fact that people has said they got feedback in the mic or headphones from 3rd party braided cables. I like the right angle jack design, but I have to make sure it faces up because if it's angled down and you put your controller/phone down, you're more prone to it messing it up so be careful. It also comes with a splitter for 🎧/🎤 respectively. I'm going to make sure my cat doesn't get to this cable and hope not to land the angled jack the wrong way. Besides that, I consider this one a safe bet of you don't trust the braided cables considering this is the highest rated 3rd party cable I've seen.

title: better than a rift s and mobile
text: I bought the Rift S instead of this at launch day, preordered. I was on the fence between both units... I returned the rift S. It was terrible!!!! I waited to buy the Quest afterwards actually it was so bad. Until I heard about the Oculus Link technology and witnessed first hand ALVR running PC VR on a Quest.... Bought one, I love it, Best thing ever!!!!! Adding hand tracking soon along with the Link make this a no brainer! The Rift S is dead! This becomes a Rift Q with a good USB 3.0 cable. or wireless with ALVR like I said. One pro tip I can give you all though. instead of connecting to your local wifi network. buy a good USB 3.0 wifi dongle. and then create a hotspot network in windows withit. Conect to your hotspot via the quest and make sure your PC is wired to your network instead of wireless. but that last part is not a big deal with this method actually. But doing this will remove any network latency or traffic from your wifi. Simply go into your hardware settings for your wifi card and manually set it to 40 mhz and to only use 802.11 a/n/c or any combo of those otherwise the hotspot will default to b/g mode which you don't want. If you do this you can play ALVR wireless PC VR no problem! It's literally amazing!!!!! don't listen to the other methods. do it this way.

title: not ready for release...
text: not ready or defective. not sure because oculus tech support was fail. I'm actually sad I had to send mine back and get a refund. It was almost an awesome product. But oculus tech support did not do the needful. I'm certain the issue was the cable included with the headset. Lots of snow and static on screen that didnt show up in a screen mirror on your real screen. Was ignored and treated very poorly by oculus support. After almost a month of using I frantically boxed it up and sent it back to amazon. I think I might pick up another from best buy and see if it does the same thing or not. I tested 3 high end vr pcs with it btw. But either way. I feel let down by oculus support. And Amazon didnt offer replacement of item. They only offer return or dealing with oculus. So I realized I better return this thing asap! I wish they were being more honest about the issues as I would repurchase once issues are fixed. Biggest let down with this device is trying to play non vr games in a vr theater. It absolutely does not work! The oculus drivers upscale everything into 4k even if the monitor being displayed is only 1920x1080... this results in unbearable stutter in the majority of non vr games. And this is something that an oculus go can handle over wifi with open source software like alvr and moonlight for go so I am shocked to see they dropped the ball so badly by not having a 1080p theater gaming mode.... it's actually unforgivable and I think I would have returned this item due to that fact alone if I wasnt having the USB power and snow static issues.... I think they rushed the software and the skimped on costs for a high quality cable...
