title: My Switch Lite is freaking adorable
text: Last Friday night I noticed my OEM switch shell was no longer closing correctly; likely due to case clips breaking during one of the two times I have replaced my left joystick (this Switch Lite has at leas 1000 hours of play time, and is the only Switch controller that I have had drift issues with). By midnight, I had fully fallen down the shell swap rabbit-hole. I decided on this pink case, but having a turquoise Switch Lite, I was apprehensive about the screen bezel as I don’t feel like a screen protector is the best solution. Pretty soon, I had this shell, a “white” digitizer (which ended up actually being gray), a new LDC (because separating the original screen from the digitizer seemed like a good way to break it), thermal paste, screen adhesive, and a fan (because mine has been sounding a bit loud lately, but the one I ordered ended up not fitting, so I just cleaned the original one well and reinstalled it). Overall, the price was a bit much considering this was an impulse purchase in the middle of the night, but I did what I did and I don’t really have any regrets about it. The swap took a little over an hour to complete (remember, I didn’t remove the old screen, so I got done a little quicker - besides, this isn’t a race). It wasn’t too hard, but I had already disassembled my Switch Lite a couple times for joystick replacements, so I felt well prepared (plus I watched some videos and reviewed iFixIt’s screen replacement instructions). I didn’t find anything to be terribly difficult, only tedious. Anyone who has the right tools, takes their time, keeps track of their screws, and follows instructions shouldn’t have too much of an issue with this swap. If you have ever replaced a joystick, you shouldn’t have much of an issue with this. Things to note: The finish on this case feels velvety soft- very pleasant in the hand. It makes me wonder how it will hold up to wear and use in the long term though. I have seem some reviews that show what looks like the finish wearing off, but those switches were put into cases. I haven’t seen anyone who uses their switch lite naked complaining of issues- only time will tell. This case also has a less than 1mm gap along the top and bottom - isn’t really anything that will ruin my day, but I felt it needed to be mentioned since I can’t account for it (putting the tiniest amount of pressure on the case closes the gap - I made sure my screws in the back of the case were tight, but still, there is a gap). Other than that, I am very happy with the way this turned out :) Tips for success: -Have the right tools. You will need 00 Philips, 00 Tri-wing, Spudgers, adhesive (in case the screen adhesive isn’t usable when you remove the old one or want to use a new one), thermal paste (it isn’t really expensive and will save your device from overheating), heat gun (if you aren’t replacing the screen with a new one) -Take your time - this isn’t a race. A mod that takes 60 minutes instead of 4 hours is not worth it if you break your device. -Clean as you go - If you are using a switch lite that has been around, you will likely find dust and grime inside, have some rubbing alcohol and canned air to clean anything you run into. Just make sure any alcohol you use has evaporated before turning the device back on. -Replace any parts you have concerns about. The fan and joysticks are common parts that fail. If you have issues that you notice (loud fan or slight drift), use this opportunity to swap the part(s) while you are in there. That being said, the fan I bought ended up not fitting my Switch Lite - I cleaned it out well with cabbed air while the device was open (see Clean as you go) and it runs much better now. -Follow instructions. iFixIt has a screen replacement guide that I followed. It identified the screw type for each hole. I separated my screws by size and had no problem grabbing the right one for each step when I reassembled. A little more on why I decided to replace my screen and digitizer. At the end of the day, I wanted to end up with a mod that made me most happy and a screen protector wouldn’t do that (nor would a turquoise bezel around the screen). In addition to being a better fit for my desired outcome, it gave me the flexibility to more easily move back into the old case if I ever felt the need (or ended up breaking the screen). I considered trying to separate the digitizer, but decided it was too risky (in hindsight, it probably would have been fine). Even if, at the end of the day, the screen bezel ended up being gray, I feel like it is the best end product I could have ended up with and the one that makes me most happy. Update 9/22: this shell had me a little worried since the soft-touch finish feels like it will wear off with use. I am happy to report that I see no signs of an issue after 10 months of use. I will note that the shell makes the switch 7g heavier than the original for anyone interested.

title: Great replacement part
text: I decided to replace my screen and digitizer when I re-shelled my switch lite since I thought turquoise wasn’t a good match for the light pink case I wanted. I figured leaving the original in the old shell would make it easier should I ever need to go back to that case and separating a screen from the digitizer seems a little too risky (in hindsight, I think it would have been fine, but still no regrets). This screen was easy to attach to the digitizer, and I liked that they included some adhesive (though I used my own). While the ribbon cables didn’t have the bends in them like the originals, I found them easy enough to fit into their slots without damaging them. The screen looks as good as new (actually better since I also have a new digitizer). Would definitely recommend this as a replacement for anyone who is comfortable taking apart their devices (if you have replaced a joycon, it really isn’t much harder to replace the screen). Just make sure you have all the right tools and parts… oh, and replace your thermal paste!

title: White is more of a gray
text: I ordered the white digitizer as part of a mod. I was disappointed to find that the border on this was actually gray - lighter gray than the border on the gray switch (I think, though I don't have a gray switch to compare it to), but still far from white and noticeably not the same color as the white buttons and joysticks. I also wish there was a screen protector on the underside of the digitizer - nothing worse than putting a device back together only to realize you left a fingerprint on the inside of the screen (which can be avoided by giving the underside of the digitizer a good wipe down before attaching the screen, but still a potential problem that could be avoided by simply putting a screen protector on the bottom of the digitizer. This also doesn’t come with adhesive. I feel like it would have been pretty cheap to include, but I got some kaisiking phone repair tape that worked perfectly and wasn’t too expensive. Apart from some minor gripes, I am overall very happy with this part. It installed with no issues and works like it should.

title: Good price and nice to have extra tools
text: I bought this after my switch light developed left stick issues (dead spot). This was a stick that I have previously replaced (it had drift and was replaced in early 2020). I grabbed this kit and had it delivered to a family member’s house so I could do the replacement over the holiday, so it was nice that the kit had all the tools I needed. I was able to swap the stick in about 20 minutes and found it was working fine after rebooting the device. I should note, the pictures do not accurately show what is in the kit. It came with the following: -2 Y screws -2 pry tools (spudger and pick type) -1 replacement stick -1 Y screwdriver -1 Philips screw driver -1 teal paw print stick cover -1 yellow paw print stick cover

title: Better than waiting for Nintendo
text: I have had drift on my switch lite for the last few months. It wasn't that bad and since I use my lite mostly for tetris 99, I didn't use the stick that much. Now that Animal Crossing is out, I am using the stick more; the issue was getting worse and more annoying. It was to the point that I was playing with my pro controller connected to my lite. I picked this up and it came quick (original arrival date was the 25th (ordered on the 20th), but it still arrived on the 22nd. You should note that this kit doesn't include the tri-wing driver or philips that you need to do the replacement, just some extra screws (that you don't need unless you aren't careful and end up stripping the tri-wing screws). The replacement took less than 20 minutes, following a youtube video of the left stick replacement (it looks like the right stick replacement is a bit harder and more involved - the video said that the right stick may be too much for most people on the switch lite). Put everything back together and I am happy to report that this stick works perfectly. The color is a good match for the original and feels like the sticks probably felt when they we’re new. Update 11/2021: My left stick finally started to die again, but instead of drift, it started to be unresponsive when pushing to the right. Couldn’t remember where I put the extra stick from the last swap so I bought a new one.

title: I like it better than the New 3DS XL
text: I bought a New 3DS XL a while back, but quickly learned that it was a little bulky for my liking and I was noticing that I was having a bit of fatigue in my hands and wrists. I really wanted the smaller device, but I didn't want to sacrifice the benefits of the new 3ds (better 3d and the C-nub). I was also excited about the interchangeable faceplates. When I bought this device, it was the only North American option for a non-XL, so while I wasn't really into Animal Crossing, I was very into the smaller device, and since the faceplates are interchangeable, it wasn't a big deal to me (though I do wish that this bundle included the plain white plates as well). I shopped around and found a great deal online where I got this bundle for under $180 on Jet, so this was really a no-brainer. I do find that I still get some hand strain, not because of weight, but because of the way I hold the console; my hands are just slightly too big for long use comfort (typically, I get strain after about 1.5 hours of use). The new 3D face tracking is a big step up from the original 3DS. The C-stick is not used for happy home designer, but has been useful in the handful of games that have C-stick functionality. I like the layout of this console better. The cartridge in front design seems more ergonomic than the last 3DS, which had it in back where your fingers naturally lie. Overall, I think the New 3DS is a wonderful, polished console. It is the perfect size for travel. The new features increase the options for game developers (ZL/ZR buttons, c-stick). The new 3D face tracking makes using 3D more immersive and less of a practice of patience. As for the Happy Home Designer, I don't really have any interest, but all of those components are interchangeable, and the game arrives as a code that can be given to someone who will actually use it (it is not locked to the device). I have no regrets with my purchase of this console. If I had list any complaint is that the new 3DS consoles do not come with the power supply.

title: Perfect game for taking on the go.
text: This game is fun. I love music and rhythm, so I really do enjoy playing this game. Everything about this game is bite size, so it is perfect for those times you have a minute to kill. There are plenty of other games that I love, but I need to sit and play them for long periods of time. This is just one of those games that you can pick up and play for a few minutes at a time. It is also varied enough that you can sit and play long stretches if you want without getting bored. I find the game a little more challenging then I anticipated, but certainly something that can be mastered.

title: Wonderful, but not without some faults!
text: I enjoy the occasional game and decided I wanted to get back into handheld gaming. While cell phone games do have plenty of engaging time-killing games to offer, I was missing games with some depth and story; like Zelda! So I decided to go back to my roots and get a Nintendo console (my roots are the old DMG-1). After a shockingly small amount of research, I went and impulse purchased the New 3DS XL. If this is your first 3DS, be sure to pick up a charger as well, since, unlike just about any other device that NEEDS a charger, this system does not come with one! Taking the device out of the box, the first thing you will notice is the pristine shiny surfaces that greet you! The exterior is shiny, but don't expect it to stay pretty. It will pick up finger prints if you just look at it. Not only that, but I had scratches on it after a couple weeks of keeping it in my bag (in a pocket that was microfiber lined and all by itself). Next thing you will notice is the weight. This device actually has some heft to it! It is only 1 or 2 tenths of an ounce lighter than the original Nintendo! I found that I did get a but of hand and wrist strain during the first could days of play. Just something to keep in mind! Another thing you will notice is that the hinge is a bit flappy. When you open the hinge, you will hear it snap into place in two positions (and by snap, it sounds and feels like you are doing something wrong). This wouldn't be a problem since the second position is where you will want the screen opened to, but the screen moves within that position. I play a lot from a reclined or laying position, so I do notice the top screen wobbling quite a bit. I would estimate that the movement is about 5 degrees. It is enough that, if I am playing while laying down, I often find myself awkwardly positing my index fingers so they wrap around to the front of the device to keep it from moving while I am playing. I have seen video of New 3DS XLs that do not have this issue with the hinge, but most people seem to have it, and people who have contacted Nintendo say that Nintendo does not consider this to be a defect. Even with all of the negatives I have listed, there is still so much to love about this device. The top screen is beautiful and sharp. The Super Stable 3D does great (even when you play in the dark). The console comes with a few interesting games, so even if you don't by games right away, there is definitely lots of interesting stuff to do on the device. The e-shop is great and even has some great games that you can get for relatively cheap including some old NES and Gameboy games. The controls are generally ergonomic, although I find that the D-pad can be a little uncomfortable if you are playing a game that uses that instead of letting you use the thumb pad. Streetpass and spotpass add a whole other dimension of entertainment. There are a lot of great games available for the system for almost any genre. All the old Nintendo franchises have games for the 3DS that have a terrific balance between familiar characters and new spins on gameplay that develop the story.

title: It's so pink and nostalgic
text: Believe it or not, I have been using my original DMG-1/1989/Original Gameboy, which still works (and with eneloop batteries, is a lot more cost efficient to run). My DMG-1 plays games like the day it was bought, but cosmetically, it has seen better days! I decided to upgrade to a gameboy pocket. For price under $20, you can't beat this find! It was even cheaper than the housing I ordered for my DMG-1! Don't worry that it is a Japan import! Nintendo didn't have region codes associated with games or consoles at the time, so every game you have will still work, no matter where it came from! The pink isn't really a rare color, and gameboy pockets have saturated the market (if you are looking into a rare/collectable gameboy pocket in pink, check out the hello kitty or tamagotchi limited edition models, which can still be found for relatively cheap). I got this console very quickly (3 weekdays)! It only had minor cosmetic scratches and what looked like battery acid in a couple crevices (but the battery contacts looked pristine). It runs great!

title: Love this controller
text: For a while, I wanted to get a pink controller to add to my collection. This controller is exactly what I wanted. I have only one complaint- the right joystick drifts a little bit sometimes. This can be annoying when playing a game that requires precision. I truly believe that this is an isolated case and something that could happen with any microsoft controller- not just the pink ones. I could probably recalibrate it easily, but honestly, the problem isn't so bad that I have felt the need. I love that this is a pink controller- it is mine and all of the guys don't mess with it when they come over!

title: Batman is still good and interesting, release after release....
text: You know, I didn't buy this game initially because I read a couple of so-so reviews. I must say, I'm glad I got the game eventually. As a fan of the franchise, I was afraid it would be more of the same old, same old. And there is a little bit of that, after all, it IS a Batman title and there's a certain amount of button mashing/timing you need to do. But the story is good, the challenges are good, and you die enough that it requires a healthy degree of tactics and skill upgrades to make life easier for you. The only negative I have is the sheer number of Riddler challenges, but that may just be me. I'm not a fan of hunting down every question mark in the game and solving every puzzle. But, I am glad I got it and would recommend it to any Batman fan.

title: Pretty, smooth, jumbled, meaningless.
text: If you get it for the right price, it is worth it. The movement is fluid, the variety of weapons is good, the battles are interesting enough. But the game has serious problems. First, the story is incomprehensible. Second the missions and locations all blend into one another. Third, controlling your team is not horrible, but they aren't the quickest to engage the enemy, get to certain locations, or get to you when you are down. This game does not feel complete. It does not feel like a continuation of Halo 4. The enemies and allies eventually all look alike and you pretty much fall into the "shoot everything in front of you" mindset without thinking about it. Maybe the multiplayer has more value for people, but I was disappointed with the solo campaign, which, I'm sure everybody knows by now, you cannot co-op on the same console. That effectively destroyed father/son time and brother/brother time that I enjoyed in previous releases.

title: Impressive graphics, but slow load times...
text: Anime fighting games get a bad reputation, but this game defies those expectations and creates a surprisingly deep combat system. (So long as you play on manual, other wise its just mashing.) It includes a pretty large cast of characters, none of which feel to similar. The first thing you notice when you open it up is that the graphics are amazing. Frankly, this is what surprised me the most. Every character model looks like it came straight out of the anime. All of these thing cost of very slow load times, and a very repetitive story mode. Overall I still think this is a solid four star game that any fan of the anime should give a try.

title: An amazing collection of video game history
text: From my teenage son: This is by far my favorite smash game. In every inch of this game you can really feel how much heart the developers put into this. This game is massive and I have been playing it on and off for nearly two years. To start with there are over eighty different fighters all of which are unique and express their own individual personalities. I can't even imagine how much work it must have been to accomplish this, I have the utmost respect for these developer. Since I got the game I have spent nearly the entire game mastering the character link, it would take a lot of gameplay to master all of them. There are two major complaints when it comes to this game: online mode, and balancing. First of all, yes... I agree that online mode lag can be excessive, but I don't find that it causes me to lose many matches. Balancing is kind of tricky... As it is quiet apparent that not every fighter is made equally, I feel like most of these accusations of overpowered or weak characters are over exagerated, as every fighter has their own strengths and weaknesses. for example, little mac is well known to be one of if not the worst characters, due to his trouble returning to the stage, but when on stage, a good little mac player can be hard to challenge. The point is I think this is an amazing game, and I would absolutely recommend it to anyone of any skill level.

title: Too easy...should be for 5 and under!
text: my son who just turned 6 finished the entire complete game in less than 2 hrs...probably in about one really! I could not believe him and made him show me and he in fact did all the characters missions and got the certificate at the end. the problem is that the two modes show you or tell you exactly what to do with in one a voice and the other a big obvious arrow. title: Great mouse for the price overexceeded expectations

title: Destiny, but way better
text: There was a point early in The Division where I found the remnants of a voicemail left by a daughter trapped in the city and facing eminent death. She was calling her parents to tell them — emotionally and with her voice slurring from the few drinks she admitted to having imbibed to gain the courage to make the call — that she was gay and this was why she had moved to New York in the first place, to find a more accepting community. It was at that point, where I was listing to this message while also ducking behind cover to avoid the gunfire from looters, that The Division hooked me. I am a big fan of Destiny, a game The Division shares a lot with in terms of a persistent online world, but in that one moment The Division showed more story than Destiny's entire campaign, The Taken King expansion included. Up until this point it was kind of a nonchalant "Yah, take back New York, whatever." Now, however, the game had weight. You aren't fighting against some vague alien presence that for one reason or another is mad at the human race but everyone is too busy to explain why they are too busy to explain it to you, you are fighting for these people whose lives were suddenly uprooted. That's what makes The Divsion great. Ohh and the matchmaking is much better too.

title: a bit too easy but still fun
text: I still bought this game despite the DRM issues because frankly i really care about DRM problems. i don't forsee needing to reinstall it 3 different times and i'm only putting it on one pc. It is a pretty fun game that i bought for my girlfriend to play while i use my 360 but i've found myself enjoying the game despite the fact that it's super easy (you can't really die). It can be very pretty at times and just a pleasure to look at, especially in the cell stage. It's no The Sims but still pretty fun, here's to hoping for some sweet expansion packs.

title: An Experience Unlike Any Other
text: It’s about as easy to describe the game Journey to someone as it is to describe Doctor Who. You love it, you know why you love it, but to put it into words is nearly impossible. While describing your love for Doctor Who may make you sound certifiably insane, trying to describe Journey makes it sound boring, which it is certainly far from. Yet, despite that potentiality, I will do my best to paint a more detailed picture as to why we still love it and will continue to love it for years to come. You’ve probably heard from so many mouths that Journey (crafted by thatgamecompany) is “touching” and “beautiful” to the point where it almost sounds cliche, but it’s true. This game genuinely provides you with an experience unlike that which you could have with any other game. I haven’t played it in nearly two years, and yet I can still remember precisely how I felt when I reached the end. This is going to sound cheesy, so prepare yourself, but you don’t play Journey to have fun, you play Journey to be moved and to be taken on a ride you’ve never been on before. If you end up having fun anyway, then that’s great, but sitting down to play Journey is more like going to a museum of art, as opposed to strapping in for a day at the theme park. I don’t want to spoil the ending for you, but to sum up, it pretty much falls into the categories of: unforgettable, shocking, moving, touching, resonating, and sobering. It will put a smile on your face moments after it makes you cry, and you will come to understand how you can bond on a deeper level with a real person whom you’ve never met. And single player is not an option - well, at least at certain points. You’ll understand why when you play. While you may delightfully frolic with your anonymous companion on your mission to get to the mountain (located at the end of what seems like the largest desert imaginable), you can do nothing more than jump or speak to each other in song, something that would, in reality, be more than sufficient, should we ever end up alone on such a quest - a quest that becomes more evident by the end of the game and will have you nodding in approval. Under any other circumstances, Journey would probably suck. But it’s with those kid gloves with which thatgamecompany makes all of their games, including flOw (a subtle game of evolution) and Flower (where you control flower petals on the wind), that make their gaming experiences more of an interactive meditation than a traditional gaming session. You play games like Call of Duty and God of War to release your aggression, but you pick up a thatgamecompany game to soothe your soul. The fact that Journey is an indie title makes it even more impressive that it was so memorable, though less surprising that it is as profound. The visuals are breathtaking, particularly the glimmering pink sands, and the soft sounds are unlike any you’ve heard before in a video game. Journey is the perfect example of why you don’t need a lot of glitz and glamour - sometimes less truly is more...so much more.

title: Solid Game from the Franchise
text: Dynasty Warriors 8 essentially plays like every other Dynasty Warriors game. Read as: you don't play for the plot, you play to level up your weapons and your attack power so that you can take down foes in one hit. Thankfully, the beautifully rendered cut scenes (which, while appreciated, are slowing our progress), can be skipped, though there is an option on one of the boards in the Wei dynasty where, if you play it a certain way, you can unlock new dialogue for Lu Bu. I can't imagine anyone racing to do that. Anyway, the generals, of course, have musou, too, and here they'll take you out in one clip, even if you have full health. So unless you are seriously packing heat, you might want to stay out of the way until they're done raging. In "Story" mode, you can play through each dynasty to unlock boards and characters that you can then play on "Free" mode, which is normally a less than satisfying mode in other games, but since we're not here for the plot, "Free" mode is a great way to level up your favorite character., as well as their respective weapons. Though, you don't have to stick to the weapons you're given - you can choose from any on the list. One annoying thing about this, though, is that you do not land, by default, on your character's weapon when you choose the list. You have to scroll down until you see the "EX" next to the weapon - that's how you know you're on your character's default weapon. But don't feel limited by that - you can mix and match the "elements" of different weapons to provide better attacks (though, of course, your default weapon will give you a specific attack that only your character can do). You can also use animal accompaniments which come with their own perks, depending on the sidekick you choose. There's also "Ambition" mode, which is new to the series, and here you can build up a town, but not in the "Farmville" engine that every app seems to come with these days. You make the area stronger by participating in various battles, and these battles will either give you materials to construct the Tongquetai Tower, fame, or new partners. Later on, you can also unlock a co-op version of "Ambition" mode. My favorite character is "Flute Chick," a.k.a. Zhang He, and while her attacks are purple and pretty, her musou was a bit of a let-down. Plus, you don't get to unlock her until much later, which leads me to believe that she's one of everyone else's favorites as well. All in, it's a solid game, and it doesn't fall short of what you would expect from the Dynasty Warriors series.

title: NOT for beginners
text: I am a heavier individual and have been wanting to find a fun way to exercise, as I've never been a major fan of any type of exercise. So, I bought this game as it has received many wonderful reviews. Unfortunately I was very disappointed and ended up returning it to the store I purchased it from, which thankfully they let me do that! First of all, the band that is supposed to go around your thigh did not fit mine, so I had to put it just above my knee. I think it still worked ok, but it just wasn't comfortable and wanted to slide down. Secondly, I have bad ankles and knees and the exercises were not meant for beginners at all, with the squats causing me pain. I think this would be a great game for anyone who is already in shape and wants to add variety to their pre-existing exercise program, but it was just not for me. Eventually it might be once I get in better shape, but if you're a beginner, I recommend the Wii Fit over Wii Active, as there are more progressive exercises on the Wii Fit than on the Wii Active....just be careful of the Wii Fit's weight limit. It's worth it to pay more money to get the Wii Fit than the Wii Active game if you're a beginner, in my opinion.

title: Bravely Default II is a gem
text: Just like the previous chapters, Bravely Default II delivers a true-to-the-roots JRPG experience that is a little short in surprises, but truly enjoyable. The battle and job systems are where I found most of my joy while playing Bravely Default 2. Bravely Default’s excellent job system also returns to add another layer of complexity to battles. Bravely Default II’s boss battles are particularly great as well, especially some of the more challenging ones. It is user friendly yet stubbornly uncompromising, happy to offer a helping hand one minute then throw you to the wolves the next. Much of the adventure spans just four regions, each with a city that needs saving, a handful of dungeons and various side missions as well. This game has amazing visuals with a combat system that both veterans and newcomers will love. It has excellent characters with a rich in-game world, and delivers it with a majestic OST. It's not perfect but it's an excellent RPG that every Switch owner should try. Overall, I recommend it and is fun to play.

title: Great characters and sharp and witty humor.
text: This is a beautiful game and quality product, crafted with love. The battles always feel winnable, even against tougher opponents, but you can always unlock new combat and passive abilities to defeat them. I like that Fenyx is a fully customizable character, shipwrecks on the Golden Isle, a magical land where some of the gods reside. The storyline ia like A Greek comedy! If you love The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, you would be out of your mind not to try Immortals Fenyx Rising. Pros: Lots of upgradeable stats and special abilities Cons: Controls are somewhat complex, though they can be customized Embrace the game for what it is – a fun retelling of classic mythology.

title: Good Quality and excellent response time!
text: This stick is worth every penny. Got it on sale so it was a good buy. This stick also makes the game more fun to play as well as accessible. This Sanwa joystick works very well and has quick response time, which we all know is a must for every player. I also like that no controllers are needed to connect the arcade stick to the different platforms. All you need to do is toggle a switch, and your done. Seems solidly made and durable for long use. Cosmetically it looks great, and has a nice finish to it with some cool lighting as well. You can store the wires in the built in compartment so you can easily take it wherever you go. Very nice product and a must for any gaming arcade lover. Fast delivery and arrived safely.

title: The wait is over ! Awesome Graphics
text: ( No Spoilers ) The wait is finally over. The graphics are really awesome and has an excellent gripping quest design. In this game I was thrust into the shoes of V, a mercenary in Night City who ends up with the psyche of long-dead rockstar and anti-corporate terrorist Johnny Silverhand trapped in their head. There is enormous amount of choices you can make in this game. Choices in dialogue options, how to build your character, how to approach missions, and much more. And even when missions stops Cyberpunk 2077 keeps things interesting by turning you into a Batman Arkham-esque investigator. The fun factor, replayability, and value for money is fantastic. This is definitley the best gaming gift for this season that will entertain everyone. ( Although there are some buggy problems in the first release ) Shipped fast and arrived with no damage to the packaging. Great value for your money. I really enjoyed this game and hope you will too.

title: Great cool functional keyboard! Well priced.
text: It's a simple USB keyboard with good size keys, there is a key that turns on the rainbow colored lights, it took me a minute to discover it, but it's on the top right. Great keyboard, but the colors can only be in a rainbow pattern. Which is pretty cool. The keys are well separated and have a nice positive feedback when pressing them. Reminds me of the keyboards from the 1980's. This Rii keyboard is wired, but It needs to be to power up the LED background. My son loves it for the gaming, but I like to use it in the dark while my baby sleeps. Also good for nurses who don't want to disturb their patients.

title: Fun game, wish night mode had off road events.
text: Pretty fun game, though the story line is pretty short. Multiplayer isn’t enjoyable because it seems no matter how fast my car is, it’s like I’m walking compared to other connected players in the game. And just being able to honk at each other is stupid. As for single player mode, I like the arcade racer genre very much, and the cop chases are more difficult. It has replay ability after the story is complete, but it’s really just to collect more cars. Personally I think the off-road events are the most fun, but they are also the least available compared to race and drift events. A definite improvement over the previous NFS games, but there is still a lot of room for playing improvement. One specific annoyance is the inability to change the controls. The horn is located as a push on the left stick which also has major functionality for steering, so frequently as I turn a corner, the horn goes off. SUPER ANNOYING, seemingly an easy fix by allowing custom button controls.

title: Great gameplay, online play sometimes spotty
text: I have logged 281 hours playing this game. That in itself shows how much I like the game. The campaign mode is challenging, and fun. Online mode is where I spend most of my time now that I have finished the campaign. I love the hacking invasion of another player. It’s a lot of fun to mess with people by blowing stuff up, sending gang members after them etc. My only complaint though is a big one. The online play frequently locks up and actually causes my Xbox One X to shut off! This happens about 20% of the time. I’ve reached out to Ubisoft, but they have no response other than reinstalling the game, which isn’t the problem. It ONLY locks up when playing online through their Ubisoft servers. Watch dogs 1 did not have this issue, and checking the forums, I am far from alone, yet Ubisoft refuses to release a bug patch. Overall, it’s one of my favorite games, which is why I’m so frustrated when the game randomly locks up hard. I have also found that there doesn’t seem to be a whole lot of people playing online. title: Fun game
text: 007 Nightfire is out for all major platforms, in time for the latest Bond film. The graphics are stunning, gameplay is amazing. Well worthy of the series! I'm a huge fan of the Bond games, and we have all of the previous ones. We got this one as soon as it came out, and were definitely not disappointed! The graphics are a huge step up from previous versions. In the first 'training' mission, you're driving a car through city streets. The lights reflect off of the curves of the car, you can see inside to all of his controls and movements, the dents show up realistically, the back up lights glow softly, and if you bash it a bit, the trunk comes loose. The city around you has cobblestone streets, water rippling, streetlights that come down when you hit them. The attention to detail is just amazing! As you then move on through the various levels, you see this same level of detail everywhere. From the Austrian castle and other alpine scenes, to the city scenes, watery scenes and more, each really shines. The plot is very engaging and typically Bond. But in an attempt to show that this isn't about violence - he's a SPY after all, not a Rambo - you get bonus points for being stealthy instead of blasting in with guns, and for stunning or capturing enemies instead of killing them. In fact, just about every area can be 'accomplished' in many ways. Bluster your way into an objective by a full frontal assault ... or sneak in the side way for extra points. Since you're also rewarded for your time and health, often the sneaky, non-violent way is the best. You've got a huge array of equipment, weapons, armor and vehicles, and all work just the way you'd expect them to. I found the default controller configuration REALLY annoying, but a quicks stop in the config area got it back to the way I'm used to playing. Plus, there's multiplayer! Play with up to four people at once on REALLY great maps with quite a bit of customization options on each one. Grab some bots for practice, and play arena, team arena, king of the hill, capture the flag, or other game types. Definitely worthy of the Bond series, and highly, highly recommended to any first person shooter fan!

title: Frustratingly difficult. Despite anything you do, you're punished!
text: I've been playing the game for the last 3 days, and I'm about to just give up in frustration. A game is supposed to be fun, isn't it? My Player mode is extremely unforgiving difficult game. Part of the goal of the mode is to be a good team mate and work your way up as a starter. To do that, you do the nitty gritty things like set screens for your players. This works, only sometimes, and other times the AI players simply just stand there. Wasting time, waiting for your ballhandler to make a move. I'm begging the AI to come on, please start the play! We'll talk about being hypocritical in a moment here. Playing as point guard, you get punished for holding the ball too long, by a large margin. Hey now, I'm trying to survey the floor looking for a good pass! Oh hey, a player is cutting towards the basket so I'll pass the ball to him. But oops! He continues running around the opponent and they intercept or tip the ball. Bass pass penalty, major points lost. What? So what is it? Do I take my time looking for the players to stop running and get the good pass or do I try to rush a pass to a running player? Playing defense is brutal as well. You can't stand in close because the opponent will run right past you leaving you chasing them. Or you can't stand back a bit and they'll just shoot a jumper over you. Is there even anything we can do to prevent the major lost of points for allowing your man to score? Okay well another problem is deciding who to defend running back after your team misses a shot. Well, hmm, the player defending arrows is pointing one way.. okay I'll go head there to defend. If you rely on the blue circles around opponents to defend, well, good luck because sometimes there are two players which you need to defend at once. Huh? WHAT? Okay, let's pick our position to defend instead. Makes sense right? Wait why is my team mate defending this guy too? The open opponent who just scored was the guy you were supposed to defend. You just lost a major amount of team mate points. Okay now we're chasing a fast breaking opponent down. There are 2 other team mates in front of him and the guy still makes the basket....just trying to help out, but yes more penalties to the team mate score. Oh also, sometimes the passes don't go to the right guy as well. Whatever you do, you're going to get penalized. It's extremely frustrating. There's probably more things I've forgot to mention that's wrong with this game, but let's close up this review. I realize I've ranted long enough already. Another major issue is that it loads slowly. Can't the game play the cut scenes while loading? You simply have to wait out the load times, and watch the cut scenes that are forced on you, for the hundredth time. Get me into the game please! I mean, parts of the game can be fun when you get to play but there are some really difficult things to master, like the shooting timing, the freethrow timing, the idiotic penalties. Don't add on to the frustration with it being just so darn slow to load. And come on, don't throw the player in there on Pro difficulty with no chance to learn the system. Why don't they have rookie enabled for My Player, I don't know. I give up on you NBA 2K11. Maybe I'll try 2K12 when prices drop to more reasonable level.

text: [[VIDEOID:526540efc86f0b351cd8c3fe4de35af7]] The For Honor game eats up a whopping 32.30GB and that is before I add the Legacy Battle Pack. game. The graphics are gorgeous. After much time waiting for the game to get on my hard drive and then update, finally got through the servers to start playing the game. Got the game running and did the practice sparring with the dummies. This appears to be an exciting game with lots of slicing and dicing. The boy child should love it. Even after the beginning video ends, the graphics continue to be great. The only complaint I have is how long it took to connect to the servers. I would prefer for me to play by myself. The boy child likes to play with the universe. Not really an issue because the boy child will mainly play the game while I watch, fascinated by how well he plays and interacts with others.

title: Comfortable communicator for Xbox pals.
text: This lightweight Titanfall 2 Official Marauder Six Four Communicator for Xbox One works great. I hooked it up to my iPhone and my laptop and made volume adjustments on each until I got perfection. I highly recommend that you read the instruction booklet that comes with this Communicator, otherwise, you will most likely not get the volume adjustment and the off on to work very well. Also, when using your Xbox, make sure you adjust that volume accordingly on your tv for optimal results. When I used it to make a phone call, I could barely hear my hubby until I checked the volume level on my iPhone. Once I increased the audio level for that, then I could increase or decrease on the communicator. I could also turn off the ability for anyone on the other end to hear me. I liked that I could use my controller (only the new model) without any other attachments. It will not plug into the first gen Xbox one controllers.

title: FINALLY A WORTHY DOOM GAME!
text: If you have been a gamer since gaming existed then you know doom. Been hooked on it since I first opened it, (20 min steam download on 300mbit) ID 6 engine graphics are perfect for this, other render modes are fun. I use gritty and it's like an old grindhouse movie with the chainsaw ripping. Has never crashed. Runs buttery smooth on my 780ti (with 125+gpu offset and 248+Memory offset). Almost all options are maxed out. 60fps solid, and 140fps without vsync. i7 4930k at 5ghz. 32 Ram overclocked as well. So much fun, you wont regret it. Many hidden things and very in depth levels, always surprises around every corner. DID I MENTION NO BUGS OR CRASHES! Got it on amazon day for 30.00 so it was worth every penny.

title: Not a fan at all!
text: I see a ton of positive reviews, and that might be people coming from WoW. To me, this is nothing but a cookie cutter future WoW, with some active combat. The game is fun the first few levels, then becomes a race to 50, which is very easy. Took me around 30 hours of playing time to reach 50, with the typical push button get banana quest. I also don't usually beat games up, to each their own, but this game isn't that good once you have played it for a few days. PvP is a joke, if someone runs around in circles you are screwed (Had lvl 50 Engineer). Maybe I am getting to old to keep up with the younger players, but the combat system felt silly to me. Only having 8 actions to choose from sucked too, as 2 of mine where taken up with bots, one was for the power booster, and one for spam electricity. I have played every MMO out there, and this one was just a boring game to me. I am sure some will love it, but this is just not for me. I am gonna go check out Arch Age.

title: Holiday Fun & Cheer!
text: This game is fun and I will play it each Christmas to come. There were a few spots I got stuck on but ended up figuring them out by just clicking on different things. It is short, but nonetheless fun. Plus, it has the book included that you can read (like a Nook). It is just the right thing to get you in the holiday mood and has a relaxed play mode so you don't get stressed out trying to beat the clock (except on a couple of mini games, but they are easy enough for me and I hate and don't do well at timed games.) Well worth the money if you love this story and this time of year. Well suited for all ages. I gave it a 4 because it was a shorter game than I'd would have liked.

title: For the price, this is a winner
text: I tried the new TB Stealth V2, they sounded great, but it was really tight and went back. The wireless HyperX was next up, but for $175, it felt exactly like the much cheaper wired version. The wireless has more bells and whistles with the push to mute and some sound tweaks (red/green LED mic was nice), but it didn't sound much different and comfort wise was the same. Save some cash, go with this. Plus, the wireless is all plastic, so the arms will break for sure. This is metal, hoping it lasts. Comfort wise, it's just ok, but I'd say that for most headsets because my head is large. I play for about 2 hours a day and it's fine for that usage, could be rough if you're up at 4+ hours though. Comfort depends on your head size though. I wear glasses with it, doesn't jam them into my head so you should be good on that as well. The TB set has 'slots' for glasses, but I found that totally useless as they were just super tight to begin with. I'm still looking for a better set, but I'm in no rush as these do the job just fine with solid 360 sound.

title: Great at first, then the issues started
text: The sound is great, still is, so it gets 2 stars for that. The rest is trash. The wireless option is no longer an option as the battery will last maybe 10 minutes, so I have a wired headset now that is also incredibly heavy, so the worst of both worlds with that. The arm on the right side cracked, so I have to keep that one much shorter so it doesn't dangle and extend the left side to compensate. Battery lasted 12.5 months, just enough to ensure I am stuck with a half functional product. The arm cracked at month 15. I'm just waiting for the end of the month to replace it, I'll never go back to TB again.

title: Perfect compromise until it wasn't.
text: This was perfect, I really loved it. I ordered the PS4 version and I got the different paddles directly from Collective Minds as well. Great compromise to a Scuf, which I had originally purchased (the trigger stop broke on my Vantage after 10 minutes). I bought this on November 30. Last night, 4/11, the left paddle stopped working. I swapped controllers, did a factory reset, on/off multiple times, changed paddles. It just doesn't work anymore. I used the left paddle for the X button, so I could no longer jump with that paddle. To make things worse, if I had X mapped to the paddle, I couldn't even use the button itself. I could map it to the right paddle and it worked fine, but I don't want to relearn again, it took a few weeks to get used to this as it is. I thought about buying another one since I really did love this, but after putting $60 in already and it lasted 4 months, why roll the dice again.

title: Fun... Fundamentally flawed.
text: I've been a Pokè-maniac since I was wee little, since the beginning. As soon as it hit the states I was hooked. I didn't want make up and barbies, everything had to be Pokémon. EVERYTHING. Even as an adult, I spend much of my life on Pokémon. That being said, I'm not quick to hate anything Pokémon... But I'm open and honest to criticism. 25 hours in Positives- It is fun! If you can ignore the sluggish lag, and frustrations, it's pretty okay. It doesn't feel like a chore as some of the recent main title games have. Exploring with my mons was great, but for me the best part was avoiding all possible leaks and spoilers and actually jumping in blindish, aside from announcements from Pokémon. It was so much fun seeing new creatures like "...what is that???" But also... They're ugly! So many disappointments! The negative- Okay... I'm disappointed I haven't had any major hilarious bugs as others have. I want to fall into the void! At best pokemon were in the floor and walls. At worst, the LAG and broken controls. Travel is so sluggish in areas- like holy cow, get the bricks out of your socks! I'm not an FPS queen, I still love my older games, but man... This is painful sometimes. There have been times where I'm like "oh, here it is!" Only to snap out of it after freezing momentarily. I can admit I'm anxious and won't be transferring my special past pokemon, out of fear of save corruption. I feel this game is trying so hard to keep itself together and is losing will to keep fighting. Controls... Mainly when auto-battling. Okay. I'll send out my pokemon, or try to, and they just stand there or run off somewhere else. The star bases were unreasonably frustrating. Sure, we got PLENTY of time to beat the swarms, but I'm still panicking when it seems my LR button isn't even working. I had to look up guides and exposed myself to spoilers, trying to figure out what I'm doing wrong- it's not me. I just have to run around the enemy's pokemon spamming the button, hoping my Pokémon will eventually cue in and attack. I've even used multiple joy cons. It's not me. The UGLY pokemon... I'll avoid spoiling, but there were two pokemon I got very excited for! The one has a RIDICULOUS evolution... Like, fans wanted this creature of the sea in Pokémon form for years, and you did WHAT to it!? I boxed it forever. And this one cutie, I love! But there's no evolution, and as of now, I can't find a way to make it carry it's place on the team... Literally, turn it into a beast or roll or literally something. It's too cute to end there. Otherwise, most evolutions are sad... Most Pokémon are too. Don't get me going on starter evolutions I feel GF designed some of these to be as unappealing as possible and to pull a joke on long time fans. Despite it all, this is better than SW/SH. I was so bored with that game... But this had so much potential and promise, and it feels like a slap in the face. I didn't even criticize SWSH much because it was new to the Switch console- I don't have that excuse here. I'd have rather waited for a better game. I'm very happy we got a few more Pokémon this gen than the last 2, but please- build the numbers! I need a game with more to do and more creatures to hoard. Also! PLEASE MAKE SHINY POKEMON GLIMMER IN THE OPEN WORLD! I'd been shiny hunting since day one, and found my 1st at hour 24. I only knew it was shiny because it was so drastically different, and I barley saw it having to make a double take. I hate knowing I probably passed other shiny mons not knowing any better. Some just don't stand out so much, some you can't tell at all... Without that glitter, we have no clue unless we battle it. It hurts the progress of wild and open spawns. Let's stop stepping back from Arceus. Also... I know Nintendo games are built around children in mind... But please, let's consider the adults who have been in this franchise for literally all their lives. Story is childish, I'm so sick of being a little kid in school. My school years were my worst, I hate anime revolving around school even. Just... Last game, Arceus, had a much better story. I find myself quickly spamming through text, not caring about the bullying arc especially. I was horribly bullied in school, but have been out of class for over 12 years... It's not a problem I can care about. And the tutorials... Let us skip them. I believe SunMoon had the longest tutorials, maybe not- but please make it stop.

title: Digital "Download" of Code is Great
text: The "online game code" facet of this Xbox Live subscription is fantastic, as you can start using Xbox Live immediately. I personally prefer purchasing here over directly through Xbox Live since it is very difficult to cancel a subscription to Xbox Live when you have your credit card tied to your account. Perhaps things have changed lately or will soon, but last time I was not using my Xbox Live account for several months, it was a complete pain to cancel the auto-renewal with my credit card that was in place, and I ended up having to call in to deal with it. With this, after 12 months, my subscription ends, and that is it - since, after all, Xbox Live does not have your credit card information if you buy here. Totally worth it.

title: Solid 4 Stars!
text: This is a mouse for gaming. The fact that it can be wired to the computer solves the frustrating moment, that when least expected, may need recharging. The design makes the SteelSeries Kana Optical Gaming Mouse-Black and Orange, a good looking one. Takes a little time getting used to it, but I let several hard core gamers give it a whirl and they all agreed it was a good mouse. One of the critics said that ergonomically was a tad too big, but right after said that it was still playable. The design of this mouse is sleek and certainly looks good. The color Black and Orange just about perfect on the looks department. Made by gamers for gamers, it fits the bill. Their claims of superior tracking are right on the money, but I can see where not everyone would agree. Superior scrolling features makes this mouse a good addition. Like always Amazon delivers beyond the Call of Duty, and I, for one, remain fiercely loyal to this company. I think this mouse would make a fine investment for people with slightly bigger hands and with time can prove itself, over and over, to be a very good choice for gamers, and having the properties to be played with either hand adds to the value. 4 Stars!

title: Does not disappoint!
text: Gran Turismo 5 does not disappoint. Provides hours of entertainment and depending on the level, the competition gets tougher. Just the license requirements part is a world onto itself. This game is for the true and tried racing car enthusiast. Ever since I played Gran Turismo 1 on the first Play Station this game has been one of the standouts and Gran Turismo 5 follows on the that fine tradition. Hours of playability, large variety of cars, continuos challenges, all this and more, make for a very solid title. I guess I did rate it the maximum 5 Stars when I noticed that some fellow reviewers had not been so kind. The fact remains that among the many good games for PS3 Gran Turismo 5 does for the racer what Uncharted 1 and 2 does for the treasure hunter and does not disappoint at all.

title: Finally...
text: Finally I got burned with Call of Duty: Black Ops. At the time of purchase there was no reference or opinion to this game and since I had so far been able to get some awesome titles for the PS3 (Red Redemption, Uncharted, God of War, Little Big Planet, Batman Arkham Asylum, etc.) I thought I could not do wrong. Well, I could and I did when I purchased this very annoying and certainly way below my expectations title. So much, in fact, that after playing it for 1 hour I want nothing more to do with this let down game. It freezes, its movement is tedious and all you do is blast away while screams and total chaos unfold. This is the first and last time I will venture on my own, without the valuable opinion of those who play and know, and purchase a video game for the PS3 or any other system. Now I am burdened with the task of unloading this CIA fiasco before it damages my PS3 console, who so far has delighted us every playing hour. Will not risk the abuse this game puts it through, it is not worth it. Also, this first person angle where all you see is the front of your weapon or knife or whatever crap you are holding is seriously two steps back from the more developed titles I have been enjoying. You are supposed to follow follow, not really knowing where you are going and how you got there. Beware of this shooter! All it's going to do is shoot your day down and is not worth it. 1 sad star!

title: I Concur, Therefore I like!
text: Castlevania: Lords of Shadow is a fun game. I was totally immersed in the graphics and the story line has some wonderful twists, plus (I forgot her name) is kind of good looking. Very Athletic and has a companion that invites respect, this thing looks menacing so I just admire and enjoy. Come to think of it: who really needs to go to the movies and spend almost the value of a game like this? This is as good as a movie, plus you are in the comfort of your own home, properly baked, and in front of you is this amazing and challenging game. I have always favored the Castlevania series from Konami and this one is no exception. I am sure the experts, those that play and know so much, might be able to find faults or criticisms on this and any other game. But from where I sit, just about every chance I get, I love the hell (stress hell since the surroundings are very much like I could easily imagine hell to be...) out of Castlevania: Lords of Shadow. Had to learn the hard way what I was doing wrong in order to defeat and advance the many violent situation that one faces in this game. Money has been scarce, which attests to my limited abilities for now, but once you get those experience point and start investing in the future, let's just say I can't wait for the end result, for this guy is one tough hombre of the Castlevania era. I give it 5 for value, awesome graphics (although I must say that with Little Big Planet, Red Redemption, Unchartered 2, et., the Playstation is one powerful machine), story line and sheer entertainment factor. When it comes down to it: Why would you go to a movie where so many in the end suck, when you can make the best deal and start buying games such as this for a collection that surely will endure the test of time? Who needs a movie when you can be part of this movie? Beware! This journey is long and tedious, dangerous and exciting and will test the skills and endurance of Gabriel every step of the way. Yes, it has moments when it goes into full majestic movie mode where you are kind of required to watch instead of participate but us people of the stoner age rather welcome such moments. 5 Stars, no ifs or buts, for Gabriel is indeed the man of the hour!

title: Astro a50 > Sony gold/platinum > Steelseries arctic pro wireless
text: These are the ones boys. Astro A50 gen 3 vs Steelseries Arctic pro wireless vs PlayStation platinums & golds Astros win. I’ve owned all of them. Sound quality Astros > Sony > steelseries This comes down to the surround sound support. Which is miserably bad in Steelseries. Absolutely able to discern someone jumping over you or behind you in pvp. Mic Steelseries > Astro > Sony It’s close though. Base station is fantastic. Magnets. Incredible battery life. 1000% the most comfortable. Listen for ps4 this as good as it gets. I’ve used em all. It costs a ton but man is it good.

title: Needs a firmware update or it will disconnect.
text: The keyboard itself is fairly compact and the font is kind of weird. The RGB patterns are neat, but the 2nd day I owned it, it wouldn't turn on until I unplugged it and switched USB ports, a pain in the butt. Did some research, turns out many others had the same problem, until they went to the EVGA site and upgraded the firmware for this model, Z15. The keyboard automatically goes into sleep mode and the lights all go out, depending on the number of minutes you set before it goes into 'sleep' mode. It's a clacky keyboard, not a silent one. It's probably worth the $45 price, not the $129 that Amazon says was the MSRP.

title: So Far, So Good
text: Now, I just got this game pad, but so far everything is working as it should. Took a few minutes to understand how to set it up. I am using this game pad only for Steam games and it seems to work just fine. I cannot comment on battery life at this early stage, but if lasts a reasonable time on a full charge I will be even more pleased. My only complaint might be that the handles would be better with a soft grip wrapping, rather than the slippery hard plastic. UPDATE: After using now for a few weeks, I have had no problems with this game pad. All and all I am very pleased.... 2nd UPDATE: The controller continues to impress me. Have been using for many hours now over the last 3 months. No glitches at all. Works perfectly. Battery charge lasts a very long time. If you are looking for a good controller to use on a PC running Steam, this is it.

title: If you have small hand I guess and you have to signup with Razer with horrible UI
text: Update 3rd time it just stops working while gaming, now going in a box since I can't return it. Stay away from this Junk !! They make you signup with them in order to use the software that has a really bad UI, you think you are about to do something and it opens the web browser and starts showing you your account info.. WTH just the poorest UI, also the serial number you have to type in to let the software to even work with the product is wrong, I typed it in a number of times didn't work so I thought maybe a knock off and then I reformatted it and it worked.. Just poor QA. The mouse seemed ok at 1st, more of I need to get used to it, but no it sucks. It's to low so when you cup it with your hand your finger tips and palm are now arc'd higher than the mouse, so you have to move your hand to a dragging position.. the button are loud and the power switch is the 1st most button on top.. Dahhhh dumb.. Skip this and the company.

title: Finally a game to match BF2
text: I was hugely into Battlefield 2 awhile back, even though it lacked a single-player campaign. Well Battlefield is back with EPIC multiplayer, and an decent campaign mode. For those of you comparing this to Call of Duty it is comparing apples and oranges. Some like citrus some like pomaceous. I am a huge fan of the very tactical multiplayer where you can use a wide array of vehicles and weapons on some very diverse maps. One thing to note is that the multiplayer maps are limited to 32 players on consoles, get the PC version to play with up to 64 players: [[ASIN:B005WWZUQ0 Battlefield 3 [Download]]]

title: HORRIBLE MIC/CORD TO CONTROLLER. MIC CUTS IN AND OUT CONSTANTLY ON 2 DIFFERENT HEADSETS.
text: Literally sent me a broken headset, then sends me another broken one as “replacement” I’ve been making due without using the mic because game audio works but mic audio is very inconsistent, cuts in and out constantly and sometimes doesn’t even work. Still debating on getting my money back. Might give one more chance and replace these horrid excuses for durable high quality headsets they’ve sent so far. I’m sick of having my time wasted when it comes to headsets and their durability. Seems like unless you want to spend $200+ you can’t get something actually strong and reliable. Very frustrating to deal with, not happy AT ALL.... only upside is good in game audio. The cord from the headset to the controller is absolutely horrible. 2/2 times it’s been sent broken or already on the verge of being broken. Maybe I need a mix amp. Maybe the mic is just faulty on 1 and the cord on another. Not sure, what I am sure of though is that this is pathetic.

title: Does not work on Windows 10
text: I got this as a replacement for the older program on my laptop. Huge mistake. Even though Encore claims it works with Windows 10, it does not. And Amazon will not allow anyone to return it and remove it from the Software and Downloads section of my account. I've attempted to contact Amazon, but have received no reply. At this point, I am contacted Encore, and they can deal with the bad review. Do not waste your money if you intend on trying this on a Windows 10 computer. It won't even load correctly. Update: Amazon did end up refunding me what I'd paid for this software after I spoke to customer service and explained the situation. If I had a computer that was running something other than windows 10, I would have just loaded this on that particular computer. But that wasn't possible. If you've purchased this and it has failed, contact or TRY to contact, Encore directly. You might get a response, I did not. After waiting for a response from Encore, I contacted Amazon via chat.

title: Thought it would be a better game
text: The first thing I discovered is that you cannot read the description here, or the one included with the game. This game refused to run on my old laptop (that is used for just this purpose). It would only run on a Windows 8 or higher computer. That was a disappointment, because that put it on a computer that can't be moved easily. Once I had it running, it appears to be ok, although there are parts of the game where you have to search the screen carefully to see what's going on. If you are playing with the computer, its moves are on the upper right, but yours will be in the center of the screen. I like that you can change the rules to play a short game, rather than the regular length. Overall, though, while I found it to be a good value for my money, I was sorely disappointed that it will not run on older laptops (older meaning Windows 7), and that the graphics were a little confusing.

title: You will certainly get your money's worth with these!
text: Shopping for a headset is daunting, what with all the choices that are out there. I'm happy with this choice. The price was right, because I don't believe it is necessary to pay a hundred dollars for a USB headset. I received this last week and before I could use it with the software I have, my bestie's daughter, who is 15 and plays online a lot, decided to give them a try. After using them for a couple of hours, she informed me that these were better than the ones she normally uses, and could she trade. Heh heh. No, I didn't trade, but I DID try them with my software also. First, I was impressed by the fit. These were not too big (which is normal), instead they fit comfortably on my head. Second, the sound quality was quite good considering the price. And third, the Mic works effectively. All in all, I definitely think anyone buying these would be getting their money's worth!

title: Great Mouse!
text: Disclaimer: I was given one of these to review by the company to give my honest opinion of the product. This mouse is great! It is weighted better than their other gaming mouse. It is well built and well balanced. Very ergonomic and comfortably fits in my hand. It has many buttons to set to use with gaming and is functional on a pc and works with games. Remember to use the software given. The color can be changed from blue. Its DPI is fast (faster than most mice and trackpads I have used through the years. This mouse works well on both Mac and WIN PC as a basic mouse. It is an excellent mouse for gaming on the WIN PC only. Physical features of the device and accessories: - Braided Cable - Constructed of metal and durable comfort plastic - Has a case for weights - Ergonomic design - wheel made of durable rubber - great packaging The only downsides are 1) they use the small CDROMs for the software (but a plus is they have it available online.) 2) they do not have driver support for the Mac and there is no sufficient third party driver that would recognize all the buttons. I hope that with future renditions the company considers making a Mac driver as gaming is improving on the Mac and a sturdy well built mouse like this would do wonders to improve the gaming on the MAC OS X.

title: Great mouse, but hopefully you don't ever have to deal with their support process.
text: I love the mouse, but unfortunately the right mouse button broke. It is still under warranty, and razer's support has told me it will be replaced, but after talking to them two times (three if you count the first time I called, waited on hold for an hour to talk to somebody, and then was hung up on) I still have yet to get the promised confirmation email that my replacement is on the way. Each time I talked to them I was told that I would receive an email in the next day or two with instructions on how to proceed with the replacement process. It's now been a week since I last talked to them.

title: Seriously, get this one...
text: My fiance and I just got a Switch and we wanted the screen protected, so we went with some “officially licensed” garbage from Best Buy for $8. As soon as I put it on, there were bubbles all over and two ridiculous smudges that seemed to have appeared out of nowhere (and I know I didn’t cause them). I immediately afterwards put an order in for this product. It only took two days because of Prime and arrived in perfect condition. I put up pics of both the Best Buy one which brought only one protector, a wipe, a crappy cheap cloth, and a thing for bubbles (barely worked) and the Cellularize one which brought two protectors, two wipes, two nicer cloths, two things for bubbles (which I only had a couple very tiny ones so not a big deal), and two sticky sheets in case anything got stuck to the adhesive side of the protector. The quality between the two products is immediately noticable, especially when you feel the protectors. I feel like the Best Buy one was plastic. No joke it could bend like crazy. If you do that with tempered glass (what an actual screen protector SHOULD be) then it will shatter after force is applied. Anyways, this one feels SO nice and heavy duty. It was easy to apply and is VERY clear with perfect cutouts for the little areas that need them. I highly recommend this to anyone thinking about switching screen protectors or buying a new one. I mean $6 for two quality pieces. You just can’t beat this. My ONLY minor complaint is that they advertise it as “bubble-free” but that’s not accurate. However, if you know what you’re doing, it takes seconds to get rid of them. If you have trouble using the bubble-removing thing, just gently and slowly lift the corner nearest the bubble and reapply which will make it disappear.

title: Almost perfect...
text: I bought this at a Frys and decided to leave a full, honest review on here. I got this because of the review for this product I read that gave it 5 stars, but ended up returning it after trying it on in the parking lot. So here are some pros and cons if you are reading this and trying to make a decision. PROS: - Feels great in your hands - Solid grip, not slippery - All cutouts are almost completely accurate - Has big controller-like bumps in the back for better grip - Kickstand is still usable unlike with most cases - Easily removable- hassle free CONS: - Two buttons (right arrow and Y) rub slightly against case (makes it feel a little off)- other than that, all cutouts are flawless - The front top and bottom pieces of the case are not anywhere near snug like the rest of the case, they are actually somewhat flappy and loose- nothing major, hence why only one star was deducted, but for $30, it really should be a little better I’d say this case is worth $10, maybe $15 if these problems were addressed. I would definitely buy again if they were. But those small things were enough to bother me (I’m a perfectionist with stuff though so I’m very articulate/picky). However, this would definitely be a 5-star product for the people who would shrug these issues off. Overall, I do recommend but I definitely wouldn’t buy again for $30.

title: Full of rages & very challenging!
text: I wouldn't call myself a hardcore gamer (due to lots of work and energetic ferrets), but I am quite experienced and it's my passion and life. I played the original DK Country and good god it really requires patience and fast puzzle solving skills. This version is just as tough. Just when you come across a level and think after finishing it, "god, what kind of douchery was that..." The very next level will be ten times harder (not all the time, but very often). This game will make you rage. I don't care if you're the most experienced gamer in the world- there's never gonna be any gamer that says they beat every level without dying at least once. I died maybe 40 times on one level alone. I almost broke my Wii but I chilled and eventually beat it. It is super challenging and I highly recommend this game to anyone who is tired of playing intense RPG or FPS games. Trust me you'll be in for a treat. Just don't kill your stuff while playing. 5/5 for a challenge which games these days lack, cute sound FX, nice graphics, easy game controls, and fun puzzles. Long live DK!

title: Extremely pleased w/ the seller I got it from...
text: Okay so I've been keeping an eye on the pink Microsoft 360 controller for a few years now. I've been an avid gamer since I was about 11 (til present-23), and when I saw this controller existed I flipped and just knew I had to have it. However, the times I almost bought it, it was at a ridiculous price of $160 or so. I waited it out in hopes of getting it for half that price if I was lucky. Finally about a month or so ago I got it from a great seller for about $60. I immediately bought it. I was really worried, as the seller was just launched, but after emailing them and getting polite and prompt responses about my inquiries, I took a chance. I'm glad I did because when I opened the box, a brand new boxed up pink 360 mint condition wireless controller was in it. I absolutely love it and can't believe how fast it came. I got an incredible deal and I'm so glad I waited to get it. This controller is sick and I also love how the Xbox home button on the controller glows white instead of green! Highly recommended!

title: When you need a break from Zelda
text: Great game! I never played Cave Story before. I know it was a browser game at first, and has been released on numerous platforms, but I needed more games on my Switch and had been wanting to try this one out for a while. It's a 2d side scroller. You get health and weapon upgrades as you shoot your way around a few different parts of an underground world. There are multiple endings and after I won the game I actually went right into a second game to see a different ending. Included are some trial levels too, like use X gun and Y ability and get to the end of the stage. They unlock as you do things in game, I only unlocked one and I didn't enjoy it much. There are some downloads coming later this year I think, multiplayer or something, and more trials. If you like other versions of the game, or have never played before, this is the game to get.

title: Great hardware, fun software.
text: Rockband 4 is wicked fun! The Rivals expansions adds a lot to it as well. We needed a new guitar, and though I already have the game, this price was so good I couldn't pass it up. The guitar works flawlessly, even better than the red one I bought a few weeks ago. I like how it can fold to be carried around, and it seems a better quality than the other guitar I bought; I don't feel like it will fold up while I play if I push on it hard enough. If you need a new guitar, this one is it. If you want the game too, then this is a good bundle. Get it on sale for a great deal!

title: The grip is good but it no longer charges.
text: The Vita is so small, this grip makes it much easier to play and hold, and it has an extra battery built in that helps me play many more hours between charges.. It worked great for a few months. My Vita lasted so much longer, I rarely had to charge it. Then one day I plugged it in and heard a *click* and now it won't charge and the plug is all loose and wiggles. The grip still works great, but I can't charge it so it goes from 5 starts to 2 stars. I have yet to contact Nyko to see about a replacement but I will update this review when I do. EDIT: I emailed Nyko and they said to send it to them so they can check if it is broken and replace it if necessary. I don't like the idea of having to pay to ship it to them, but if it is replaced I guess it's a small price to pay. I will update as things progress.

title: Do not buy this game until it is patched again. Still broken as of 7/11/15
text: I love this game on PC, it is great! You team up with people and pull off heists, so very fun. I had it on the 360 but it never got all the DLC or updates that the PC did, so when I saw it was coming out for the Xbone with all the maps included I had to get it. That was a mistake. There are some issues with the voice chat, but that can be worked around by being in an XBL party and chatting there. When you try and pick your heist online, in game it's called Crime.net, the game locks up for few moments every 10-15 seconds seconds, but that is more of an annoyance then anything. The real issue is trying to join games online: you can't. When you go to Crime.net and see a game that someone is in that you want to join, you select it then on the next screen you can join it. If you try and join, it locks up for a few seconds then boots you back to the main Crime.net screen with an error message stating you can't join the game. You can't play with people online. You can start a game and invite people, and be invited by others, but if you have no friends with the game or none are online when you are, you will not be able to play with others. There is a single player game of course, but you only get 2 AI players and they can do nothing except shoot and be shot. So good luck hauling bags of jewels to the escape van, it's all on you. If the game worked it would probably get 5 stars from me. The state it is in now, it gets 1. Oh, and as of this review it's been out in the US for about a week and there is still no patch. It was also released in the UK even earlier and there is still no patch. The previous console versions were never updated and never got the DLC that they promised players, which makes me wonder if they are going to do the same for current gen consoles now.
