title: Great upgrade once you figure out installation
text: Overall a good upgrade from the OEM it’s a 5 star product with 4 star installation. It helped the quest fit better for sure . Reduced the slippage of the headset making game play smoother . Made my son a happy camper , his head is pretty big for 11 but not quite adult sized so this helped with the fit , and to keep it from getting soggy with sweat . A good upgrade . I did have to assist in the installation process but after a bit of research it was clear on what needed to be done . I’d order it again if I had to do over.

title: Worth the wait
text: Worth the wait , bought from Amazon for retail. Amazon has such a better process for buying a ps5 compared to the PS store . If you ask for an invitation to buy a ps5 from amazon and get an invitation in your email , you for sure 100% can order one . It’s not a free for all like the other method for buying it from the manufacturer for retail . I love that Amazon made the process easy and straightforward. It’s a great system , our ps4 couldn’t handle some games and would sound like it was getting ready to take off flying . The ps5 is so smooth and quiet . Doesn’t overheat . It’s been fun for sure . Worth the wait . Paying Retail is awesome. I like buying directly from amazon as the seller. It did get dropped off with my bottled water boxes and just left . If you order one be aware it will just be left on your doorstep like it’s a $12 case of water . Not signing for it surprised me a lot .

title: Well worth it.
text: Much better than expected. The joystick tips are awesome, and the little stubby on the controller handles have like a massaging effect. It just feels awesome without being too cumbersome. The best part is, you have full access to your battery compartment. Whether you have replaceable batteries, or a dock charger, this shouldn't interfere. Honestly for the price, you can not beat these. Only thing I wish is that it was more form-fitting on the back above the battery compartment, but it does not interfere with game play. You just have to slightly hold it up when you change the battery. Not even a big deal.

title: Sensational!
text: Anyone who gives this book a one star is either stupid or a left-wing liberal who hates the military and never has anything good to say about it. Even the ones who claimed they served. I read this book from cover to cover and found Chris Kyle interesting, funny and truthful. I love the way he talked honestly about his deployment and realization of war as well as his love for his children and wife, Taya. I could not put this book down, except to sleep. I recommend this book to all who care about what our troops are doing in the Middle East and the sacrifice they all make...not just their lives on the line, but what it cost their families. God bless you Chris Kyle...RIP! LOVE!

title: A lot more comfortable than the head strap that came with the Oculus
text: I would have given this 5 stars but I had a couple of issues so I deducted one star for those. They are minor issues that would not prevent me from buying this strap again but hopefully, the manufacturer will read this and take the issues under consideration when they design any future models. The issues I had were one, the directions were a little complicated and it took me a few minutes to get the strap put together and on my head correctly. I couldn't figure out how to attach the top strap (over or under the sides?) Two, the strap was more comfortable than the one that came with the Oculus but not as tight as I would have liked and I was still able to see light around the bottom (over my nose). I did purchase a sweat band to wear underneath the Oculus and now I have a nice tight fit (the sweat band also keeps me from getting too hot so that issue worked out in the end. Three, the strap does not fit inside any of the Oculus carrying cases. It is wider than most other 3rd party straps and after trying all the different 3rd party cases, I gave up and found a nice sized box and lined it with felt to protect the Oculus. I am hoping the strap manufacturer will come out with a carrying case that the strap will fit inside of. Fourth, I bought extra batteries to use when I am playing but when I plug them into the strap nothing happens except the battery falls off. I still have not figured out any work around for this problem so I have to stop playing and plug the Oculus up to a power source to restore battery life. Like I said, all minor issues that don't reduce the quality of the strap and it is still better than all the other straps I tried.

title: Worth every penny
text: By far the best version of the previous 2 releases. Battery: this seems to be a plaguing issue with the previous versions. The battery indicator on the base station eliminates the guessing game of your battery capacity. And the fact that you can put the headset down and walk away for a few minutes. The headset will power off or go into idle mode until you pick it up again. Setup: It's plug and play. It's paired up with your PS4 once it goes into the base station Quality: Outside material seems to be the same as the 2nd gen model. Their is a $50 mod kit available if you want to get leather ear pads. This is probably the only fault of the product. For $300, I would expect the leather ear pads to be included Audio quality: This is where the value comes in. In the 1st and 2nd gen models. When placing a FPS, the bass and sounds get too distorted at times. Almost like it can't handle it. I set the EQ setting to Pro (option 3) and played it really loud. Sound quality didn't skip a beat Ease of use: Previous models required the mixamp to be plugged in for a firmware update. The base station can be plugged in directly into your computer. Along with a software download so that you can manage the sound from a user friendly interface. Adjusting sound quality or using the preset options. You will always have the latest firmware update. I've had issues with the 2nd gen model on this issue, and it seems like they solved it Price: Yes it's pricey. You can get some other headsets that are considered premium for half the cost. The strength in Astro is the comfort and quality. After a few hours of gaming or long raids. You'll tend to feel the discomfort in some headsets. If you have the money to spend. Go for it. You won't be disappointed. This comes with a 1 year manufacturers warranty. If you can get an extended warranty through Bestbuy. I would do so in a heart beat. Playing this over the course of 2 years at maximum output might have its wear and tear issue.

title: A modern classic.
text: Yes, everybody thinks that Robobot is superior to this game in every way, but I think that Triple Deluxe feels much more like classic Kirby than it. Although Robobot has a lot of quality of life improvements over Triple Deluxe, it strays quite a ways away from the natural Kirby feel with its Robobot Armor mechanic being almost half of the game. The Hypernova mechanic doesn't appear quite as much but makes it feel more powerful as a result. Overall, Robobot is if you want a fresh breath of air and something Kirby that isn't all that Kirby, while Triple Deluxe is if you like the same old Kirby and want more of the same old Kirby.

title: Hands down best Paper Mario game!
text: Paper Mario the Thousand Year Door is definitely the best Paper Mario game! The partner mechanics, the versatility with badges, the heart-touching story, and the unique characters make this game a whole! I personally like how there are completely unique characters (not being a toad or another genaric npc) that don't contribute to the main story (Wonkey and Ishnail to name a few). One thing this game could use, though is a sort of boss rush mode or at least a way to refight bosses. Other than that, though, this is an easy 5 stars and is great all around!

title: I personally really like this game
text: I personally really like this game. It's not the best quality graphics wise. Doesn't help that my husband does 3D modeling, makes it easy to point out all the visual flaws. Overall the game control is good and to me it wasn't as graphic as I had expected. Some controversial material within, but not what I had expected. It has 7 unique endings depending on how you play out the game and an estimated 12 hrs of game play. Be warned if you're expecting any kind of battling, this game is mainly discovery and hiding. Much like Clocktower for the PS. Not bad for an indie crowd funded game. Looking forward to the upcoming patch that will uncensor the game.

title: Mine works great!
text: No problems with mine. I did have an interesting event though. When I initially plugged this into my monster surge protector it would not power on and I figured "oh great" But remembering an occasion with another device I figured I'll plug it directly into the wall and voila! Powered on. I noticed that when I plugged in my HMDI cable "a known good one from amazon" it goes in but there is a snap when fully plugged in like plugging in an optical cable. Booted up fine, downloaded 1.50 and installed three games. Been going strong for 24 hours being left on. Killzone is kind of a let down, I'm enjoying Ghosts and BF4 multiplayer especially. Being a PC gamer for the last 7 years I can finally say I have a console that I enjoy playing and the graphics are pretty darn good. A+ Sony, Love the controller too!

title: Good for the money but a step down from the G930
text: I used to have a G930 for several years and decided to give the G533 when my last G930's frame cracked and I needed a headset the same day from a local store. If you're just looking for something above-average and can deal with little annoyances, then this is a decent choice. THE GOD: An audiophile might find fault in the sound quality but for us normal human beings, it sounds fine - rich, booming bass and decent mids and highs. I use these all the time for conference calls and can hear everyone very clearly and my voice seems to come through perfectly fine. Would I use this to record myself if I wanted to become a singer? No, but that's not what these are for. It's also pretty comfortable. Fairly lightweight, and I can wear these all day every day without my ears hurting at the end of the day. I have average-sized ears and these fit comfortable over them. They're not really noise-canceling (at least not more than any other device that goes over your ears). This isn't a good or bad thing - it was just one of the star ratings, and I'm not sure why. The battery life seems decent, and I have yet to have an audio signal glitch (which was a rare but recurring problem with all the G930s I ever owned), which is good. The range is pretty decent, as well. I wore these while I went to the kitchen to make myself lunch, and I was probably a good 30-40 feet away from the receiver with about 4-5 walls in-between and no line-of-sight, and there was no audio dropout or loss in quality. I have 2 big complaints with this headset: 1. My first main complaint with the microphone is that my old G930 used to have a red LED at the tip of the microphone that would come on whenever my microphone was muted, so it was easy to know at a glance. It may not seem like it would be hard to remember if you're muted or not, but when you're on lots of calls where you're constantly muting and unmuting, it's pretty handy. On the G533, the mute/unmute button will simply play a 2-tone sound - there's no visual indicator. When there's a lot of other audio happening, it can occasionally be hard to tell if the 2-tone sound was the UNmute or the MUTE sound, so I might have to press it again to figure out what mute state I'm in. 2. My second main complaint is that plugging in the micro-USB cable to charge this headset is a serious pain, especially if you're just trying to keep the headset on while doing it. First of all, the volume dial is right next to the charging port, so if you're just trying to feel for the space where the charging port is, you're going to accidentally roll the volume dial, which is annoying. Then, since it's micro-USB, the cable will only plug in in one direction. So if you finally manage to get the cable into the little space, if you had the plug facing the wrong way, you have to do it all again. And even when you do get it in the right way, there's enough space to turn it into one of those situations where the plug never seems to find the port, and after about 15-20 seconds of fumbling, you get irritated and have to take off the headset to see to plug it in. This was a problem with the G930, too, although at least the G930 didn't have the volume dial so close to the port. I read that the G733 is USB-C, which should help quite a bit, since you don't have to worry about the direction anymore.

title: Good sound, but no noise isolation and bad mic
text: I picked up a pair of these when I needed to send my trusty G930 headset in to get exchanged. My wife and I work back-to-back in a home office, and she is on the phone a lot, so I was looking for a headset that was comfortable to wear all day and would effectively isolate noise so that her voice wouldn't carry into my mic for my calls (mic noise cancellation), and also would not intrude on my music when I wasn't on a call (headphone noise cancellation). The box advertised all of this, so I went ahead and got it. PROS: - It is indeed comfortable for all-day wear. - Good audio quality (better bass than the G930, but otherwise equal quality, IMO) - Being able to retract the mic is nice. - The 3.5mm plugs mean I can use these with portable music players when I travel. CONS: - Microphone quality is terrible. - Microphone mute switch doesn't work 100%. - No advertised "30dB noise isolation" in the headphones. On my very first call, I kept being asked whether I was in a busy office or a train station or something because the microphone was picking up -everything-. I tried to lower the volume, but it was impossible to find a setting where the other party could hear me without hearing everything else in the room (not to mention noise / static galore). I also tried to use the in-line mic mute switch, but it apparently didn't do a full job - it just muted the volume of the microphone by about 90%, so you could still hear things through the mic at a very low volume (confirmed by listening to the audio stream on loopback). These two things meant that I had to keep going to the softphone's mute button and un-muting myself to talk, then re-muting afterwards. Very inconvenient. As far as the "30dB noise isolation" goes, I might as well not be wearing the headphones. I can hear everything outside the headphones extremely clearly, even my wife typing on the keyboard (it's a soft-touch keyboard, too, so the raw sound is not that loud). I have no idea who thought that there was ANY noise isolation whatsoever. These will be going back to the store as soon as I get my G930 back.

title: PvP; not so much econ or PvE
text: This game has been out for 2 years; I played in it from beta up to Fall of 2009. In this time frame, a lot of changes happened. FSL opened up with high hopes and 8 servers. In the past 2 years, that shrank to 2. The ship combat system is very innovative, and that is the game's main strength. The emphasis these days is on PvP play, with the balance of power constantly shifting between British, French, Spanish, and Pirate realms. You can still have fun if you prefer PvE, but that is secondary, and it is difficult to make a difference in the Realm vs. Realm plot of the game if you are not a combat monster or part of an organized group. There are areas where incautious or new players can be forced into involuntary PvP play, which is part of what drove me away from the game. If you lose a ship in combat, you will be penalized with loss of gear, which was a major irritant for casual play because of the effort to rebuild. There can be a lot of trash talk, so go into it with a thick skin. I liked the game while I was playing, but I was mostly a PvE or economic player, and the gradual drift towards PvP eventually made me look for alternatives.

title: serious no go
text: I've purchased this from the same seller twice. the first one was wonderful until the battery died. the backlight was great, worked great, easy to use on the tv and pc. However, it would not charge. I tried multiple outlets, wall boxes, USB directly into tv and pc. Nada. I tried to find another cord. Nope. Asked to buy an extra. Nothing. So I bought a second. Why? Because two WORKING units would be great for this home. New unit, new cord, except this time it wouldn't charge to use. Using second cord the first wouldn't recharge either. I tried the comments and finally gave up. I bought a different keyboard from another seller and have had not one issue.

title: Not Comfortable
text: They sound good. Good reports from people about mic quality. They are just not comfortable. Somewhat heavy + pressure points make them not useful for long gaming sessions or binging some netflix. I really wanted to like these. I even replaced the ear pads with the ones from the 600 but to no avail. I do not recommend this headset due to the above + the price. Way too expensive for something I can only wear for 30 mins or so at a time. [Yes I have tried to adjust them. Over and over up and down, levers from side to side. Nothing works...]

title: Awesome Keyboard for Anything!
text: [[VIDEOID:fde036749dec9bb4a99e2fc8728e7f60]] Now this comes down to personal preference of the type of keyboard you like. If you like a quite soft touch keyboard then I wouldn't purchase this one. This is a great mechanical keyboard that has so many different and unique options you'll be playing with different configurations for a while. I love this style keyboard myself and wouldn't trade it for anything. I had been looking for a good mechanical keyboard at a good price and this one was perfect. This has the look and feel of a full mechanical keyboard with the benefits of a membrane keyboard. I didn't realize this until I had gotten it and used it a while. After realizing it I saw the uniqueness of it and how well it worked. I honestly couldn't notice until I removed a key. I love the fact that it is heavy and feels solid. The edges are sharp and can cut you if you aren't careful so this certainly isn't for younger kids. I sincerely believe that this keyboard will outlast the next three computers. It really seems that well built and sturdy. I'm don't find the mobile phone holder useful but that's probably because I don't really use my phone in landscape mode and it has to sit on something solid to remain in portrait mode while resting there. This is an amazing keyboard for the price and feels exactly the way I like a keyboard to feel. Just remember it feels much more like a full mechanical keyboard then a membrane one so if that is what you are looking for then this is defiantly it and you won't be disappointed!

title: Phenomenal Value, Good DPI Adjustments, Smooth Movement
text: [[VIDEOID:91d60f98665af166ab9949cc9dfcaf24]] I have to say I was very skeptical of anyone saying this could be considered a gaming mouse but I was wrong. This is a very good mouse for the money. Don't get me wrong it's not anywhere near a competition mouse but it's still a good gaming mouse. It is simple to install, just plug and play no 3rd party software required at all. It's very easy to configure your favorite or preferred color color or array of colors as you can see in the video. You can even change colors on the fly. The DPI is easy to set and there are plenty of choices to fit most people needs. I have to say that there is no way you could be disappointed with this mouse for the money. It's a bit light for my personal taste because I like a little heft but it seems that most people now-a-days prefer lighter products. I really expected to be sending this back but instead it is currently running on one my systems. I haven't tried it on an Xbox One or PS/4 yet, but I don't see why it wouldn't work. To be completely honest the USB C adapter that comes with it is worth the price of the mouse. I sincerely hope everyone enjoys this value priced gaming mouse as much as I do. Please note that a good mouse pad is a must.

title: Decent product, Easy to Install
text: It causes annoying interference with the microphone. The paddles are in a strange and uncomfortable location in my personal opinion. The fact that it doesn't work with other micro-USB cords is horrible because the cheap cable is worthless. It was very easy to setup and configure. I would much rather have a MS Elite controller but they are junk also now. If you are going to make a USB cord proprietary then at least make sure it has the clips that lock it in place. I can't say I have tried the mods because that's cheating and wouldn't be fair. However, if I had to guess I would say they would work great based on what I have seen. It was a waste of money for me because I just couldn't get over the location of the paddles because they weren't natural to me and I didn't want them to become muscle memory encoded.

title: Great Product lots of fun!
text: This system works very well with the Alienware AW17R4-7345SLV-PUS 17" Laptop (7th Generation Intel Core i7, 16GB RAM, 1TB HDD, Silver) VR Ready with NVIDIA GTX 1070 that I purchased from Amazon also. I took of one star because I have had problems with the sensors not calibrating correctly and it wants you to configure it standing. I got the Oculus Rift over the HTV because I wanted a sitting VR experience to start. I am still working on the configuration and playing with settings. So far I have gotten it to work but have never gotten a perfect calibration of the sensors which makes it hard to use the controllers that come with it. I also have not been able to get it to work with steam VR as of yet.

title: Simple, clean, easy
text: Exactly what it says it is. Can't go wrong with OEM products. Have tried most of the other charging options and with the new Elite controller the old ones no longer work. Their are some nice charging systems out there I will probably try out, but for now this works with all controllers for Xbox One and is Li-Ion. So for my Elite controller this is the best solution. It is Microsofts fault that their elite controller will not work with the other charging systems because the used a different battery cover. I have tried the other charger and battery options before my elite and they all took up too much space and usually had cheap batteries. So I will stick with these until I see something new that has the same quality battery.

title: Still a Great Game All These Years Later!
text: I have been playing this game every year since it came out in 2007, 2K Sports have always had the edge over EA Sports when it came to basketball games. The fluid motions, ease of playing and overall enjoyment is great. For those who are unaware, College Basketball games have stopped being made since 2009, the last of which was NCAA Basketball 10 by EA Sports. While the EA game has an ESPN feel, the game seems to lack the heart and excitement that College Hoops gives you. The legacy mode in College Hoops cannot be beat, everything is controllable from recruiting, training, schedules, even creating your own chants. Oh and of course the weekly NCAA show, (the same thing EA still has yet to put into any of its games). The fact that NCAA Basketball 10 is 2 years older than the last College Hoops game is the only reason people are paying 3x the amount than Hoops 2K8. If you are stuck on the fence between the 2, choose 2K8, you will not regret your decision.

title: A Must For Every WWE Fan Old & New
text: So i was able to get this when Amazon had it on sale for $30. At that price i was sure not to be let down had i not liked the game, like WWE 12, which for some reason came off as too big of a change with very little payoff. The main selling point to me, much like many others was the Attitude Era, which hands down is the greatest feature ever put into a WWE game. Being able to relive all the moments i remember from my childhood, the classic matches, incredible moments, and all the characters in between. (Not to mention they show stock video footage as you progress, heck they show more in this game than the WWE Attitude Era dvd recently put out). There were times when i was jumping up and down with excitement like i did all those years ago, the same excitement i would get from playing old classic THQ games No Mercy and Wrestlemainia 2000 for Nintendo 64. The entrances are great, still some issues with commentary and crowd noise, maybe not as noticeable without surround sound, but a minor flaw to say the least. The roster is impressive, but with some of the characters missing, does disappoint, the DLC packs do help a bit with adding a few of the up and coming talent but with THQ going bankrupt dont expect to see any additional content to be released. Having said that creating superstars or using the online community to download other created superstars is very impressive to give you those must have superstars not in the game. For what i paid i am very happy with the game, and is a great step up for WWE 12. Dont know what will happen going forward, but this was a game to put THQ out on a high note.
